beacons.comment: Strip any leading run of NODE_DECORATION_SYMBOLS (and surrounding whitespace) from a beacon role/comment value before it is used to build a Workflowy node NAME. Prevents trident/AST-emoji from being baked into role=/comment= and then compounding on each deterministic F12 refresh. Whitespace-and-symbol-only input collapses to "". SINGLE HOME: moved from nexus_map_codebase to beacon_mutation_contract (SPEC v5 §2); nexus_map_codebase imports + re-exports it.

THE ONE beacon-comment validator (SPEC v5 §3), shared by every mutation ingress. Rejects LF/CR/NUL, all other C0 controls, DEL, C1 controls, U+2028/U+2029, block delimiters (/* */ <!-- -->), beacon delimiters (@beacon[ / BEACON (), and Workflowy transport-entity patterns (named lt/gt/amp/quot + decimal/hex numeric refs -- fixpoint rule B). Applies the single-home leading-decoration strip so the accepted value is a fixpoint of the F12 round-trip (fixpoint rule A). Empty/whitespace normalizes to None. Commas, = and ] are SAFE and never rejected (Dan's ruling) -- internal AND trailing.

THE ONE beacon field parser shared by every per-language block parser (nexus_map_codebase + beacon_obtain_code_snippet): a line starts a field only if it begins with a KNOWN key and '='; any other line continues the previous field (multi-line values, joined with one space); the trailing ',' / ']' run is stripped from the value's last line only, then surrounding quotes. Single-line blocks parse exactly as the legacy per-site loops did.

The field parser's silent decision, said out loud: the keys of lines that look like key=value but name no BEACON_FIELD_KEYS key, which parse_beacon_field_lines glues onto the previous field (or ignores before the first). Same start regex, same key set; pure. Called by the block parsers only when a diagnostics sink is passed.

The typed comment intent carried by a mutation operation (2R4E1P). preserve: no comment requested -- keep the pre-existing comment (disk-parsed authoritative, note fallback), never rejects. fill_if_empty: the DEFAULT fill semantics -- fill ONLY an empty comment; a conflicting existing comment is now KEPT with a warning (kept_existing_conflict), labels still ensured, never an error. replace: explicit opt-in overwrite. append: keep the existing comment and extend it with the requested text.

THE ONE comment resolver (SPEC v5 §5 step 7 ordered contract; 2R4E1P). NORMALIZATION FIRST: requested / note_comment / disk_comment are all compared in parser-normalized form (trailing run of , and ] stripped, replicating the legacy field parser) and the value WRITTEN is the normalized form. preserve never rejects (disk value wins, note fallback, divergence is NOT an error). fill_if_empty NEVER errors: divergent note+disk -> kept_existing_conflict (disk wins); disk == requested -> idempotent; disk != requested -> kept_existing_conflict (existing comment kept, WARNING carries both texts); disk empty + note != requested -> kept_existing_conflict (the note's claim is kept); disk empty (note empty or == requested) -> fill (materialize; a re-run then noops via the idempotent rule -- invariant 10). A kept conflict means LABELS STILL ENSURED, comment kept, comment_outcome='kept_existing_conflict' + warning; re-run with replace/append to change it. replace writes the requested text (equal text -> idempotent). append keeps the existing comment and extends it: empty disk -> fill, already-appended text -> idempotent, else existing + ' ' + requested.

strip_leading_decoration_symbols(comment) if not comment: return None for ch in comment: code = ord(ch) if ( code < 0x20  # C0 controls (incl. \n, \r, \x00) or code == 0x7F  # DEL or 0x80 <= code <= 0x9F  # C1 controls or code in (0x2028, 0x2029)  # LINE / PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR ): raise ValueError( f"unsafe beacon comment {comment!r}: contains forbidden " f"control character U+{code:04X}" ) for token in _FORBIDDEN_COMMENT_TOKENS: if token in comment: raise ValueError( f"unsafe beacon comment {comment!r}: contains forbidden token {token!r}" ) if _TRANSPORT_ENTITY_RE.search(comment): raise ValueError( f"unsafe beacon comment {comment!r}: contains a Workflowy " "transport-entity pattern (would drift on the next F12 write cycle)" ) return comment # @beacon[ #   id=auto-beacon@_parser_normalize_comment_value-l0ro, #   role=_parser_normalize_comment_value, #   slice_labels=beacon-writeback, #   kind=ast, # ] def _parser_normalize_comment_value(value: Optional[str]) -> str: """Replicate the legacy beacon field parser's rebuild-time normalization. The legacy parsers strip a trailing run of ',' / ']' when re-reading a rebuilt beacon block. All comment equality/conflict comparisons happen in this PARSER-NORMALIZED form (SPEC v5 §5 step 7, NORMALIZATION FIRST) so a trailing-comma comment converges in ONE cycle instead of producing a false conflict on re-run. Nothing is ever REJECTED here for a trailing delimiter (§3) -- normalization exists purely for comparison/writing. """ text = (value or "").strip() while text and text[-1] in ",]": text = text[:-1].rstrip() return text # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # THE ONE beacon field parser (key/value logic shared by every block parser) # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Every field name any beacon block parser reads. A line starts a NEW field # only when it begins with one of these names followed by '=' (optional # spaces before the '='); every other line CONTINUES the previous field. BEACON_FIELD_KEYS = frozenset({ "id", "role", "slice_labels", "kind", "start_snippet", "end_snippet", "comment", "comments", "show_span", }) _BEACON_FIELD_START_RE = re.compile(r"^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*=") # @beacon[ #   id=auto-beacon@parse_beacon_field_lines-mlbf, #   role=parse_beacon_field_lines, #   slice_labels=beacon-writeback,carto-fwd-source, #   kind=ast, #   comment=THE ONE beacon field parser shared by every per-language block parser (nexus_map_codebase + beacon_obtain_code_snippet): a line starts a field only if it begins with a KNOWN key and '='; any other line continues the previous field (multi-line values, joined with one space); the trailing ',' / ']' run is stripped from the value's last line only, then surrounding quotes. Single-line blocks parse exactly as the legacy per-site loops did., # ] def parse_beacon_field_lines(texts: Any) -> dict[str, str]: """Parse a beacon block's inner lines into ``{key: value}``. ``texts`` are the block's inner lines with the language's comment prefix ALREADY stripped by the caller, and the caller's structural lines (the ``@beacon[`` opener, ``<!--`` / ``-->`` wrappers, the closing ``]``) already excluded. Each caller keeps its own prefix stripping and block collection; only this key/value logic is shared. Rules: a line whose text begins with a key in ``BEACON_FIELD_KEYS`` followed by ``=`` starts a new field (value = the text after the first ``=``); any other non-empty line continues the current field (a wrapped value); text before the first field is ignored; parts are joined with ONE space; the trailing run of ``,`` / ``]`` is stripped from the joined value (i.e. from its LAST line only -- a wrapped inner line may end in a comma), then one pair of surrounding quotes; a repeated key: the last occurrence wins. For a block whose fields are all single-line this returns exactly what the historical per-site loops returned. """ fields: dict[str, str] = {} cur_key: Optional[str] = None parts: list[str] = [] def _flush() -> None: if cur_key is None: return val = " ".join(p for p in parts if p).strip() while val and val[-1] in ",]": val = val[:-1].rstrip() # Same quote rule as the historical loops (byte-identical results). if (val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"')) or ( val.startswith("'") and val.endswith("'") ): val = val[1:-1] fields[cur_key] = val for raw in texts or (): text = (raw or "").strip() if not text: continue m = _BEACON_FIELD_START_RE.match(text) if m and m.group(1) in BEACON_FIELD_KEYS: _flush() cur_key = m.group(1) parts = [text[m.end():].strip()] elif cur_key is not None: parts.append(text) _flush() return fields # @beacon[ #   id=auto-beacon@beacon_field_unknown_keys-ufk1, #   slice_labels=beacon-writeback,carto-fwd-source, #   kind=ast, #   comment=The field parser's silent decision, said out loud: the keys of lines that look like key=value but name no BEACON_FIELD_KEYS key, which parse_beacon_field_lines glues onto the previous field (or ignores before the first). " "Re-run with comment_mode 'replace' to overwrite, or 'append' to extend." ) @dataclass(frozen=True) # @beacon[ #   id=auto-beacon@BeaconCommentIntent-le7f, #   role=BeaconCommentIntent, #   slice_labels=beacon-writeback,agent-kit-vendor, #   kind=ast, #   comment=The typed comment intent carried by a mutation operation (2R4E1P). preserve: no comment requested -- keep the pre-existing comment (disk-parsed authoritative, note fallback), never rejects. fill_if_empty: the DEFAULT fill semantics -- fill ONLY an empty comment; a conflicting existing comment is now KEPT with a warning (kept_existing_conflict), labels still ensured, never an error. replace: explicit opt-in overwrite. append: keep the existing comment and extend it with the requested text., # ] class BeaconCommentIntent: """The typed comment intent carried by a mutation operation. ``mode='preserve'``       -- no comment requested: keep the pre-existing comment (disk-parsed authoritative, note fallback); never rejects; a label-only mutation never erases a comment. ``mode='fill_if_empty'``  -- a comment was requested: fill ONLY when the disk field is empty; a DIFFERENT existing comment is KEPT (kept_existing_conflict resolution + warning), never an error and never an overwrite (2R4E1P). ``mode='replace'``        -- explicit opt-in overwrite: write the requested comment even when one exists (equal text stays idempotent). ``mode='append'``         -- keep the existing comment and extend it with the requested text (empty disk fills; already-appended text stays idempotent). Evaluate in EXACTLY this order (SPEC v5 §5 step 7, 2R4E1P): NORMALIZATION FIRST: before ANY equality/conflict comparison, requested, note_comment and disk_comment are compared in PARSER-NORMALIZED form (the same trailing ','/']' strip the legacy field parser applies on rebuild). THE ONE beacon-comment validator (SPEC v5 §3), shared by every mutation ingress. CAS fingerprint mismatch at the atomic source writer. Raised by _write_markdown_lines_sanitized when the optional expected_sha256 compare-and-swap check fails: the on-disk raw bytes changed after the caller computed its plan, so the planned write must NOT land. The file is left byte-for-byte untouched (zero write). The Lightning Rod mutation commit seam maps this to error_kind='source_changed_since_plan' (distinct from 'plan_mismatch', which covers every OTHER plan/disk divergence).

THE mandatory beacon write path for ALL language helpers -- now an ATOMIC REPLACE (build sanitized output in memory -> temp file in the same directory -> write -> flush+os.fsync -> shutil.copymode(source,temp) [permissions only, NOT timestamps -- a successful mutation always leaves a fresh mtime] -> os.replace -> temp cleanup on failure). Optional expected_sha256 CAS: mismatch raises SourceChangedSincePlanError with ZERO bytes written. Zero-preliminary-writes invariant: a planned beacon commit performs no disk write before its one final atomic replacement.

Used for NOTE no-op suppression in reconcile_trees_cartographer so a whitespace-only edit to a slurped comment/docstring (e.g. '#nexus' -> '# nexus') is still seen as a real on-disk change and propagated by F12+1. Fixes the silent skipped-update where the header whitener collapsed the lone inserted space and declared the note unchanged.

Strip Workflowy presentation-only underline markup from tag tokens. Workflowy may expose rendered tags through /nodes-export as #<u>tag</u> or #tag<u>-emoji</u>; those <u> wrappers are visual styling, not tag content. Also removes the interim malformed <-u> artifact created by the emoji-preserving sanitizer before this fix.

Per-token slice-label sanitizer. Converts STRUCTURAL separators/punctuation (whitespace, : . / \ , # |) to hyphens but PRESERVES Unicode letters and emoji, because Workflowy tags fully support emoji (e.g. #nexus--curation-🏷️). Also strips Workflowy's presentation-only <u> tag-underlining wrappers when they leak through /nodes-export. The previous ASCII-only allow-list [^A-Za-z0-9_-] silently ate every emoji/Unicode codepoint, which mangled or deleted emoji-bearing tags on F12+2/F12+3 write and the following F12+1 reconcile. Shared by the plan seam's anchor reconciliation and the commit seam's verification.

Unlike the legacy per-writer closures it ALSO preserves start_snippet/end_snippet (a labels-only mutation can never drop a span beacon's anchors, §5 step 10) and it SKIPS the note-derived decoration strip / transport-entity decode (explicit plan-resolved values only, §3 fixpoint rules).

Never open on marker mentions or borrow fields/terminators across blocks; Markdown requires a complete dedicated HTML comment outside code fences. Malformed or differently identified blocks are not deleted.

beacons.role: _execute_beacon_write_plan(language, file_path, name, note, write_intent, write_plan, occurrence)
beacons.comment: THE shared plan-branch execution engine for every language helper (SPEC v5 §6). VERIFIES the plan against live disk state (dispatch path, planned operation, plan-selected physical target, raw-bytes sha256 CAS) -- a sha divergence is source_changed_since_plan, every OTHER divergence is plan_mismatch, both with ZERO write. Then executes the planned operation with the plan-resolved comment, sourcing metadata per §5 step 10: slice_labels + comment from the plan; role/kind/show_span/start/end snippets from the FRESH DISK PARSE (a labels-only mutation never rewrites them). 2R4E1P: the plan's comment decision is authoritative -- fill keeps an existing comment (a kept conflict's resolved comment IS the on-disk text; only a fill plan that would overwrite a DIFFERENT live comment is refused, existing_comment_present/plan_mismatch); replace/append overwrite/extend explicitly. Span deletes also remove the matching @beacon-close[ block. Exactly ONE atomic replacement via _write_markdown_lines_sanitized(expected_sha256=...).

Locate a @beacon[ block in a .vue file whose PARSED id EQUALS bid (never a prefix/substring test -- the id=foo vs id=foo2 collision fix, SPEC v5 §6). Skips @beacon-close[ blocks. Returns (start_idx, end_idx) or None.

F12+3 phase 8 reads, this writes (during F12 ingest path).
Explicit claimed Markdown C0 repair authority: pure in-memory transform, cancellation check before one same-directory fsync/copymode/os.replace commit, evidence logging, and zero-write no-op.

The file is left byte-for-byte untouched (zero write). The Lightning Rod mutation commit seam maps this to error_kind='source_changed_since_plan' (distinct from 'plan_mismatch', which covers every OTHER plan/disk divergence).

THE mandatory beacon write path for ALL language helpers -- now an ATOMIC REPLACE (build sanitized output in memory -> temp file in the same directory -> write -> flush+os.fsync -> shutil.copymode(source,temp) [permissions only, NOT timestamps -- a successful mutation always leaves a fresh mtime] -> os.replace -> temp cleanup on failure). Optional expected_sha256 CAS: mismatch raises SourceChangedSincePlanError with ZERO bytes written. Zero-preliminary-writes invariant: a planned beacon commit performs no disk write before its one final atomic replacement.

Fixes the silent skipped-update where the header whitener collapsed the lone inserted space and declared the note unchanged.

Strip Workflowy presentation-only underline markup from tag tokens. Also removes the interim malformed <-u> artifact created by the emoji-preserving sanitizer before this fix.

Per-token slice-label sanitizer. Converts STRUCTURAL separators/punctuation (whitespace, : . / \ , # |) to hyphens but PRESERVES Unicode letters and emoji, because Workflowy tags fully support emoji (e.g. #nexus--curation-🏷️). Also strips Workflowy's presentation-only <u> tag-underlining wrappers when they leak through /nodes-export. The previous ASCII-only allow-list [^A-Za-z0-9_-] silently ate every emoji/Unicode codepoint, which mangled or deleted emoji-bearing tags on F12+2/F12+3 write and the following F12+1 reconcile. Single source of truth shared by _canonicalize_slice_labels and _canonicalize_slice_labels_union.

Canonicalize legacy beacon metadata alias comments= to comment= during F12 flows.

PURE disk read+beacon-parse for the Lightning Rod mutation plan seam (SPEC v5 §5 step 4). Returns (lines, beacons) for any of the 7 beacon languages. The Markdown control-char sanitize is IN-MEMORY ONLY here (zero preliminary writes, §7); parse_markdown_structure is not called on this path. Vue files are parsed with BOTH the JS parser (script // + style /* */ forms) and the Markdown parser (template <!-- --> form) so id-cardinality checks see every beacon in the file. Optional keyword-only diagnostics= list is forwarded to the one parser called; refused for Vue (a whole-file Vue parse sees template blocks twice: use _vue_section_beacons).

Compute the 0-based inclusive (start_idx, end_idx) extent of one parsed beacon block. Markdown/HTML: comment_line is the @beacon[ line; the block runs from the nearest preceding <!-- (blank-line tolerant) through the matching -->. Line-comment languages (python/js_ts/vue-script/sql/shell/yaml): the block runs from the @beacon[ line through the line whose prefix-stripped body is exactly ]. Shared by the plan seam's anchor reconciliation and the commit seam's verification.

ONE pure Python decorator-syntax authority shared by forward beacon attachment, outline/comment-context starts, and reverse beacon identity matching. AST ownership plus tokenizer logical-line boundaries covers stacked/multiline/parenthesized decorators. Builds a whole-file index once; callers may supply the AST from the same source snapshot to avoid reparsing. No I/O, evaluation, mutation, or attachment policy.

Shared physical-block anchor matcher for preflight/JIT identity reconciliation and legacy writer idempotency. Python gaps may cross only AST-owned decorator syntax ranges (including stacked/multiline/parenthesized decorators); beacons before, between, or after decorators retain their identity. All other gap rules and cardinality checks stay unchanged: unrelated code is never crossed, and a block embedded inside a decorator expression is not a leading beacon. Optional keyword-only decorator_ranges_by_definition= takes the whole-file decorator index precomputed once for the same lines (a whole-file check then parses once, not once per target).

Resolve a node's anchor target to a 0-based line (AST def line via the PURE outline builders; Markdown heading via _find_markdown_heading_insert_idx with the occurrence ordinal). Returns (idx0, ambiguous): (None, False) = unresolvable (exact-ID identity branch), (None, True) = ambiguous outline match (fail closed). Never writes; never calls a mutating parser. Optional keyword-only outline= takes the file's already-built outline in place of re-parsing it per target.

beacons.comment: Module-level beacon block renderer for the commit-seam plan branch (§6). Covers every language grammar: python/shell/yaml (#), js_ts/vue-script (//), sql (--), markdown/vue-template (<!-- -->), vue-style (/* */). Unlike the legacy per-writer closures it ALSO preserves start_snippet/end_snippet (a labels-only mutation can never drop a span beacon's anchors, §5 step 10) and it SKIPS the note-derived decoration strip / transport-entity decode (explicit plan-resolved values only, §3 fixpoint rules).

Find a structural close-marker comment block with the exact id and return its 0-based inclusive extent for every writer's span delete. Never open on marker mentions or borrow fields/terminators across blocks; Markdown requires a complete dedicated HTML comment outside code fences. Malformed or differently identified blocks are not deleted.

beacons.role: _execute_beacon_write_plan(language, file_path, name, note, write_intent, write_plan, occurrence)
beacons.comment: THE shared plan-branch execution engine for every language helper (SPEC v5 §6). VERIFIES the plan against live disk state (dispatch path, planned operation, plan-selected physical target, raw-bytes sha256 CAS) -- a sha divergence is source_changed_since_plan, every OTHER divergence is plan_mismatch, both with ZERO write. Then executes the planned operation with the plan-resolved comment, sourcing metadata per §5 step 10: slice_labels + comment from the plan; role/kind/show_span/start/end snippets from the FRESH DISK PARSE (a labels-only mutation never rewrites them). 2R4E1P: the plan's comment decision is authoritative -- fill keeps an existing comment (a kept conflict's resolved comment IS the on-disk text; only a fill plan that would overwrite a DIFFERENT live comment is refused, existing_comment_present/plan_mismatch); replace/append overwrite/extend explicitly. Span deletes also remove the matching @beacon-close[ block. Exactly ONE atomic replacement via _write_markdown_lines_sanitized(expected_sha256=...).

Locate a @beacon[ block in a .vue file whose PARSED id EQUALS bid (never a prefix/substring test -- the id=foo vs id=foo2 collision fix, SPEC v5 §6). Skips @beacon-close[ blocks. Returns (start_idx, end_idx) or None.

Optional keyword-only diagnostics= list: it then also records each opener's outcome (kept / skipped_unknown_kind / skipped_empty_id) with its end line and field keys, each close candidate its second pass examines, and each close it matches; the return value never changes.

Attach Markdown beacons under headings or decorate headings directly. Writes BEACON (MD AST) blocks into Workflowy heading notes — ANY field-ordering or whitespace difference between cache and on-disk reapply triggers spurious UPDATE in node_data_equal. F12+3 phase 8 reads, this writes (during F12 ingest path).
Explicit claimed Markdown C0 repair authority: pure in-memory transform, cancellation check before one same-directory fsync/copymode/os.replace commit, evidence logging, and zero-write no-op.

CAS fingerprint mismatch at the atomic source writer. Raised by _write_markdown_lines_sanitized when the optional expected_sha256 compare-and-swap check fails: the on-disk raw bytes changed after the caller computed its plan, so the planned write must NOT land. The file is left byte-for-byte untouched (zero write). The Lightning Rod mutation commit seam maps this to error_kind='source_changed_since_plan' (distinct from 'plan_mismatch', which covers every OTHER plan/disk divergence).

THE mandatory beacon write path for ALL language helpers -- now an ATOMIC REPLACE (build sanitized output in memory -> temp file in the same directory -> write -> flush+os.fsync -> shutil.copymode(source,temp) [permissions only, NOT timestamps -- a successful mutation always leaves a fresh mtime] -> os.replace -> temp cleanup on failure). Optional expected_sha256 CAS: mismatch raises SourceChangedSincePlanError with ZERO bytes written. Zero-preliminary-writes invariant: a planned beacon commit performs no disk write before its one final atomic replacement.

Parses Markdown into NEXUS node tree (AST). Phase 8 of F12+3 (post-write reconcile reads back from disk via this) — emits MD_PATH metadata for every heading. Suspect for spurious-UPDATE generation if MD_PATH ordering or whitespace round-trips differ from cache.

Shared junk-stripper for structural comparison (markup/backtick/HTML-entity/quote/emoji handling in ONE place). collapse_whitespace gates ONLY the final whitespace removal: True (default) = the original header/name comparison behavior, byte-for-byte unchanged; False = preserve whitespace so a whitespace-only content change is still seen as a difference (used by whiten_note_for_compare for the note no-op-suppression path).

Note-comparison twin of whiten_text_for_header_compare: identical junk-stripping (markup/backtick/HTML-entity/quote/emoji), but whitespace is PRESERVED (collapse_whitespace=False). Used for NOTE no-op suppression in reconcile_trees_cartographer so a whitespace-only edit to a slurped comment/docstring (e.g. '#nexus' -> '# nexus') is still seen as a real on-disk change and propagated by F12+1. Fixes the silent skipped-update where the header whitener collapsed the lone inserted space and declared the note unchanged.

Sibling of _extract_beacon_id_from_note. Reads the slice_labels: line out of the BEACON (...) block in a node note. Used by the F12+3 step [3] bulk-apply pre-filter to detect nodes whose name #tags already match the on-disk beacon block (skipping the ~480ms MarkdownIt parse for those nodes).

Sibling of _extract_beacon_id_from_note. Reads the role: line out of the BEACON (...) block in a node note. Used by the F12+3 step [3] bulk-apply pre-filter to detect nodes whose decoration-stripped name matches the on-disk beacon block's role (e.g. catches Workflowy heading renames that need a disk write).
Heuristic filter for noisy JS/TS local variables so F12 maps meaningful locals without single-letter spam.
Create per-scope JS/TS parser state so anonymous lambda identities and local occurrence counters stay stable across formatting-only edits.
Assign stable parent-local ordinal identities to anonymous JS/TS lambda scopes instead of using file line numbers.
Assign stable occurrence-index suffixes to meaningful lambda-local declarations so comments and whitespace do not churn AST_QUALNAMEs.

beacons.role: Cartographer virtual groups: stable source-authored grouping wrappers
beacons.comment: Shared helpers for source-comment-driven virtual grouping. Comments like '# @carto-group id=x label="X"' or '// @carto-group id=x label="X"' create synthetic non-AST Workflowy wrapper nodes while preserving runtime source semantics. Also supplies group identity extraction and any-depth UUID seeding so first migration is MOVE-not-delete/create.

Strip Workflowy presentation-only underline markup from tag tokens. Workflowy may expose rendered tags through /nodes-export as #<u>tag</u> or #tag<u>-emoji</u>; those <u> wrappers are visual styling, not tag content. Also removes the interim malformed <-u> artifact created by the emoji-preserving sanitizer before this fix.

Per-token slice-label sanitizer. Converts STRUCTURAL separators/punctuation (whitespace, : . / \ , # |) to hyphens but PRESERVES Unicode letters and emoji, because Workflowy tags fully support emoji (e.g. #nexus--curation-🏷️). Also strips Workflowy's presentation-only <u> tag-underlining wrappers when they leak through /nodes-export. The previous ASCII-only allow-list [^A-Za-z0-9_-] silently ate every emoji/Unicode codepoint, which mangled or deleted emoji-bearing tags on F12+2/F12+3 write and the following F12+1 reconcile. Single source of truth shared by _canonicalize_slice_labels and _canonicalize_slice_labels_union.
Strip normalized beacon metadata blocks from context; construct the close-marker test without a literal marker so older span writers cannot mistake this code for a closer.

Helper: True iff id looks like prefix@000123 (digits after @). Used by F12 beacon normalization.

Python implementation for normalize_duplicate_ast_beacons_in_file (anchor skips blank/#comments/@decorators).

Select Python assigned names that should become Cartographer outline nodes, including module-level dunder globals like __version__ and __all__
Choose the note label for mapped Python assigned names, distinguishing module-level dunder globals from regular constants
Public wrapper (R1): runs the ungrouped core parse_file_outline_core and applies virtual-group grouping; a parse failure returns the same Parse Error warning node as before
Module-level helper lifted in Phase A consolidation: decode a tree-sitter node's source bytes to text. Shared by parse_js_ts_outline and _parse_js_ts_outline_from_source.
Module-level helper lifted in Phase A consolidation: True when v is a tree-sitter arrow_function or function node. Shared by parse_js_ts_outline and _parse_js_ts_outline_from_source.

Module-level helper lifted in Phase A consolidation: extract the trailing identifier of a call_expression's callee (e.g. computed in computed(...)). Shared by parse_js_ts_outline and _parse_js_ts_outline_from_source.

Module-level helper lifted in Phase B.1 consolidation: detect wrapper calls like computed(() => ...) so nested computed declarations appear in Workflowy AST maps. Shared by parse_js_ts_outline and _parse_js_ts_outline_from_source.

Module-level helper lifted in Phase B.1 consolidation: return the BODY node of the setup function passed to defineStore (Pinia setup-store form), else None. Shared by parse_js_ts_outline and _parse_js_ts_outline_from_source.

Module-level helper lifted in Phase B.1 consolidation: return the options object passed to defineStore (Pinia options-store form), else None. Shared by parse_js_ts_outline and _parse_js_ts_outline_from_source.

Module-level helper lifted in Phase B.1 consolidation: extract the text of an object-literal property key, stripping surrounding quotes. Shared by both outline builders inside _extract_define_store_options_children.

Module-level helper lifted in Phase B.1 consolidation: extract a function-like node's parameter list as a parenthesized string (e.g. (a, b)). Shared by both outline builders inside _extract_define_store_options_children.

Module-level helper lifted in Phase B.1 consolidation: return the body field of a function-like tree-sitter node, or None. Shared by both outline builders inside _extract_define_store_options_children.

Per-parse JS/TS outline context. Encapsulates file/source data, the Vue line_offset0 + qual_prefix configuration, and the shared priority counter so both outline builders can invoke a single shared _js_walk function.

Module-level Phase D helper: extract method/getter functions from a defineStore options object. Calls back into _js_walk for nested scopes. Behaves identically for whole-file JS/TS and Vue script blocks via ctx.qualify and ctx.abs_line.

The crown-jewel Phase D consolidation. Single shared recursive walker for both whole-file JS/TS (parse_js_ts_outline) and Vue script blocks (_parse_js_ts_outline_from_source). All Vue-vs-non-Vue divergence is encapsulated in the JsTsOutlineContext's abs_line/qualify methods so the walker body is identical.

Ungrouped core of parse_js_ts_outline (R1): maps the extension to a tree-sitter language name, parses the file and walks the outline, then parses and applies JS/TS beacons; assumes tree-sitter is importable and does no grouping and no parse-error handling -- errors propagate to the wrapper

Public wrapper (R1): checks the extension and tree-sitter availability, runs the ungrouped core parse_js_ts_outline_core and applies virtual-group grouping; a parse failure returns the same Parse Error (JS/TS) warning node
Rebases a Vue section's parsed beacons (or, with keys=, the parser's diagnostics records) from section-local lines to .vue file lines.

THE Vue SFC section split: the top-level template / script / style elements of a parsed .vue file, in order, each as {type, start_tag, content_row0, raw_text}. Extracted from parse_vue_outline, which calls it with _parse_vue_sfc_tree's root; the beacon check calls the same pair.

THE per-section beacon parse of a Vue SFC: template sections through the Markdown parser, script and style through the JS parser, rebased to file lines. Extracted from parse_vue_outline's three branches; an optional diagnostics= list receives the section parser's records, rebased the same way.

Builds a .vue file's section nodes (template / script / style). The section split is _vue_sfc_sections over _parse_vue_sfc_tree (only the tree-sitter parse becomes the Parse Error (VUE) node) and each section's beacons come from _vue_section_beacons: both extracted, shared with the beacon check.

Pure root→target parent-chain walk over a pinned /nodes-export map — the F3 walk lifted verbatim out of the WS handler (512-hop cap, visited-set cycle guard, HTML-entity-decoded names) so the F3 hotkey and the node.ancestors verb share ONE walk. Returns [] when the target is absent; a broken parent link truncates at the last resolvable ancestor. Source node dicts are never mutated (the decoded name rides on owned entries — the pre-lift handler wrote _decoded_name back into cache dicts; this core does not).

The ONE ancestor-chain document composer shared by the F3/F2 WS handler and the node.ancestors verb (they can never drift): heading per ancestor with ⦿/• bullets, key line + dock.peek-verbatim metrics legend at the top of every standalone render, right-side markers in peek's compact order (⚓ ⭐ Ⓛ ✓) plus 🗺️ mapped folder / 📄 mapped file via the existing _classify_node_map_state authority, four source metrics via build_dock_peek_index rooted at the chain's topmost ancestor (ONE post-order pass). uuids: 'leaf' (F3 → `uuid` tail) | 'every-level' (F2 per-node UUID lines + Use Leaf UUID tail) | 'none'. standalone=False composes a fragment (no key/legend/tail — the WS handler's mirror-context block). Pure: callers pass the pinned map; source nodes never mutated; Dock classification runs only with the caller-supplied configured vocabulary (base_tags AND postfix kwargs — never defaulted per site).

ONE normalized, immutable AnchorDockUpdate request (frozen) -- the FIRST semantic concern on the section-9 client->server mutation channel. Produced by from_wire (browser ingress); the MCP path needs no twin because anchor.dock.update passes params straight to _anchor_dock_update_impl, which owns the pure shape validation (the impl IS the shared core). Carries INTENT ONLY: dock_handle + favorite/local (set/unset) + optional families (the family base the attribute write targets). The client composes NO tag, resolves NO handle, picks NO postfix word, reads NO node name to decide state (the UI sends favorite=!is_favorite from the server-supplied row). _anchor_dock_update_impl stays the sole semantic authority -- from_wire validates the transport shell only (K3).

THE exact-archive test (E2 at every handle, rev 2 §4.4.3): is the supplied string — bracket-unwrapped and hyphen-normalized as the prefix kernel compares — EXACTLY the full id of a VISIBLE archived record? Asked by the Layer-1 UUID primitive whenever its live kernel outcome is SHAVED, in EVERY mode and with no operation context alike, so an exact archived full UUID never becomes a wrong-target shave (F2); a beacon operation never asks it (Axiom 12 — its shave stands, as before this program). Answered from the map's archive partition when the map carries one (the record marker is the authority), else through the store's ONE lookup with exact_only=True against the active overlay for the operation's live view (lazy load; no second match algorithm). Side-effect-free: never raises, never resolves, never records, never requests the re-run; with no folder configured the answer is always no (G1). Only an exact full UUID counts — a prefix that also matches an archived record never displaces a shave.

THE fallback gate (§4.4.3): called by the two resolution primitives ONLY in their archive phase, when the map carries no archive partition — the re-run request and nothing else (rev 2: the exact-archive case moved to the side-effect-free is_exact_archived_id, asked at the shave in every mode; the gate never fires from a live phase). Inert unless the current operation context's mode is 'fallback'; on a store hit it sets state.rerun_requested so the invoker re-runs the whole handler ONCE on the augmented view (§4.5) and the primitive returns unresolved. Never raises, never resolves, never returns an archived node itself: the gate is a decision, not a resolver.

THE archive-aware miss (§4.7.2): every site that reports a node handle as not found calls this FIRST. Returns the exact §5.2–§5.3 text (chosen by the context's reason: write -> §5.2.1 with the §5.2.2 how-to-copy sentence for extract / promote-move; export -> §5.3.1; sink -> §5.3.2; purge_preview -> §5.3.3; no context -> §5.3.4) when the store's lookup — against the active overlay for the operation's live view, exactly as the gate does — HITS, else None (the site then appends the light hint when the handle is AP-shaped, ap_miss_hint). The texts come only from archive_texts.py; the site raises ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError(message, extra=provenance) with what this returns — or, in a batch ledger, writes the skip row. The beacon family never calls it (Axiom 12). An unexpected reason (a read's fallback/flag context) returns None: a read never refuses an archived node — its gate hit is served by the re-run before any not-found text is built.

diagnostics.kind_raw: _handle_lookup_kind(supplied) try: store = get_archive_store() uuid_hit, provenance = store.miss_lookup( supplied, kind, live_view=_snapshot_live_view() ) except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - the miss text never raises return None, None, None if not uuid_hit or not isinstance(provenance, dict): return None, None, None path = str(provenance.get("archive_file") or "") exported_at = str(provenance.get("exported_at") or "") verb_name = verb or (context.operation if context is not None else "") or "operation" if context is None: return ( archived_no_context_text(verb_name, supplied, path, exported_at), provenance, uuid_hit, ) reason = context.reason if reason == "write": if role in ("parent", "destination"): return ( archived_parent_read_only_text( verb_name, role, supplied, path, exported_at ), provenance, uuid_hit, ) text = archived_node_read_only_text(verb_name, supplied, path, exported_at) if copy_hint == "promote_move": return text + PROMOTE_COPY_SENTENCE, provenance, uuid_hit if copy_hint == "extract" or (not copy_hint and verb_name == "anchor.point.extract"): return text + EXTRACT_COPY_SENTENCE, provenance, uuid_hit return text, provenance, uuid_hit if reason == "export": return ( archived_export_refusal_text(verb_name, supplied, path, exported_at), provenance, uuid_hit, ) if reason == "sink": return ( archived_sink_refusal_text(verb_name, supplied, path, exported_at), provenance, uuid_hit, ) if reason == "purge_preview": return ( archived_purge_preview_text(verb_name, supplied, path, exported_at), provenance, uuid_hit, ) # A read context (fallback / include / none-with-no-reason): a read # never refuses an archived node — the gate's hit is served by the # re-run before any not-found text would be built.  Fall through. return None, None, None def ap_miss_hint(supplied: str, *, beacon: bool = False) -> "str | None": """The §5.4 light hint for one AP-shaped not-found, or ``None``. ``beacon=True`` (the beacon family's resolve and scope-root surfaces) returns the beacon line without consulting the store (Axiom 12); otherwise the hint state comes from the store's facts for the current live view: A (no folder), C (folder not fully readable) or B (searched, ``n`` active archives, not found).  ``None`` when the handle is not AP-shaped — UUID-shaped misses keep today's text exactly ([ap:O8R74F]). """ from .archive_texts import ( ap_hint_beacon, ap_hint_no_folder, ap_hint_not_found, ap_hint_unreadable, ) if not _is_ap_shaped_handle(supplied): return None if beacon: return ap_hint_beacon() from .archive_store import get_archive_store try: facts = get_archive_store().ap_hint_facts(_snapshot_live_view()) except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - the hint never raises return ap_hint_no_folder() state = facts.get("state") folder = str(facts.get("folder") or "") if state == "A": return ap_hint_no_folder() if state == "C": return ap_hint_unreadable(folder)

§4.10 (Axiom 15): the daemon's memory of the extension's archive_folder option, called from _resolve_note_session_config right after every settings reply. A reply without the key (an older extension) changes nothing; a changed trimmed value updates the in-memory value AT ONCE and rewrites archive_folder.json in the runtime dir atomically ({"archive_folder", "learned_at"}) — UNLESS the current operation is augmented, in which case the file write DEFERS to the next non-augmented settings read (the dirty flag flushes even on an unchanged value; Axiom 5, E36). Every archive read uses the remembered value; no archive read ever performs a settings round trip.

THE one archive store (Archive Reads U1, §4.1-§4.2; U3 adds the inventory, the mount write and the folder memory): lists the archive folder through the injected folder provider (production: read_remembered_archive_folder), lazily and change-driven (list + stat on every ensure_loaded; reparse only on (mtime_ns, size) change; drop vanished; one store_generation counter), parses every file ONLY through node_archive.parse_archive (no second reader), classifies each file per live generation (unreadable / skipped vault / dormant root-still-live / candidate, then shadowing: live wins per subtree, newest exported_at wins per subtree, ties by file name; planting under mount_parent_id else source_parent_id else top, orphans and mount cycles at the top; sibling priority M+1+k after the live children), and builds the one overlay of 📦-marked records carrying the _nexus_archive provenance marker. Looks up: all_ap_cores (Axiom 11, every readable state), lookup(supplied, kind) for the fallback gate, and inventory(live_view) — EVERY file as one row, whatever its state, also when no overlay exists. Writes ONLY the daemon's archive_folder.json memory (remember_archive_folder_from_reply, deferred inside augmented operations) and, for the mount verb, the ONE sanctioned mount_parent_id edit through with_mount_parent + serialize_archive + a parse-back/byte-identity verification (nodes untouched). No TTL, no background reload, no on-disk index (Axiom 17).

THE one overlay accessor (§4.2.3): overlay_for(live_view) returns None when no archive record is visible (callers stay on the live view, Axiom 14 — byte-identical behaviour), else the ArchiveOverlay cached in ONE slot keyed on (live view identity, store generation), holding a strong reference to live_view; a new live generation or a store change rebuilds, nothing else is cached. overlay.augmented_view is constructed DIRECTLY (two container copies, live node dicts shared by identity, no deep copy) and lazily cached on the overlay.

beacons.role: singleton localhost websocket broker between browser extension(s) and many MCP servers
beacons.comment: Endpoint-based broker: owns ws://127.0.0.1:8765; routes by request_id + originating MCP socket, and (browser side) by logical tab ENDPOINT multiplexed over one physical per-extension connection. Supports many tabs, many browsers/profiles, many MCP clients.

Liveness probe for a browser/MCP websocket. True only when the connection's State is OPEN (websockets>=10 exposes .state; older builds expose .closed/.open). Tolerant by design: an UNKNOWN/unreadable state is treated as LIVE so we never falsely prune a usable socket -- pruning is a targeted fix for demonstrably-CLOSED sockets, not a guess.

beacons.role: BrowserEndpoint: one logical Workflowy tab behind a browser connection
BrowserConnection: one physical per-extension socket owning many endpoints

beacons.comment: Broker registry: browser connections, endpoints, MCP clients, request->origin routing, and the designated PRIMARY WORKER for browser-initiated Direction-B work frames (primary_mcp_id + self-healing primary_mcp_ws())

Designate (or clear) the user's DEFAULT GLIMPSE tab by endpoint_id (set via the 'Set default' button in a tab's UUID Explorer widget). A transient in-memory routing preference: when a GLIMPSE arrives with no target_tab and 2+ tabs are connected, resolve_target_endpoint routes to this default instead of erroring. Refuses to point at a non-live endpoint; _clear_default_if_stale drops it when its tab closes.

Registry hygiene: drop every endpoint whose owning browser socket is no longer OPEN (via _ws_is_live), remove any browser connection thereby emptied, and self-clear a now-stale default. Invoked at the TOP of resolve_target_endpoint so single-tab auto-select and multi-tab ambiguity both operate on LIVE endpoints only -- fixes the single-open-tab GLIMPSE 15s timeout where a dead-but-registered endpoint (autoping is disabled on the listener) was auto-selected and the send silently black-holed.

Option B endpoint-liveness reconcile. The service worker (the only component that can observe which Workflowy tabs exist behind its one connection) reports its live endpoint roster on each keepalive ping. This refreshes last_seen for every rostered endpoint on the reporting connection, and -- ONLY when roster_complete is True (post-settling-window, authoritative) -- REAPS endpoints registered on that connection but absent from the roster (ghosts from a killed tab whose endpoint_unregister was lost). Reap is by roster-ABSENCE, never by age, so an idle-for-hours-but-live tab is never dropped. A non-authoritative roster refreshes last_seen but prunes nothing. Scoped to the reporting connection only -- never touches endpoints on OTHER browser connections.

Direction-B PRIMARY WORKER selector. Returns the websocket of the single MCP client that should execute browser-initiated work frames (F12/CARTO/cache-refresh/windsurf/markdown-gen/uuid-path/bulk-apply). Self-healing: if the recorded primary_mcp_id is stale/disconnected it promotes any remaining MCP client; returns None only when NO MCP client is connected. Election happens in register_mcp (first client wins); promote-on-disconnect happens in unregister.

Live, in-memory broker registry snapshot for the workflowy_broker_status observability tool: browser connections (id, legacy, ws_open, endpoint_count), every endpoint (id, alias, title, url, connection_id, seconds_since_seen, is_default), the default endpoint id, and MCP clients (id, ws_open, is_primary) + the primary id. Reads nothing from disk and mutates nothing (a pure read of the registries), so it is safe to answer inline in the broker's frame loop exactly like ping->pong. This is the surface that would have made the ghost-endpoint bug visible instantly.

Resolve the SINGLE public 'target_tab' token (the one the glimpse MCP tool exposes) to one browser endpoint, ALIAS-FIRST then endpoint_id fallback (no format-sniffing). None -> single-tab default / actionable multi-tab error via resolve_target_endpoint. Replaces the confusing two-field target_endpoint_id/target_alias surface for callers; the two-field resolver remains for internal/back-compat use.

WSLIVE2 DoD-A: the SINGLE broker-owned endpoint-liveness ghost classifier. Returns True iff a resolve-miss error dict is the 'socket-alive-but-endpoint-ghost' class (code=='unknown_browser_endpoint' -- a TARGETED endpoint_id absent from the registry), False for every ordinary routing/config code (unknown_browser_alias / ambiguous_browser_alias / no_browser_connected / ambiguous_browser_target / unknown_target_tab). Every MCP->browser resolve-miss site consults THIS instead of re-deriving ghost-ness inline, so the heal-vs-ordinary-error decision can never drift across the 5+ sites. Behavior-IDENTICAL to the prior inline err_code=='unknown_browser_endpoint' check -- this is the architectural CONSOLIDATION; the behavioral symptom-3 heal is caller-intent routing (target_endpoint_id) putting stale-endpoint misses onto this exact code.

beacons.role: ƒ frame_is_liveness_ghost(frame): wire-frame twin of miss_is_liveness_ghost -- classifies an INBOUND SW reverse-map ghost reply
⚡ _safe_send(ws, obj): error-swallowing JSON send used by all broker routing

beacons.comment: Fan a 'default_endpoint_changed' frame out to every browser connection so each tab's UUID Explorer widget can render the correct 'Default tab' / 'Set default' button label after the designated default GLIMPSE tab changes (set, cleared, or self-cleared on tab close).

AMENDMENT B (WSLIVE): on a DETECTED endpoint-liveness ghost (a targeted MCP->browser miss / dead forward / SW map-miss), fan an untargeted 'broker_request_endpoint_register' frame out to every browser connection so every live tab re-announces its endpoint. Reuses the EXACT frame the SW already broadcasts to its tabs on its own reconnect: an untargeted broker->SW frame hits the SW's final else branch and is fanned to all tabs via broadcastToTabs, and each page client's existing broker_request_endpoint_register handler calls registerBrokerEndpoint(). ZERO new client mechanism; idempotent for already-live tabs (register_endpoint just refreshes last_seen). Rate-limited per endpoint_id by Broker.reregister_broadcast_allowed so a ghost-hit burst cannot storm it.

Per-connection handler: hello handshake then role-based routing. MCP->browser frames resolve a target endpoint (GLIMPSE: request_id + single public target_tab via resolve_target_tab, or legacy target_endpoint_id/target_alias) OR fan a no-target result/status frame out to all browser connections. browser->MCP frames either resolve a correlated reply by request_id OR (no request_id = Direction-B work: F12/CARTO/cache-refresh/etc.) route to the single designated PRIMARY WORKER via broker.primary_mcp_ws() instead of broadcasting — preventing duplicate detached workers / dueling disk writes under multi-server.

"browser" _log( f"Legacy browser connection inferred: {conn.connection_id} " f"(implicit single endpoint)." ) # ---- application-level keepalive ------------------------------- # Browser SW keepalive alarms send {action: "ping"} every ~30s. # This is NOT Direction-B work and should not be routed to the MCP # primary worker (which previously produced noisy "no MCP client" # logs and made the ping useless when no agent session was open). # Answer directly so the sender can prove broker liveness without # involving any MCP server. if action == "ping": # Option B: a browser keepalive ping MAY carry the service # worker's authoritative endpoint roster. Reconcile the # reporting connection's endpoints against it (refresh # last_seen; reap ghosts only when roster_complete). This is # what heals a killed tab whose endpoint_unregister was lost, # so single-tab auto-select stops seeing a phantom second tab. # MCP-client pings carry no roster and are unaffected. if role == "browser" and "endpoint_roster" in msg: broker.reconcile_browser_roster( ws, msg.get("endpoint_roster"), bool(msg.get("roster_complete")), ) await _safe_send( ws, { "action": "pong", "type": "pong", "source": "glimpse-broker", "ts": time.time(), }, ) continue # ---- routing --------------------------------------------------- request_id = msg.get("request_id") if role == "mcp": # MCP -> browser. Two sub-cases: # #  (a) A correlated REQUEST (GLIMPSE): carries a request_id #      and/or an explicit target (target_endpoint_id/_alias). #      Resolve to exactly one tab and forward (existing path). # #  (b) A browser-bound RESULT / STATUS broadcast: the reply a #      primary worker emits for a browser-initiated work frame #      (carto_*_result, *_refresh_*_result/_status, uuid_path_ #      result, bulk_apply_*_result, ...). These carry NO #      request_id and NO target. They are NOT tab-specific #      requests — they are the symmetric return/broadcast of the #      historical no-request_id fan-out, and the browser side #      dispatches them by action name and reconciles by polling. #      Fan them out to ALL browser connections rather than #      running target resolution (which would otherwise return #      an 'ambiguous_browser_target' error under multi-tab and #      strand the result). This keeps F12/CARTO status flowing #      to every tab's widget, exactly as before the broker. # #  (c) A correlated REPLY to a browser-INITIATED request: the #      primary worker's answer to a frame a tab originated with #      its OWN request_id (e.g. render_markdown_modal_result). #      It carries that request_id and NO target. We must route #      it back to the ORIGINATING BROWSER socket (tracked when #      the browser-> branch forwarded the request to the #      primary), NOT run tab target-resolution (which would #      mis-handle a no-target frame under multi-tab). Checked #      FIRST, below, before (a)/(b). Safe vs GLIMPSE: a GLIMPSE #      REQUEST's request_id is not yet tracked when the MCP #      sends it (it is track_request'd at forward-time further #      down THIS pass), so resolve_request misses and it falls #      through to target resolution as before. broker.sweep_pending() # (0) broker_status: an MCP-initiated OBSERVABILITY request the # BROKER answers itself (it owns the registries) -- exactly like # ping->pong, but carrying a live registry snapshot. Answered # BEFORE correlated-reply resolution and target routing so it is # never mistaken for a browser-bound frame. Echoes request_id so # the MCP-side demux resolves the waiter. Pure read; no routing. if action == "broker_status": snapshot = broker.describe_state() await _safe_send( ws, { "action": "broker_status_result", "success": True, "request_id": request_id, *snapshot, }, ) continue # (c) Correlated reply to a browser-initiated request: deliver # to the recorded origin (a browser socket) and stop. if request_id is not None: _origin = broker.resolve_request(str(request_id)) if _origin is not None: await _safe_send(_origin, msg) continue # Public-tool surface sends a SINGLE optional ``target_tab`` # (alias-or-endpoint_id). The legacy two-field form # (target_endpoint_id / target_alias) is still accepted for # backward compatibility / internal callers. target_tab = msg.get("target_tab") target_endpoint_id = msg.get("target_endpoint_id") target_alias = msg.get("target_alias") # TAB-AGNOSTIC capability flag (internal; never on a public MCP # tool surface). The MCP server stamps tab_optional=true on # frames for operations that read SHARED cross-tab config and # therefore do not care WHICH tab answers (anchor tools, # list_canonical_tags, ...). When set, target resolution picks # a tab deterministically under multi-tab instead of erroring. # GLIMPSE/extract_dom never sets it, so it stays tab-specific. tab_optional = bool(msg.get("tab_optional")) if ( request_id is None and target_tab is None and target_endpoint_id is None and target_alias is None ): seen: set[int] = set() for conn in list(broker.browser_connections.values()): if id(conn.ws) in seen: continue seen.add(id(conn.ws)) await _safe_send(conn.ws, msg) continue # Prefer the single-token public path when present; otherwise # fall back to the explicit two-field resolver. if target_tab is not None: ep, err = broker.resolve_target_tab( target_tab, allow_arbitrary_when_ambiguous=tab_optional, ) else: ep, err = broker.resolve_target_endpoint( target_endpoint_id, target_alias, allow_arbitrary_when_ambiguous=tab_optional, ) if err is not None: # STEP 1 + REV3.1 CODE-FILTER: distinguish an endpoint- # LIVENESS ghost from an ordinary routing/config error. # resolve_target_endpoint emits FIVE codes; ONLY # 'unknown_browser_endpoint' (a TARGETED endpoint_id miss) # is the ghost class. The other four # (unknown_browser_alias / ambiguous_browser_alias / # no_browser_connected / ambiguous_browser_target) are # normal 'pick a tab / set a default / fix the alias / open # a tab' errors -- they are PRESERVED EXACTLY (their own # loud actionable message), are NOT collapsed into # unknown_endpoint, and do NOT trigger a re-register # broadcast (that would spam re-registers on ordinary # multi-tab ambiguity and mis-tell the agent to retry). # WSLIVE2 DoD-A: consult the ONE owned classifier instead # of re-deriving ghost-ness inline. Behavior-identical to # the prior err_code=='unknown_browser_endpoint' check -- # only a TARGETED endpoint miss is a ghost; the five other # codes stay ordinary routing/config errors below. if broker.miss_is_liveness_ghost(err): # A ghost: the tab said 'endpoint X' but it is not in # the registry (reaped-but-live). Normalize to the ONE # unified liveness code the client/MCP react to, and # fire the AMENDMENT-B on-demand re-register broadcast # (rate-limited per endpoint_id) so the live tab # re-announces in the background while the originator # retries against the loud reply below. reply = { "success": False, "request_id": request_id, *err, "code": "unknown_endpoint", } await _safe_send(ws, reply) _wslive( f"MCP->browser resolve-miss ghost: " f"target_endpoint_id={target_endpoint_id!r} " f"target_tab={target_tab!r} request_id={request_id!r}" ) _ghost_eid = target_endpoint_id or None if broker.reregister_broadcast_allowed(_ghost_eid): await _broadcast_request_endpoint_register(broker) else: _wslive( f"re-register broadcast SUPPRESSED (rate-limit) " f"for endpoint_id={_ghost_eid!r}" ) continue # Ordinary routing/config error: answer the originator # directly so it fails fast/cleanly (unchanged behavior). await _safe_send( ws, { "success": False, "request_id": request_id, *err, }, ) continue # Track origin for the eventual correlated reply. if request_id is not None: broker.track_request(str(request_id), ws) # Tag the frame with the resolved endpoint so the service worker # can route it to the correct tab/page context. forwarded = dict(msg) forwarded["target_endpoint_id"] = ep.endpoint_id # STEP 1: the forward-then-swallow black hole. If the resolved # endpoint's browser socket is DEAD, _safe_send returns False # and, previously, NOTHING went back to the originator -> a 12s # client timeout -> opaque 'server unavailable'. Convert that # dead forward into the SAME unified 'unknown_endpoint' reply # and fire the rate-limited re-register broadcast (a dead SW # socket is itself a liveness event worth healing). if not await _safe_send(ep.connection.ws, forwarded): # Untrack the request we just tracked above (the forward # died, so no correlated reply will ever arrive for it); # resolve_request pops it from the pending/origin maps. if request_id is not None: broker.resolve_request(str(request_id)) await _safe_send( ws, { "success": False, "request_id": request_id, "code": "unknown_endpoint", "target_endpoint_id": ep.endpoint_id, "error": ( "The target Workflowy tab's endpoint is not " "reachable (its browser socket is not live); it " "has been asked to re-register -- retry." ), "available_endpoints": [ e.describe() for e in broker.all_endpoints()

beacons.comment: Broker registry: browser connections, endpoints, MCP clients, request->origin routing, and the designated PRIMARY WORKER for browser-initiated Direction-B work frames (primary_mcp_id + self-healing primary_mcp_ws())

Designate (or clear) the user's DEFAULT GLIMPSE tab by endpoint_id (set via the 'Set default' button in a tab's UUID Explorer widget). A transient in-memory routing preference: when a GLIMPSE arrives with no target_tab and 2+ tabs are connected, resolve_target_endpoint routes to this default instead of erroring. Refuses to point at a non-live endpoint; _clear_default_if_stale drops it when its tab closes.

Registry hygiene: drop every endpoint whose owning browser socket is no longer OPEN (via _ws_is_live), remove any browser connection thereby emptied, and self-clear a now-stale default. Invoked at the TOP of resolve_target_endpoint so single-tab auto-select and multi-tab ambiguity both operate on LIVE endpoints only -- fixes the single-open-tab GLIMPSE 15s timeout where a dead-but-registered endpoint (autoping is disabled on the listener) was auto-selected and the send silently black-holed.

Option B endpoint-liveness reconcile. The service worker (the only component that can observe which Workflowy tabs exist behind its one connection) reports its live endpoint roster on each keepalive ping. This refreshes last_seen for every rostered endpoint on the reporting connection, and -- ONLY when roster_complete is True (post-settling-window, authoritative) -- REAPS endpoints registered on that connection but absent from the roster (ghosts from a killed tab whose endpoint_unregister was lost). Reap is by roster-ABSENCE, never by age, so an idle-for-hours-but-live tab is never dropped. A non-authoritative roster refreshes last_seen but prunes nothing. Scoped to the reporting connection only -- never touches endpoints on OTHER browser connections.

Direction-B PRIMARY WORKER selector. Returns the websocket of the single MCP client that should execute browser-initiated work frames (F12/CARTO/cache-refresh/windsurf/markdown-gen/uuid-path/bulk-apply). Self-healing: if the recorded primary_mcp_id is stale/disconnected it promotes any remaining MCP client; returns None only when NO MCP client is connected. Election happens in register_mcp (first client wins); promote-on-disconnect happens in unregister.

Live, in-memory broker registry snapshot for the workflowy_broker_status observability tool: browser connections (id, legacy, ws_open, endpoint_count), every endpoint (id, alias, title, url, connection_id, seconds_since_seen, is_default), the default endpoint id, and MCP clients (id, ws_open, is_primary) + the primary id. Reads nothing from disk and mutates nothing (a pure read of the registries), so it is safe to answer inline in the broker's frame loop exactly like ping->pong. This is the surface that would have made the ghost-endpoint bug visible instantly.

Resolve the SINGLE public 'target_tab' token (the one the glimpse MCP tool exposes) to one browser endpoint, ALIAS-FIRST then endpoint_id fallback (no format-sniffing). None -> single-tab default / actionable multi-tab error via resolve_target_endpoint. Replaces the confusing two-field target_endpoint_id/target_alias surface for callers; the two-field resolver remains for internal/back-compat use.

WSLIVE2 DoD-A: the SINGLE broker-owned endpoint-liveness ghost classifier. Returns True iff a resolve-miss error dict is the 'socket-alive-but-endpoint-ghost' class (code=='unknown_browser_endpoint' -- a TARGETED endpoint_id absent from the registry), False for every ordinary routing/config code (unknown_browser_alias / ambiguous_browser_alias / no_browser_connected / ambiguous_browser_target / unknown_target_tab). Every MCP->browser resolve-miss site consults THIS instead of re-deriving ghost-ness inline, so the heal-vs-ordinary-error decision can never drift across the 5+ sites. Behavior-IDENTICAL to the prior inline err_code=='unknown_browser_endpoint' check -- this is the architectural CONSOLIDATION; the behavioral symptom-3 heal is caller-intent routing (target_endpoint_id) putting stale-endpoint misses onto this exact code.

beacons.role: ƒ frame_is_liveness_ghost(frame): wire-frame twin of miss_is_liveness_ghost -- classifies an INBOUND SW reverse-map ghost reply
⚡ _safe_send(ws, obj): error-swallowing JSON send used by all broker routing

beacons.comment: Fan a 'default_endpoint_changed' frame out to every browser connection so each tab's UUID Explorer widget can render the correct 'Default tab' / 'Set default' button label after the designated default GLIMPSE tab changes (set, cleared, or self-cleared on tab close).

AMENDMENT B (WSLIVE): on a DETECTED endpoint-liveness ghost (a targeted MCP->browser miss / dead forward / SW map-miss), fan an untargeted 'broker_request_endpoint_register' frame out to every browser connection so every live tab re-announces its endpoint. Reuses the EXACT frame the SW already broadcasts to its tabs on its own reconnect: an untargeted broker->SW frame hits the SW's final else branch and is fanned to all tabs via broadcastToTabs, and each page client's existing broker_request_endpoint_register handler calls registerBrokerEndpoint(). ZERO new client mechanism; idempotent for already-live tabs (register_endpoint just refreshes last_seen). Rate-limited per endpoint_id by Broker.reregister_broadcast_allowed so a ghost-hit burst cannot storm it.

Per-connection handler: hello handshake then role-based routing. MCP->browser frames resolve a target endpoint (GLIMPSE: request_id + single public target_tab via resolve_target_tab, or legacy target_endpoint_id/target_alias) OR fan a no-target result/status frame out to all browser connections. browser->MCP frames either resolve a correlated reply by request_id OR (no request_id = Direction-B work: F12/CARTO/cache-refresh/etc.) route to the single designated PRIMARY WORKER via broker.primary_mcp_ws() instead of broadcasting — preventing duplicate detached workers / dueling disk writes under multi-server.

main(): console-script entry point for workflowy-glimpse-broker
singleton localhost websocket broker between browser extension(s) and many MCP servers
beacons.comment: Endpoint-based broker: owns ws://127.0.0.1:8765; routes by request_id + originating MCP socket, and (browser side) by logical tab ENDPOINT multiplexed over one physical per-extension connection. Supports many tabs, many browsers/profiles, many MCP clients.

Liveness probe for a browser/MCP websocket. True only when the connection's State is OPEN (websockets>=10 exposes .state; older builds expose .closed/.open). Tolerant by design: an UNKNOWN/unreadable state is treated as LIVE so we never falsely prune a usable socket -- pruning is a targeted fix for demonstrably-CLOSED sockets, not a guess.

beacons.comment: One place for the broker's network defaults, protocol identity, and shared-secret env var so broker.py and server.py never duplicate them.

Best-effort startup log GC (2026-07): bounds the two previously-unbounded per-user log sinks. Deletes aged-out per-PID workflowy-mcp-server-<pid>.log files (the real leak: a new file per MCP-server start) past WORKFLOWY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS (default 7), and size-caps the singleton append-only glimpse-broker.log past WORKFLOWY_BROKER_LOG_MAX_BYTES (default 5 MiB) by truncation. Invoked once at BOTH broker startup (run_broker) and MCP-server startup (lifespan). Never raises, honors WORKFLOWY_FILE_LOGGING=0, each fs op individually guarded (a locked live-server file is skipped; a live file's fresh mtime keeps it out of the candidate set anyway). Complements the Cartographer F12 job-log GC, which was already handled.

beacons.comment: Phase 0.5 (ap:EXECLDG §5-Correction#3 / §9) EXACT-OR-ERROR focus contract exception. Raised by materialize_from_document_forest when a CANONICAL row focus ({mode:'row', uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence} that survived _canonicalize_focus) FAILS to resolve occurrence-exactly against the materialized document_forest. There is deliberately NO lenient fallback: not the whole document, not the first occurrence, not a uuid-set match -- a silent whole-document degrade would show the agent/user content they did NOT intend, INVISIBLY, which is exactly what this contract forbids. Only a genuinely ABSENT focus (None -- _canonicalize_focus already maps malformed/empty to None) renders the whole document. Callers (Steps 6/7) catch this to emit the actionable slice_row_stale / refresh-cache message rather than crash. Distinct from f8_slice_policy.SliceProjectionInvariantError (a Phase-4 broken-invariant guard); this is a stale-focus signal, not a corruption signal.

THE one normalizer for the render-FOCUS primitive. Coerces a loose focus value into the canonical {mode:'row', uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence} dict, or None (= the full unfocused document). Lenient with a SAFE fallback to None: a non-dict / unknown-mode / empty-uuid focus degrades to 'no focus' rather than mis-rendering. Single entry point used by RenderProjectionSpec.normalize_from_glimpse_args (and, through it, the blob/modal-frame deserializers) AND imported at module scope by server.py _compose_render_scope so the render_scope focus echo is canonicalized identically wherever a focus enters -- one shape, one source of truth, no drift. Pure; no I/O. FOCUS_MODES is the recognized-modes tuple ('row' only today; the dict shape lets a future kind be added without a wire change).

RenderPolicy — the immutable, RENDER-FOREST-KEYED carrier of the occurrence-local render directives a focused/deprecated/chronological render needs, DECOUPLED from the tree: (1) the per-file/heading H1 rebase baseline, keyed by render-forest _index_path (covers BOTH the file-node root and the bare-MD-heading root); and (2) body suppression, carried as FOUR CAUSE-LABELED sets in DISTINCT keying disciplines — breadcrumb suppression is OCCURRENCE/index-path keyed (NOT a uuid-set, because a timestamp sort re-emits the same uuid and only SOME occurrences are focus breadcrumbs), deprecated-body suppression is uuid keyed (a per-node property), chronological-ancestor suppression (U6, ap:E03BN3) is OCCURRENCE/index-path keyed like breadcrumb (every non-leaf of the final render forest on a chronological render — computed ONLY inside the materializer from the producer-supplied chronological boolean), and lens-scaffold-ancestor suppression ([ap:I506WY], unit 5g) is OCCURRENCE/index-path keyed too (on a LENS render the connective scaffolding above the lens's input roots renders heading-only even in document order; computed ONLY inside the materializer from the producer-supplied lens_scaffold_ids the shared lens projection derives). The cause label is load-bearing: emit_body_false_for(render_key, uuid) lets BOTH renderers consume the THREE occurrence-keyed causes (breadcrumb ∪ chronological-ancestor ∪ lens-scaffold-ancestor) via the render_key branch, while deprecated-body suppression stays Markdown-only (include_deprecated). It is the policy the materializer fills and the composer/serializer consume, in place of loose side-channel params (focus_index_path / body_suppressed_ids / inline _min_md_depth_in_subtree). Frozen value object, no I/O; a sibling of RenderProjectionSpec (the request) — this is the derived RESULT-side policy. Also carries the UUID-keyed source-graph facts: direct_child_counts, and ([ap:0M6VP8] part a) uuid_prefix_collisions (the tiny 8-hex->colliding-ids index the headings-only serializer lengthens ambiguous short ids through, via the ONE unique_short_uuid_prefix authority) + full_uuid_headings (the full_uuids opt-in's result-side copy) + ([ap:UH0UOU]) source_metrics (the render-side four-field headings-vocabulary index — dock.peek's ▸/desc/self/tree from build_render_source_metrics over the same pinned cache; the composer's ONE heading-metadata emitter consumes it and suppresses the whole suffix on managed source lines).

Phase 0.5 Step 5 (ap:EXECLDG) MaterializedRenderDocument -- the immutable, SERVER-INTERNAL result object that IS the materialized answer to applying a spec (or a DOM capture) to a concrete source forest. It NEVER crosses the wire (unlike RenderProjectionSpec, the request handle): the client keeps sending a spec and keeps receiving the same serialized outputs (preview_markdown / preview_tree / rows / render_scope) -- this object is built server-side, rendered FROM, and discarded. It is the cohesive replacement for the old ever-growing bag of loose composer side-channel params (focus_path / focus_leaf / focus_index_path / body_suppressed_ids / inline _min_md_depth_in_subtree). Fields: document_forest (the complete projected+sorted+since forest -- AUTHORITY for rows, row identity/occurrence, focus resolution, and the rebase baseline; NEVER shrunk by focus); render_forest (exactly what the bottom renderer consumes: whole document for focus None, or the note-PRESERVING option-Y breadcrumb+subtree for a singleton focus -- notes are NEVER blanked, per v3.1 hazard-a); policy_by_occurrence (a RenderPolicy keyed in RENDER-FOREST coordinates -- the rebase baseline VALUES come from the unpruned document_forest but are re-keyed to render coords per v3.3 #1/#2, and the breadcrumb body-suppression set is occurrence/index-path keyed); document_rows (derived from document_forest so focusing never shrinks the top-half list); focus (canonical row-focus dict or None); node_count/depth (focused stats over render_forest). Frozen value object; introduced in Step 5 and WIRED through Steps 6-12b: every production render path (render_stage2_filter_sort, _render_slice_row_view, compose_markdown_modal_view, the DOM-capture dispatch) materializes through it, and the composer/serializer consume render_forest + policy_by_occurrence.

THE normalized cache-render request object -- the keystone of the cache-render pipeline. ONE immutable, frozen dataclass every cache-projected render (raw root dump / slice / slice+override / Lightning Rod) normalizes to before projection+render, so the same shared render pipeline is driven identically from EITHER origin: the SERVER (glimpse / lightning_rod MCP tools, and the push twin _glimpse_push_slice_to_modal) OR the CLIENT (Apply button, Refresh, row click, Lightning Rod ribbon). The origin fills the object with what it already knows and passes it through -- the server NEVER queries the client for a value it can supply itself (a server push forwards headings_only explicitly rather than inheriting the client dock toggle). Field groups: SOURCE/SCOPE identity (kind + root_uuid + group_id/group_name + opaque lightning selection); SELECTION/TRAVERSAL knobs (match_scope = WHERE to look for a tag/text match; descend_policy = HOW FAR to walk, a Phase-1 traversal boundary; exclude_completed); VIEW knobs (sort_by [wire spelling 'none'|'created'|'modified'] / sort_direction / since / recent_by ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a): the recency basis of a 'newest' item_count selection; None = resolve at apply) / headings_only / ancestor_notes [U6 teaching opt-out of the chronological ancestor-note suppression, default false]); OUTPUT/RENDER contract (as_markdown / content_format / tree_mode). Two orthogonal axes kept strictly separate and NEVER conflated: match_scope (selection predicate) vs descend_policy+exclude_completed (traversal) -- and descend_policy lives at the TOP LEVEL, never inside a Lightning Rod selection (which is about WHAT matches, not how far to walk) and never in Phase 2/3/4 (presentation policy). Two classmethod normalizers -- normalize_from_glimpse_args (the glimpse/lightning_rod public-arg surface) and normalize_from_modal_frame (an incoming client Apply/push frame) -- both encode the (slice_group, root_uuid, lightning) -> kind truth table identically (lightning>override>slice>raw_root); from_render_spec_blob deserializes the opaque wire blob through that SAME normalizer. sort_by_internal() is the ONE wire('none')<->internal(None) translation; to_render_scope_fields() serializes the scope-echo knobs for the server render_scope echo; to_render_spec_blob() serializes the FULL spec (incl. the opaque lightning selection) as the nested render_spec wire blob. WIRE CONTRACT: the nested render_spec blob is the SOLE scope/view contract on every render_slice_modal / render_slice_row / apply_slice_in_dock frame -- the only flat frame keys are the transport envelope (action / request_id / endpoint_id / row / max_prerender_chars). There is NO flat-scope-field fallback anywhere (client producers send blob-only; the server reads blob-only; the tab-side push receiver reconstructs the spec from the blob). BOTH origins are fully wired through this object: SERVER -- glimpse / lightning_rod / _glimpse_push_slice_to_modal build the spec (normalize_from_glimpse_args -> with_overrides(resolved scope)) and derive render_scope FROM it via the ONE bridge _compose_render_scope_from_spec (whose sole delegate is the scalar _compose_render_scope -- the single render_scope birthplace); _handle_render_slice_modal builds ONE incoming_spec (normalize_from_modal_frame) and derives every scope/view local from it. CLIENT -- requestSliceModalRender / requestSliceRowRender send frame.render_spec only; dockedSliceContext.render_spec is the SOLE client scope handle (adoptRenderScope -> normalizeRenderScopeToSpec), reused verbatim by Refresh + per-row re-render. So this object is the one and only cache-render request contract on BOTH origins.

beacons.comment: Phase 0.5 (ap:EXECLDG §5-Correction#3 / §9) EXACT-OR-ERROR focus contract exception. Raised by materialize_from_document_forest when a CANONICAL row focus ({mode:'row', uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence} that survived _canonicalize_focus) FAILS to resolve occurrence-exactly against the materialized document_forest. There is deliberately NO lenient fallback: not the whole document, not the first occurrence, not a uuid-set match -- a silent whole-document degrade would show the agent/user content they did NOT intend, INVISIBLY, which is exactly what this contract forbids. Callers (Steps 6/7) catch this to emit the actionable slice_row_stale / refresh-cache message rather than crash. Two classmethod normalizers -- normalize_from_glimpse_args (the glimpse/lightning_rod public-arg surface) and normalize_from_modal_frame (an incoming client Apply/push frame) -- both encode the (slice_group, root_uuid, lightning) -> kind truth table identically (lightning>override>slice>raw_root); from_render_spec_blob deserializes the opaque wire blob through that SAME normalizer. sort_by_internal() is the ONE wire('none')<->internal(None) translation; to_render_scope_fields() serializes the scope-echo knobs for the server render_scope echo; to_render_spec_blob() serializes the FULL spec (incl. the opaque lightning selection) as the nested render_spec wire blob. Delegates to the canonical emoji/trident-aware nexus_map_codebase.split_name_and_tags; only if that import fails (rare -- module-load-order safety net) does it fall back to an INLINE COPY that mirrors the canonical emoji-aware semantics byte-for-behavior (trident/marker/generic-decoration trailing region peeled, content-emoji kept, tags returned '#'-only). Wire->semantic NAME normalizer for the add/remove/rename_tag merge path (the '&' -> stored '&amp;' double-encode fix). Decodes EXACTLY ONE layer of &/</> from the raw GET /nodes/{id} name form via a non-cascading single pass -- the output is never re-scanned, so '&lt;' -> '<' (a user-visible literal entity stays a literal entity), NEVER '<'. Scope: the tag tools are the ONLY name-writers that read a raw wire-form name (live GET) and rewrite it; every other name-writer sources semantic text (caller-supplied, the dewhitened /nodes-export cache, disk content, or a synthesized constant). Do NOT substitute _dewhiten_text here: its chained str.replace calls cascade ('&lt;' -> '<' -> '<'), decoding two layers. The inverse of this helper is exactly encode_for_workflowy_api(field='name'), whose plain-text alphabet is only these three entities.

beacons.comment: F12+4 "save generated file" isolated reader: extract an ABSOLUTE Path: from INSIDE a leading MD_PATH: dummy metadata block on a node that lives inside a mapped Markdown file. Deliberately NOT folded into the universal first-line-only parse_path_or_root_from_note / _extract_path_header_from_note (those stay strict line-0 so ordinary nodes are never misclassified as FILE nodes). Used ONLY as a fallback by the F12+1 file-node refresh when no line-0 Path:/Root: header is present.

Parse a FILEBASE: value from a note's leading metadata block for F12+4 filename construction. Metadata block = lines from the top until the first blank line OR a '---' line (an optional leading '---' front-matter opener is skipped). FILEBASE: may appear on ANY line in that block (first occurrence wins); the value is everything after the colon, right-stripped of any trailing run of #tags / emoji. Additive + forward-looking (YAML-front-matter-ish); does NOT touch the first-line-only Path:/Root: path-walking contract.

THE ONE shared emoji/symbol component scanner for node names. Returns the end index of one recognized emoji component/sequence at a position -- trident, ZWJ/variation selectors, supplementary-plane codepoints, So/Sk/Mn/Cs categories, digit/#/* keycap sequences, and the targeted VS16-fallback bases (accepted only with an immediately-following U+FE0F).
