beacons.comment: THE ONE target-resolution implementation for every beacon write path (SPEC v5 §5 step 3): node lookup -> enclosing FILE node ancestor walk (first-line Path:/Root: header) -> portability-model absolute path resolution -> ext/language classification -> lazy nexus_map_codebase import. Used by the legacy writer (which translates failures into its historic NetworkError messages), the plan seam, and the commit seam. Retires the mutation path's hand-rolled ancestor walk.

THE ONE shared preflight/JIT-plan computation (SPEC v5 §5 steps 1-11; PURE -- zero disk writes). Implements the independent ID/anchor reconciliation truth table (carried-identity applicability split, occurrence-aware MD matching, cardinality-aware lookups incl. ambiguous_beacon_id), the comment resolver, the end-state/noop rules, the conservative capability matrix, and the target_key contract (canonical realpath + case-normalized). 2R4E1P: a fill-mode comment conflict is KEPT, never a plan failure -- comment_outcome='kept_existing_conflict' + comment_warning on the plan (labels still ensured; replace/append apply the requested text explicitly); kept_existing_conflict counts as comment-satisfied for the noop rule (labels satisfied + kept conflict -> a noop row that still carries the warning). include_fingerprint=False -> the Phase-C preflight artifact; True -> the Phase-D executable plan with the raw-bytes sha256 CAS.

The synchronous body of commit_beacon_write_plan, run in a worker thread (NBBW): re-resolves the target from the cache, returns plan_mismatch with ZERO write on any path/FILE-node divergence, then calls the language helper with the plan (at most ONE atomic replacement behind the plan's sha256 CAS). No cache patching, no auto-refresh.

Run blocking disk work in a worker thread WITHOUT ever abandoning it: a cancellation is held (asyncio.wait never cancels the task) until the thread has finished, then re-raised. Used by commit_beacon_write_plan so a cancelled beacon batch releases its Q3 lease strictly after the in-flight write (NBBW).
Markdown-only symbol normalization: trim leading decoration and trailing tags without source-code fuzzy splitting
Markdown-only symbol resolution guard: detect Markdown-like file paths
Markdown-only symbol resolution guard: detect Markdown nodes even when scanning from a Root folder

ONE per cache generation (NBBW follow-up): everything the symbol resolver used to rebuild on every call -- the {uuid: node} map, HIDE CARTOGRAPHER filtering, the FILE nodes with their resolved absolute paths, the children index, every FILE root's subtree walk in the original order (visits), per-node pre-extracted fields (beacon id/role, AST_QUALNAME and its short name, code and Markdown normalized names, Path header, basename/stem, Markdown-ness) and one exact-key map (key -> node ids) that is a superset of every exact match. Built from the immutable nodes list of the pinned CacheView; keyed on that list's identity (every refresh, journal adoption and local COW publication makes a new list). Pure, read-only after build.

THE ONE node list the symbol legs read (Archive Reads U1, §4.8): when the current snapshot's archive context carries an overlay, the LIVE view's nodes list -- the symbol legs never see an overlay record and the per-generation symbol index stays keyed on the live list (same identity as a non-augmented operation's, so no index thrash); otherwise today's export_nodes_impl list, byte-identically. read_text_snippet_by_symbol and beacon_get_code_snippet obtain all_nodes ONLY through it. A UUID or AP item of render_symbols/render_nodes that resolves to an archive record renders from the record and is never passed to a disk or snippet tier.

The ONE accessor for the per-generation symbol index: a single slot keyed on the identity of the pinned CacheView's immutable nodes list (strong reference held, so identity is sound); a new generation rebuilds and replaces it under one lock. Called from worker threads only (the build walks the whole cache). No TTL, no knob. Always the live list (archives never reach it) -- every symbol leg obtains all_nodes through _live_nodes_for_symbol_legs, so the slot never holds an augmented list.

beacons.role: _resolve_symbol_candidates_sync(all_nodes, file_path, symbol, symbol_kind, *, return_candidates_only, suppress_tags, scope_root_ids)
beacons.comment: THE symbol-resolution pipeline behind read_text_snippet_by_symbol / read_uuid_from_symbol (beacon.resolve, beacon.snippet by name, the Q3 batch Phase B, render_symbols), synchronous so callers run it in a worker thread. Same steps and results as before the index (file_path narrowing, beacon/ast/name exact scan, dotted-tail, contains and cross-kind fallbacks, #wfy-suppress filter before 0/1/N, descriptors, errors); the per-visit match block runs only over the visits of nodes whose exact keys can match a symbol variant (a superset of every exact hit), and over every visit, exactly as before, only when the requested kinds find no exact hit. scope_root_ids ([ap:WB323O] root_handles) drops candidates outside every root AFTER suppression and BEFORE the 0/1/N decision -- the same descendant-of-any-root gate render_symbols applies; a symbol matched only outside the scope raises a not-found naming the scope (candidates-only mode reports scope_filtered_count instead of raising). Returns the candidates-only dict, or ('resolved', target_id, nodes_by_id, requested_symbol_kind, node_to_file_path) for the snippet path; raises NetworkError on none / many.
Helper: record a candidate match based on contains-substring fallback

Shared per-candidate descriptor builder (uuid/name/file_path/ast_qualname/line/via) used by BOTH the ambiguity report and read_uuid_from_symbol's candidates-only return, so a single match and one ambiguity row are byte-identical.
Render one candidate descriptor as the canonical ambiguity-report line (id=.. line=.. ast=.. name=.. file=.. via=..), preserving the exact pre-refactor string format.

beacons.role: boundary split: api_client_nexus mixed core-v1 cartographer vs lab-only nexus pipeline
core keeper: cartographer path-root portability and note-header resolution

beacons.comment: F12+4 "save generated file" isolated reader: extract an ABSOLUTE Path: from INSIDE a leading MD_PATH: dummy metadata block on a node that lives inside a mapped Markdown file. Deliberately NOT folded into the universal first-line-only parse_path_or_root_from_note / _extract_path_header_from_note (those stay strict line-0 so ordinary nodes are never misclassified as FILE nodes). Used ONLY as a fallback by the F12+1 file-node refresh when no line-0 Path:/Root: header is present.

Parse a FILEBASE: value from a note's leading metadata block for F12+4 filename construction. Metadata block = lines from the top until the first blank line OR a '---' line (an optional leading '---' front-matter opener is skipped). FILEBASE: may appear on ANY line in that block (first occurrence wins); the value is everything after the colon, right-stripped of any trailing run of #tags / emoji. Additive + forward-looking (YAML-front-matter-ish); does NOT touch the first-line-only Path:/Root: path-walking contract.

THE ONE shared emoji/symbol component scanner for node names. Returns the end index of one recognized emoji component/sequence at a position -- trident, ZWJ/variation selectors, supplementary-plane codepoints, So/Sk/Mn/Cs categories, digit/#/* keycap sequences, and the targeted VS16-fallback bases (accepted only with an immediately-following U+FE0F). Consumed by both left-edge name scanners (_split_leading_name_emoji_run, _lstrip_leading_ws_and_emoji) and the right-edge FILEBASE token predicate, so the definition of 'emoji decoration' can never drift between edges.

Right-strip a trailing run of #tags, the trident decoration, and standalone emoji tokens from a FILEBASE value so they never leak into the constructed .md filename. Whitespace-token based: pops trailing whitespace-split tokens that are #tags / trident / pure-emoji until a real content token remains. Emoji classification is delegated to the ONE shared _emoji_component_end scanner (VS16-fallback bases and keycap sequences included), so the right edge can never drift from the left-edge name scanners.

Walk the ANCESTOR chain (the node itself first, then up via parent_id) and return the nearest FILEBASE: value found in any ancestor's note metadata block. Used by F12+4 to prefix the new .md filename with a contextual base (e.g. a Curation-Capsule-root FILEBASE) independent of any capsule terminology/template. Returns None when no ancestor carries a FILEBASE.

Stateless predicate: does a Cartographer Path: value name a FILE (has a filename extension) rather than a bare FOLDER segment? A folder node's Path: is a bare segment (e.g. 'client', 'src/workflowy_mcp') with no extension; a file node's value ends in an extension (.md/.py/.js...). Root: values are always directories (caller passes kind). MOVED here from server.py (June 2026) to be the single source of truth co-located with _extract_path_header_from_note and the new _classify_node_map_state; server.py keeps a thin local-import wrapper. Self-contained (os only) so the move inverts no dependency.

Read-only classifier of a node's relationship to the Cartographer file/folder map, used as the mutation guard for the note-session tools (first consumer). Walks parent_id UP the /nodes-export cache (node itself first; cycle-guarded; ~512-hop cap), stopping at the FIRST node carrying a first-line Path:/Root: header (nearest-header-wins; header-less ancestors skipped). Classifies into UNMAPPED (no header anywhere) | FILE (header on the node ITSELF, Path: with a file extension) | INSIDE_FILE (header on an ANCESTOR, Path: with a file extension) | FOLDER (Root: anywhere, or a bare extension-less Path: anywhere). Composes ONLY on the two vetted, now-co-located helpers _extract_path_header_from_note + _path_value_looks_like_any_file. Mutates nothing, no disk, no API. Re-run live on every mutation so moving nodes in Workflowy can't leave a stale verdict.

Shared anchor/capture placement guard used by create_note_session AND add_to_anchor. Given a _classify_node_map_state verdict it returns an actionable error string when the target is a BAD home for an anchor/capture else None. Rejects FOLDER nodes and NON-Markdown mapped files (and inside such files) because those cannot be persisted to disk via F12+3 (Markdown-only) so the node would be wiped on the next F12+1. A Markdown / inside-Markdown / unmapped target returns None (allowed); the caller still surfaces the mapped_subtree F12+3 advisory for the Markdown-file case.

SHARED UUID-prefix fallback resolver (tool-neutral). The single implementation of UUID-hallucination tolerance for the whole MCP surface: anchor tools (add_to_anchor / update_note_session), the snippet resolver (beacon_get_code_snippet), and SCRY (workflowy_scry) all call this on an exact /nodes-export cache MISS. Hyphen-normalize, then character-backtrack the supplied UUID from full length down to 8 chars (the full first segment), and at the FIRST prefix length that yields >=1 match, stop. Returns {resolved_uuid, matched_prefix_len} on a UNIQUE match (the caller adopts the UUID; 23db916f adds matched_prefix_len so the Layer-1 wrapper can tell a SHAVED handle from a clean prefix and record the one-line correction echo via handle_corrections), or {candidates:[{uuid,name}...]} capped at 25 on a MULTI match (caller raises a disambiguation 'did you mean?' error -- NEVER auto-picks), or {} on no match. Exists because agents hallucinate UUIDs (correct first segment, fabricated tail) far more than expected, and a bare cache-miss reads like a staleness problem without this guard. (Formerly _resolve_anchor_uuid_with_prefix_fallback -- renamed July 2026 when it was generalized beyond the anchor tools.)

SHARED /nodes-export cache-map builder. The ONE place that turns the in-memory /nodes-export snapshot into a {uuid: node} dict, replacing the three hand-rolled idioms scattered across callers (export_nodes_impl(use_cache,no-refresh) / self.export_nodes(use_cache=True) / _get_nodes_export_cache_nodes() each followed by its own dict-comprehension). Built on the strict synchronous cache-only accessor client._get_nodes_export_cache_nodes() -- NO API call, NO refresh, cache-only (matches Dan's explicit-refresh-only discipline). For the whole-vault load these three idioms are equivalent (the cache is already dewhitened when populated and export_nodes_impl returns _nodes_export_cache verbatim on a use_cache hit; the only surface difference was RuntimeError vs NetworkError on a missing cache). Raises on a missing/malformed cache -- callers keep their own try/except framing (tag path swallows to {}, root_uuid returns a structured error, anchors let it raise). Pure/read-only.

BRACKETED-UUID HANDLE UNWRAPPER (Dan, 2026) -- the ONE pure edge normalizer for an AP-ID-style square-bracket wrapper around a UUID or its first-segment prefix ('[a2e552e3]' / '[a2e552e3-eb42-...]'), the form an agent produces when it conflates the two bracketed handle grammars. Unwraps ONLY when the whole (whitespace-stripped) candidate is [...] -wrapped AND the interior is pure hex (+ optional hyphens) with >= 8 normalized chars -- the full first segment, matching the prefix kernel's min_prefix_len floor -- so short bracketed hex cores (<8) and bracketed NON-hex AP cores ('[K7M2QF]') stay AP-ID-domain exclusive, and '[ap:CORE]' (colon => non-hex) is never touched. Returns any non-matching or non-string candidate VERBATIM (no str-coercion, no strip side effect): a pure pass-through for every other input shape. Consumed by exactly TWO originators -- the Layer-1 wrapper (resolve_uuid_like_node_handle, so EVERY funnel inherits: anchor dock verbs via _resolve_generic_node_handle / resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle, Layer-3 resolve_node_handle, glimpse roots, scry, grace-resolve) and the render_symbols per-item ROUTER (_resolve_lightning_rod_symbol_items_from_cache, whose _uuid_shaped classification runs BEFORE Layer-1) -- so the bracket leniency is ONE grammar with no per-site drift.

The ARCHIVE PARTITION of a cache map (Archive Reads U1, §4.4.1), computed ONCE per call: the ids whose records carry the _nexus_archive marker — the marker, never the operation context, is the authority, so the partition is correct in any thread and everywhere the map travels. Consumed by the Layer-1 primitive and the AP primitive to split their candidate universes live-first; empty when the map is live-only, which keeps every kernel call byte-identical to pre-archive behaviour. (U2: the beacon block this helper inherited at the U1 insertion point carried a duplicate id — the map refresh flagged it; this is now the helper's own block with a unique id.)

LAYER-1 UUID PRIMITIVE -- the single confluence point for ALL UUID-like node-handle resolution. Folds the EXACT-hit check and the shared prefix kernel (_resolve_uuid_with_prefix_fallback) into ONE pure function used by beacon_get_code_snippet / workflowy_scry / add_to_anchor / update_note_session / root_uuid GLIMPSE / the tag path. HYBRID CACHE LOAD (Commit 1.5, per Opus+GPT-5.5+Dan): nodes_by_id is OPTIONAL. If a caller already holds the cache map (because it needs it AFTER resolution -- ancestor walk, node classification, subtree projection), it PASSES the map and there is NO double read. If a caller only needs resolution (the tag path), it passes client= and nodes_by_id=None, and the primitive self-loads via the shared load_nodes_by_id_from_cache helper. EITHER WAY the primitive RETURNS the nodes_by_id it used, so a self-loading caller can reuse the exact same map downstream. Exactly one of {nodes_by_id, client} must be provided. Still does NOT render error strings (callers keep their own miss-policy: beacon SURFACES ambiguity as a loud did-you-mean carrying the candidates [ap:G5C9BX]; anchors SURFACE _anchor_uuid_cache_miss_error; scry SURFACES on ambiguous, FALLS THROUGH on no-match). Tri-state return + nodes_by_id: {success:True, resolved_uuid, input_kind:'exact_uuid'|'uuid_prefix', nodes_by_id} on hit; {success:False, candidates, matched_prefix_len, truncated, input_kind:None, nodes_by_id} on ambiguous; {success:False, input_kind:None, nodes_by_id} on unresolved. key_prefix passes to the kernel (slice-group 'grp-' parity); the slice-group resolver stays OUT of this wrapper by design (matches the config map, not the nodes cache). BRACKETED-UUID LENIENCY (Dan, 2026): the candidate passes through unwrap_bracketed_uuid_handle FIRST -- an AP-ID-style bracket wrapper around a pure-hex >=8-char body ('[a2e552e3]' / '[full-uuid]') is stripped ONCE here so EVERY funnel surface inherits the leniency with no per-site branching; '[ap:CORE]' and bracketed non-hex cores are never unwrapped and stay AP-leg territory. HANDLE-CORRECTION ECHO (23db916f): on a kernel UNIQUE hit the wrapper compares the kernel's matched_prefix_len against the normalized (key-prefix-stripped, hyphen-stripped, bracket-unwrapped) supplied length and records ONE correction via handle_corrections.record_handle_correction IFF the handle was SHAVED (matched_prefix_len < supplied length) -- an exact hit, an AP-ID and a clean prefix that matched at its own full length stay silent; _mcp_operation_result_finalizer drains the record into the one 'resolved: <short> <name> (corrected from <supplied>)' echo line / resolved_corrections key. The return SHAPE is unchanged (still pure tri-state + nodes_by_id); the echo state is side-band. ARCHIVE READS TWO-PHASE (universe param, U1; rev 2 ruling [ap:WNV4ZW]): live first -- the EXACT hit runs over the LIVE partition only and the kernel over the LIVE partition -- and the archive phase (the kernel over the ARCHIVE partition, or the fallback gate when the map carries no partition) runs only after a TOTAL live miss; universe='live'/'archive' restrict to one phase, and an archive record's key is never a live exact hit. The EXACT archived full UUID beats a SHAVED live match in EVERY mode (E2/Axiom 2; the side-effect-free is_exact_archived_id is asked at the shave, the beacon family excepted — Axiom 12), so a read serves the archive and a write stays unresolved for its site's archive-aware refusal; the re-run request stays the gate's job, in the archive phase only. Callers tell an archive answer by is_archive_record(nodes_by_id[resolved]) -- the return shape is unchanged.

Left-strip a leading run of whitespace and pure-emoji/symbol CHARACTERS from a node name, so a leading decoration (a lightning bolt, a bullet emoji, etc.) never blocks a leading-anchored match. Character-level (NOT whitespace-token based) on purpose: an AP-ID handle like '[ap:K7M2QF]' can sit flush against a leading emoji with no space (e.g. '\U0001f3f7\ufe0f[ap:...]'), so a token-splitter would miss it. Every component decision is delegated to the ONE shared _emoji_component_end scanner (the v1 'predicate lives in three places' ARCH NOTE is RETIRED: here, _split_leading_name_emoji_run, and the _strip_trailing_tags_and_emoji token predicate all consume that single authority).

Normalize a caller-supplied AP-ID argument into its bare uppercase base36 core, accepting lenient forms ('[ap:APRSLV3]', 'ap:APRSLV3', bare 'APRSLV3', with/without brackets, any case). Core length is VARIABLE (>=3 base36 chars): the live vault carries mnemonic cores like APRSLV3/APCHILD/APFAMILY2 alongside the doc's canonical 6-char hash, so a fixed {6} would fail to resolve them. Returns None for anything that is not a valid base36 core after stripping the optional [ap:]/[ ]/ap: wrappers -- this is INPUT normalization only (no fuzzy matching), keeping the resolver a strict 100% WHOLE-core exact match.

THE ONE pure leading-name-emoji update policy behind node.update_emoji. Validates via the ONE shared _normalize_supplied_emoji_run (blank = remove here, loudly rejected by the prepend/append sibling policy; multiple glyphs/ZWJ/keycaps/VS16-fallback bases allowed; ordinary text rejected with invalid_emoji_value), then replaces ONLY the leading emoji run of the ordinary name section. AP-ID splitting happens outside this helper, so legacy decoration before an AP token is untouched; middle/right emojis remain in the remainder; output uses one separating space. Pure; no I/O.

THE ONE pure leading-name-emoji insertion policy behind node.prepend_emoji and node.append_emoji. Validates via the shared _normalize_supplied_emoji_run (blank LOUDLY rejected -- removal belongs to node.update_emoji), then inserts the supplied run BEFORE (prepend) or AFTER (append) the existing leading emoji run of the ordinary name section, always left of the title; existing leading emojis are preserved, middle/right emojis are ordinary remainder content never touched, and with no existing run the two positions coincide. Output joins regions with one canonical space. Returns (new_title, resulting full run, added run). Pure; no I/O.

THE ONE protected-name policy for every free-form rename surface (node.edit / anchor.dock.update / legacy update_anchor) and every dedicated protected-region mutation. Composes final NAME = protected leading prefix + ordinary title + trailing #tags, parsing BOTH names only via the canonical emoji/trident-aware _resolve_split_name_and_tags and the ONE leading-AP grammar (_split_leading_ap_handle). Rules: supplied trailing #tags -> ProtectedNameViolation(tags_in_name_rejected), even when identical to current; a supplied leading [ap:] absent-from or different-than current -> ProtectedNameViolation(ap_id_mutation_rejected); an IDENTICAL existing AP-ID may be repeated and is emitted exactly once in stored spelling; omitted AP-ID/tags auto-preserve. LEADING EMOJI RUN (Z8Q0PF+LITF2F): a free-form rename also preserves the ordinary title's existing leading emoji run -- you need not pass an emoji -- unless the supplied title begins with its own run (explicit wins); replace_leading_emoji=True hands the run to the supplied title wholesale (its run replaces the existing one, its absence clears it; the byte-verbatim fast path does not bypass the preservation). Validation order is deterministic: tags first, then AP-ID. Narrow internal channels only (never a generic bypass): tag_transform rewrites Dock locality; assign_ap_core adds a reserved AP core; remove_ap_id removes only the leading AP token; leading_emoji_mutation carries the typed replace/prepend/append request of the node emoji verbs (update_emoji / prepend_emoji / append_emoji) against only the leading emoji run of the ordinary name section after any AP. A mid-title [ap:X] or middle/right emoji is ordinary title content. Pure; no I/O.

THE SHARED AP-ID PRIMITIVE ([ap:APRSLV3]) -- resolve a Mechanical-Convention-1 anchor-point handle ([ap:CORE], variable-length base36 core) to its Workflowy UUID(s), for PURE-Workflowy (non-disk-backed) nodes that read_uuid_from_symbol (correctly) cannot resolve. Deliberately DEAD SIMPLE per Dan's v1 spec: a single EXACT WHOLE-core match (uppercased; VARIABLE length -- the live vault mixes 6-char hashes with mnemonic cores like APRSLV3/APCHILD/APFAMILY2, so no fixed {6}), found ONLY at the LEADING edge of a node NAME after whitespace+emoji left-strip (leading-only avoids matching notes that merely REFERENCE an AP-ID). NO prefix/fuzzy fallback, NO ancestor/suppression walk (unlike the UUID Layer-1 resolver). Lenient INPUT (brackets/ap: prefix optional, any case) via _normalize_ap_id_input. Returns the read_uuid_from_symbol candidate shape {success, match_count, candidates:[{uuid,name}]} -- 0/1/N, N>1 only on a duplicated handle (never auto-picked, returned as ambiguities with UUID+name, the richest reporting meaningful here since there are no file paths). HYBRID cache load like resolve_uuid_like_node_handle: pass nodes_by_id (caller-owned) OR client (self-load via load_nodes_by_id_from_cache); exactly one. This ONE function backs both the MCP tool and the forthcoming anchor-point family generalization ([ap:APFAMILY2]) + add_to_anchor-by-AP-ID ([ap:APCHILD]). ARCHIVE READS TWO-PHASE (universe param, U1): the scan partitions its matches off the record marker -- universe='auto' returns live matches if any, else archive matches; 'live'/'archive' restrict to one partition; a unique archive match is recorded side-band (record_archive_served); when the map carries no archive partition the fallback gate is consulted (inert outside fallback mode). The 0/1/N shape is unchanged.

NARROW PURE-WORKFLOWY handle resolver: UUID-or-AP-ID ONLY (NO source-code symbol domain), for the Layer-1-direct callers that scope/target a GENERIC Workflowy node -- GLIMPSE root_uuid (raw-dump + slice-override), SCRY, add_to_anchor/ETCH parent, update_anchor -- where a code symbol is semantically meaningless. It is the shared home for 'try UUID, else AP-ID' so that conversion is NOT copy-pasted inline at each call site (GPT-5.5's design: a named narrow sibling to the Layer-3 resolve_node_handle, which is the WIDER UUID|AP-ID|symbol boundary). Preserves resolve_uuid_like_node_handle's EXACT tri-state shape byte-for-byte (success/resolved_uuid/input_kind/candidates/matched_prefix_len/truncated/nodes_by_id) so existing callers that branch on it need ZERO changes; it ONLY adds an AP-ID fallback on the UUID leg's UNRESOLVED branch (UUID exact/prefix wins first; an ambiguous UUID prefix STILL STOPS with its candidates and never falls through -- same stop-on-success-or-ambiguity invariant as Layer 3). Adds one extra key resolved_via ('uuid'|'anchor_point') for callers that care; ignore it and the shape is identical to Layer 1. HYBRID cache load like its siblings (pass nodes_by_id OR client; exactly one; the map used is echoed back). NO symbol leg by design -- callers wanting symbols use resolve_node_handle instead. ARCHIVE READS TWO-PHASE (U1): runs live UUID -> live AP -> archive UUID -> archive AP (legs at universe='live' then universe='archive'), each stage keeping today's stop-on-success-or-ambiguity rule; the archive legs only ever answer on a total live miss (Axiom 1), and a caller tells an archive answer by is_archive_record(nodes_by_id[resolved]) -- the return shape is unchanged. U2: an optional universe='live' skips the archive phase entirely -- the BEACON family's marker (Axiom 12: beacon serves nothing from archives; _resolve_beacon_graph_handle pins it).

THE identifier-vocabulary builder behind the three resolve verbs ([ap:CZ95R6]): given an already-resolved UUID and the map it resolved against, return the node's full identifier vocabulary {short, uuid, ap_id} -- short via the ONE shared unique_short_uuid_prefix display authority (CF-22/O3: 8 hex, lengthened just enough when the 8-hex prefix is ambiguous across the passed map, so a returned short handle can be pasted back as a handle AND resolves uniquely -- the same "short" rendered headings print via RenderPolicy.uuid_prefix_collisions, so the two can never drift), uuid verbatim, and ap_id as the canonical '[ap:CORE]' token read from the node NAME's leading edge via the shared _split_leading_ap_handle grammar (the same detector anchor.point.assign_id uses), or the literal string 'no anchor point available' when the node carries none. Pure; no I/O; absent nodes yield the short/uuid of the id with the no-anchor literal (callers only pass resolved ids); a None map degrades to the plain 8-hex form (no id universe to be unique within).

The shared identity RECORD BUILDER behind node.resolve / anchor.point.resolve / beacon.resolve ([ap:CZ95R6]). Family routing is explicit order DATA consumed by WorkFlowyClientNexus.resolve_node_handle -- THE single arbitration loop, which owns unique/ambiguous stops, unresolved fall-through and self-load degradation. This function never calls the UUID/AP primitives or arbitrates domains itself. Enriches the arbiter's outcome with node_identity vocabulary and candidate rows, retaining the established non-raising 0/1/N MCP record, AP core, prefix and symbol/scope diagnostics. Beacon injects its lazy scoped/suppressed symbol runner and UUID-shape gate; enrichment reuses the arbiter's map or best-effort loads it after a symbol-first hit. No second resolver. Archive Reads U2 (§5.4): a 0-match record for an AP-SHAPED candidate gains a top-level hint -- the beacon line for beacon.resolve (never the store, Axiom 12), states A/B/C for node.resolve and anchor.point.resolve; UUID-shaped misses stay byte-identical.

Build the actionable cache-miss error message for an anchor UUID that did not resolve exactly. Leads with the hallucination/mistype hypothesis (the dominant real cause -- agents fabricate the UUID tail from the first segment) rather than the old 'refresh the cache' staleness framing. When prefix-fallback candidates exist (the supplied UUID's prefix matched MULTIPLE nodes) it appends a 'did you mean?' list of full real UUIDs + node names so the agent self-corrects in one step instead of refreshing-and-retrying the same bad UUID. When there are no candidates it falls back to suggesting a cache refresh (genuine staleness / wrong vault).

note_file ingestion for add_to_anchor: read a UTF-8 text file through the ONE host-aware path resolver (tool_path_resolution: translated where a mapping exists, refused loudly where none does) and normalize it into the standard single-node ETCH payload [{name: file STEM (extension deliberately dropped so the node is never mistaken for a Cartographer-mapped file), note: raw text}] -- the guarded capture funnel downstream (resolver -> guard -> parse-peek -> etch -> tags) then runs byte-for-byte unchanged. LOUD failures (NetworkError): empty/relative path, missing file, directory, non-UTF-8 (never errors='replace' -- the note is ingested verbatim). Newlines normalized CRLF/CR -> LF via universal-newlines read (the system's pure-LF note convention). A Workflowy trailing-#tag region in the STEM is REJECTED via the canonical split_name_and_tags (note_file tags MUST go through tags=, never the filename -- enforced, not advisory). AP-ID FILENAME CONVENTION (Dan, 2026): a leading '[ap_CORE]' handle in the stem -- the colon of '[ap:CORE]' is illegal in Windows filenames -- is canonicalized to '[ap:CORE]' (lowercase ap + uppercased core, matching _AP_ID_LEADING_RE so the handle resolves); echoed via meta['ap_id_transformed']. OPTIONAL name_override (Dan, 2026): when supplied, the override (stripped, non-empty) is used as the node name VERBATIM, and the stem-derived behaviors that exist ONLY to produce a name (tag-region rejection + AP-ID transform) are SKIPPED -- the name comes from the caller, not the filename. meta gains name_override=True (False when absent).

content-string ingestion for add_to_anchor: normalize (name, content) into the standard single-node ETCH payload [{name: name, note: content}] -- the guarded capture funnel downstream (resolver -> guard -> parse-peek -> etch -> tags) then runs byte-for-byte unchanged. Sibling of _node_payload_from_note_file but with no file I/O -- name comes directly from the caller (stripped, non-empty; a trailing #tag region is ALLOWED since name is a directly-authored string, unlike a filename). Newlines normalized CRLF/CR -> LF (the system's pure-LF note convention). content="" is legal (a subject-only capture with an empty note); presence is `is not None`.

beacons.role: ƒ _merge_file_note_header(old_note: str, fresh_line_count: int, pending_path_segment: str | None = None)
beacons.comment: THE ONE preservation-safe FILE-header merge (FILE-NOTE HEADER FRESHNESS, Dan 2026): merges a fresh LINE COUNT into an existing FILE note's OWNED header region — the strict line-0 Path: line plus the immediately following contiguous LINE COUNT:/Source-SHA1: metadata lines — and preserves every other byte of the note (suffix, spacing, terminal newline) verbatim. Drops legacy Source-SHA1: lines (no operational reader; deliberately hash-free), applies an optional deferred portability Path-segment migration inside the same preserved note, refuses non-Path-first notes (Root:/MD_PATH dummy/ordinary) by returning None rather than inserting a header. Pure; no I/O; callers raise loudly on None.

THE ONE repository-relative path composition (U1, MasterSpec §5.4): the body of weave_worker._resolve_carto_file_relpath_for_progress moved here (beside resolve_cartographer_path_from_node), so the repository view and the CARTO progress worker share ONE composition -- the resolver over a passed nodes_by_id + _portable_relpath, with the basename fallback for legacy absolute-Path file nodes with no Root: ancestor. Returns (relative_path_or_basename_or_None, root_abs); the weave worker keeps its memo and delegates. Pure read over the cache dict; the only _portable_relpath call site in src/.

F12+4 materialize-note-as-Markdown: resolve the on-disk DIRECTORY (and the note Path: value form) for a brand-new FILE node from its ANCESTORS, since the node itself has no Path:/Root: header yet. Reuses resolve_cartographer_path_from_node ancestor mechanics on the nearest header-bearing ancestor; falls back to the extension's default_markdown_folder when no Root:/Path: ancestor exists. SPECIAL CASE: when the nearest header-bearing ancestor is itself a mapped MARKDOWN FILE node (Path: resolves to .md), returns is_temporary=True + source=temp_default_folder so the caller writes a THROWAWAY .md to the default folder (errors if none configured), splits the node via an override-path F12+1, then deletes the temp file — avoiding unsupported mapped-Markdown-inside-mapped-Markdown nesting.
CARTOGRAPHER_COSMETIC_SUFFIX_FIRST_CODEPOINTS (cosmetic path/name normalization only)

ƒ _is_cartographer_parse_error_sentinel(name): narrow pure diagnostic predicate (S06) — producer-exact match against the Cartographer-generated parse-error sentinel name grammar (the five _warn_name forms in nexus_map_codebase, with optional '[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS]' timestamp suffix), replacing the retired broad Notes emoji whitelist in the folder-refresh parse-error promotion. Never classifies arbitrary user nodes, including same-emoji (⚠️) user headings.

Self-contained reader of the BEACON (AST|SPAN) block 'id:' line from a Workflowy node note. Duplicate of nexus_map_codebase._extract_beacon_id_from_note kept local so the duplicate-beacon-id detector needs no cross-module import; semantics must stay identical (first 'id:' line inside a BEACON (.../@beacon[ note).

File-scoped detector for the intra-file duplicate-beacon-id hazard that causes non-idempotent F12+1 (endless CREATE+DELETE+reorder churn). Given the EXISTING Workflowy FILE subtree's flat node list, groups nodes by their note's BEACON id: and returns {beacon_id: [{id,name,parent_id}...]} for every id claimed by 2+ nodes. Beacon ids are only required unique WITHIN one file, so this is exactly the poison condition reconcile_trees_cartographer's id-keyed match cannot resolve. Read-only; consumed by refresh_file_node_beacons to emit a non-fatal WARNING that surfaces as completed_with_warnings in the widget.

Current-disk duplicate-beacon-id detector for F12+1 warnings. Traverses the freshly parsed Cartographer source tree (not the pre-refresh Workflowy export) and groups generated BEACON ids so warnings describe this run's on-disk file state with no one-refresh lag.

Pure short-handle display primitive for the compact inventory views: strip an optional literal key prefix ('grp-' for slice-group ids), hyphen-normalize, and return the first 8 characters -- exactly the prefix form the shared resolvers (_resolve_uuid_with_prefix_fallback / _resolve_slice_group_id) already accept, so a displayed short handle can be pasted back as a handle. Deliberately never labeled 'unique': a colliding prefix resolves to a loud candidate list, never a wrong pick. For UUID DISPLAY where uniqueness matters (rendered headings, the resolve verbs' short field -- CF-22/O3) route through unique_short_uuid_prefix instead; this primitive stays the inventory/base-8 form (and the base the unique helper lengthens from).

ONE pure collision index for SHORT UUID DISPLAY ([ap:0M6VP8] + CF-22/O3): map each 8-hex prefix carried by MORE THAN ONE id to the list of original (dashed) ids sharing it; unambiguous prefixes are ABSENT (the overwhelmingly common case, so the index stays tiny). Consumed by unique_short_uuid_prefix (the ONE lengthening authority shared by rendered headings and the resolve verbs' short field); built once per render next to build_direct_child_counts from the same pinned cache map. Hyphen-normalized comparison, matching the shared prefix kernel. Pure; no I/O.

THE one SHORT-UUID display authority (CF-22/O3: "short" has ONE meaning): shortest resolver-compatible prefix (>= 8 hyphen-stripped chars, lengthened just enough) that is unique among the ids in the caller's build_uuid_prefix_collisions index -- the same prefix form the shared kernel _resolve_uuid_with_prefix_fallback accepts at its own full length, so a displayed handle pastes straight back and resolves SILENTLY (no did-you-mean). With no/absent collision index (or an unambiguous 8-hex prefix) this is exactly _short_handle_prefix's 8-hex form. Route BOTH render headings (via RenderPolicy.uuid_prefix_collisions) and the resolve verbs' node_identity.short through THIS -- a second shortener is the known failure mode. Pure; no I/O.

THE shared middle-ellipsis truncation for the compact inventory views: when len(text) > max_chars, emit exactly max_chars characters as head...tail with a 60/40 head bias (floor(budget*0.60) head, remainder tail); max_chars 0/None disables truncation and 1 yields a bare ellipsis. Both cut boundaries are adjusted through the ONE _emoji_component_end authority so a recognized emoji/ZWJ/variation-selector component is never bisected (a straddling component is dropped from the head entirely; the tail never begins mid-component). Pure; no I/O.

beacons.role: _render_anchor_tree_raw_text(anchor_tree, global_count, local_count, show_local, compact, max_chars, max_description_chars, show_description, favorites_only, favorites_fallback, favorite_count, total_dock_count, favorite_tag_hint)
beacons.comment: Pure anchor-inventory raw-text serializer: renders the anchor-only tree as a UUID-left / indented-name-right text outline. Domain serializer like Lightning Rod gather, deliberately NOT a Markdown/node-tree render or Stage-1/Stage-2 path. TWO modes: legacy (the defaults -- byte-for-byte the established widget clipboard format: full 36-char UUID column, blank line per row, '  [local]' suffix) and compact=True (the consolidated anchor.dock.list default: an 8-char resolver-compatible [prefix] column that NEVER indents -- only the Dock name receives two spaces per Dock-ancestry level -- plus ' ⭐' favorite (BEFORE ' Ⓛ') and ' Ⓛ' local markers, no blank spacer rows, and a one-line teaching header ending detail='full' for JSON). The favorites kwargs (favorites_only EFFECTIVE value, favorites_fallback, favorite_count, total_dock_count, favorite_tag_hint) drive the compact header grammar ONLY -- fallback header says 'no favorites configured: showing all' + the composed #base--word hint; an effective favorites header reports shown/favorites/hidden counts with the 'favorites_only=false to show' teaching. [ap:YLHDIN] part 2: compact rows carry the Dock's FIRST description line as a ' -- excerpt' tail after the markers (_compact_description_excerpt: the first non-empty line of the row's metadata-stripped description, middle-ellipsised; show_description=true default, max_description_chars default 120, 0 hides; a row without a description gets no tail at all). Legacy mode IGNORES the favorites AND description kwargs (byte-identical).

THE ONE note parse: a mapped note as an ordered stream of body lines, generated beacon records and MD_PATH blocks (identity-shaped constructs after the body boundary tagged as source-authored body items); the one parse the legacy stripper, the repository-view projection and the agent-kit engine all read; an agent-kit build root

span(t) for the repository view: t between backtick runs one longer than the longest backtick run inside t, with one space of padding when t starts or ends with a backtick; the one span composer for file headings and every entry title; an agent-kit build root
The §4.1 entry test: True when the note's first line starts with an entry marker (AST_QUALNAME: / BEACON ( / MD_PATH:); an agent-kit build root

Labels and comment for one repository-view entry, taken from the first GENERATED beacon record of the ONE note parse only (a source-authored beacon example in the body never replaces them); the one labels authority shared by the projection and the agent-kit engine's counts; an agent-kit build root

THE per-entry display of the repository view (§4.3/§4.4/§4.5): the kind + span(title) heading and the Labels/comment body with the full mode's fenced parts, read from the ONE note parse; hoisted out of _repository_view_forest (R2) so the agent-kit engine shares it byte for byte through strip_text
The kind word of a rendered repository-view heading (its first token); decides the enclosure kind its children inherit; an agent-kit build root

beacons.role: core keeper: glimpse-scry plus cartographer snippet resolution surface

beacons.comment: Formatter over the ONE note parse (parse_cartographer_note_for_preview, U1 §5.3): strips MD_PATH/AST_QUALNAME/BEACON blocks and re-emits the block's comment as a 'comment: X' line, byte-identical to the pre-split loop (pinned by tests/test_repository_view_stripper_characterization.py); the repository view reads labels/comment/body parts from the same parse. Chain 1 r1 (W3): source-authored identity-shaped body items (ast_qualname_body/md_path_body/beacon_body) keep today's baseline output too -- dropped, or their comment re-emitted -- so the off-mode render of a docstring example is unchanged; only the repository projection retains them. Chain 1 r2 (WO [ap:4Q3LQV] W2): the parse's body boundary moved earlier (the generated prefix's '---' terminator), which flips no consumed line -- this formatter's output is byte-identical for every input, both settings.

Hazard-fence literal heading-like body lines (^ {0,3}#{1,64} + ws/eol) in the structural branch of the markdown-preview walk so a note's '#'/'##' line (e.g. a source-file '#'-comment) cannot masquerade as a real heading and corrupt the fused hierarchy. Fence-aware (respects existing fences), start-of-line #tags left alone, dynamic backtick fence length. This is the §5 source-comment-fencing keeper.

MARKDOWN heading-level reset sentinel detector for the unified markdown-preview walk; leading token == 'MARKDOWN' (all caps, ':'/'-'/ws delimited) after left/right decoration strip. Sole renderer (the JS twin was deleted July 2026)

Build a flat {uuid: abs_path} map for Cartographer FILE/FOLDER/ROOT nodes in a GLIMPSE preview tree, used by FULL (UUID/JSON) mode to surface on-disk paths inline. Resolves via resolve_cartographer_path_from_node over shadow copies (synthesized parent_id); never mutates the source tree

Phase 0.5 Step 4 (ap:EXECLDG) rebase-baseline PRODUCER: precompute the per-file / per-heading H1 rebase baseline for a forest ONCE, keyed by the RENDER-FOREST _index_path (same coordinate system _build_markdown_preview_from_tree / _iter_markdown_focus_rows use -- (top_index,) seed, index_path+(ci,) per child, ALL children incl. sentinels enumerated). Records _min_md_depth_in_subtree(node) at every node the composer's two rebase call-sites query -- a Cartographer file/folder/root node (parse_path_or_root_from_note) OR an md-heading node (_md_depth_from_note_for_preview>0) -- but ONLY when that shallowest depth is a REAL int, so a source/no-md-heading subtree stores NO entry and the composer's inline-None fallback matches byte-for-byte (no None-value vs absent-key ambiguity). Computed from the UNPRUNED document_forest so a later focus prune cannot shift the shallowest-visible depth (hazard-b immune by construction, v3.3 #2 covers BOTH root kinds). Returns a frozen RenderPolicy carrying ONLY the rebase map (body-suppression sets stay empty until Steps 6/7). Pure/read-only; the input forest is never mutated.

Phase 0.5 Step 5 hygiene helper: deep-ish clone a render/document forest into fresh node dicts + fresh child lists, preserving id/name/note/metadata byte-for-byte and never mutating/aliasing the caller's input. Used by materialize_from_document_forest so MaterializedRenderDocument owns its internal forests instead of merely holding a shallow list copy of the caller's mutable node dicts -- keeping the 'server-internal immutable result / input never mutated' invariant honest. Iterative (explicit stack) to avoid recursion limits on very deep Workflowy trees. Non-dict children are ignored, matching the renderer/enumerator's dict-child semantics.

Phase 0.5 Step 5 (ap:EXECLDG) the SHARED MATERIALIZER CORE: build a MaterializedRenderDocument from a concrete document_forest + a (canonical or None) focus. repository_view=True (U1) sets the composer's G1-G3 policy flag on the policy this method builds (the other two RenderPolicy constructions are untouched). repository_view=True (U1) sets the composer's G1-G3 policy flag on the policy this method builds (the other two RenderPolicy constructions are untouched). This is the ONE place row construction, focus resolution (exact-or-error), render_forest construction, and render-forest-keyed policy live -- the producers (render_stage2_filter_sort, _render_slice_row_view, compose_markdown_modal_view, the DOM-capture dispatch, and -- Unit C, ap:W53A69 -- the bare live-DOM GLIMPSE compose in workflowy_glimpse, BOTH its in-memory and output_file-fallback sites) differ ONLY in how they obtain document_forest and converge here. OWNS: (1) document_rows via _iter_markdown_focus_rows over the UNPRUNED document_forest (focus never shrinks the top-half list); (2) focus resolution via _resolve_focus_index_path + _node_uuid_at_index_path round-trip -- a canonical focus that fails to resolve raises FocusResolutionError (exact-or-error §5-Correction#3/§9; NO whole-document / first-occurrence / uuid-set degrade), a root-row focus (top-level node, empty ancestor_path) is treated as the whole rooted document, and None renders the whole document; (3) render_forest via a NOTE-PRESERVING option-Y builder (_focused_render_forest_with_origin) that keeps every retained note INTACT (v3.1 hazard-a) and records each render node's ORIGIN document index_path so policy can be re-keyed exactly; (4) policy_by_occurrence: rebase VALUES computed from the UNPRUNED document_forest (hazard-b immune) then RE-KEYED to render-forest coords via the origin map (v3.3 #2) -- NOT recomputed over the pruned tree (which would lose an off-path sibling's shallower depth) -- PLUS the cause-labeled body-suppression sets: breadcrumb (focus spine, occurrence-keyed), deprecated (uuid-keyed), and, when the producer passes chronological=True, the U6 CHRONOLOGICAL-ANCESTOR cause (ap:E03BN3, Dan's ruling 'any chronological sort of any form never displays ancestor notes'): the occurrence/index-path-keyed STRICT PREFIXES of collect_leaf_branches(render_forest) -- every non-leaf of the FINAL forest (root included when non-leaf) renders heading-only, leaf notes print, computed ONLY here (never uuid-keyed, never producer-side; the ancestor_notes teaching opt-out is folded into the boolean by the producer) -- and, when the producer passes lens_scaffold_ids ([ap:I506WY], unit 5g), the LENS-SCAFFOLD-ANCESTOR cause: the NON-LEAF occurrences of those ids (the connective scaffolding above a lens's input roots, computed once by lens_engine.lens_scaffold_ancestor_ids) render heading-only EVEN IN DOCUMENT order, input roots and their subtrees unaffected; occurrence/index-path keyed exactly like the chronological cause, computed ONLY here; the ancestor_notes opt-out is folded producer-side so an overridden lens render passes nothing and stays byte-identical; (5) focused node_count/depth over render_forest. Pure: builds shadow dicts; the input document_forest is never mutated. WIRED since Phase 0.5 Steps 6-12b (ap:S12BREMAIN / ap:S12BSURG): every production render path materializes through it, and the composer (_build_markdown_preview_from_tree) is focus-agnostic, consuming render_forest + policy_by_occurrence. The policy also carries the producer-built source-graph facts (direct_child_counts / uuid_prefix_collisions / full_uuid_headings and -- [ap:UH0UOU] -- source_metrics, the four-field headings-vocabulary index each producer builds once from its pinned cache map and forwards through the source_metrics param).

THE repository-view projection (U1, MasterSpec §5.5, [ap:YGYP2O] §4): turns the Stage-2 forest into the clean commit document's forest BEFORE the one composer -- one top-level node per file (name = the spanned repository-relative path), each mapped entry (AST_QUALNAME/BEACON/MD_PATH first line under a file Path: header) as kind + span(title) with its labels, comment and (full mode) fenced SPAN TEXT/CONTEXT COMMENTS parts, virtual groups and folders spliced out, files sorted by path, non-source nodes left out and counted. Chain 1 r1 (W3): source-authored identity-shaped body text (a docstring example) is retained verbatim in the parts via the ONE parse's body items; generated identity blocks stay absent. Chain 1 r2 (WO [ap:4Q3LQV] W2): the body context also starts at the mapper's generated-prefix '---' terminator (so a FIRST source line survives), and the part cut applies inside body items too. Reads labels/comment/body/title from the ONE note parse; paths from the ONE relpath helper over the pinned cache; refuses a multi-root render. Returns (projected_forest, left_out, ap_ids_removed, error_or_None) -- a forest, never a document; builds shadow dicts and never mutates the cache or the input forest. R2 (agent-kit): the per-entry display (the note-is-entry test, labels/comment, body parts, heading kind) lives in the module-level repository_view_* functions; this projection passes its counting AP stripper as strip_text.

Phase 0.5 Step 5 helper: build the NOTE-PRESERVING option-Y render_forest for a resolved focus_index_path AND record each render node's ORIGIN document index_path (the render->document coordinate bridge the materializer uses to re-key the rebase policy). Unlike the legacy _prune_forest_to_focus_index_path -- which BLANKS breadcrumb notes (note='') and so both violates the v3.1 hazard-a no-blank invariant AND destroys the Path:/MD_PATH: header the rebase baseline + abs-path leader need -- this keeps EVERY retained note byte-for-byte intact (body suppression is a render POLICY, applied later, not a tree mutation). Shape is identical option-Y: nodes strictly ABOVE the focused node N keep only their single on-path child; N keeps its FULL subtree. Returns (render_forest, render_ip->doc_ip map) where both index_paths are list-rooted in their OWN forest's coordinate system (render coords for the new tree, document coords for the original). Pure: shadow dicts, input never mutated.

Phase 1 multi-select (ap:MULTISEL) MINIMAL-COVERING-SUBTREE builder -- the multi-row sibling of _focused_render_forest_with_origin. Given a SET of occurrence-exact focus_index_paths resolved over the SAME document_forest, build the note-preserving render_forest that is the UNION of every selected row's option-Y breadcrumb spine (shared prefixes coalesce naturally), where every SELECTED node keeps its FULL occurrence-specific subtree and every strictly-above breadcrumb ancestor keeps ONLY its on-path children. ANCESTOR-ABSORBS-DESCENDANT: a selected index_path that is a strict prefix of another selected index_path is a FULL node whose subtree already contains the deeper selection, so the deeper one is subsumed (rendered inside the ancestor's full subtree, never double-rendered, never treated as breadcrumb). Notes preserved byte-for-byte (v3.1 hazard-a; body suppression is render policy). Returns (render_forest, render_ip->doc_ip map) exactly like the single-focus sibling so the materializer re-keys the rebase policy + computes the breadcrumb-suppression union identically. Pure: shadow dicts, input never mutated. mode='row' single-select deliberately still uses the single-focus helper (byte-identical regression anchor); this runs ONLY for mode='rows'.

THE ONE headings-only end-of-line metadata emitter ([ap:UH0UOU]): every covered surface's heading suffix comes from HERE and nowhere else. One vocabulary with dock.peek: when the policy carries the render's source_metrics index, the suffix is exactly format_dock_peek_metrics over the same build_dock_peek_index engine (counts/bytes cover the FULL pinned-cache subtree -- completed and suppressed descendants included, never the filtered render forest). THE EXEMPTION: a managed source line (managed_metadata. is_managed_source_line -- a Cartographer/beacon source-map marker in the note's FIRST line) is source code and carries NONE of it, not even the legacy child count; an unmanaged parent of a managed subtree still shows its metrics (they legitimately include the managed descendants). No index in hand (an ad-hoc render with no cache operand) keeps the prior child-count-only suffix byte-for-byte; a uuid missing from a present index renders explicit '?' fields, never a silent zero. Pure; no I/O.

Unified interleaved markdown-preview walk for GLIMPSE markdown mode + output_file write AND the docked Markdown modal (via compose_markdown_modal_view). REPOSITORY VIEW (U1): a policy carrying repository_view=True gates G1 (heading text = name verbatim -- no DOM strip, no [id], no metrics), G2 (every node classified structural -- no file branch/---, no MD-heading branch, no sentinel, no breadcrumb) and G3 (the body is the note verbatim -- no metadata strip, no hazard fence, no embedded-Markdown), honouring the above_leaf/body_suppressed gates; False (every other policy) is byte-identical. REPOSITORY VIEW (U1): a policy carrying repository_view=True gates G1 (heading text = name verbatim -- no DOM strip, no [id], no metrics), G2 (every node classified structural -- no file branch/---, no MD-heading branch, no sentinel, no breadcrumb) and G3 (the body is the note verbatim -- no metadata strip, no hazard fence, no embedded-Markdown), honouring the above_leaf/body_suppressed gates; False (every other policy) is byte-identical. Renders Markdown-mapped files (per-file H1 rebase) AND non-Markdown structural subtrees in one pass, with file-exit re-anchoring and MARKDOWN reset sentinel. The root_in_non_md_file seed (default False) lets a caller mark the render ROOT as living inside a non-Markdown source file when its FILE node is above the received tree (zoom-inside-.py fix) so source '#'-comment notes are not mis-promoted to headings; visible in-tree file boundaries still re-seed their own subtrees. SOLE renderer (the JS twin collectVisibleMarkdownTree was deleted July 2026). Headings-only [id] tokens print the node's SHORT resolver-compatible handle (8 hex, lengthened just enough when ambiguous across the policy's uuid_prefix_collisions index; the full_uuids opt-in rides RenderPolicy.full_uuid_headings) -- the ONE heading-id emission site ([ap:0M6VP8], CF-22/O3). The same headings-only emission point composes the END-OF-LINE METADATA ([ap:UH0UOU]) through the ONE emitter _headings_line_metadata_suffix: dock.peek's four-field vocabulary (▸children · desc:N · self: · tree:) from RenderPolicy.source_metrics, the legacy child-count-only suffix without an index, and NOTHING on a managed source line (Cartographer/beacon markers in the note's first line).

NESTED helper of the markdown-preview walk: shallowest MD_PATH heading depth among md-heading nodes in a subtree, used to PER-FILE rebase a whole Markdown file's heading hierarchy to one consistent base (file marker + shallowest visible heading -> H1). Mirrors JS minMdDepthInSubtree. (Tree-mapping test: a Python nested def.)

NESTED helper of the markdown-preview walk: clamp a MODEL heading level into the full [1,64] range (the model range, distinct from the render-only [1,6] clamp in _render_hashes). (Tree-mapping test: a Python nested def.)

NESTED helper of the markdown-preview walk: RENDER-ONLY heading clamp -- emits a '#' run clamped to [1,6] so marked.parse/CommonMark always treats it as a heading (7+ would spill a literal '####### text' paragraph). Pure display transform; never touches Workflowy/disk/the Cartographer model. (Tree-mapping test: a Python nested def.)

NESTED helper of the markdown-preview walk: emit a node's NOTE body into the rendered output -- option-Y above-leaf suppression (heading-only breadcrumb), optional Cartographer-metadata strip, Workflowy DOM-markup strip, and optional hazard-fencing (fence_hazards=True on the structural/source branch so '#'-comment lines never masquerade as headings). (Tree-mapping test: a Python nested def.)

NESTED helper of the markdown-preview walk: rewrite the heading lines of a MARKDOWN-IN-MARKDOWN note body so the shallowest embedded heading sits at container_level+1 (preserving the body's internal relative heading structure), fence-aware. Implements handoff sec.4 -- a plain node whose note body is Markdown is NO LONGER promoted to a fresh H1 block; its body is embedded one level beneath its containing node instead. (Tree-mapping test: a Python nested def.)

NESTED helper of the markdown-preview walk: emit the heading-only structural BREADCRUMB DELIMITER (handoff sec.3) after a FILE/MARKDOWN-sentinel/markdown-content block closes. Re-renders the structural ancestor chain (render root -> the next structural node's parents) at root-relative heading levels, headings only (no bodies), so the reader is visibly relocated back into the global Workflowy tree rather than appearing nested inside the H1 block that just ended. Repeated ancestor headings are intentional -- the repetition IS the delimiter. RESET-AWARE (mirrored-branch sentinel fix): an ancestor flagged is_reset_boundary (a MARKDOWN sentinel, or a standalone-mode file node -- the kinds that pushed a child-depth structural anchor during their own visit) renders at H1 and re-anchors the remainder of the chain to its child depth, exactly as its anchor push did in the main walk, so a breadcrumb passing THROUGH a sentinel/file reproduces the block's original levels instead of drifting to raw root-relative depths. (Tree-mapping test: a Python nested def.)
Coerce the browser's docked-modal payload ({root,children} or a nested root) into one nested root node dict for the markdown-preview composer; returns None when unusable.

DFS pre-order flatten of the docked-modal visible tree -> (ordered uuid/node pairs, by_id with synthesized parent_id, parent_of); drives option-Y focus paths, the root match, and the UUID-set membership staleness intersect.

THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for modal row identity + occurrence. One preorder DFS over the render forest (list of top-level nodes) that, for every non-empty-uuid node (Workflowy 'Home'/sentinel nodes are transparent: skipped as rows, NOT added to ancestor_path, but DO consume an index slot so the structural index_path still routes through them), emits a record carrying BOTH the PUBLIC identity triple (uuid, ancestor_path[non-empty uuids only], occurrence[per-(uuid,ancestor_path) run-length ordinal]) AND a PRIVATE list-rooted _index_path (child-index route from the forest down to the node, INCLUDING sentinel hops). _build_modal_rows strips the private field; the focused composer resolves a clicked triple to its exact _index_path and prunes positionally -- so the row list, the server match, and the rendered focus can never disagree on which occurrence a click means (drift-proof by construction). LIST-ROOTED: index_path[0] selects the top-level node in `nodes`.

Resolve a clicked PUBLIC row identity (uuid + root-first ancestor_path + occurrence) to its PRIVATE list-rooted _index_path by matching against _iter_markdown_focus_rows over the SAME forest the composer will render. The single bridge between 'what the user clicked' and 'which exact node the composer focuses', so occurrence can never be mis-resolved. Returns the index_path list, or None when no row matches (caller renders whole-tree / stale message).

Round-trip verifier for occurrence-exact focus: follow a list-rooted index_path (index_path[0] selects the top-level node in `nodes`, the rest are child indices) back down the SAME forest and return the landed node's uuid (or None if the path runs off the tree). Callers assert this equals the clicked uuid before trusting focus_index_path, so a resolved path that does not land on the expected node fails loud (falls back to whole-tree) rather than silently focusing the wrong node.

JOB B (Phase 0.5 Step 10, ap:EXECLDG section 6): the DOMAIN RE-ROOT primitive for the Scoped Lightning Rod occurrence-exact re-root pre-step. Follows a resolved list-rooted index_path and returns a shadow-cloned copy of the LANDED node WITH its full subtree (all notes intact) and NO breadcrumb ancestors -- the exact-occurrence subtree, nothing above it. This is deliberately DISTINCT from JOB A (the render-focus option-Y projection -- the shared materializer's _focused_render_forest_with_origin -- which KEEPS the modal-root breadcrumb heading-only above N because a rendered focused view needs that context). Job B narrows a SEARCH DOMAIN and wants ONLY the occurrence's subtree, so a separate narrowly-named primitive keeps the two jobs from sharing one helper (separating them IS the point -- reusing one helper for both would preserve the seam under a new name). NOTE (Steps 12a/12b): the earlier full/UUID-mode Job-A helper _prune_forest_to_focus_index_path was deleted (Step 12a) once the materializer core took over full-mode focus, and the composer's own in-walk focus pruning was deleted (Step 12b sub-commit 3b) -- so Job A now lives SOLELY in the shared materializer (materialize_from_document_forest -> _focused_render_forest_with_origin) and Job A / Job B are fully separate surfaces. Pure: shadow dicts + fresh child lists; the input forest is never mutated. Returns None on a None/empty/out-of-range index_path (the caller guards on isinstance(dict)).

Build the ORDERED flat row list the docked-modal TOP-HALF tree view renders. Thin wrapper over _iter_markdown_focus_rows (the SINGLE occurrence authority): runs it over [render_root] and strips the private _index_path, leaving each row's PUBLIC identity triple (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) + depth + display name. Sharing the enumerator with the focused composer's index-path resolver guarantees the row list and the rendered focus can never disagree on occurrence. name is DOM-markup-stripped for display; the browser supplies its own per-uuid kind/halo (child-visibility is a DOM concern), so this row carries order + structure + identity; and (Aug 2026) when cache_by_id is passed it ALSO stamps each row's own created/modified epoch-seconds (joined from the /nodes-export cache) -- additive presentation-only metadata for the client's per-row hover tooltip + leaf-driven day-change timeline, NEVER part of selection/occurrence identity.

Render ONE Apply-slice tree-view row's option-Y view from an already-projected (and optionally sorted) slice tree. STEP 12b (ap:S12BREMAIN): MATERIALIZER-DRIVEN -- mints a CANONICAL row focus from the clicked (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) triple (only when it resolves occurrence-exactly + round-trips), calls the ONE shared materializer core materialize_from_document_forest to get the NOTE-PRESERVING render_forest + render-forest-keyed policy, then renders via _build_markdown_preview_from_tree with render_policy and NO loose focus_*/body_suppressed_ids side channels. Occurrence-exactness + breadcrumb (occurrence-keyed) + surviving---deprecated (uuid-keyed, via deprecated_ids=body_suppressed_ids) body suppression are all owned by the policy. A root/falsy/unresolvable focus degrades to focus=None (whole tree) -- unchanged here (the exact-or-error flip is a later sub-commit; per-row is guarded exact-triple-or-stale upstream in _handle_render_slice_modal). Used by BOTH the snapshot pre-render (per row, keyed by _slice_row_key) and the single on-demand render_slice_row path.

Feature LEAF COUNT: over the FINAL rendered slice forest, count the LEAF nodes from a clicked tree-view row DOWN to the end of the render order -- exactly the `since='last N'` value a user would pass to keep 'this row and everything below it'. Single-sourced on the SAME primitives everything else uses: collect_leaf_branches (the ONE leaf definition, shared with the sort / since window / since item-count) supplies the ordered leaf branches, and the occurrence authority _iter_markdown_focus_rows (via _resolve_focus_index_path) resolves the clicked (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) triple to the exact focused node object. 'From the row down' = leaves whose branch passes THROUGH the focused node (its subtree, a contiguous DFS run) plus every leaf after it = total_leaves - (index of the first leaf-branch containing the focused node, by object identity). focus None / root -> the whole document's leaf count. Returns None on a stale/unresolvable focus so the caller omits the label rather than showing a wrong number.

Build the zoom-proof uuid->node map from the /nodes-export cache for the docked-modal render context; fail-soft to {} only for genuinely unavailable cache reads. S03-CR-03: a missing operation boundary (CacheViewError) is a migration bug and now fails CLOSED — never silently render the modal without cache context.

Shared root-regime seed for the markdown-preview composer (zoom-inside-source-file fix). Returns True iff root_uuid classifies (via the zoom-proof cache walk _classify_node_map_state) as INSIDE a non-Markdown source file (state='inside_file', non-.md/.markdown file_path). Single source of truth used by BOTH the docked modal (_build_modal_render_context) and the as_markdown GLIMPSE path so GLIMPSE==modal output is preserved; fail-soft False on FILE/FOLDER/UNMAPPED/inside-.md roots and on any cache miss.

Resolve zoom-proof absolute on-disk path leaders {uuid: abs_path} for visible Path:/Root: file/folder nodes against the cache (full ancestry) via resolve_cartographer_path_from_node; best-effort, unresolved nodes omitted. This is why a file leader survives even when the modal is zoomed BELOW the Root:/folder ancestors.

Membership staleness gate for the docked modal (the ONLY staleness check; there is no node-content comparison): returns the DOM-only UUIDs absent from the /nodes-export cache (a structural add the cache hasn't ingested). Any such UUID => stale. Inverse direction (hidden cache nodes) is deliberately NOT staleness. No refresh forced (detect+warn); fail-soft [] when cache unavailable.

Best-effort intersection render tree for the docked modal's phase-1 UUID-MISMATCH case: prunes the DOM tree so the rendered LEAF set is a SUBSET of the DOM leaf set (keep cache-matched leaves + their DOM ancestors, prune dead branches, prefer DOM-sent name/note). Returns None when nothing survives so the caller can message the refresh-cache case.

THE single branch-date rule shared by the timestamp SORT (_reorder_tree_by_timestamp) and the GLIMPSE `since` window/curation-cursor pivot. Given a root->leaf branch as a list of (uuid, node) and the sort_by ('created' | 'modified'), returns the branch's comparison timestamp: created = the LEAF's own createdAt; modified = max(modifiedAt) over EVERY node on the branch. Returns None when the timestamp is unavailable (uuid absent from cache / no int value). Factored out so the sort and the `since` filter can NEVER drift on what a branch's date means -- both call this.

SHARED timestamp-sort pre-pass for the Markdown modal AND as_markdown GLIMPSE. Reorders a visible node tree by leaf createdAt (created sort) or branch-max modifiedAt (modified sort), then trie-merges the sorted root->leaf branches so a shared ancestor straddled by an out-of-cluster branch correctly RE-EMITS its file leader/breadcrumb. sort_by=None is identity passthrough (current behavior). Returns a NEW shadow tree (inputs never mutated); the composer's regime-threading + file-rebase + md-in-md all stay correct by construction because every leaf keeps its FULL ancestor path. Keys are joined from the /nodes-export cache by UUID (the DOM payload has no timestamps); a UUID absent from the cache sinks last (defensive; the modal already flags true desync via membership staleness). Branch-date rule delegated to _branch_timestamp_key_static so the SORT and the GLIMPSE `since` pivot share ONE definition.

The heart of the DOM<->cache sync layer for the docked Markdown modal: computes ALL tree-global render invariants ONCE (normalized root, flatten, cache map, zoom-proof abs-path overrides, root-regime seed, membership-staleness UUID-set verdict, intersection-pruned render_root) so both the single-view and snapshot composer paths reuse it. Reconciles the visible-only DOM tree against the zoom-proof /nodes-export cache without forcing a rate-limited refresh. NOTE: staleness is a UUID-SET MEMBERSHIP check only -- there is NO node content (NAME/NOTE) comparison (removed as unwinnable; see TODO anchor). Accepts an optional sort_by/sort_direction that reorders render_root (and re-flattens render_ordered/by_id/parent_of) via _reorder_tree_by_timestamp so option-Y focus paths + snapshot rows + the composer all see the SAME sorted tree.

Compose ONE docked-modal row's option-Y Markdown view server-side (the canonical single source of truth shared with as_markdown GLIMPSE). Builds the shared render context (or reuses a prebuilt one), resolves the clicked focus occurrence-exactly (sorted branch from the supplied ancestor_path+occurrence; unsorted branch via the Step-9 scalar-focus bridge over render_parent_of, canonicalized occurrence=0), FAILS LOUD (focus_unresolved) on a requested-but-unresolvable leaf. STEP 12b (ap:S12BREMAIN): MATERIALIZER-DRIVEN -- mints a CANONICAL row focus from the resolved focus_index_path and routes through the ONE shared materializer core materialize_from_document_forest, feeding the composer render_forest + render_policy (breadcrumb body suppression occurrence/index-path keyed) with NO loose focus_* side channels; abs_path_overrides still forwarded (zoom-proof leaders survive over the note-preserving render_forest). Returns markdown + truncated + root_matched + membership-staleness cache_stale/stale_nodes (UUID-set check only; no content comparison). Unmatched focus_leaf on a stale/pruned tree -> empty + actionable refresh message.

Pre-render EVERY visible row's option-Y view (below-threshold path) returning {uuid:{markdown,truncated}} the browser caches for instant row clicks. Builds the tree-global render context ONCE (cache map / abs-path overrides / UUID-set membership staleness / intersection prune) and reuses it per row, so only the irreducible O(N) per-row render walk remains (the prior per-row context rebuild was gratuitously quadratic-plus).

ROWS-ONLY docked-modal response (FIX 2 corollary ⑥b): build the SAME render context the snapshot/single paths build (sort + since prune -> render_root) and emit ONLY the ordered tree-view rows via the shared _build_modal_rows authority -- NO per-row markdown compose, so it is O(N) and never triggers the FROZEN-DOM-SINGLE freeze hang. Feeds the frozen top-half list + the occurrence triples that make each subsequent single render occurrence-exact. Reuses _build_modal_render_context + _build_modal_rows verbatim, so row identity cannot drift from the snapshot/single paths.

beacons.role: workflowy_glimpse(self, node_id, use_efficient_traversal: bool, output_file, suppress_metadata: bool, as_markdown: bool, target_tab, sort_by, sort_direction, headings_only, since, _ws_connection, _ws_queue)

beacons.comment: STEP 3 (WSLIVE) helper: inspect a correlated Direction-A reply and, if it carries the unified endpoint-liveness ghost code 'unknown_endpoint' (emitted by the broker on a targeted resolve-miss / dead forward, or by the SW on a targeted-frame map-miss/purge -- AMENDMENT A), raise a distinct actionable NetworkError naming the ghost + the remedy (the tab was asked to re-register; retry). No auto-retry here (REV3): the broker's detection-site re-register broadcast is the heal and the next identical call is the retry. A non-ghost reply passes through untouched.

Generic MCP-initiated WS request/response over the broker: stamps a unique request_id, sends the frame (optionally target_tab OR target_endpoint_id), and consumes ONLY the matching reply off the shared queue (dropping foreign frames). Extracted from workflowy_glimpse so every Direction-A call (GLIMPSE, get_extension_settings, ...) shares one correlation impl. STEP 3 (WSLIVE): a correlated reply carrying code:'unknown_endpoint' is raised as a distinct actionable NetworkError via _raise_if_unknown_endpoint (never returned as data). WSLIVE2 (caller-intent routing): a caller holding a REAL endpoint_id passes target_endpoint_id (NOT laundered through target_tab), so the broker routes via resolve_target_endpoint and a miss is the unknown_browser_endpoint liveness ghost (heal + re-register) rather than an unknown_target_tab routing error; target_endpoint_id wins over target_tab if both are passed.

MCP-initiated Direction-A WS call: ask the target Workflowy tab for its LIVE extension settings (note-session tags, global tags, default note-sessions parent UUID). Fails loudly if no tab. The second-ever MCP->browser request after GLIMPSE.

Gather ALL trailing #tags found by walking a session node's descendants, using the canonical emoji-aware split_name_and_tags parser (NEVER reads the note field). Returns a de-duped, first-seen-ordered list including the note-session tag(s) themselves.

Pure root->node Show-Path renderer reusing the same cache parent-chain walk as _resolve_uuid_path_and_respond (server), returning a list of name lines (HTML-unescaped) instead of sending a WS frame. Shared by list_note_sessions output.

Return anchors in Workflowy VISUAL order via a nested-priority DFS of the cache. Default/public mode enumerates GLOBAL anchors only (local anchors are recognized but hidden); private widget flags can include local anchors and add an anchor-only tree + raw-text inventory. Anchor-hood + attributes (local/favorite) are decided by the ONE shared classify_anchor_tags matcher over the FULL family vocabulary (local/favorite/deprecated word lists; --deprecated never confers Dock identity), so listing and boundary can never drift. favorites_only=True switches membership to the ⭐ shortlist: every favorite (global OR local, regardless of show_local), PLUS -- with show_local -- locals reachable from a favorite through an UNBROKEN chain of local Docks (an intervening non-favorite GLOBAL Dock cuts the chain and is connective; non-local non-favorite descendants of a favorite are hidden). Zero favorites in the vault -> favorites_fallback: the full list, flagged, with a composed favorite_tag_hint + favorites_notice. Rows/tree nodes carry is_favorite; the result echoes favorite_count / total_dock_count / shown counts. This is anchor inventory, NOT a Stage-1/Stage-2 render.

Create one plain note-session node (name = description + trailing union of session tag(s) + extra_tags; note = detail) under parent_uuid via ETCH. No metadata block, no children. Attribute tags are ONE per attribute (family encoding): when local_postfix / favorite_postfix WORDS are given, _attribute_tags emits <SEP><word> variants as SEPARATE tags appended to EACH anchor/session tag only (NOT extra_tags) -- #wfy-ns--local and/or #wfy-ns--fav -- producing a LOCAL anchor (hidden from list_anchors, still a descendants boundary) and/or a FAVORITE anchor (the dock.list ⭐ shortlist); neither word -> the bare tag, byte-for-byte the prior behavior. Guards the PARENT via _classify_node_map_state: a FOLDER parent is REJECTED with an actionable message (map to a FILE first); FILE/INSIDE_FILE parents are allowed but carry a mapped_subtree_warning (F12+3 to persist); UNMAPPED (the normal case for a plain note-sessions parent) is allowed silently. Returns whatever ETCH returns.

beacons.role: ⚡ add_to_anchor(self, parent_uuid: str, nodes, tags, note_file, content, name)
beacons.comment: Guarded capture wrapper around workflowy_etch: etch one or many nodes under an anchor (parent_uuid) AFTER the shared placement guard (_anchor_target_guard_error) confirms the target is not a FOLDER and not a NON-Markdown mapped file. Fails CLOSED on an uncached parent. Surfaces a mapped_subtree F12+3 advisory when the parent is a Markdown file / inside Markdown. This is the ONLY value-add over calling workflowy_etch directly (the guard); dialect-neutral by design (the anchor's dialect -- todo/note/brainstorm/etc -- is unknown at call time). THREE payload forms, EXACTLY ONE required (loud on both/neither -- deliberately unlike workflowy_etch's nodes_file, which silently WINS over inline nodes): `nodes` (an ETCH forest) XOR `note_file` (an absolute-path UTF-8 text file -> exactly ONE node: file STEM = NAME, raw text = NOTE, normalized at the edge via _node_payload_from_note_file so the funnel is untouched; filename-embedded #tags REJECTED -- tags must go through tags=; a leading '[ap_CORE]' filename handle is canonicalized to '[ap:CORE]') XOR `content` (a raw string -- write_file-parity -- with REQUIRED `name`; normalized at the edge via _node_payload_from_content into ONE node: name = NAME verbatim, content = NOTE verbatim; a trailing #tag in name is ALLOWED since it is directly authored). OPTIONAL `name` with note_file: overrides the stem as the node name (stem-derived tag-region check + AP-ID transform SKIPPED).

Edit an existing anchor: rename its TOPIC and/or replace its DESCRIPTION (note). The rename runs the ONE protected-name composer on ONE live snapshot (never a stale cache name): supplied trailing #tags or an added/changed leading [ap:] handle are loud errors; existing tags + AP-ID are preserved automatically. Refuses non-anchor nodes via the ONE shared classify_anchor_tags matcher on is_anchor -- so a LOCAL anchor (#wfy-ns--local) is editable exactly like a global one (locality only hides it from list_anchors, never from editing). Leaves any Cartographer metadata untouched and flags when the node lives in a mapped subtree (advise F12+3) -- never reconciles disk.

MCP-initiated Direction-A WS read: ask the target tab for its LIVE slice-group config (expand_groups [each {id,name,prefixes,root_uuid,description}], active_group, the three F8 postfix words, the global-never-expand list, and the tiny Anchor Dock tag/local-postfix vocabulary needed by one-read LensSpec Stage 0). Same page-side handler the F8 copy button's nested read uses; the server is the single settings reader for the slice-group MCP tools.

MCP-initiated Direction-A WS read answered by the BROKER ITSELF (not a tab): stamps a request_id and sends action=broker_status; the broker replies broker_status_result with its live registry snapshot (browser connections, endpoints incl. seconds_since_seen + is_default, default endpoint, MCP clients incl. is_primary, primary id). Rides the same request_id correlation rail as GLIMPSE. NOT tab-specific -- there is no target_tab and no tab_optional; the broker answers directly (like ping->pong), so it works even with zero browser tabs connected. Backs the workflowy_broker_status observability tool.

MCP-initiated Direction-A WS write: hand the target tab the FULL canonical expand_groups array + active_group id to persist (the server did all policy/normalization). The tab persists via its own persistExpandGroups path (atomic storage write + broadcast) and ACKs with the re-normalized groups. The ONLY server->tab write path for slice groups.

beacons.role: ⚡ workflowy_scry(self, node_id: str, use_efficient_traversal: bool, depth, size_limit: int, output_file)
