LAYER-4 snippet EXTRACTION -- the back half split out of beacon_get_code_snippet (Commit 2). Given an ALREADY-RESOLVED node (resolved via Layer 1 by the caller), it owns everything downstream of handle resolution: parse the node's BEACON/AST_QUALNAME/MD_PATH note, walk ancestors over nodes_by_id to the enclosing FILE (Path:) node, resolve the on-disk absolute path, and delegate to beacon_obtain_code_snippet for language-specific (AST/span/MD_PATH/text) snippet extraction. LAYER-3 UNIVERSAL BOUNDARY RESOLVER -- THE single arbitration loop for UUID / AP-ID / symbol handles, shared by tag/mutator callers and resolve_node_identity_record (all three resolve verbs). Delegates mechanics to Layer 1 / the AP primitive / Layer 2 or the injectable async symbol_runner (beacon's scoped/suppressed leg). The DEFAULT symbol leg honours the global suppression list too ([ap:7ORCPL]): when the caller passes suppress_tags_provider (the tag and mutator fronts do), the leg awaits it ONLY when it actually runs -- after the UUID and AP-ID legs came back unresolved -- and drops suppressed candidates before the 0/1/N decision; without a provider the leg stays unfiltered (the established tri-state, other callers unchanged). Default order remains [prefer] + RESOLUTION_DOMAIN_ORDER; domain_order can supply the ruled beacon orders as data. Unique or ambiguous STOPS, only unresolved falls through; self-load failure is unresolved. Existing prefer/allow_* callers retain byte-identical tri-state results. The internal _with_leg_details posture exposes the raw leg extras (AP core, prefix, truncation, symbol/scope fields) and the reused map to the record builder, which never resolves again. No domain loop or primitive calls remain in the record builder. ARCHIVE READS TWO-PHASE (U1): the UUID and AP legs run at universe='live' in the family's order, and ONLY after every allowed domain missed live do they run again at universe='archive' in the same relative order -- the symbol leg NEVER runs on the archive phase (Axiom 12: symbols are live-only). Delete outside the mutex after exact-path/sequence recheck. The floor never moves backward; adopters hold the mutex while copying. Cleanup failure warns and leaves retryable residue, never hard-dirties an already coherent epoch. Applies to checkpoint, full-refresh and compat-patch cuts; CUT-1 removed lease-reference deferral and its admission-mutex stage.

S01 physical journal commit protocol: locked validate/recover/allocate/write-record/advance-head; manifest never points past a missing record; deterministic orphan adoption/quarantine with F2 epoch-lineage rule; the ATTEMPTED SEQUENCE is stamped onto every post-record publication failure (type preserved) so the S04 sealer's recovery can identify the exact transaction, and PHASE-AWARE exact-record durability evidence (record_durable: True exactly when the failure phase proves the exact record occupied the attempted sequence) rides with it so sequence allocation alone can never manufacture committed recovery (Remediation Chain 2, Rounds 1–2); CALLER-SUPPLIED effect-validation / verified-record-construction failures are stamped (verified_record_construction_failed) so the sealer hard-dirties them as verified_effect_unpublishable before the failure returns, never confused with EXISTING-lineage typed errors which propagate unstamped under invariant 6 (Remediation Chain 3); the append's in-lock LINEAGE CONTEXT (actual pre-attempt manifest journal head + account/epoch, plus the attempted sequence as a distinct value) is stamped onto every caller-supplied failure so the sealer's DirtyBarrierPublicationError carries real lineage coordinates with no second manifest read (Remediation Chain 4).

S03 operation-boundary authority (§7): one adoption per cache-backed operation via a ContextVar snapshot; nested reuse; cancellation-safe set/reset; create_isolated_context_task clears the snapshot for NEW-operation spawns (asyncio.create_task copies context by default); publish_local_cache_view COW bridge with task-scoped read-your-writes overlay (§6.3/W1). The admission-phase seams establish_admission_snapshot / rebase_during_admission are dormant with zero production calls after CUT-1, retained for N05.

THE one new writer of _OPERATION_CACHE_SNAPSHOT beside the boundary itself (Archive Reads U1, §4.3.1): sets the task's snapshot to a copy of the current one carrying archive=context — and, when view is given (an augmented view), that view's view/nodes_export/nodes_by_id — with operation_id, label, owner, dirty_ids and boundary_status copied unchanged; the outer snapshot is restored exactly on exit. _snapshot_for_view and rebase_during_admission carry archive forward unchanged; create_isolated_context_task clears the snapshot, so spawned NEW operations never inherit a context (E41).

S03-B Gate (c) worker-scope pin (§7.1 bullet 3): capture + pin the operation snapshot for a process-lifetime worker/job scope (detached CARTO/MARKDOWN workers) where the process IS the operation and no nested reset exists; interactive/async operations use cache_operation_boundary (automatic reset) instead.

Transition COW bridge: archive guard first, private outer containers plus detached changed fragments, explicit transferred build sharing unchanged nodes on every CAS attempt. The winning sparse effects and dirty sample commit under the publisher mutex; retries discard losing bookkeeping. Same-authority task overlays preserve pinned markers and apply only own sparse effects across generations.

Fail closed; never weaken validation to save the span. """ target = Path(path) try: current = _stat_identity(target) except OSError as exc: raise CoherenceStateMissingError( "candidate snapshot was deleted between validation and " "publication (TOCTOU guard); discard and restart from a fresh basis", path=target, ) from exc if current != proof.identity(): raise CoherenceSchemaError( "candidate snapshot identity changed between validation and " "publication (TOCTOU guard): the candidate was replaced or " "deleted mid-publish; Single shared source of truth for CARTO job-status classification: CARTO_TERMINAL_STATUSES (the complete set of DONE states) and CARTO_GC_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES (the clean-exit subset the age-based GC may auto-delete), plus is_carto_job_terminal()/is_carto_job_active(). Consumed by _gc_carto_jobs AND _clear_carto_job_history so 'is this job still running?' is answered in ONE place. DENY-BY-DEFAULT: any unrecognized/blank/future status is NON-terminal => treated as active => never deleted; it simply surfaces in the widget until we knowingly add it here.

Sentinel-sealed guarded merge-write for CARTO job JSON status. Applies the exact terminal/cancelling precedence table, forces non-terminal writes to cancelling while the job-scoped sentinel exists, and performs one bounded post-replace corrective write. Shared by server and workers; best-effort and never raises.

Single shared source of truth for CARTO job-status classification: CARTO_TERMINAL_STATUSES (the complete set of DONE states) and CARTO_GC_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES (the clean-exit subset the age-based GC may auto-delete), plus is_carto_job_terminal()/is_carto_job_active(). Consumed by _gc_carto_jobs AND _clear_carto_job_history so 'is this job still running?' is answered in ONE place. DENY-BY-DEFAULT: any unrecognized/blank/future status is NON-terminal => treated as active => never deleted; it simply surfaces in the widget until we knowingly add it here.

Sentinel-sealed guarded merge-write for CARTO job JSON status. Applies the exact terminal/cancelling precedence table, forces non-terminal writes to cancelling while the job-scoped sentinel exists, and performs one bounded post-replace corrective write. Shared by server and workers; best-effort and never raises.
Build default search order for workflowy_nexus config files when WORKFLOWY_NEXUS_CONFIG is not set
Resolve explicit WORKFLOWY_NEXUS_CONFIG path or first discovered default config candidate
Read and validate the external workflowy_nexus JSON config file before model validation
One import-safe raw JSON discovery authority shared by full ServerConfig loading and the narrow MCP registration-profile bootstrap
Normalize and fail-loud validate the two supported import-time MCP registration profiles

Credential-free import-time profile bootstrap: non-blank environment wins over raw mcpProfile config, then consolidated default; a blank/whitespace env value is treated as unset; never instantiates ServerConfig or touches its cache
Normalize (strip+lower) and fail-loud validate the two published-params-schema modes (object | union) for the six family tools

Credential-free import-time bootstrap of the published-params-schema mode: a non-blank WORKFLOWY_MCP_PARAMS_SCHEMA wins (invalid raises at import); blank/whitespace/absent is unset and yields the `object` default; environment-only by decision -- no config-file key
Apply environment-variable precedence over JSON-file values when building the resolved ServerConfig
Central loader implementing config-file discovery, environment precedence, validation, and cached resolved config state
Cached access wrapper for the resolved ServerConfig used by server and worker bootstrap flows
Startup logging helper that lazily loads the resolved config when no config is supplied

beacons.role: single-daemon HTTP transport: URL/token resolution, liveness probe, ensure-running spawn, and the HTTP run entrypoint
beacons.comment: The one Workflowy MCP execution domain as a standalone Streamable-HTTP listener; stdio shims and HTTP-native hosts both attach here

beacons.role: resolve_transport(): stdio|http from CLI arg or env
http_dial_host(): concrete address clients dial (never the wildcard bind address)
shared_token(): the ONE local-mesh secret, reused from the broker
is_daemon_listening(): TCP liveness probe of the daemon port
ensure_daemon_running(): probe-or-spawn the detached singleton daemon (the broker pattern applied to the server)
beacons.comment: Spawns `python -m workflowy_mcp --transport http` with the SAME interpreter/env (no second uv resolution; inherits WORKFLOWY_API_KEY / WORKFLOWY_NEXUS_CONFIG from the host blob); on Windows in its own visible console so the human sees it like the broker

beacons.role: run_http_daemon(): attach bearer auth and run the FastMCP app as the Streamable-HTTP daemon
beacons.comment: The transport switch itself: same `mcp` object server.py builds, same lifespan, different transport; auth is attached here so server.py construction is untouched

Pure Dock-peek source index: existing direct-child authority plus priority-ordered ID lists and iterative bottom-up descendant/title+note UTF-8 byte totals beneath one root. Totals include completed/suppressed nodes and content behind nested Dock signposts; display traversal owns Dock boundaries separately. No source aliases in output, cache publication, live reads, or renderer changes.

THE render-side source-metrics index ([ap:UH0UOU]): the SAME build_dock_peek_index bottom-up aggregator, merged over every top-level root of one render, so rendered headings carry dock.peek's four-field vocabulary (▸children · desc · self · tree) from the ONE metrics engine -- counts and byte totals cover the FULL pinned-cache subtree (completed/suppressed descendants included), never the filtered render forest, exactly dock.peek's semantics. Roots absent from the map are skipped (DOM-capture fail-soft); ids missing from the result stay unknown (the composer prints explicit '?' fields, never silent zeros). Consumed via RenderPolicy.source_metrics at the composer's ONE heading-metadata emitter. Pure; no I/O.

Pure Dock-peek recency policy shared by compact AND detail='full' so both select identical items: recent=N keeps the N newest walked rows on the ITEM's own created_at/modified_at (recent_by, default modified; ancestors are never injected or counted), then the whole result is ordered by sort_by/sort_direction (recent implies sort_by=recent_by unless overridden; ascending is the default direction EVERYWHERE -- desc is an explicit sort_direction opt-in, SSVIC9; 'none' keeps document order). THE completed filter for dock.peek lives HERE and nowhere else: rows already flagged completed are excluded from the candidate pool by default on EVERY path -- recency views (recent=N or a timestamp sort_by) AND the plain document-order inventory -- unless include_completed=true opts back in (U6/J11: the inventory no longer lists ✓ rows by default). Peek's walk marks completed via the shared _node_is_completed predicate; this policy only consumes the row flag. Missing timestamps sink last under either direction; ties keep document order. Returns owned row copies plus a selection/sort description (selection carries completed_excluded) for the header and JSON.

[ap:TVIIBN] 4e the ONE peek-side recency-rule line: under recent=N the compact peek renders this explicit sentence on its own line right below the header (beside describe_dock_peek_selection's selection phrase, same vocabulary) naming what was selected and teaching the 4d(a) rule -- sort_direction only orders these rows, it never changes which rows were chosen. The RENDER-verb twin (since_applied/render_scope wording) is server.py's _recency_header_sentence inside _shape_glimpse_family_return; two data shapes, one rule, each surface one composer. Pure.

Pure server-side F8 slice-policy core: Phase 1 (simplified search evaluator + minimal-subtree builder), Phase 0 (UUID-MEMBERSHIP-ONLY DOM-vs-cache validator -- every visible UUID must exist in cache; NO parent_id edge or name/note comparison, matching the proven docked-modal staleness contract; fail-closed only on a genuinely-missing UUID), and Phase 2 (suppression/ deprecated/expand plan builder). No WebSocket / no DOM / no broker; plain functions over plain dicts.

Canonicalize a cache-stored tag token by stripping presentational HTML-tag markup (<u></u>, <b>, <code>, ...; pattern mirrors whiten_text_for_header_compare) + de-whitening common HTML entities, BEFORE the leading-'#' strip. This is the DOM-vs-cache PARITY fix: the live F8 path harvests clean data-val tags, but the cache slice-group GLIMPSE path reads the raw /nodes-export name where a tag may arrive as #<u>nexus--skills</u>; without this, the garbage token fails the literal prefix match and Phase 1 silently evicts the (tag-agnostic) member + its ancestors. Feeds _strip_hash + extract_name_tags, so every membership/classify consumer is fixed in one place.

THE single shared middle-segment wildcard matcher: does '#'-stripped tag T match base prefix P as P [ '-<middle>' ] [ '--<postfix>' ]? Front is literal startsWith P; the middle (everything between P and any recognized trailing '--<postfix>') must be EMPTY or start with '-' (hyphen = required segment delimiter, Dan's ruling -- so comm-jim matches comm-jim / comm-jim-teams / comm-jim--deprecated but NOT comm-jimx). Recognized postfix is matched in the trailing '--<word>' region against the LIVE postfix set (POSTFIX_SEP + word). Returns {matched, matched_prefix, middle, postfix} -- postfix is '' for a bare/plain family variant. This is the ONE recognizer is_slice_member + classify_node_tags + the deprecated-exclusion all call, so F8 / Markdown modal / server-side slice GLIMPSE never drift. Accepts the right-boundary-at-whitespace divergence from Workflowy's boundaryless search as a documented, rare, accepted edge case.

THE single shared anchor-tag matcher: does '#'-stripped tag T match ONE base anchor tag B under the EXACT-base rule -- T == B (the bare base, attribute None) or T == B<SEP>w for ONE registered attribute word w in the UNION of the local/favorite/deprecated word lists (attribute local|favorite|deprecated; one tag per attribute, postfixes never stacked)? Deliberately EXACT (no middle segment), unlike slice_tag_variant_match, so an anchor tag is a specific identity marker that cannot bleed into a sibling (wfy-ns !-> wfy-nsx / wfy-ns-project). Returns {matched_base, postfix, attribute, is_local} or None. Word collision across two lists resolves deterministically local > favorite > deprecated; longest-word-first across the union so a suffix word never shadows. --deprecated is REPORTED (attribute='deprecated') but never confers Dock identity -- that ruling lives in classify_anchor_tags. Shares only POSTFIX_SEP with the slice matcher; the anchor attribute words are a separate semantic domain from slice --expand/--suppress/--deprecated.

Classify a node's NAME tags against the configured base anchor tags + the THREE attribute-word lists (local/favorite/deprecated), via the shared match_anchor_tag matcher. UNION semantics (I5): is_anchor True iff at least one PROPER family tag matched (bare base, --local or --favorite); is_local / is_favorite are the union of their attribute over ALL proper family tags across ALL bases (a bare base asserts NOTHING, so #wfy-ns + #wfy-ns--local IS local -- the historical global-form-dominates rule is SUPERSEDED); a --deprecated match NEVER confers Dock identity (I4) and is reported via has_deprecated / family_tags(proper=False) only. Also returns matched_base/matched_tag (the FIRST proper family tag in name order), matched_bases (distinct bases with a proper tag, first-occurrence order -- the dock.update families: detector's input) and family_tags (every family-form tag in name order with base/attribute/postfix/proper). This is the ONE classifier BOTH list_anchors (is_anchor AND NOT is_local) and build_anchor_boundary_predicate (is_anchor -- a favorite or local anchor still stops descent; a deprecated-only node does NOT) call, so anchor-hood + attributes can never drift between the enumeration and the GLIMPSE 'descendants' boundary. Empty base set -> not an anchor. Pure; no I/O.

Per-tag-FAMILY auto-expand postfix rule for add_to_anchor's tags= arg. Groups the union tag set by family (first hyphen-delimited segment); within each family, if NO tag already carries ANY recognized postfix (--expand/--suppress/--deprecated, detected via slice_tag_variant_match) it appends --expand to EVERY tag in that family; if ANY tag in the family already carries a postfix it leaves the WHOLE family untouched (don't-clobber rule). Families are processed INDEPENDENTLY. Pure/deterministic; no I/O. Applied only to a tree ROOT that has descendants (gating lives in the caller).

THE name-only tag reader: return the '#'-stripped tags in a node NAME's TRAILING tag region, via the ONE canonical authority nexus_map_codebase.split_name_and_tags (reached BY IMPORT, never copied -- Pin 1). This is what match_scope='name' means on every semantic tag-search surface (is_slice_member / node_is_curated_for_prefixes / build_tag_predicate / node_is_live_self / build_anchor_boundary_predicate / gather / classify_node_tags / name_has_global_never_tag): a tag is a tag only when it sits at the end of the name, exactly as the add/remove/rename_tag mutation core reads them. Contrast extract_name_tags (whitespace-token, ANYWHERE in the title) -- the pre-flip behaviour, kept only for the free-form search-string parser (parse_search_string_to_base_prefixes); suppression and the postfix classification read THIS reader (084). Lazy function-local import mirrors _resolve_split_name_and_tags (api_client_core): nexus_map_codebase imports nothing from workflowy_mcp, so there is no cycle; the import is cached after first success.

Normalize an agent-supplied slice-group tag list (comma-separated string OR list) into canonical '#'-stripped BASE prefixes for storage: strip a leading '#', trim, drop empties/internal-whitespace/embedded-'#', de-dupe (order-preserving), and COLLAPSE any '--<postfix>' variant (auto-expand/suppress/deprecated, the three LIVE postfixes) down to its base so foo--expand/foo--deprecated both become foo. Lenient by design (help the agent out); returns (bases, collapsed_info, dropped) for transparency. Postfix words are passed in (server reads them live from the client) so this never hardcodes policy.

The ONE get_slice_group_config REPLY parser for the policy operands (post-IMPPTX audit, Finding 5): given the live Direction-A reply, return {auto_expand, suppress, deprecated, global_never_expand} with DEFAULT_* fallbacks and the global-never list VALIDATED (must be a list of non-empty strings, else [] -- a malformed string is NEVER character-split into bogus single-letter stems). Consumed by EVERY Stage-0 originator that reads the live postfix config so the reply means ONE thing everywhere: _resolve_slice_group_config (the MCP-return helper), the _handle_render_slice_modal slice cell + Lightning render_tags 'slice' branch + render_symbols suppression read, _project_slice_base_tree_for_scoped_lightning, and the F8 expansion-plan handler. Transport stays per-originator (each keeps its own WS read + ghost-endpoint handling); the INTERPRETATION of the reply is unified here. Pure; no I/O.

THE server-side parser for the slice-group NAME grammar (pipe-delimited category path + optional trailing [n] order index on the last segment; a LEADING [n] marks a category/expander row). Bug-for-bug port of the client's parseSliceGroupName in glimpse-cache-client.js (the display authority) so server-side handle resolution and the agent-facing public view interpret a stored name EXACTLY the way the widget displays it: same expander quirk (the expander branch does NOT strip a trailing [n] from its last segment), same empty-segment survival ('nexus|' -> ['nexus','']), same literal treatment of an unparseable bracket ('[foo]nexus' is just a name). Derives short_name (the final segment; for a LEAF its trailing [n] index is stripped) -- the semantic name accepted as a group_handle form and shown in compact displays. Pure; no I/O. If the grammar ever changes, BOTH runtimes must change together (locked by tests/test_parse_slice_group_name.py).

THE server-side Python twin of the client's buildNestedDisplayItems(..., expandAll=true) nested display builder (glimpse-cache-client.js) -- the exact tree/flatten policy behind the compact slice_group.list inventory. Faithful to the GUI grammar, not a resort-by-path: (1) every stored name is parsed through the ONE parse_slice_group_name grammar; (2) missing intermediate category paths are AUTO-VIVIFIED as synthetic category nodes; (3) a leaf attaches to the category node of ALL BUT its final segment; (4) a leading-[n] record is an explicit expander definition for its category path; (5) when several expander definitions target one path, the lowest-indexed definition is canonical and owns the descendants; the rest render as empty duplicate rows; (6) leaves and categories intermix per level, sorted by (order index, nulls last; case-insensitive display name) -- negative indices and gaps are valid; (7) every category is expanded (the server keeps no persisted collapse state). Returns a flat list of {kind:'leaf'|'expander', name, depth, group, duplicate, synthetic} rows in display order. Pure; no I/O. If the GUI builder ever changes, BOTH runtimes must change together.

Parse a FREE-FORM Workflowy search string (manual-F8 override) into canonical '#'-stripped BASE slice prefixes. Harvests only '#'-tag tokens via extract_name_tags (so a leading '-' negation, the '>' subtree-order operator, parentheses, the 'OR' keyword, and any raw prose are ignored -- a '-#foo' token starts with '-' not '#', so it is naturally dropped), then runs them through normalize_slice_group_tags to strip any trailing '--<postfix>' (auto-expand/suppress/deprecated, read live from options) down to the base and de-dupe. Deliberately simple: covers both a hand-pasted plain '#a OR #b' search AND an advanced curated search; anything that is not a legal '#'-tag is discarded. Postfix words are passed in (single source of truth).
Literal startsWith prefix test on a '#'-stripped tag against a list of '#'-stripped active prefixes — byte-for-byte mirror of JS tagTokenMatchesExpandPrefix so server and client never drift.

THE single membership predicate (per-prefix OR). A node is in the slice iff SOME active prefix P matches one of its tags AND no tag matches P--deprecated. Per-prefix scoping mirrors Workflowy's negation-binds-to-preceding-tag semantics (#P -#P--deprecated OR ...), so deprecating ONE tag does not evict a node still live via another. match_scope (SELECTION-stage scope knob) picks WHERE tags are read: 'name_and_note' (default) -> extract_node_tags (Workflowy-search parity, note counts); 'name' -> _core_trailing_name_tags (the NAME's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter nexus_map_codebase.split_name_and_tags -- a mid-title prose '#tag' or a note-only '#tag' does NOT count; the accepted divergence from a pasted Workflowy search, which has no title-only mode). match_scope is ORTHOGONAL to the --deprecated OPERATION semantics (unchanged). Shared by Phase 1 membership, the compiled search string, and Phase 2's live-hit rescue so the three can never drift.

Form-B (GLIMPSE since='curated') CURATION predicate. True iff the node carries ANY tag that matches an active slice prefix under the SHARED middle-segment matcher (slice_tag_variant_match), read under the SAME match_scope SELECTION-stage scope knob is_slice_member uses ('name' -> _core_trailing_name_tags (the NAME's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter), so neither a mid-title prose family tag nor a family tag living only in a note body curates and neither can move the cursor; 'name_and_note' default -> extract_node_tags(NAME or NOTE, Workflowy-search parity) -- the scope plumbing the server render callers thread into the since='curated' pivot, fixing the Session-019 misread where prose quoting a literal #curated in a note (ap:SP9EY1) advanced a match_scope='name' cursor past every earlier uncurated capture) -- INCLUDING the --deprecated postfix AND middle-segment variants (comm-jim-teams--deprecated curates the comm-jim slice), because a --deprecated tag is ITSELF a curation act (the user tagged it, then triaged it; they must NOT re-see it in the uncurated tail). EXCLUDING the --suppress / --expand postfix variants: those are PRESENTATION (a lens carve-out / auto-expansion -- e.g. a nested program Dock root tagged #curated--suppress to keep its subtree out of a tail), NOT a triage decision; counting them let a suppressed Dock root become the newest 'curated' node and advance the high-water mark past everything captured before it (Session-019 curated-cursor bug). Still DELIBERATELY looser than is_slice_member on the DEPRECATED axis (a node deprecated on every prefix is NOT a member but IS curated), but IDENTICAL on the FAMILY-BOUNDARY axis: it uses the same hyphen-delimited matcher, so comm-jimx does NOT curate the comm-jim slice (a different family). Using the shared matcher (not the loose tag_matches_prefix) keeps the family boundary consistent with membership/classification everywhere.

Scan the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid for the DEPRECATED MIDDLE-SEGMENT variant tags of each active prefix (via the shared slice_tag_variant_match), returning {prefix: [dep_variant_tag, ...]}. Feeds compile_slice_search_expression so the wildcard-less Workflowy search can enumerate each P<middle>--deprecated as its own negation -- the server discovers them; the compiler lists them. Pure over the cache; empty map when cache unavailable. NOT needed by the server-side FILTER (is_slice_member reasons over the cache directly) -- this exists ONLY to make the live-GUI-sync search string reproduce the same member set.

Classify ONE node's NAME tags against the active slice config -> flags has_active / has_auto / has_suppress / has_deprecated / has_global_never_expand. The atomic per-node primitive feeding membership (Phase 1) and the plan (Phase 2). match_scope (keyword, default 'name_and_note') governs WHERE the family-postfix flags read: under 'name' (the 084 ruling) they read ONLY the name's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter -- a mid-title or note-authored --expand/--suppress/--deprecated is prose, not an operation; under 'name_and_note' they read name+note (Workflowy-search parity, the prior behavior). The global-never flag is TRAILING-REGION-ONLY under EVERY scope (Dan's 084 D1: an absolute structural control must be a deliberate trailing tag) via the ONE shared helper pair (normalize_global_never_stems + name_has_global_never_tag).

Build the STOP-RECURSION boundary predicate for the anchor-points projection: a pure (node)->bool that is True iff the node is an anchor (its NAME trailing-tag region carries any configured base anchor tag -- bare, or with ONE registered attribute word: local OR favorite). Routes through the shared classify_anchor_tags matcher on is_anchor -- so a LOCAL anchor (#wfy-ns--local) and a FAVORITE anchor (#wfy-ns--fav) STILL bound a 'descendants' GLIMPSE exactly like a bare-base one (I10: favorite has no bearing on descent; locality only hides an anchor from list_anchors, never from the recursion boundary). A --deprecated-ONLY node is NOT an anchor (I4) and therefore does NOT bound. Reads the NAME's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter (_core_trailing_name_tags -> nexus_map_codebase.split_name_and_tags), the SAME reader _anchor_dock_root_guard / list_note_sessions / the anchor tooling use, so 'what is an anchor' cannot drift between this traversal boundary, the enumeration, and the anchor tooling (and a mid-title prose '#wfy-ns' is NOT a boundary). Anchor tags are matched EXACTLY (no wildcard middle -- wfy-ns !-> wfy-nsx), unlike slice prefixes. Passed as build_selected_subtree_from_cache(boundary_predicate=...) so a raw-root / lightning projection stops descending at child anchors while still emitting the child-anchor node itself as a visible leaf signpost. Empty/blank anchor-tag list -> a predicate that is always False (no boundaries). Pure; no I/O.

THE generic Stage-1 SELECTION primitive: walk the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, admit a node iff member_predicate(node) is True, and build the minimal connective subtree (every admitted node + all ancestors up to and including root_uuid, children priority-ordered). Returns a nested {id,name,note,children} root, or None if root_uuid is absent from the cache. Every cache-sourced selection source converges here by supplying its own admit predicate over ONE tree-walk machinery: slice groups (the is_slice_member closure, via the build_slice_subtree_from_cache wrapper), the raw-dump root GLIMPSE (member_all -> lambda node: True), and Lightning Rod tag/text-search predicates. Two orthogonal TRAVERSAL policies ride alongside the membership predicate: exclude_completed prunes a completed CHILD at admit time (its whole subtree becomes invisible; no downstream --expand can un-hide it), and boundary_predicate is a stop-recursion boundary (a child satisfying it is still visited/admitted and anchors the connective spine, but the walk does not descend into it -- it renders as a leaf). Both policies exempt the root by construction (each is tested only when deciding whether to descend into a CHILD). A THIRD traversal policy, max_depth (ap:EPR86W part a; the spec's recursive=false maps to 1): the walk descends only while the CURRENT node's depth < max_depth (root = depth 0), so max_depth=1 renders the root + its DIRECT children and nothing deeper -- child Docks and plain nodes alike; descend_policy is moot under the cap (the cap stops the descent first). The same gate stops the materialize recursion, so a capped node is childless in the output by construction. None (the default) is the ordinary unbounded walk -- byte-for-byte prior behavior; only the raw-root surfaces thread the cap (a membership selection is unbounded by construction and refuses recursive=false loudly at the spec normalizer).

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD (ap:LRSCOPE) — the SECOND selection substrate. The forest-walking SIBLING of build_selected_subtree_from_cache: same admit-by-member_predicate + minimal-connective-subtree + optional stop-recursion boundary contract and the SAME {id,name,note,children} output shape, but it iterates a PROVIDED in-memory forest (the frozen-DOM captured tree) instead of walking the /nodes-export cache from a root. Reuses the SINGULAR predicates (build_tag_predicate / build_search_predicate) verbatim — predicates are substrate-agnostic (node)->bool, so there is NO predicate duplication. It is a PURE SELECTION SUBSTRATE (forest in -> pruned forest out, feeding the ONE shared composer via _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture); it grows NO predicates / sort / composer of its own — the moment it did, the pipeline would fork. Dan ACCEPTED this dual walk as legitimate architecture (it mirrors the already-blessed cache_render_spec vs dom_captured_tree source axis), NOT a crack.

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD (ap:LRSCOPE) gather-over-forest — the in-memory-forest sibling of gather_tags_in_subtree. Unions every REAL '#'-stripped tag (STRICT recognizer, same as the cache gather) found in a PROVIDED captured-DOM forest, honoring match_scope (name-only vs name+note). Returns the sorted, de-duped '#'-less list. Pure/read-only; used by the DOM-frozen Scoped gather mode so a gather->render_tags handoff surveys the SAME on-screen forest the subsequent render filters (not the whole cache root).

render-symbols CONNECTIVE ROOT: compute the lowest common ancestor of a set of root_uuids by intersecting their root-first ancestor chains and taking the DEEPEST (last) shared id. For a SINGLE root the LCA is that root itself (degenerate -- 'begins at the root_uuid'). Returns None if the roots share no common ancestor (disjoint trees) or any is uncached. This is the connective spine fed to build_selected_subtree_from_cache; the descendant-of-any-root gate (not the LCA) is the real membership filter, so a wider LCA never widens what actually renders.

GLOBAL-NEVER-EXPAND doctrine (Dan, 2026-07, post-IMPPTX audit; tightened 2026-10 by the 084 ruling): the ONE shared stem-normalizer + NAME matcher for the f8_global_never_expand_tags operand. DOCTRINE: global-never suppression reads ONLY the name's TRAILING tag region, under EVERY scope -- it is an ABSOLUTE STRUCTURAL control ('never render this subtree'), so it must be a deliberate, visible TRAILING NAME tag; a tag buried in a NOTE body, or wedged mid-title among prose, never suppresses. (Exact match also gives the user the clean off-switch: rename #wfy-suppress -> #wfy-suppress-old to release while keeping the stem available to re-apply.) normalize_global_never_stems ('#'-optional, whitespace-trimmed, empties dropped) + name_has_global_never_tag (EXACT tag==stem, NOT family/prefix, via _core_trailing_name_tags) are consumed by EVERY reader of the operand so the config field means ONE thing across the whole system: Phase-2 classify_node_tags (has_global_never_expand), render_symbols absolute suppression (node_has_suppress_ancestor), the render_symbols per-item expand sweep (collect_subtree_ids), the merge coverage walks (compute_merge_full_cover / compute_merge_tag_plan), and the HYDSUP Phase-3 hydration seal (apply_expansion_plan_to_subtree). Pure; no I/O.

THE ONE global-never NAME test: True iff the name's TRAILING tag region (via _core_trailing_name_tags, the core splitter) carries an EXACT-match global-never stem -- never a note body, never a mid-title prose mention, under EVERY match_scope (Dan's 084 D1). Change the reading HERE and every consumer (classify_node_tags, node_has_suppress_ancestor, collect_subtree_ids, the HYDSUP hydration seal, the merge coverage walks, _unpersistable_global_never_leaves) follows; never re-implement the test at a call site.

render_symbols PER-ITEM EXPAND sweep (ap:EXPSWP; D1 member-set sweep, NOT the rejected Phase-3 plan hijack): collect the id of EVERY DESCENDANT of each id in root_ids into ONE set, so a caller-flagged node's whole cache subtree joins the Stage-1 member set exactly 'as though those descendants had been passed in the list'. The SEED ids themselves are NOT included -- the caller unions with its explicit resolved set, which already holds them. SUPPRESSION GUARD: before descending into a child, its name's TRAILING tag region (name_has_global_never_tag, the core splitter) is EXACT-matched against suppress_tags, mirroring node_has_suppress_ancestor's trailing-region exact-match semantics (NOT family/prefix; 084: a mid-title or note-only global tag never suppresses) -- a matching child is neither included nor descended into, so render_symbols' ABSOLUTE suppression doctrine is preserved at sweep time (the seeds are guaranteed non-suppressed by the upstream resolution gate). Does NOT filter completed nodes -- Phase 1 owns completed exclusion at admit time (the sweep adds them harmlessly; collect() never materializes them). Boundary-free by design: a flagged node's subtree is swept fully, child anchors included (the selection is an explicit agent request; descend_policy stays rejected for render_symbols). Pure, no I/O; sibling of _ancestor_chain_ids / is_descendant_of_any_root / compute_lca_from_cache.

LIGHTNING ROD gather-tags: union of all REAL '#'-stripped tags found under root_uuid in the /nodes-export cache, sorted + de-duped. match_scope (SELECTION-stage scope knob) picks WHERE tags are harvested: 'name_and_note' (default) -> name AND note (strict recognizer); 'name' -> the NAME's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter (_core_trailing_name_tags; a mid-title prose '#tag' or a note-only '#tag' is not gathered) -- matched to the two render modes so a gather->render_tags handoff surveys exactly the fields the render will filter on. boundary_predicate (Phase-C descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors', default None) is a STOP-RECURSION traversal knob: when a descendant satisfies it (a child anchor), that node's OWN tags are still harvested (visible signpost) but its subtree is NOT surveyed -- so gather and a subsequent render_tags see the SAME bounded universe (root exempt). Uses the STRICT extract_strict_tags_from_text recognizer (NOT the generalized Workflowy-search harvester) so it does NOT return junk harvested from '#' glued inside prose/code (').strip()', 'f8-expand),', etc.). Lightning Rod is unmoored/divergent-from-Workflowy, so gather is free to be smarter about what counts as a genuine tag. Pure, no rendering, no pipeline -- the discovery call whose result feeds a follow-up Lightning Rod render_tags.

LIGHTNING ROD gather SERIALIZER -- the tag-domain peer of the node-tree composer. Turns a flat, sorted tag list (from gather_tags_in_subtree) into a prefix-grouped, hyphen-segment-nested RAW TEXT outline (4 spaces per level, alphabetical within a level). This is the intentional serialization seam for gather: gather produces a TAG SET (not a node tree), so its correct serializer is THIS pure function, NOT the node-tree render tail render_stage2_filter_sort (which would need a fake tree). The shared universal contract is 'one final rendered string', re-unified at the delivery boundary, not at the tree renderer. HYPHEN RULE (Dan): a run of >=1 hyphens collapses to a SINGLE separator, then split -- so double-hyphen postfixes (--deprecated/--suppress/--expand) are NOT special-cased and just become an ordinary trailing segment. SYNTHESIZED PARENTS: an intermediate segment path that is not itself a literal gathered tag still gets an outline header line for readability; those synthetic headers appear ONLY in this text, never in the caller's literal `tags` array. Pure / no I/O -- the tag-set analog of _build_markdown_preview_from_tree.

SLICE-GROUP wrapper over the generic build_selected_subtree_from_cache: it supplies the slice-group admit predicate so the generic primitive does the tree walk. member_all=True -> lambda node: True (the raw-dump: every descendant is a member); otherwise -> the is_slice_member closure (per-prefix membership, deprecated-excluding, NAME-only or NAME+NOTE per match_scope). exclude_completed, boundary_predicate and max_depth (ap:EPR86W part a: the raw-dump recursive=false depth cap; a membership projection is unbounded by construction) thread straight through to the generic primitive's traversal policies. Callers: the slice-group GLIMPSE, the Apply-slice modal, and (via member_all) the raw-dump root GLIMPSE.

PHASE 0 (DOM path) — UUID-MEMBERSHIP-ONLY validation that the browser's visible subtree is known to the /nodes-export cache: every DOM uuid must EXIST in cache. Deliberately NO parent->child edge (parent_id) comparison and NO node-content (name/note) comparison — exactly the proven docked-modal staleness contract (_modal_staleness), which dropped both as unwinnable/overzealous (parent_id boundary+normalization mismatches at the zoom root / virtual nodes produced constant false 'cache_stale'). Fail-closed only on a genuinely-missing UUID (F8 must not act on a node the server doesn't know); a present UUID is sufficient. The inverse direction (cache nodes not in the DOM) is NOT staleness (the DOM is visible-only).

DIAGNOSTIC ONLY (not a gate) — compare the visible DOM subtree's parent->child edges against the /nodes-export cache parent_id and return RICH per-row mismatch detail (node id+name, dom_parent id+name, cache_parent id+name). Purpose: empirically find WHY the old strict edge check tripped (search-mode serialization vs canonical tree) rather than theorize. Returns {missing:[...], edge_mismatches:[...], checked:int, root_id, root_name}. Never raises; never fails the plan.

PHASE 2 (the heart) — given a VALID Phase-1 subtree + active slice config, compute the expansion plan {collapse_suppressed, collapse_deprecated, expand}. Annotates each node, applies the "don't collapse a deprecated node through a live in-slice descendant" rescue rule, normalizes each set topmost-only, and resolves cross-set conflicts via the ASYMMETRIC merge: a contraction dominates a nested expansion, but an expansion does NOT dominate a nested contraction -- so a suppress/deprecated pocket can survive inside an --expand region. BOTH Phase 3 (server) and the JS client executeF8ExpansionPlan execute the plan EXPAND FIRST, THEN collapse_suppressed, THEN collapse_deprecated -- expanding first so a nested contraction is not overwritten by a later re-hydration. Also emits the Tier-2 pending_* live-GUI-sync metadata + the deprecated-body-suppression body_suppressed_ids set (surviving --deprecated nodes render header-only). match_scope (default name_and_note) threads the SELECTION-stage scope into THREE questions: the rescue's liveness membership (compute_live's is_slice_member; post-Sol-audit Finding 2), the promotion pass's ACTIVE-self check (node_is_live_self title-harvests under 'name'), AND -- 084 ruling -- the --expand/--suppress/--deprecated OPERATION classification itself (annotate passes it into classify_node_tags: under 'name' a family postfix counts only in the name's TRAILING tag region; under 'name_and_note' it also counts in the note). The global-never tag is TRAILING-only under every scope (name_has_global_never_tag).

PHASE 3 (no-DOM path) -- apply a Phase-2 expansion plan to the Phase-1 membership subtree IN MEMORY, emulating the browser's executeF8ExpansionPlan against the live DOM. Mandated order EXPAND FIRST, THEN COLLAPSE: (1) expand, (2) collapse_suppressed, (3) collapse_deprecated -- expanding first so a contraction nested inside an expanded region survives (collapse-first would let the expansion re-hydrate and overwrite the nested collapse). COLLAPSE (both sets, identical effect once a UUID is in hand) = drop every descendant of the target node from the subtree (node stays as a childless leaf), mirroring WF.collapseItem. EXPAND = re-hydrate the target node's FULL descendant subtree from the /nodes-export cache (priority-ordered, INCLUDING non-members -- exactly as opening a bullet in the GUI reveals every child regardless of tags), mirroring the recursive WF.expandItem. LOAD-BEARING BOUNDARY SEAL: boundary_predicate + boundary_root_uuid (default None) make the EXPAND hydration honor the SAME stop-at-child-anchors boundary Phase 1 used -- without it, an --expand ancestor of a child anchor would silently re-inflate from the raw cache the very subtree Phase 1 pruned (Phase 1 stopping is not enough because hydration reads raw cache). A child-anchor node hydrates as a childless leaf; boundary_root_uuid exempts the projection root so expanding AT a boundary still reveals its immediate children. LOAD-BEARING GLOBAL-NEVER SEAL (HYDSUP): global_never_expand_tags (default (); EXACT-match, TRAILING-tag-region stems via name_has_global_never_tag, mirroring node_has_suppress_ancestor -- 084: a mid-title or note-only global tag never suppresses, under every scope) makes the EXPAND hydration skip + NOT-descend into any child carrying a global-never (e.g. wfy-suppress) tag -- without it, a globally-suppressed node ABSENT from the Phase-1 minimal tree (so Phase 2 never classified it) was silently re-grafted from the raw cache under an --expand ancestor (the Phase-3 hydration leak, fixed for persisted slices AND Lightning render_tags postfix_policy='slice'). Tested on the CHILD only, so the expand TARGET itself is exempt -- same construction as the completed seal. The result REPLACES the subtree so a slice-group GLIMPSE renders exactly what an F8'd live GLIMPSE of the same slice renders. Returns a NEW subtree (input not mutated).

PHASE 4 (RENDER-ONLY, cache-projected-slice ONLY) -- remove the collapsed contraction nodes that Phase 3 left behind as CHILDLESS ZOMBIE LEAVES. Phase 3 mirrors WF.collapseItem, which hides a node's descendants but leaves the node ITSELF present as a childless leaf; there is NO expand/contract DOM op that removes the node itself, so the live Workflowy GUI (and the live-DOM GLIMPSE / F8, which must match it) legitimately keeps these leaves. Phase 4 is the DELIBERATE, ISOLATED divergence: on the cache-projected render path ONLY (slice-group GLIMPSE + Apply-slice modal), it drops those leaves from the RENDER TREE so a slice that deprecated hundreds of leaves actually shrinks. Fed the UNIFIED contraction set plan['pending_collapse_ids'] (suppress_final | deprecated_final; topmost-only; root already discarded) -- it does NOT re-derive tags or re-stratify suppress vs deprecated (both are identical collapses). INVARIANT (asserted, fail-loud via SliceProjectionInvariantError): every contraction node PRESENT in the tree is childless; a present-and-has-children contraction node is an upstream logic error. A contraction UUID simply ABSENT from the tree (e.g. nested under another collapse target) is normal and skipped. NEVER runs on the raw root_uuid dump (which has no plan). Returns {subtree, pruned_zombie_count} (new tree; input untouched).

STAGE 1 (the base tree): the SHARED cache-projected slice funnel -- the ONE place the full STAGE-1 base-tree projection Phase 1 (build_slice_subtree_from_cache) -> Phase 2 (build_expansion_plan) -> Phase 3 (apply_expansion_plan_to_subtree) -> Phase 4 (prune_collapsed_leaf_zombies) lives (membership + expand/suppress/deprecated + completed-exclusion + anchor-boundary + global-never hydration seal + zombie prune). STAGE 2 (filter(since)+sort+render) runs LATER, in render_stage2_filter_sort; this function is purely STAGE 1. BOTH cache-projected consumers call it: the slice-group GLIMPSE (_glimpse_slice_group_from_cache) AND the Apply-slice docked modal (_handle_render_slice_modal) -- AND, under postfix_policy='slice', the Lightning Rod render_tags projectors (ap:IMPPTX) -- which previously hand-duplicated the identical three-call sequence and had to be kept in sync by hand -- so Phase 4 (and any future projection change) can NEVER diverge between GLIMPSE-slice and modal-slice by construction. boundary_predicate (Phase-C descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors', default None) threads the stop-at-child-anchors traversal into BOTH Phase 1 (admit-time boundary) AND Phase 3 (hydration boundary, the load-bearing seal against --expand re-inflating a pruned child anchor) via boundary_root_uuid=root_uuid, so the boundary holds across the whole funnel by construction. global_never_expand_tags threads into Phase 2 classification AND Phase 3 hydration (HYDSUP: a globally-suppressed node outside the Phase-1 minimal tree can no longer be re-grafted from raw cache under an --expand ancestor). Returns (final_subtree, plan, prune_meta); final_subtree is None iff Phase 1 found no such root (caller reports the cache-miss). prune_meta carries pruned_zombie_count for observability/warning rows. Deliberately NOT used by the raw root_uuid dump (member_all=True, no plan, no Phase 2/3/4). Raises SliceProjectionInvariantError up through Phase 4 on a broken upstream invariant so callers fail closed + loud.

Pure server-side F8 slice-policy core: Phase 1 (simplified search evaluator + minimal-subtree builder), Phase 0 (UUID-MEMBERSHIP-ONLY DOM-vs-cache validator -- every visible UUID must exist in cache; NO parent_id edge or name/note comparison, matching the proven docked-modal staleness contract; fail-closed only on a genuinely-missing UUID), and Phase 2 (suppression/ deprecated/expand plan builder). No WebSocket / no DOM / no broker; plain functions over plain dicts.

Canonicalize a cache-stored tag token by stripping presentational HTML-tag markup (<u></u>, <b>, <code>, ...; pattern mirrors whiten_text_for_header_compare) + de-whitening common HTML entities, BEFORE the leading-'#' strip. This is the DOM-vs-cache PARITY fix: the live F8 path harvests clean data-val tags, but the cache slice-group GLIMPSE path reads the raw /nodes-export name where a tag may arrive as #<u>nexus--skills</u>; without this, the garbage token fails the literal prefix match and Phase 1 silently evicts the (tag-agnostic) member + its ancestors. Feeds _strip_hash + extract_name_tags, so every membership/classify consumer is fixed in one place.

THE single shared middle-segment wildcard matcher: does '#'-stripped tag T match base prefix P as P [ '-<middle>' ] [ '--<postfix>' ]? Front is literal startsWith P; the middle (everything between P and any recognized trailing '--<postfix>') must be EMPTY or start with '-' (hyphen = required segment delimiter, Dan's ruling -- so comm-jim matches comm-jim / comm-jim-teams / comm-jim--deprecated but NOT comm-jimx). Recognized postfix is matched in the trailing '--<word>' region against the LIVE postfix set (POSTFIX_SEP + word). Returns {matched, matched_prefix, middle, postfix} -- postfix is '' for a bare/plain family variant. This is the ONE recognizer is_slice_member + classify_node_tags + the deprecated-exclusion all call, so F8 / Markdown modal / server-side slice GLIMPSE never drift. Accepts the right-boundary-at-whitespace divergence from Workflowy's boundaryless search as a documented, rare, accepted edge case.

THE single shared anchor-tag matcher: does '#'-stripped tag T match ONE base anchor tag B under the EXACT-base rule -- T == B (the bare base, attribute None) or T == B<SEP>w for ONE registered attribute word w in the UNION of the local/favorite/deprecated word lists (attribute local|favorite|deprecated; one tag per attribute, postfixes never stacked)? Deliberately EXACT (no middle segment), unlike slice_tag_variant_match, so an anchor tag is a specific identity marker that cannot bleed into a sibling (wfy-ns !-> wfy-nsx / wfy-ns-project). Returns {matched_base, postfix, attribute, is_local} or None. Word collision across two lists resolves deterministically local > favorite > deprecated; longest-word-first across the union so a suffix word never shadows. --deprecated is REPORTED (attribute='deprecated') but never confers Dock identity -- that ruling lives in classify_anchor_tags. Shares only POSTFIX_SEP with the slice matcher; the anchor attribute words are a separate semantic domain from slice --expand/--suppress/--deprecated.

Classify a node's NAME tags against the configured base anchor tags + the THREE attribute-word lists (local/favorite/deprecated), via the shared match_anchor_tag matcher. UNION semantics (I5): is_anchor True iff at least one PROPER family tag matched (bare base, --local or --favorite); is_local / is_favorite are the union of their attribute over ALL proper family tags across ALL bases (a bare base asserts NOTHING, so #wfy-ns + #wfy-ns--local IS local -- the historical global-form-dominates rule is SUPERSEDED); a --deprecated match NEVER confers Dock identity (I4) and is reported via has_deprecated / family_tags(proper=False) only. Also returns matched_base/matched_tag (the FIRST proper family tag in name order), matched_bases (distinct bases with a proper tag, first-occurrence order -- the dock.update families: detector's input) and family_tags (every family-form tag in name order with base/attribute/postfix/proper). This is the ONE classifier BOTH list_anchors (is_anchor AND NOT is_local) and build_anchor_boundary_predicate (is_anchor -- a favorite or local anchor still stops descent; a deprecated-only node does NOT) call, so anchor-hood + attributes can never drift between the enumeration and the GLIMPSE 'descendants' boundary. Empty base set -> not an anchor. Pure; no I/O.

Per-tag-FAMILY auto-expand postfix rule for add_to_anchor's tags= arg. Groups the union tag set by family (first hyphen-delimited segment); within each family, if NO tag already carries ANY recognized postfix (--expand/--suppress/--deprecated, detected via slice_tag_variant_match) it appends --expand to EVERY tag in that family; if ANY tag in the family already carries a postfix it leaves the WHOLE family untouched (don't-clobber rule). Families are processed INDEPENDENTLY. Pure/deterministic; no I/O. Applied only to a tree ROOT that has descendants (gating lives in the caller).

THE name-only tag reader: return the '#'-stripped tags in a node NAME's TRAILING tag region, via the ONE canonical authority nexus_map_codebase.split_name_and_tags (reached BY IMPORT, never copied -- Pin 1). This is what match_scope='name' means on every semantic tag-search surface (is_slice_member / node_is_curated_for_prefixes / build_tag_predicate / node_is_live_self / build_anchor_boundary_predicate / gather / classify_node_tags / name_has_global_never_tag): a tag is a tag only when it sits at the end of the name, exactly as the add/remove/rename_tag mutation core reads them. Contrast extract_name_tags (whitespace-token, ANYWHERE in the title) -- the pre-flip behaviour, kept only for the free-form search-string parser (parse_search_string_to_base_prefixes); suppression and the postfix classification read THIS reader (084). Lazy function-local import mirrors _resolve_split_name_and_tags (api_client_core): nexus_map_codebase imports nothing from workflowy_mcp, so there is no cycle; the import is cached after first success.

Normalize an agent-supplied slice-group tag list (comma-separated string OR list) into canonical '#'-stripped BASE prefixes for storage: strip a leading '#', trim, drop empties/internal-whitespace/embedded-'#', de-dupe (order-preserving), and COLLAPSE any '--<postfix>' variant (auto-expand/suppress/deprecated, the three LIVE postfixes) down to its base so foo--expand/foo--deprecated both become foo. Lenient by design (help the agent out); returns (bases, collapsed_info, dropped) for transparency. Postfix words are passed in (server reads them live from the client) so this never hardcodes policy.

The ONE get_slice_group_config REPLY parser for the policy operands (post-IMPPTX audit, Finding 5): given the live Direction-A reply, return {auto_expand, suppress, deprecated, global_never_expand} with DEFAULT_* fallbacks and the global-never list VALIDATED (must be a list of non-empty strings, else [] -- a malformed string is NEVER character-split into bogus single-letter stems). Consumed by EVERY Stage-0 originator that reads the live postfix config so the reply means ONE thing everywhere: _resolve_slice_group_config (the MCP-return helper), the _handle_render_slice_modal slice cell + Lightning render_tags 'slice' branch + render_symbols suppression read, _project_slice_base_tree_for_scoped_lightning, and the F8 expansion-plan handler. Transport stays per-originator (each keeps its own WS read + ghost-endpoint handling); the INTERPRETATION of the reply is unified here. Pure; no I/O.

THE server-side parser for the slice-group NAME grammar (pipe-delimited category path + optional trailing [n] order index on the last segment; a LEADING [n] marks a category/expander row). Bug-for-bug port of the client's parseSliceGroupName in glimpse-cache-client.js (the display authority) so server-side handle resolution and the agent-facing public view interpret a stored name EXACTLY the way the widget displays it: same expander quirk (the expander branch does NOT strip a trailing [n] from its last segment), same empty-segment survival ('nexus|' -> ['nexus','']), same literal treatment of an unparseable bracket ('[foo]nexus' is just a name). Derives short_name (the final segment; for a LEAF its trailing [n] index is stripped) -- the semantic name accepted as a group_handle form and shown in compact displays. Pure; no I/O. If the grammar ever changes, BOTH runtimes must change together (locked by tests/test_parse_slice_group_name.py).

THE server-side Python twin of the client's buildNestedDisplayItems(..., expandAll=true) nested display builder (glimpse-cache-client.js) -- the exact tree/flatten policy behind the compact slice_group.list inventory. Faithful to the GUI grammar, not a resort-by-path: (1) every stored name is parsed through the ONE parse_slice_group_name grammar; (2) missing intermediate category paths are AUTO-VIVIFIED as synthetic category nodes; (3) a leaf attaches to the category node of ALL BUT its final segment; (4) a leading-[n] record is an explicit expander definition for its category path; (5) when several expander definitions target one path, the lowest-indexed definition is canonical and owns the descendants; the rest render as empty duplicate rows; (6) leaves and categories intermix per level, sorted by (order index, nulls last; case-insensitive display name) -- negative indices and gaps are valid; (7) every category is expanded (the server keeps no persisted collapse state). Returns a flat list of {kind:'leaf'|'expander', name, depth, group, duplicate, synthetic} rows in display order. Pure; no I/O. If the GUI builder ever changes, BOTH runtimes must change together.

Parse a FREE-FORM Workflowy search string (manual-F8 override) into canonical '#'-stripped BASE slice prefixes. Harvests only '#'-tag tokens via extract_name_tags (so a leading '-' negation, the '>' subtree-order operator, parentheses, the 'OR' keyword, and any raw prose are ignored -- a '-#foo' token starts with '-' not '#', so it is naturally dropped), then runs them through normalize_slice_group_tags to strip any trailing '--<postfix>' (auto-expand/suppress/deprecated, read live from options) down to the base and de-dupe. Deliberately simple: covers both a hand-pasted plain '#a OR #b' search AND an advanced curated search; anything that is not a legal '#'-tag is discarded. Postfix words are passed in (single source of truth).
Literal startsWith prefix test on a '#'-stripped tag against a list of '#'-stripped active prefixes — byte-for-byte mirror of JS tagTokenMatchesExpandPrefix so server and client never drift.

THE single membership predicate (per-prefix OR). A node is in the slice iff SOME active prefix P matches one of its tags AND no tag matches P--deprecated. Per-prefix scoping mirrors Workflowy's negation-binds-to-preceding-tag semantics (#P -#P--deprecated OR ...), so deprecating ONE tag does not evict a node still live via another. match_scope (SELECTION-stage scope knob) picks WHERE tags are read: 'name_and_note' (default) -> extract_node_tags (Workflowy-search parity, note counts); 'name' -> _core_trailing_name_tags (the NAME's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter nexus_map_codebase.split_name_and_tags -- a mid-title prose '#tag' or a note-only '#tag' does NOT count; the accepted divergence from a pasted Workflowy search, which has no title-only mode). match_scope is ORTHOGONAL to the --deprecated OPERATION semantics (unchanged). Shared by Phase 1 membership, the compiled search string, and Phase 2's live-hit rescue so the three can never drift.

Form-B (GLIMPSE since='curated') CURATION predicate. True iff the node carries ANY tag that matches an active slice prefix under the SHARED middle-segment matcher (slice_tag_variant_match), read under the SAME match_scope SELECTION-stage scope knob is_slice_member uses ('name' -> _core_trailing_name_tags (the NAME's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter), so neither a mid-title prose family tag nor a family tag living only in a note body curates and neither can move the cursor; 'name_and_note' default -> extract_node_tags(NAME or NOTE, Workflowy-search parity) -- the scope plumbing the server render callers thread into the since='curated' pivot, fixing the Session-019 misread where prose quoting a literal #curated in a note (ap:SP9EY1) advanced a match_scope='name' cursor past every earlier uncurated capture) -- INCLUDING the --deprecated postfix AND middle-segment variants (comm-jim-teams--deprecated curates the comm-jim slice), because a --deprecated tag is ITSELF a curation act (the user tagged it, then triaged it; they must NOT re-see it in the uncurated tail). EXCLUDING the --suppress / --expand postfix variants: those are PRESENTATION (a lens carve-out / auto-expansion -- e.g. a nested program Dock root tagged #curated--suppress to keep its subtree out of a tail), NOT a triage decision; counting them let a suppressed Dock root become the newest 'curated' node and advance the high-water mark past everything captured before it (Session-019 curated-cursor bug). Still DELIBERATELY looser than is_slice_member on the DEPRECATED axis (a node deprecated on every prefix is NOT a member but IS curated), but IDENTICAL on the FAMILY-BOUNDARY axis: it uses the same hyphen-delimited matcher, so comm-jimx does NOT curate the comm-jim slice (a different family). Using the shared matcher (not the loose tag_matches_prefix) keeps the family boundary consistent with membership/classification everywhere.

Scan the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid for the DEPRECATED MIDDLE-SEGMENT variant tags of each active prefix (via the shared slice_tag_variant_match), returning {prefix: [dep_variant_tag, ...]}. Feeds compile_slice_search_expression so the wildcard-less Workflowy search can enumerate each P<middle>--deprecated as its own negation -- the server discovers them; the compiler lists them. Pure over the cache; empty map when cache unavailable. NOT needed by the server-side FILTER (is_slice_member reasons over the cache directly) -- this exists ONLY to make the live-GUI-sync search string reproduce the same member set.

Classify ONE node's NAME tags against the active slice config -> flags has_active / has_auto / has_suppress / has_deprecated / has_global_never_expand. The atomic per-node primitive feeding membership (Phase 1) and the plan (Phase 2). match_scope (keyword, default 'name_and_note') governs WHERE the family-postfix flags read: under 'name' (the 084 ruling) they read ONLY the name's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter -- a mid-title or note-authored --expand/--suppress/--deprecated is prose, not an operation; under 'name_and_note' they read name+note (Workflowy-search parity, the prior behavior). The global-never flag is TRAILING-REGION-ONLY under EVERY scope (Dan's 084 D1: an absolute structural control must be a deliberate trailing tag) via the ONE shared helper pair (normalize_global_never_stems + name_has_global_never_tag).

Build the STOP-RECURSION boundary predicate for the anchor-points projection: a pure (node)->bool that is True iff the node is an anchor (its NAME trailing-tag region carries any configured base anchor tag -- bare, or with ONE registered attribute word: local OR favorite). Routes through the shared classify_anchor_tags matcher on is_anchor -- so a LOCAL anchor (#wfy-ns--local) and a FAVORITE anchor (#wfy-ns--fav) STILL bound a 'descendants' GLIMPSE exactly like a bare-base one (I10: favorite has no bearing on descent; locality only hides an anchor from list_anchors, never from the recursion boundary). A --deprecated-ONLY node is NOT an anchor (I4) and therefore does NOT bound. Reads the NAME's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter (_core_trailing_name_tags -> nexus_map_codebase.split_name_and_tags), the SAME reader _anchor_dock_root_guard / list_note_sessions / the anchor tooling use, so 'what is an anchor' cannot drift between this traversal boundary, the enumeration, and the anchor tooling (and a mid-title prose '#wfy-ns' is NOT a boundary). Anchor tags are matched EXACTLY (no wildcard middle -- wfy-ns !-> wfy-nsx), unlike slice prefixes. Passed as build_selected_subtree_from_cache(boundary_predicate=...) so a raw-root / lightning projection stops descending at child anchors while still emitting the child-anchor node itself as a visible leaf signpost. Empty/blank anchor-tag list -> a predicate that is always False (no boundaries). Pure; no I/O.

THE generic Stage-1 SELECTION primitive: walk the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, admit a node iff member_predicate(node) is True, and build the minimal connective subtree (every admitted node + all ancestors up to and including root_uuid, children priority-ordered). Returns a nested {id,name,note,children} root, or None if root_uuid is absent from the cache. Every cache-sourced selection source converges here by supplying its own admit predicate over ONE tree-walk machinery: slice groups (the is_slice_member closure, via the build_slice_subtree_from_cache wrapper), the raw-dump root GLIMPSE (member_all -> lambda node: True), and Lightning Rod tag/text-search predicates. Two orthogonal TRAVERSAL policies ride alongside the membership predicate: exclude_completed prunes a completed CHILD at admit time (its whole subtree becomes invisible; no downstream --expand can un-hide it), and boundary_predicate is a stop-recursion boundary (a child satisfying it is still visited/admitted and anchors the connective spine, but the walk does not descend into it -- it renders as a leaf). Both policies exempt the root by construction (each is tested only when deciding whether to descend into a CHILD). A THIRD traversal policy, max_depth (ap:EPR86W part a; the spec's recursive=false maps to 1): the walk descends only while the CURRENT node's depth < max_depth (root = depth 0), so max_depth=1 renders the root + its DIRECT children and nothing deeper -- child Docks and plain nodes alike; descend_policy is moot under the cap (the cap stops the descent first). The same gate stops the materialize recursion, so a capped node is childless in the output by construction. None (the default) is the ordinary unbounded walk -- byte-for-byte prior behavior; only the raw-root surfaces thread the cap (a membership selection is unbounded by construction and refuses recursive=false loudly at the spec normalizer).

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD (ap:LRSCOPE) — the SECOND selection substrate. The forest-walking SIBLING of build_selected_subtree_from_cache: same admit-by-member_predicate + minimal-connective-subtree + optional stop-recursion boundary contract and the SAME {id,name,note,children} output shape, but it iterates a PROVIDED in-memory forest (the frozen-DOM captured tree) instead of walking the /nodes-export cache from a root. Reuses the SINGULAR predicates (build_tag_predicate / build_search_predicate) verbatim — predicates are substrate-agnostic (node)->bool, so there is NO predicate duplication. It is a PURE SELECTION SUBSTRATE (forest in -> pruned forest out, feeding the ONE shared composer via _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture); it grows NO predicates / sort / composer of its own — the moment it did, the pipeline would fork. Dan ACCEPTED this dual walk as legitimate architecture (it mirrors the already-blessed cache_render_spec vs dom_captured_tree source axis), NOT a crack.

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD (ap:LRSCOPE) gather-over-forest — the in-memory-forest sibling of gather_tags_in_subtree. Unions every REAL '#'-stripped tag (STRICT recognizer, same as the cache gather) found in a PROVIDED captured-DOM forest, honoring match_scope (name-only vs name+note). Returns the sorted, de-duped '#'-less list. Pure/read-only; used by the DOM-frozen Scoped gather mode so a gather->render_tags handoff surveys the SAME on-screen forest the subsequent render filters (not the whole cache root).

render-symbols CONNECTIVE ROOT: compute the lowest common ancestor of a set of root_uuids by intersecting their root-first ancestor chains and taking the DEEPEST (last) shared id. For a SINGLE root the LCA is that root itself (degenerate -- 'begins at the root_uuid'). Returns None if the roots share no common ancestor (disjoint trees) or any is uncached. This is the connective spine fed to build_selected_subtree_from_cache; the descendant-of-any-root gate (not the LCA) is the real membership filter, so a wider LCA never widens what actually renders.

GLOBAL-NEVER-EXPAND doctrine (Dan, 2026-07, post-IMPPTX audit; tightened 2026-10 by the 084 ruling): the ONE shared stem-normalizer + NAME matcher for the f8_global_never_expand_tags operand. DOCTRINE: global-never suppression reads ONLY the name's TRAILING tag region, under EVERY scope -- it is an ABSOLUTE STRUCTURAL control ('never render this subtree'), so it must be a deliberate, visible TRAILING NAME tag; a tag buried in a NOTE body, or wedged mid-title among prose, never suppresses. (Exact match also gives the user the clean off-switch: rename #wfy-suppress -> #wfy-suppress-old to release while keeping the stem available to re-apply.) normalize_global_never_stems ('#'-optional, whitespace-trimmed, empties dropped) + name_has_global_never_tag (EXACT tag==stem, NOT family/prefix, via _core_trailing_name_tags) are consumed by EVERY reader of the operand so the config field means ONE thing across the whole system: Phase-2 classify_node_tags (has_global_never_expand), render_symbols absolute suppression (node_has_suppress_ancestor), the render_symbols per-item expand sweep (collect_subtree_ids), the merge coverage walks (compute_merge_full_cover / compute_merge_tag_plan), and the HYDSUP Phase-3 hydration seal (apply_expansion_plan_to_subtree). Pure; no I/O.

THE ONE global-never NAME test: True iff the name's TRAILING tag region (via _core_trailing_name_tags, the core splitter) carries an EXACT-match global-never stem -- never a note body, never a mid-title prose mention, under EVERY match_scope (Dan's 084 D1). Change the reading HERE and every consumer (classify_node_tags, node_has_suppress_ancestor, collect_subtree_ids, the HYDSUP hydration seal, the merge coverage walks, _unpersistable_global_never_leaves) follows; never re-implement the test at a call site.

render_symbols PER-ITEM EXPAND sweep (ap:EXPSWP; D1 member-set sweep, NOT the rejected Phase-3 plan hijack): collect the id of EVERY DESCENDANT of each id in root_ids into ONE set, so a caller-flagged node's whole cache subtree joins the Stage-1 member set exactly 'as though those descendants had been passed in the list'. The SEED ids themselves are NOT included -- the caller unions with its explicit resolved set, which already holds them. SUPPRESSION GUARD: before descending into a child, its name's TRAILING tag region (name_has_global_never_tag, the core splitter) is EXACT-matched against suppress_tags, mirroring node_has_suppress_ancestor's trailing-region exact-match semantics (NOT family/prefix; 084: a mid-title or note-only global tag never suppresses) -- a matching child is neither included nor descended into, so render_symbols' ABSOLUTE suppression doctrine is preserved at sweep time (the seeds are guaranteed non-suppressed by the upstream resolution gate). Does NOT filter completed nodes -- Phase 1 owns completed exclusion at admit time (the sweep adds them harmlessly; collect() never materializes them). Boundary-free by design: a flagged node's subtree is swept fully, child anchors included (the selection is an explicit agent request; descend_policy stays rejected for render_symbols). Pure, no I/O; sibling of _ancestor_chain_ids / is_descendant_of_any_root / compute_lca_from_cache.

LIGHTNING ROD gather-tags: union of all REAL '#'-stripped tags found under root_uuid in the /nodes-export cache, sorted + de-duped. match_scope (SELECTION-stage scope knob) picks WHERE tags are harvested: 'name_and_note' (default) -> name AND note (strict recognizer); 'name' -> the NAME's TRAILING tag region via the core splitter (_core_trailing_name_tags; a mid-title prose '#tag' or a note-only '#tag' is not gathered) -- matched to the two render modes so a gather->render_tags handoff surveys exactly the fields the render will filter on. boundary_predicate (Phase-C descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors', default None) is a STOP-RECURSION traversal knob: when a descendant satisfies it (a child anchor), that node's OWN tags are still harvested (visible signpost) but its subtree is NOT surveyed -- so gather and a subsequent render_tags see the SAME bounded universe (root exempt). Uses the STRICT extract_strict_tags_from_text recognizer (NOT the generalized Workflowy-search harvester) so it does NOT return junk harvested from '#' glued inside prose/code (').strip()', 'f8-expand),', etc.). Lightning Rod is unmoored/divergent-from-Workflowy, so gather is free to be smarter about what counts as a genuine tag. Pure, no rendering, no pipeline -- the discovery call whose result feeds a follow-up Lightning Rod render_tags.

LIGHTNING ROD gather SERIALIZER -- the tag-domain peer of the node-tree composer. Turns a flat, sorted tag list (from gather_tags_in_subtree) into a prefix-grouped, hyphen-segment-nested RAW TEXT outline (4 spaces per level, alphabetical within a level). This is the intentional serialization seam for gather: gather produces a TAG SET (not a node tree), so its correct serializer is THIS pure function, NOT the node-tree render tail render_stage2_filter_sort (which would need a fake tree). The shared universal contract is 'one final rendered string', re-unified at the delivery boundary, not at the tree renderer. HYPHEN RULE (Dan): a run of >=1 hyphens collapses to a SINGLE separator, then split -- so double-hyphen postfixes (--deprecated/--suppress/--expand) are NOT special-cased and just become an ordinary trailing segment. SYNTHESIZED PARENTS: an intermediate segment path that is not itself a literal gathered tag still gets an outline header line for readability; those synthetic headers appear ONLY in this text, never in the caller's literal `tags` array. Pure / no I/O -- the tag-set analog of _build_markdown_preview_from_tree.

SLICE-GROUP wrapper over the generic build_selected_subtree_from_cache: it supplies the slice-group admit predicate so the generic primitive does the tree walk. member_all=True -> lambda node: True (the raw-dump: every descendant is a member); otherwise -> the is_slice_member closure (per-prefix membership, deprecated-excluding, NAME-only or NAME+NOTE per match_scope). exclude_completed, boundary_predicate and max_depth (ap:EPR86W part a: the raw-dump recursive=false depth cap; a membership projection is unbounded by construction) thread straight through to the generic primitive's traversal policies. Callers: the slice-group GLIMPSE, the Apply-slice modal, and (via member_all) the raw-dump root GLIMPSE.

PHASE 0 (DOM path) — UUID-MEMBERSHIP-ONLY validation that the browser's visible subtree is known to the /nodes-export cache: every DOM uuid must EXIST in cache. Deliberately NO parent->child edge (parent_id) comparison and NO node-content (name/note) comparison — exactly the proven docked-modal staleness contract (_modal_staleness), which dropped both as unwinnable/overzealous (parent_id boundary+normalization mismatches at the zoom root / virtual nodes produced constant false 'cache_stale'). Fail-closed only on a genuinely-missing UUID (F8 must not act on a node the server doesn't know); a present UUID is sufficient. The inverse direction (cache nodes not in the DOM) is NOT staleness (the DOM is visible-only).

DIAGNOSTIC ONLY (not a gate) — compare the visible DOM subtree's parent->child edges against the /nodes-export cache parent_id and return RICH per-row mismatch detail (node id+name, dom_parent id+name, cache_parent id+name). Purpose: empirically find WHY the old strict edge check tripped (search-mode serialization vs canonical tree) rather than theorize. Returns {missing:[...], edge_mismatches:[...], checked:int, root_id, root_name}. Never raises; never fails the plan.

PHASE 2 (the heart) — given a VALID Phase-1 subtree + active slice config, compute the expansion plan {collapse_suppressed, collapse_deprecated, expand}. Annotates each node, applies the "don't collapse a deprecated node through a live in-slice descendant" rescue rule, normalizes each set topmost-only, and resolves cross-set conflicts via the ASYMMETRIC merge: a contraction dominates a nested expansion, but an expansion does NOT dominate a nested contraction -- so a suppress/deprecated pocket can survive inside an --expand region. BOTH Phase 3 (server) and the JS client executeF8ExpansionPlan execute the plan EXPAND FIRST, THEN collapse_suppressed, THEN collapse_deprecated -- expanding first so a nested contraction is not overwritten by a later re-hydration. Also emits the Tier-2 pending_* live-GUI-sync metadata + the deprecated-body-suppression body_suppressed_ids set (surviving --deprecated nodes render header-only). match_scope (default name_and_note) threads the SELECTION-stage scope into THREE questions: the rescue's liveness membership (compute_live's is_slice_member; post-Sol-audit Finding 2), the promotion pass's ACTIVE-self check (node_is_live_self title-harvests under 'name'), AND -- 084 ruling -- the --expand/--suppress/--deprecated OPERATION classification itself (annotate passes it into classify_node_tags: under 'name' a family postfix counts only in the name's TRAILING tag region; under 'name_and_note' it also counts in the note). The global-never tag is TRAILING-only under every scope (name_has_global_never_tag).

PHASE 3 (no-DOM path) -- apply a Phase-2 expansion plan to the Phase-1 membership subtree IN MEMORY, emulating the browser's executeF8ExpansionPlan against the live DOM. Mandated order EXPAND FIRST, THEN COLLAPSE: (1) expand, (2) collapse_suppressed, (3) collapse_deprecated -- expanding first so a contraction nested inside an expanded region survives (collapse-first would let the expansion re-hydrate and overwrite the nested collapse). COLLAPSE (both sets, identical effect once a UUID is in hand) = drop every descendant of the target node from the subtree (node stays as a childless leaf), mirroring WF.collapseItem. EXPAND = re-hydrate the target node's FULL descendant subtree from the /nodes-export cache (priority-ordered, INCLUDING non-members -- exactly as opening a bullet in the GUI reveals every child regardless of tags), mirroring the recursive WF.expandItem. LOAD-BEARING BOUNDARY SEAL: boundary_predicate + boundary_root_uuid (default None) make the EXPAND hydration honor the SAME stop-at-child-anchors boundary Phase 1 used -- without it, an --expand ancestor of a child anchor would silently re-inflate from the raw cache the very subtree Phase 1 pruned (Phase 1 stopping is not enough because hydration reads raw cache). A child-anchor node hydrates as a childless leaf; boundary_root_uuid exempts the projection root so expanding AT a boundary still reveals its immediate children.
