Duration-unit -> seconds table for the Form-A `since` window token grammar (s|m|h|d|w). Single source of truth now that the transform lives in the pure glimpse_since_policy module; server.py re-exports it for back-compat.

THE opaque `since` handle: a normalized, immutable membership-filter request carrying its OWN timestamp axis (created|modified) + direction (asc|desc), so the date-form pivots (window / curated) measure branch-dates against the axis the SINCE object names rather than borrowing the PRESENTATION sort. form is 'window'|'item_count'|'curated'; window_seconds is set for a window, count for item_count, both None for curated. axis/direction default to created/asc and are INERT for form=='item_count' (a pure tail-count over the forest's current order has no date pivot). item_count also carries selection ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a)): 'newest' keeps the N newest leaves by the recency basis (resolve_item_count_basis over recent_by/sort_by), 'bottom' keeps the positional tail of the current order; the FIELD default is 'bottom' (the legacy positional meaning, so a hand-built / old-wire item_count spec behaves exactly as before), and the token codec sets 'newest' for 'last N'/'newest N' and 'bottom' for 'bottom N' (since_from_wire defaults an object without the key to 'bottom' -- wire back-compat). A raw human/API token string is parsed ONLY at the edge by since_from_edge, which delegates to SinceCodec.from_token; interior code carries SinceSpec or None only. since_to_wire serializes SinceSpec to an object dict or None; since_from_wire reads that object dict back and rejects strings. Display token text is produced only by SinceCodec.to_token.

THE chronological-render predicate (U6, ap:E03BN3 -- Dan's ruling 'any chronological sort of any form => never display ancestor notes'): True iff a render is CHRONOLOGICAL -- a resolved presentation sort_by of 'created' or 'modified' (EITHER direction) OR ANY since (window / curated / item_count). An item-count since ALONE counts since CF-13 = Option A (Dan's ruling 2026-09-22, relayed Manager-Session-033; supersedes U6 ap:UXYCID §2 invariant 6 + §9 tests 3/10) -- under [ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a) of EITHER selection: 'last N'/'newest N' is now the genuine newest-N recency cut, and the positional 'bottom N' (also the legacy-blob reading) keeps CF-13's tail behavior; both withhold ancestor notes exactly like the date forms while their excerpt order STAYS document order unless the caller sorts (the predicate classifies NOTE PRESENTATION only, never ordering). Callers evaluate it on the RESOLVED sort_by (after slice-group default inheritance; None/'none' = document order) and on the SinceSpec actually handed to Stage-2 prep. THE single definition of 'chronological' every materializer-fed render surface consults to decide ancestor-note body suppression (the third RenderPolicy cause, occurrence-keyed, computed ONLY inside materialize_from_document_forest). Direction is deliberately NOT a parameter: created OR modified, asc OR desc -- one rule, no created/modified distinction.

THE Python since token codec. Owns the human/API token grammar only: SinceCodec.from_token parses tokens like '1w' / 'last 10' / 'curated' into SinceSpec, and SinceCodec.to_token renders a SinceSpec as the canonical display token. It does NOT read or write the interior wire shape; wire paths use since_from_wire / since_to_wire.

EDGE-ONLY Python ingester for public/human/API input. Accepts only the public edge shape (a token string or None), delegates token parsing to SinceCodec.from_token, and returns SinceSpec|None. Interior wire/blob/render-spec paths must call since_from_wire instead, which rejects strings.

Strict interior wire reader for `since`. Accepts None, SinceSpec, or an object dict and returns SinceSpec|None. A string on this path is invalid and is rejected rather than parsed; public token strings belong only to since_from_edge / SinceCodec.from_token.

INTERIOR Py wire writer for `since`. Serializes SinceSpec|None to object-dict-or-None only; it never emits a token string. Human-readable token strings belong solely to SinceCodec.to_token for display.

Parse a Form-A `since` window token (<number><unit? s|m|h|d|w>; a BARE number means DAYS) into SECONDS. Case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant. Returns None for a blank / malformed / non-positive token (caller raises). THE single token grammar for every GLIMPSE `since` path; moved into the pure module so server + client agree.

Parse a Form-C `since` ITEM-COUNT token: 'last N' / its synonym 'newest N' / the positional 'bottom N' (optionally '... N item[s]'), N a positive integer. Case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant. Returns the integer N, or None when the token is not an item-count token at all (so the caller can fall through to the Form-A window grammar) OR is a malformed 'last ...' (N missing / non-integer / <= 0) -- the caller distinguishes 'not mine' from 'mine but bad' by first checking is_item_count_token. WHAT the N selects is decided by the FIRST keyword via _ITEM_COUNT_SELECTION_BY_KEYWORD (last/newest -> the newest N, [ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a); bottom -> the positional tail); this function owns only the count. THE single item-count grammar for every GLIMPSE `since` path; the readable 'last 10' spelling was chosen over a '10i' pseudo-unit so it never collides with the bare-number=days Form-A rule.

Cheap prefix classifier: does this `since` token START the item-count family ('last ...' | 'newest ...' | 'bottom ...')? Lets callers ROUTE a token to the item-count grammar (parse_since_item_count) vs the window grammar (parse_since_window) BEFORE parsing, so a malformed 'last banana' is reported as a bad item-count rather than silently falling through to the window parser. Pure; no I/O.

Shared DFS that decomposes a node forest into its root->leaf BRANCHES, each a list of (uuid, node) from a top-level node down to a leaf (a node with no dict children). This is the ONE branch-collection walk reused by reorder_tree_by_timestamp, prune_tree_since, compute_since_window_pivot, AND prune_tree_to_last_leaf_count -- the definition of 'leaf' (no VISIBLE/dict children; hidden descendants are absent from the final forest) is therefore single-sourced, which is exactly what makes item-count's 'count only leaves' rule fall out for free. Preserves DFS/document order of leaves. Pure; inputs never mutated.

Shared prune-rebuild: given a forest and a set of KEPT leaf node object ids (id(node)), rebuild a NEW forest keeping only root->leaf paths that terminate in a kept leaf (connective ancestors preserved; dead branches dropped). Returns shadow dicts (inputs never mutated). Reused by prune_tree_since AND prune_tree_to_last_leaf_count so the 'keep the paths to these surviving leaves' mechanic is single-sourced; the two differ ONLY in HOW they choose the kept-leaf set (date-vs-pivot vs the last-N-in-order).

THE ONE node-limit cap for the search verbs' headings tier ([ap:O3MDOY] half 2, unit 5e): slice_group.sift / lightning_rod.render_search with max_nodes truncate the FINAL render forest (after the sort and the since prune, so selection -> order -> cap compose in that order, mirroring the grep tier) to the first max_nodes MATCHING nodes in display order, counted through the caller's member predicate (the lens's sift predicate / the search predicate); connective ancestors never consume budget and survive only while a kept descendant does. Not a since form and not a ranking: a positional display cap beside the prune family -- the count-and-stop mechanic mirrors prune_tree_to_last_leaf_count's positional tail at the node level. Returns (new_forest, echo|None); echo is None when nothing was hidden (the whole forest fit), so callers stay byte-identical otherwise. Pure; inputs never mutated.

THE single branch-date rule shared by the timestamp SORT (reorder_tree_by_timestamp) and every GLIMPSE `since` pivot (window + curation cursor). Given a root->leaf branch as a list of (uuid, node) and sort_by ('created' | 'modified'), returns the branch's comparison timestamp: created = the LEAF's own createdAt; modified = max(modifiedAt) over EVERY node on the branch. None when unavailable (uuid absent from cache / no int value), matching the sort's missing-key-sinks-last handling. Factored into the pure module so the sort and the `since` filter can NEVER drift on a branch's date; WorkFlowyClientNexus._branch_timestamp_key_static delegates here.

SHARED timestamp-sort pre-pass for the Markdown modal AND as_markdown GLIMPSE (and the `since` prune's re-merge). Reorders a visible node forest by leaf createdAt (created) or branch-max modifiedAt (modified), then trie-merges the sorted root->leaf branches so a shared ancestor straddled by an out-of-cluster branch RE-EMITS its file leader/breadcrumb. sort_by=None is identity passthrough. Returns a NEW shadow tree (inputs never mutated); every leaf keeps its FULL ancestor path so the composer's regime-threading + per-file H1 rebase + md-in-md all stay correct by construction. Keys join the /nodes-export cache by UUID (DOM payload has no timestamps); a UUID absent from the cache sinks last. Branch-date rule delegated to branch_timestamp_key so the SORT and the `since` pivot share ONE definition. WorkFlowyClientNexus._reorder_tree_by_timestamp delegates here.

GLIMPSE `since` Form-A (time-window) PIVOT. Data-relative leading edge: pivot = the branch-date of the MOST RECENT leaf branch in the ALREADY-FINAL forest (ascending) MINUS the window -- so 'last 1 week' on data whose newest branch is 2 years old means the week ENDING at that 2-year-old edge, NOT wall-clock now. Descending flips to the OLDEST edge PLUS the window (the commensurate corner). Uses the SHARED branch_timestamp_key so the branch-date matches the sort's. Returns None if no branch has a resolvable date (caller then returns the tree unfiltered). Both the server and client `since` paths reach this through apply_since_to_forest.

GLIMPSE `since` PRUNE -- the shared leaf-branch filter run LAST (after Phase1/2/3 AND after the timestamp reorder), on the already-final sorted forest. Decomposes the forest into root->leaf branches (same DFS the sort uses), keeps a branch iff its branch-date (via the SHARED branch_timestamp_key) is beyond the pivot: ascending -> STRICTLY GREATER than pivot (most-recent tail; pivot node excluded); descending -> STRICTLY LESS (the commensurate 'oldest tail'). A branch with no resolvable date is DROPPED. Then re-merges surviving branches via reorder_tree_by_timestamp so straddled ancestors re-emit exactly as in the unfiltered render. Returns a NEW forest (inputs untouched); [] when nothing survives; the input unchanged when no prune applies. Shared by the server (_prune_tree_since delegates here) and, historically, a client twin (_prune_forest_since) that has since been DELETED -- the client now reaches `since` only through apply_since_to_forest.

GLIMPSE `since="curated"` FORM-B PIVOT (the self-maintaining curation cursor). Walks the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, finds every CURATED node (curated_predicate(name, note) True -- the caller injects f8_slice_policy.node_is_curated_for_prefixes, deliberately looser than slice MEMBERSHIP on the triage axis: --deprecated variants still count, because deprecating a tag is itself a curation act; the --suppress/--expand PRESENTATION variants do NOT count and never move the mark -- Session-019 curated-cursor fix), computes each curated node's branch-date via the SHARED branch_timestamp_key over its root->leaf cache path, and returns the MAX (ascending; MIN descending) = the high-water mark. Returns None when NOTHING under root is curated (whole subtree is the uncurated tail). curated_predicate is passed IN (not imported) so this module needs no f8_slice_policy dependency -> zero import-cycle risk; the walk itself is postfix-agnostic -- the curation semantics live entirely in the injected predicate. server._compute_curated_high_water_mark delegates here.

GLIMPSE `since` FORM-C POSITIONAL prune ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a): the selection spelled 'bottom N', and the legacy meaning of every old wire blob) -- the ITEM-COUNT tail filter over the forest's CURRENT order. Runs LAST, exactly like the date prune, on the already-final (optionally sorted) forest, but is orthogonal to the sort: 'the bottom N' is defined purely by the forest's CURRENT leaf order (the new 'newest N' SELECTION lives beside it in prune_tree_to_newest_leaf_count). Counts LEAVES only (a node with no dict children in the final forest; hidden descendants are already absent) via the SHARED collect_leaf_branches, keeps the LAST N leaf branches in that order (the tail: most-recent under an ascending chronological sort, earliest under descending, last-in-document-order when unsorted), and rebuilds via the SHARED _rebuild_forest_from_kept_leaves. When N >= leaf count the whole forest is returned unchanged (by identity of the kept set). Does NOT re-sort/re-merge -- the input order IS the truth (first pass: no nestedness weighting; a subtree with K leaves consumes K of the count). Returns a NEW forest; [] only if the forest has no leaves at all. Pure; inputs never mutated.

[ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a) THE ONE recency-basis resolution for an item-count 'newest' selection: recent_by when the caller supplied one, else the PRESENTATION sort_by axis when it is a timestamp (so 'last 10 by modified' selects on the same axis it displays), else 'modified' (current attention -- dock.peek's default basis, the same rule). Pure; the ONE definition every caller (apply_since_to_forest and any direct prune_tree_to_newest_leaf_count caller) shares so the selection basis can never drift from the describe rule.

[ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a) the 'newest N' SELECTION prune (beside prune_tree_to_last_leaf_count, never instead of it): keeps the N NEWEST leaf branches by branch_timestamp_key on the resolved recency basis (the SAME branch-date rule the sort and the date pivots share, so selection and sort can never disagree on a branch's date), whatever the presentation sort direction -- sort_direction only orders, never chooses (Dan's ruling). Ranking is newest-first with ties keeping document order; a branch with no resolvable timestamp ranks AFTER every dated branch (and is selected only when N exceeds the dated count), mirroring dock.peek's missing-timestamps-sink-last rule. Rebuilds via the SHARED _rebuild_forest_from_kept_leaves so the SURVIVORS keep the forest's CURRENT order (selection never reorders; display order stays with the caller's sort). When N >= leaf count the whole forest is returned unchanged; counts LEAVES only via the SHARED collect_leaf_branches. Pure; inputs never mutated.

THE single classifier for a `since` token's FORM + PRECONDITIONS, consulted by BOTH the cheap upstream fail-fast guard (glimpse() dispatcher + the modal handlers' early reject) AND the final apply_since_to_forest application, so the rule set (which form, does it need an axis, does it require a slice group, is the token malformed) lives in ONE place and the two layers only differ in WHEN they consult it and WHICH dispatch facts they supply (only the dispatcher knows 'is a slice_group present?'). Returns {form, requires_axis, requires_slice_group, error}. requires_axis (renamed from the former requires_sort in the since<->sort DECOUPLE) means 'this form's pivot is a branch-DATE so it needs a timestamp AXIS' -- and the axis is ALWAYS supplied by the SinceSpec object (default created/asc), so it is satisfied-by-construction and callers no longer reject a date-form since for lacking a presentation sort (that was Seam B). form is 'item_count'|'window'|'curated'|None (None => no `since`). error is a human string for a MALFORMED token (bad 'last N' / bad window); the axis/slice-group PRECONDITIONS are reported as booleans (the caller combines requires_slice_group with the facts it owns to decide whether to reject; requires_axis needs no rejection anymore). Pure; no I/O; adding a new `since` value = one edit here + its prune in apply_since_to_forest, and the upstream guards inherit the new preconditions for free.

Object-only `since` orchestrator: given an already-final forest + SinceSpec|None, it reads the object's form/axis/direction/count/window_seconds/selection fields, computes the pivot when needed, runs the matching prune, and builds the since_applied echo. recent_by (optional, [ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a)) is the caller's explicit recency basis for a 'newest' item_count selection -- resolve_item_count_basis resolves it against the presentation sort. Token grammar is edge-only and is not visible here. Pure; no I/O (curated pivot is injected, not computed here).

Duration-unit -> seconds table for the Form-A `since` window token grammar (s|m|h|d|w). Single source of truth now that the transform lives in the pure glimpse_since_policy module; server.py re-exports it for back-compat.

THE opaque `since` handle: a normalized, immutable membership-filter request carrying its OWN timestamp axis (created|modified) + direction (asc|desc), so the date-form pivots (window / curated) measure branch-dates against the axis the SINCE object names rather than borrowing the PRESENTATION sort. form is 'window'|'item_count'|'curated'; window_seconds is set for a window, count for item_count, both None for curated. axis/direction default to created/asc and are INERT for form=='item_count' (a pure tail-count over the forest's current order has no date pivot). item_count also carries selection ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a)): 'newest' keeps the N newest leaves by the recency basis (resolve_item_count_basis over recent_by/sort_by), 'bottom' keeps the positional tail of the current order; the FIELD default is 'bottom' (the legacy positional meaning, so a hand-built / old-wire item_count spec behaves exactly as before), and the token codec sets 'newest' for 'last N'/'newest N' and 'bottom' for 'bottom N' (since_from_wire defaults an object without the key to 'bottom' -- wire back-compat). A raw human/API token string is parsed ONLY at the edge by since_from_edge, which delegates to SinceCodec.from_token; interior code carries SinceSpec or None only. since_to_wire serializes SinceSpec to an object dict or None; since_from_wire reads that object dict back and rejects strings. THE chronological-render predicate (U6, ap:E03BN3 -- Dan's ruling 'any chronological sort of any form => never display ancestor notes'): True iff a render is CHRONOLOGICAL -- a resolved presentation sort_by of 'created' or 'modified' (EITHER direction) OR ANY since (window / curated / item_count). An item-count since ALONE counts since CF-13 = Option A (Dan's ruling 2026-09-22, relayed Manager-Session-033; supersedes U6 ap:UXYCID §2 invariant 6 + §9 tests 3/10) -- under [ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a) of EITHER selection: 'last N'/'newest N' is now the genuine newest-N recency cut, and the positional 'bottom N' (also the legacy-blob reading) keeps CF-13's tail behavior; both withhold ancestor notes exactly like the date forms while their excerpt order STAYS document order unless the caller sorts (the predicate classifies NOTE PRESENTATION only, never ordering). THE single definition of 'chronological' every materializer-fed render surface consults to decide ancestor-note body suppression (the third RenderPolicy cause, occurrence-keyed, computed ONLY inside materialize_from_document_forest). INTERIOR Py wire writer for `since`. Serializes SinceSpec|None to object-dict-or-None only; it never emits a token string. Human-readable token strings belong solely to SinceCodec.to_token for display.

Parse a Form-A `since` window token (<number><unit? s|m|h|d|w>; a BARE number means DAYS) into SECONDS. Case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant. Returns None for a blank / malformed / non-positive token (caller raises). THE single token grammar for every GLIMPSE `since` path; moved into the pure module so server + client agree.

Parse a Form-C `since` ITEM-COUNT token: 'last N' / its synonym 'newest N' / the positional 'bottom N' (optionally '... N item[s]'), N a positive integer. Case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant. Returns the integer N, or None when the token is not an item-count token at all (so the caller can fall through to the Form-A window grammar) OR is a malformed 'last ...' (N missing / non-integer / <= 0) -- the caller distinguishes 'not mine' from 'mine but bad' by first checking is_item_count_token. WHAT the N selects is decided by the FIRST keyword via _ITEM_COUNT_SELECTION_BY_KEYWORD (last/newest -> the newest N, [ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a); bottom -> the positional tail); this function owns only the count. THE single item-count grammar for every GLIMPSE `since` path; the readable 'last 10' spelling was chosen over a '10i' pseudo-unit so it never collides with the bare-number=days Form-A rule.

Cheap prefix classifier: does this `since` token START the item-count family ('last ...' | 'newest ...' | 'bottom ...')? Lets callers ROUTE a token to the item-count grammar (parse_since_item_count) vs the window grammar (parse_since_window) BEFORE parsing, so a malformed 'last banana' is reported as a bad item-count rather than silently falling through to the window parser. Pure; no I/O.

Shared DFS that decomposes a node forest into its root->leaf BRANCHES, each a list of (uuid, node) from a top-level node down to a leaf (a node with no dict children). This is the ONE branch-collection walk reused by reorder_tree_by_timestamp, prune_tree_since, compute_since_window_pivot, AND prune_tree_to_last_leaf_count -- the definition of 'leaf' (no VISIBLE/dict children; hidden descendants are absent from the final forest) is therefore single-sourced, which is exactly what makes item-count's 'count only leaves' rule fall out for free. Preserves DFS/document order of leaves. Pure; inputs never mutated.

Shared prune-rebuild: given a forest and a set of KEPT leaf node object ids (id(node)), rebuild a NEW forest keeping only root->leaf paths that terminate in a kept leaf (connective ancestors preserved; dead branches dropped). Returns shadow dicts (inputs never mutated). Reused by prune_tree_since AND prune_tree_to_last_leaf_count so the 'keep the paths to these surviving leaves' mechanic is single-sourced; the two differ ONLY in HOW they choose the kept-leaf set (date-vs-pivot vs the last-N-in-order).

THE ONE node-limit cap for the search verbs' headings tier ([ap:O3MDOY] half 2, unit 5e): slice_group.sift / lightning_rod.render_search with max_nodes truncate the FINAL render forest (after the sort and the since prune, so selection -> order -> cap compose in that order, mirroring the grep tier) to the first max_nodes MATCHING nodes in display order, counted through the caller's member predicate (the lens's sift predicate / the search predicate); connective ancestors never consume budget and survive only while a kept descendant does. Not a since form and not a ranking: a positional display cap beside the prune family -- the count-and-stop mechanic mirrors prune_tree_to_last_leaf_count's positional tail at the node level. Returns (new_forest, echo|None); echo is None when nothing was hidden (the whole forest fit), so callers stay byte-identical otherwise. Pure; inputs never mutated.

THE single branch-date rule shared by the timestamp SORT (reorder_tree_by_timestamp) and every GLIMPSE `since` pivot (window + curation cursor). Given a root->leaf branch as a list of (uuid, node) and sort_by ('created' | 'modified'), returns the branch's comparison timestamp: created = the LEAF's own createdAt; modified = max(modifiedAt) over EVERY node on the branch. None when unavailable (uuid absent from cache / no int value), matching the sort's missing-key-sinks-last handling. Factored into the pure module so the sort and the `since` filter can NEVER drift on a branch's date; WorkFlowyClientNexus._branch_timestamp_key_static delegates here.

SHARED timestamp-sort pre-pass for the Markdown modal AND as_markdown GLIMPSE (and the `since` prune's re-merge). Reorders a visible node forest by leaf createdAt (created) or branch-max modifiedAt (modified), then trie-merges the sorted root->leaf branches so a shared ancestor straddled by an out-of-cluster branch RE-EMITS its file leader/breadcrumb. sort_by=None is identity passthrough. Returns a NEW shadow tree (inputs never mutated); every leaf keeps its FULL ancestor path so the composer's regime-threading + per-file H1 rebase + md-in-md all stay correct by construction. Keys join the /nodes-export cache by UUID (DOM payload has no timestamps); a UUID absent from the cache sinks last. Branch-date rule delegated to branch_timestamp_key so the SORT and the `since` pivot share ONE definition. WorkFlowyClientNexus._reorder_tree_by_timestamp delegates here.

GLIMPSE `since` Form-A (time-window) PIVOT. Data-relative leading edge: pivot = the branch-date of the MOST RECENT leaf branch in the ALREADY-FINAL forest (ascending) MINUS the window -- so 'last 1 week' on data whose newest branch is 2 years old means the week ENDING at that 2-year-old edge, NOT wall-clock now. Descending flips to the OLDEST edge PLUS the window (the commensurate corner). Uses the SHARED branch_timestamp_key so the branch-date matches the sort's. Returns None if no branch has a resolvable date (caller then returns the tree unfiltered). Both the server and client `since` paths reach this through apply_since_to_forest.

GLIMPSE `since` PRUNE -- the shared leaf-branch filter run LAST (after Phase1/2/3 AND after the timestamp reorder), on the already-final sorted forest. Decomposes the forest into root->leaf branches (same DFS the sort uses), keeps a branch iff its branch-date (via the SHARED branch_timestamp_key) is beyond the pivot: ascending -> STRICTLY GREATER than pivot (most-recent tail; pivot node excluded); descending -> STRICTLY LESS (the commensurate 'oldest tail'). A branch with no resolvable date is DROPPED. Then re-merges surviving branches via reorder_tree_by_timestamp so straddled ancestors re-emit exactly as in the unfiltered render. Returns a NEW forest (inputs untouched); [] when nothing survives; the input unchanged when no prune applies. Shared by the server (_prune_tree_since delegates here) and, historically, a client twin (_prune_forest_since) that has since been DELETED -- the client now reaches `since` only through apply_since_to_forest.

GLIMPSE `since="curated"` FORM-B PIVOT (the self-maintaining curation cursor). Walks the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, finds every CURATED node (curated_predicate(name, note) True -- the caller injects f8_slice_policy.node_is_curated_for_prefixes, deliberately looser than slice MEMBERSHIP on the triage axis: --deprecated variants still count, because deprecating a tag is itself a curation act; the --suppress/--expand PRESENTATION variants do NOT count and never move the mark -- Session-019 curated-cursor fix), computes each curated node's branch-date via the SHARED branch_timestamp_key over its root->leaf cache path, and returns the MAX (ascending; MIN descending) = the high-water mark. Returns None when NOTHING under root is curated (whole subtree is the uncurated tail). curated_predicate is passed IN (not imported) so this module needs no f8_slice_policy dependency -> zero import-cycle risk; the walk itself is postfix-agnostic -- the curation semantics live entirely in the injected predicate. server._compute_curated_high_water_mark delegates here.

GLIMPSE `since` FORM-C POSITIONAL prune ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a): the selection spelled 'bottom N', and the legacy meaning of every old wire blob) -- the ITEM-COUNT tail filter over the forest's CURRENT order. Runs LAST, exactly like the date prune, on the already-final (optionally sorted) forest, but is orthogonal to the sort: 'the bottom N' is defined purely by the forest's CURRENT leaf order (the new 'newest N' SELECTION lives beside it in prune_tree_to_newest_leaf_count). Counts LEAVES only (a node with no dict children in the final forest; hidden descendants are already absent) via the SHARED collect_leaf_branches, keeps the LAST N leaf branches in that order (the tail: most-recent under an ascending chronological sort, earliest under descending, last-in-document-order when unsorted), and rebuilds via the SHARED _rebuild_forest_from_kept_leaves. When N >= leaf count the whole forest is returned unchanged (by identity of the kept set). Does NOT re-sort/re-merge -- the input order IS the truth (first pass: no nestedness weighting; a subtree with K leaves consumes K of the count). Returns a NEW forest; [] only if the forest has no leaves at all. Pure; inputs never mutated.

Resolves every atom once against injected snapshots, delegates group/tags/subtree meaning to the canonical Stage-1 primitives, extracts effective leaves, performs union/intersection/ordered-difference algebra over leaf IDs only, and returns a canonicalized recipe plus exact per-atom diagnostics. A group/tags atom that OMITS its own match_scope takes ctx.default_match_scope (the surface threads 'name' for a recipe render, 'name' for sift tag atoms); an explicit per-atom match_scope always wins. Chain-1 r2 (F5): a sink (write/export/purge_preview) whose GROUP atom's STORED root names a visible archived node raises ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError with the universal §5.3.2 envelope — the same answer _resolve_root gives an override root — while every other resolution failure stays a path-bearing LensSpecError. Chain-2 r1 (F1): a group atom's INHERITED stored root resolves through the SAME _resolve_root/Stage-0 resolve_root seam an override root uses (the shared two-phase composite resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle), so an exported-and-deleted stored root is served by the automatic fallback re-run and an include-mode run records the archive answer (banner + provenance); a live stored root resolves to itself, and every resolution failure falls through to the pre-existing refusal check + group_resolution_failed error unchanged. Chain-2 r2 (R1): the inherited branch resolves under the STORED-IDENTITY policy — a SHAVED corrective match is REJECTED (never adopted as the atom's scope, even with no archive folder), the speculative correction echo is surgically discarded, and the rejection falls into the same miss path (group_resolution_failed / the archived-stored-root sink refusal); explicit override atoms keep today's forgiving correction, echo included, and an exact archived record still beats a shave upstream (E2).

Chain-1 r2 (F5): a sink (write/export/purge_preview) whose GROUP atom's STORED root names a visible archived node raises ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError with the universal §5.3.2 envelope — the same answer _resolve_root gives an override root — while every other resolution failure stays a path-bearing LensSpecError. Chain-2 r1 (F1): a group atom's INHERITED stored root resolves through the SAME _resolve_root/Stage-0 resolve_root seam an override root uses (the shared two-phase composite resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle), so an exported-and-deleted stored root is served by the automatic fallback re-run and an include-mode run records the archive answer (banner + provenance); a live stored root resolves to itself, and every resolution failure falls through to the pre-existing refusal check + group_resolution_failed error unchanged. Chain-2 r2 (R1): the inherited branch resolves under the STORED-IDENTITY policy — a SHAVED corrective match is REJECTED (never adopted as the atom's scope, even with no archive folder), the speculative correction echo is surgically discarded, and the rejection falls into the same miss path (group_resolution_failed / the archived-stored-root sink refusal); explicit override atoms keep today's forgiving correction, echo included, and an exact archived record still beats a shave upstream (E2).

Post-algebra LensSpec materializer. Empty selections become a typed zero-root result; non-empty leaf sets compute one real LCA, reject phantom/disjoint roots, and rebuild the minimal connective tree through the canonical cache selection primitive while re-enforcing completed exclusion.

Fed by _project_render_lens_from_cache (per-atom resolved roots + final post-sift tree + pinned cache) to the materializer's existing lens-scaffold cause. An input root absent from the final tree still protects all its descendants; if the final root is at-or-below an input root the scaffold set is empty. Distant-LCA connective paths stay heading-only by default; nested input roots never suppress an outer root's member notes. Reuses the canonical ancestor-chain/descendant predicates; pure, no I/O or second suppression path.

Surfaced on the batch result row so a skipped # write is never silent (Manager-Session-088). noop_reason: Optional[str] = None # 2R4E1P: the agent-facing kept-conflict message (both texts) when # comment_outcome == 'kept_existing_conflict' -- a fill-mode comment # conflict is a WARNING (labels still ensured), never a plan failure. comment_warning: Optional[str] = None def to_dict(self) -> dict: return { "success": self.success, "planned_operation": self.planned_operation, "node_id": self.node_id, "target_key": list(self.target_key) if self.target_key else None, "cached_name": self.cached_name, "intended_name": self.intended_name, "write_intent": self.write_intent.to_dict() if self.write_intent else None, "occurrence": self.occurrence, "file_node_id": self.file_node_id, "source_path": self.source_path, "language": self.language, "beacon_id": self.beacon_id, "note_comment": self.note_comment, "disk_comment": self.disk_comment, "comment_outcome": self.comment_outcome, "resolved_comment": self.resolved_comment, "intended_slice_labels": list(self.intended_slice_labels), "source_sha256": self.source_sha256, "error": self.error, "error_kind": self.error_kind, "comment_warning": self.comment_warning

THE ONE per-line span matcher for a note-line grep over an already node-level-ADMITTED document set (slice_group.sift's tier='context' report today; render_search's and anchor.search's grep tiers adopt it rather than compiling a second matcher). Same query grammar as build_search_predicate -- it shares _smart_terms -- but applied to ONE logical line: smart mode hits on any POSITIVE term/phrase of any OR-group (negations and AND-grouping were enforced at the node level) with globs matched through a lazy unanchored span regex (_glob_span_pattern) so the span can centre a crop window; regex mode compiles IGNORECASE per line (line-local, so no DOTALL -- the same flags compile_note_query uses). Returns the ONE span contract: [] is no hit, otherwise every (start, end) character span left to right (end exclusive). Raises LightningRodQueryError exactly when the node-level predicate build would, so the two can never disagree on a valid query.

THE ONE Q4 operations-grammar normalizer core (STAGE-0 DOCTRINE: interpretation unified, transport per-origin). Consumed by BOTH ingress fronts -- WorkflowyTagMutationSpec.normalize_from_tool_args (MCP tool args) and .from_wire (the section-9 client wire frame) -- so the two transports can never drift. Grammar: operations is a non-empty list of {handle, operation:'add'|'remove', tags:[...]} or {handle, operation:'rename', old_tag, new_tag} objects; unknown fields rejected per-operation-kind; duplicate handles rejected; '#'-prefix optional (canonicalized '#'-less); internal-whitespace tags rejected. Returns (tuple-of-TagMutationOperation, None) or (None, error-string) -- errors are returned, never raised, so boundaries produce structured failures. Pure; no I/O.

THE ONE managed-metadata inventory ([ap:BNNUZ4]): one deterministic registry for detect_managed_metadata, detect_trail_skip_metadata and first_refuse_guard_hit. Skip-trail kinds include program_interface, StageConfiguration, ConductorState, dispatch, estate payloads, manifests and snapshot/ledger names; mapped kinds retain the existing refusal. Estate classification delegates entirely to glimpse_estate_payload's candidate parser/extractor and requires a valid entry -- no private estate keys or shape recogniser. Ambiguous bare group names remain outside metadata recognition; the estate grammar itself treats leading promote provenance as inert, so move/copy cannot change their parcels. Other kind detectors and mapped refusal are unchanged. Pure; no I/O.

THE source-map marker test ([ap:UH0UOU]): True iff the note's FIRST line carries a Cartographer/beacon source-map marker -- AST_QUALNAME: / MD_PATH: / BEACON ( / @beacon[ prefixes (the shapes the display stripper strips; the first three are also the refuse guard's first-line set) or a Path:/Root: header whose first whitespace-delimited token is exactly "Path:" or "Root:" (byte-identical to parse_path_or_root_from_note's first-line grammar, mirrored here to keep this module import-light -- the same mirror discipline as _REFUSE_FIRST_LINE_RE). This is the "the line is source code" signal the headings-only end-of-line metadata exemption keys on: the composer's ONE heading-metadata emitter suppresses the whole four-field vocabulary on such lines. Markers below line 1 are prose, never managed. Pure; no I/O.

Ordered per-family registry and sole authority for canonical routes, aliases, collision checks, family error-code union, compact index text, and full progressive-disclosure describe output. Owns the intrinsic describe operation so families cannot register a competing route.

Hand-rolled JSON-Schema-subset envelope validator shared by every family dispatcher. Enforces required/forbidden/type/enum/items-type rules, rejects Python bool as integer/number, and gathers every envelope problem into one deterministic OperationValidationError.

The standardized public family error-envelope builder. Produces operation-aware describe hints, preserves structured error.extra, and fail-closes on undeclared domain codes so handlers cannot leak undocumented vocabularies.

Canonical asynchronous family-operation acknowledgement: one operation-qualified job envelope with optional operation-specific job metadata merged beneath job. Every family uses system.job.status and system.job.cancel for later control.

Canonical mutation acknowledgement wrapper. Keeps the complete legacy payload or ledger verbatim under detail while giving every family a consistent success/operation/changed/warnings top level. Changed is explicit caller knowledge, never guessed from payload shape.

One public family-dispatch and immediate failure-documentation funnel. The unchanged _dispatch_operation_core owns validation, admission, cache boundaries, handlers and advisory/exception hooks. A1: THE effective-leaf extractor for a projected slice final tree. A final-tree leaf L is EFFECTIVE iff DIRECTLY LIVE (is_slice_member with the SAME operands Phase 1 used) OR EXPANSION-ADMITTED (L's root-to-leaf branch passes through a surviving plan['expand'] target). The root-as-lone-leaf case fails BOTH tests -> correctly empty (a no-hit group contributes nothing, NOT {root}). Fixes the false-member bug where collect_leaf_branches alone reports the connective root as a 'leaf' when the funnel unconditionally keeps it. Pure; reuses collect_leaf_branches + is_slice_member verbatim -- no new membership engine.

A2: bottom-up coverage set -- the workhorse compute_merge_tag_plan calls. Returns the set of node ids B where EVERY visible TERMINAL leaf under B is in merged_leaf_ids (recursive). 'Visible' = NOT suppression-invisible (name_has_global_never_tag on the CHILD, root-exempt) and, when skip_completed=True, NOT completed (CHILD-only test, root-exempt) -- mirroring the Phase-3 HYDSUP hydration seals so a later render of the expand tag reproduces exactly the covered set. O(N) per start subtree; the children-by-parent index mirrors collect_subtree_ids' construction.

A7: the MERGE TAG PLANNER (Phases C+D+E of the goal spec). Given the merged leaf set + the LCA root (or top-level start_ids for vault-root), walks the cache top-down and locates the HIGHEST-LEVEL fully-covered branches (expand_nodes -- tagged once with tag+--expand) and the remaining uncovered merged leaves (plain_nodes -- tagged with just the tag). 'Highest-level' falls out by construction: full_cover is tested BEFORE descending; an expand node ends the walk beneath it. The PLANNER COMPLETENESS ASSERTION (A7) verifies every merged leaf ends up in (union of expand-covered sets) OR plain_nodes; on assertion failure the result carries spine_blockers naming any completed/global-never node(s) strictly between a start root and a blocked leaf (A6 diagnostics). Pure; no I/O.

A3/A4: the Ruling-3 SAFETY CHECKER with the A3.2 CONGRUENT-RESIDUE rule folded INSIDE the walk. Walks every descendant of each start_id IGNORING global suppression (suppression must not hide a collision) and skipping completed nodes CHILD-ONLY (Ruling A + A5: completed DESCENDANTS are invisible; an explicit start ROOT stays completion-exempt). For every node the name is split FIRST via the canonical _resolve_split_name_and_tags and the THREE regions are scanned INDEPENDENTLY (trailing NAME tags / non-trailing base NAME text / NOTE body) -- extract_node_tags dedupes name+note, which would let a congruent trailing copy hide a duplicate note/inline occurrence of the same tag (post-audit fix). A match is TOLERATED as congruent resume residue ONLY when the node is in planned_node_forms AND the matched tag equals the exact required form (target_tag | expand_form) AND sits in the trailing NAME region. Every base-NAME or NOTE occurrence, a wrong form, an unplanned node, or an unrelated family variant is NONCONGRUENT. Counting happens DURING the full walk (never from a capped report): returns {count (true noncongruent total), collisions (first max_rows rows, document order, each with a source field), truncated, congruent_count}. Pure; no I/O.

A7: build an in-memory OVERLAY cache for the pre-mutation dry-run. Shallow dict-copy of the affected node entries with the planned tags appended to their NAMEs (rendered exactly as workflowy_add_tag would append them). The overlay is a full cache_by_id dict so build_stage1_base_tree can project against it identically. Pure; no I/O.

A7: run a PRE-MUTATION DRY-RUN projection of the generated family through build_stage1_base_tree over the overlay cache. Returns the projected NODE SET (spine + leaves). The caller compares this against the expected set (spine ∪ merged leaves) -- mismatch catches spine-blocked merges (A6), compiler bugs, and postfix-generation mistakes BEFORE a single tag is written. For the vault-root case (lca=None), simulates once per top-level start root and unions the node sets. Pure; no I/O.

A3.4: POST-MUTATION VERIFICATION. After a fully-successful mutation, re-project the generated family from the (patched) cache via build_stage1_base_tree and compare the node set against expected (spine ∪ merged leaves). Returns {matched: bool, missing: [...], unexpected: [...]} so the orchestrator can gate persistence and emit the verification block (A12). Shares the comparison core with the dry-run (simulate_merge_projection). Pure; no I/O.

Pure; reuses collect_leaf_branches + is_slice_member verbatim -- no new membership engine.

A2: bottom-up coverage set -- the workhorse compute_merge_tag_plan calls. Returns the set of node ids B where EVERY visible TERMINAL leaf under B is in merged_leaf_ids (recursive). 'Visible' = NOT suppression-invisible (name_has_global_never_tag on the CHILD, root-exempt) and, when skip_completed=True, NOT completed (CHILD-only test, root-exempt) -- mirroring the Phase-3 HYDSUP hydration seals so a later render of the expand tag reproduces exactly the covered set. O(N) per start subtree; the children-by-parent index mirrors collect_subtree_ids' construction.

A7: the MERGE TAG PLANNER (Phases C+D+E of the goal spec). Given the merged leaf set + the LCA root (or top-level start_ids for vault-root), walks the cache top-down and locates the HIGHEST-LEVEL fully-covered branches (expand_nodes -- tagged once with tag+--expand) and the remaining uncovered merged leaves (plain_nodes -- tagged with just the tag). 'Highest-level' falls out by construction: full_cover is tested BEFORE descending; an expand node ends the walk beneath it. The PLANNER COMPLETENESS ASSERTION (A7) verifies every merged leaf ends up in (union of expand-covered sets) OR plain_nodes; on assertion failure the result carries spine_blockers naming any completed/global-never node(s) strictly between a start root and a blocked leaf (A6 diagnostics). Pure; no I/O.

A3/A4: the Ruling-3 SAFETY CHECKER with the A3.2 CONGRUENT-RESIDUE rule folded INSIDE the walk. Walks every descendant of each start_id IGNORING global suppression (suppression must not hide a collision) and skipping completed nodes CHILD-ONLY (Ruling A + A5: completed DESCENDANTS are invisible; an explicit start ROOT stays completion-exempt). For every node the name is split FIRST via the canonical _resolve_split_name_and_tags and the THREE regions are scanned INDEPENDENTLY (trailing NAME tags / non-trailing base NAME text / NOTE body) -- extract_node_tags dedupes name+note, which would let a congruent trailing copy hide a duplicate note/inline occurrence of the same tag (post-audit fix). A match is TOLERATED as congruent resume residue ONLY when the node is in planned_node_forms AND the matched tag equals the exact required form (target_tag | expand_form) AND sits in the trailing NAME region. Every base-NAME or NOTE occurrence, a wrong form, an unplanned node, or an unrelated family variant is NONCONGRUENT. Counting happens DURING the full walk (never from a capped report): returns {count (true noncongruent total), collisions (first max_rows rows, document order, each with a source field), truncated, congruent_count}. Pure; no I/O.

A7: build an in-memory OVERLAY cache for the pre-mutation dry-run. Shallow dict-copy of the affected node entries with the planned tags appended to their NAMEs (rendered exactly as workflowy_add_tag would append them). The overlay is a full cache_by_id dict so build_stage1_base_tree can project against it identically. Pure; no I/O.

A7: run a PRE-MUTATION DRY-RUN projection of the generated family through build_stage1_base_tree over the overlay cache. Returns the projected NODE SET (spine + leaves). The caller compares this against the expected set (spine ∪ merged leaves) -- mismatch catches spine-blocked merges (A6), compiler bugs, and postfix-generation mistakes BEFORE a single tag is written. For the vault-root case (lca=None), simulates once per top-level start root and unions the node sets. Pure; no I/O.

A3.4: POST-MUTATION VERIFICATION. After a fully-successful mutation, re-project the generated family from the (patched) cache via build_stage1_base_tree and compare the node set against expected (spine ∪ merged leaves). Returns {matched: bool, missing: [...], unexpected: [...]} so the orchestrator can gate persistence and emit the verification block (A12). Shares the comparison core with the dry-run (simulate_merge_projection). Pure; no I/O.

Uncontended acquisition is a synchronous fast path (O(1) dict work, no loop yield — §10 latency).
U01 diagnostics (spec §5): the CALLING task's currently held keys — its re-entrancy set (tests + diagnostics). Empty when the task holds none / has no state yet.

ONE semantic note line authority for windowed reads and grep (and future range extraction). Normalize CRLF/CR to LF then splitlines; empty text has zero lines and a final terminator creates no phantom line. No decoding or I/O here; callers acquire semantic text through the existing live decoder or pinned canonical cache.

THE ONE note-line query matcher (literal or Python regex, IGNORECASE|DOTALL defaulting as before) behind node.search -- sift's grep mode and anchor.search adopt it rather than compiling a second matcher. Returns the line's MATCH SPANS: [] is no hit, otherwise every non-overlapping (start, end) character span left to right (end exclusive), so presentation can centre crop windows on the match; a plain hit test is bool(spans). Not Lightning Rod's smart/Boolean grammar; whitespace is valid literal text; only the empty string is rejected; regex anchors are line-local.

THE ONE node-level match-control policy for every note-line grep surface ([ap:O3MDOY] half 2, unit 5e): node.search, anchor.search, slice_group.sift tier 'context' and lightning_rod.render_search tier 'context' all pass the SAME normalized controls (sort_by none|created|modified, sort_direction asc|desc, recent = the N newest matching NODES, recent_by, max_nodes = a node cap distinct from the matched-line cap). build_search_node_controls assembles/normalizes and returns None when everything is inactive so the report stays byte-identical; select_note_documents_for_report identifies the matching documents and delegates ALL ranking to the ONE recency idiom dock_peek_metrics.apply_dock_peek_recency (recent keeps the N newest by the resolved basis, survivors keep document order unless sorted, missing timestamps sink last, ties keep document order -- the peek/render rule; include_completed=True because each search owns its completed semantics upstream), then applies max_nodes as a POSITIONAL cap on the (optionally sorted) candidate order. Selection never reorders: without sort_by the report stays traversal order. Justification for the two helpers: assembly/facts only -- the ranking itself is apply_dock_peek_recency's, reused verbatim, not a third idiom (CF-25). Pure; no I/O.

Pure paged COMPACT grep report over semantic (uuid, title, note) documents -- the ONE formatter every note-line grep surface shares (node.search today; sift's grep tier and anchor.search adopt it; the all-caps pagination banner format_pagination_banner, one implementation, opens every truncated report, then the optional header_line slot for a caller's Source line). One 'Matched N lines in  :' header per node, then ripgrep-style rows through the shared format_note_lines: right-aligned 1-based number, ' | ', text; '> ' marks hits only when context is shown; context windows merge and a single '...' row separates windows whose line numbers jump (context only -- a bare hit list has no separators); no blank lines inside a node, one between nodes. match_width crops hit rows to match-centred windows (_match_row_texts: one row per distant match, same line number repeated; 0 = off like null); context_width crops context rows head-first (_crop_context_row); null/0 = no crop. matches is the ONE span matcher (compile_note_query or lightning_rod_search.build_line_span_matcher): a hit is a non-empty span list. A document may carry a 4th MARKER element (D6, grep tiers): a node the node-level predicate admitted whose note has no single matching line still appears -- its header row alone, marked '(title match)' or '(match spans lines)', zero lines for paging. Optional collect dict (out-param) reports the page facts (has_more/next_offset/returned_matches/returned_occurrences) for structured variants; omitted = byte-identical string. Paging stays in matched LINES (global offset, per-page cap, one-hit lookahead); the footer also reports returned_occurrences. Stateless, no tree composer, no I/O.
