(3) MARKDOWN / RAW-TEXT mode -- a RENDERED TEXT STRING is present -> return it RAW (real newlines, like read_text_file), NOTHING ELSE: preview_markdown (every Markdown-mode render across GLIMPSE live-DOM / slice_group / raw root_uuid / render_spec modal+blob / dom_capture, AND Lightning Rod render_tags/render_search/render_symbols) OR preview_text (the Lightning Rod gather raw-text tag outline, byte-identical to the modal's Gather). The rendered string IS the whole semantic payload in this mode, so no envelope is wanted. This is the single future-proof seam: ANY future raw-text mode just fills preview_text (or preview_markdown) and is delivered raw with ZERO further change here. (4) FULL / UUID mode -- a preview_tree is present -> return the STRUCTURED DICT, preserving preview_tree AND all the genuinely-useful metadata (node_count, depth, _source, render_scope, since_applied, ...), but STRIPPING ONLY the redundant CONTENT twins: `rows` (modal tree-view metadata that duplicates preview_tree) and any stray preview_markdown/preview_text; additionally, when headings_only=True (the compact UUID-harvest pass), strip bulky live-DOM raw `root`/`children` to keep the payload small. Full mode is for structural / UUID work, so the stats ARE wanted here -- only the duplicative rows/markdown clutter is dropped. (5) everything else (errors success:false, push_to_modal acks, gather's structured tag list when preview_text is somehow absent, empty payloads with neither field) -> pass the structured dict through unchanged so failures/acks still signal correctly. The rich internal payloads (rows, render_scope, since_applied, node_count) are LEFT INTACT on the helper returns -- they still flow to the browser/modal WS reply handlers that need them; this finalizer only shapes the AGENT-facing tool return. preview_markdown is checked before preview_text before preview_tree: at most one is ever populated on a given result, so order is belt-and-suspenders. STALE-FOCUS GUARD [ap:XDVDRG]: a Markdown/raw-text result that carries focus_unresolved is NEVER delivered raw -- its always-empty string would read as a legitimately empty view; the structured stale payload is returned instead (success flipped to false, the empty preview twins and modal rows dropped, error + focus_unresolved kept) so the shared family error boundary surfaces the loud stale-focus error. A legitimate empty (empty since-window, no focus_unresolved) still returns its raw '' when NO recency selection is active -- the (empty) stub then fires at the public funnel (9a); when a recency selection IS active ([ap:TVIIBN] 4e), the Markdown body is passed through the ONE empty-output stub (stub_empty_text_result, caveat C1) and the result opens with ONE '> Recency selection: ...' rule line naming what was chosen and teaching that sort_direction only orders (the structured full/UUID twin carries the same sentence as a top-level recency_header key, no quote marker). The header text is composed ONLY by _recency_header_sentence -- one composer, no second header writer; the browser modal / push / file paths never pass through here and are untouched by construction.

Pure simple-form identity interpretation over caller-injected cache/config operands. Reuses the existing node/group resolvers and Dock classifier, and the two pure decisions; returns a lowering or read_note intent, never acquires state or renders. Transport and note-read control flow stay per origin.

ONE estate entry through the EXISTING server render funnel (no new render path): a named-group entry normalizes via normalize_from_glimpse_args(group_id=<handle>, match_scope='name') — a slice spec at the group's stored root with its saved default sort/policy, resolved by the SAME _resolve_slice_group_handle glimpse(group_handle=…) uses; a spec entry deserializes via RenderProjectionSpec.from_render_spec_blob (spec VERBATIM, focus included), rides the UUID prefix-grace, then the loud focus-intent-loss check (a saved selection that collapses to None aborts the entry rather than dumping the whole scope). Both go through the ONE override+guard seam (_apply_modal_view_overrides_and_guard → with_view_overrides) and _glimpse_dispatch_spec — which honors single-row AND mode='rows' covering-subtree focus via the shared Stage-2 tail, and NEVER runs the in-band Anchor-Dock raw-dump guard (every estate entry passes as allow_anchor_dock=true by construction). Returns a flat per-entry record; every failure shape (invalid entry, unresolvable group, root_not_in_cache, stale focus, guard rejection, funnel error, unexpected exception) is a LOUD record — the caller keeps rendering the others. Chain-1 r2 (F5/R2-W1): ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError is the one re-raised exception — an entry whose root names a visible archived node refuses the WHOLE sink call with the universal envelope, never an isolated failed row an assembly could write into a delivery-success file.

Estate OUTPUT origin: simple forms/full JSON directly or a Dock/estate handle, interpreted by the pure grammar and injected-snapshot resolver. Dock first (no note read), else ONE live _node_read_impl; entries never nest. Lowered entries use the same TWO-branch _glimpse_estate_render_entry and _glimpse_dispatch_spec. Existing alias/title headings, scope echoes, per-entry isolation, view overrides, output_file and reserved tabs semantics remain; no renderer, wire, cache writer or transport fork. Chain 1 r2 (WO [ap:4Q3LQV] W1): under repository_view the estate delivers the ONE coherence advisory authority's warning on its own reply -- the canonical line on the screen (text adapter on the document part, below the composed '> ' lines) and the structured key on the successful file acknowledgement -- while every file byte and assembled D stays clean; applicability rides the operation's captured status and is byte-identical when clean or with the flag off.

beacons.role: glimpse(output_file, as_markdown: bool, target_tab, sort_by, sort_direction, slice_group, root_uuid, headings_only, render_spec, allow_anchor_dock)
beacons.comment: GLIMPSE ingress: modal sentinel first; simple forms use the pure grammar and snapshot resolver before the existing spec/grace/view-override/push/render path. Explicit scope truth table and low-level defaults remain unchanged. [ap:EPR86W] part a: the raw-root cell honours recursive=False (root + direct children only, via the ONE shared walker's max_depth gate) and threads it to the push funnel; recursive=False on a slice-group scope or a live-DOM GLIMPSE is refused loudly at the boundary (and, for blobs, at the ONE spec normalizer).

Server helper: acquire the live WS peer (grace wait) and fetch the target tab's extension settings, returning normalized (note_session_tags, global_tags, default_parent). Fails loudly if no tab is reachable. Shared by both note-session MCP tools. Archive Reads U3: the raw reply ALSO feeds remember_archive_folder_from_reply — the daemon's memory of the extension's archive_folder option, so archive reads never need a tab (the file write defers inside an augmented operation, Axiom 5/E36).

Extract the configured LOCAL-anchor postfix word list from a get_extension_settings raw reply, defaulting to [DEFAULT_LOCAL_ANCHOR_POSTFIX] ('local') when absent/empty/malformed. The ONE server-side place the local-postfix default lives -- the Dock-favorites unit added the exact siblings _favorite_anchor_postfixes_from_reply / _deprecated_anchor_postfixes_from_reply and the ONE aggregator _anchor_postfix_kwargs_from_reply, so list_anchors and every classify/boundary call site read the full family vocabulary identically (no per-site defaulting, no drift). Rides in the raw reply (note_session_local_postfixes) rather than a widened _resolve_note_session_config tuple, to avoid an arity change across every existing unpack site.

Extract the configured FAVORITE-anchor postfix word list from a get_extension_settings raw reply (note_session_favorite_postfixes), defaulting to [DEFAULT_FAVORITE_ANCHOR_POSTFIX] ('fav') when absent/empty/malformed -- the exact sibling of _local_anchor_postfixes_from_reply (trim, strip one leading '#', drop non-strings/empties, order-preserving de-dup). The ONE server-side place the favorite-postfix default lives, so an extension that never sends the new key keeps working unchanged (I8: no vocabulary hardcoded in behaviour; words come from the reply through this helper).

Server helper for the slice-group MCP tools: acquire the live WS peer (grace wait) and read the target tab's LIVE slice-group config via client.get_slice_group_config -> returns (groups, active_id, postfixes_dict, global_never_expand, raw). Fails loudly if no tab. The server is the single settings reader (one source of truth), exactly like _resolve_note_session_config for anchors.

CFGOP1: the ONE nested get_slice_group_config TRANSPORT for the SIX browser-facing handlers/helpers that read the live slice-group/postfix config (_handle_compile_slice_search, _handle_f8_expansion_plan, _handle_render_slice_modal's slice cell + Lightning render_tags postfix_policy='slice' branch + render_symbols suppression read, and _project_slice_base_tree_for_scoped_lightning). Consolidates the six hand-duplicated blocks (ws-acquire -> _ws_request_response('get_slice_group_config', target_endpoint_id=ORIGINATING tab, tab_optional for the endpoint-absent case, 15s) -> unknown_endpoint ghost catch -> per-site error envelope) into ONE Stage-0 transport helper. Per the STAGE-0 DOCTRINE: transport/interpretation envelopes consolidate, control flow NEVER does -- each caller keeps its own group resolution, operand parsing (parse_slice_policy_config), and reply shape. The WSLIVE2 ghost rail is PRESERVED exactly: route by the originating tab's real endpoint_id (never degraded to unknown_target_tab masking); a ghost surfaces as code='unknown_endpoint' so the client retries after the broker's re-register broadcast. context = the caller's verb-phrase (error wording stays per-site); error_type (site 6's scoped_lightning_config_read_failed) folds into BOTH envelopes. Returns (reply, None) on success or (None, envelope) on any failure.

SGSORT semantic resolve-point for a slice group's effective render sort. Preserves the inviolable None-vs-'none' distinction until the live chosen group dict is in hand: Python None / JSON null inherits the group's stored default_sort_by + default_sort_direction pair; the string 'none' is explicit document order and canonicalizes direction to asc; created/modified pass through with sanitized direction. Called only at the two slice config resolve-points (_glimpse_slice_group_from_cache and _handle_render_slice_modal), so downstream render_scope/render-tail code sees only resolved wire values and never re-decides inheritance.

Advisory short-name collision detector for slice-group WRITES (create / update-rename / merge.persist). Parses the candidate full name with the ONE grammar parser and lists every OTHER leaf group whose semantic short name collides (case-insensitive); expander/category rows and empty short names never participate (they are not short-name-resolvable), and an expander CANDIDATE yields no warnings (its short name is organizational, not a resolvable handle). Non-fatal by design: the report-only result rides in the write reply as short_name_collisions so an agent learns at WRITE time that the new name will be ambiguous as a short handle (the resolver still fails loudly with colliding_ids at USE time). Pure; no I/O.

Resolve an agent-supplied slice-group id against the in-hand groups list, with the SAME hallucinated-UUID prefix backtracking used everywhere else (anchor/snippet/SCRY) via the SHARED _resolve_uuid_with_prefix_fallback -- but with key_prefix='grp-' since group ids are 'grp-'+uuid4().hex (not in the /nodes-export cache; matched against the slice-group config instead). Returns (index, error_dict): exact id wins; else a UNIQUE prefix match is adopted silently; a MULTI prefix match returns an error with candidate ids; no match returns a not-found error. None error => index valid.

Layer-1 shared slice-group HANDLE resolver ([ap:9QK4MV] refactor; semantic short names added 2026). Resolve an agent-supplied slice_group handle against an in-hand groups list, returning (group_dict|None, error|None). Resolution order: (1) exact id; (2) unique 'grp-' prefix via _resolve_slice_group_id; (3) case-insensitive FULL stored-name match (pipe path + trailing [n] included); (4) case-insensitive semantic SHORT-name match -- the final pipe segment, index-stripped, via the ONE grammar parser parse_slice_group_name; LEAF groups only, the supplied handle participates only when it parses as a bare leaf (a trailing [n] ON THE HANDLE is tolerated), empty short names never match. At every name stage: 1 hit -> adopt; >1 -> colliding_ids error (never auto-pick); a stage-3 full-name hit outranks stage-4 short-name hits. Pure: no network/cache/I/O. This is the ONE home for 'resolve a slice-group handle' -- every render/CRUD/purge site AND the LensSpec group-atom resolver (via its raise-style adapter) route through here, so the handle grammar can never drift between surfaces.

MCP tool wrapper: resolve live config from the target tab, then delegate to client.list_note_sessions (cache walk + nested-priority DFS). Exposed publicly as 'list_anchors' (anchor = the user-facing name for what the internals still call note_session).

Internal anchor listing wrapper: public list_anchors calls it with default flags; the private widget endpoint passes tree/raw/local/favorites flags. Keeps live config resolution + client.list_note_sessions delegation in one place while preserving the public MCP tool signature. favorites_only defaults to FALSE here so the legacy list_anchors tool (all flags False) is unchanged; the public anchor.dock.list default (true) lives in _anchor_dock_list_impl alone.

MCP tool: return the user's canonical/global tag vocabulary (a routing HINT, not a constraint) read from SHARED cross-tab extension config via the tab-agnostic _resolve_note_session_config path. Tab-agnostic by design — never errors under multi-tab; only fails when no tab is reachable.

MCP tool wrapper: resolve default parent + anchor tag(s) from the target tab when not passed, then delegate to client.create_note_session (single ETCH). Fails loudly with no silent root fallback. local=True -> resolve the FIRST configured local postfix (via _local_anchor_postfixes_from_reply) and pass it as local_postfix so the anchor tag becomes base--local (a LOCAL anchor: hidden from list_anchors but still a descendants boundary). Exposed publicly as 'create_anchor' with exposed kwarg anchor_tag (internals still say note_session / session_tags).

MCP tool wrapper: resolve live anchor tags from the target tab, guard the 'note session' terminology rule, then delegate to client.update_note_session (rename base name preserving tags / replace note; mapped-subtree advisory surfaced for the agent to report). Exposed publicly as 'update_anchor' (internals still say note_session).

beacons.role: ⚡ add_to_anchor(parent_uuid: str, nodes, tags, target_tab, note_file, content, name)
beacons.comment: MCP tool wrapper: validate the EXACTLY-ONE payload contract (nodes XOR note_file XOR content; loud on both/neither/all; checked FIRST, before any live config read), then delegate to client.add_to_anchor (placement-guarded ETCH). The guard (folder + non-Markdown-file rejection) is the only value-add over workflowy_etch; dialect-neutral capture primitive for anchors. note_file: absolute-path UTF-8 text file -> exactly ONE node (file stem = name, raw text = note). content: raw string with required name= -> exactly ONE node (name = NAME, content = NOTE). name: optional override with note_file (skips stem as name).

beacons.role: ⚡ scry(node_id: str, depth, size_limit: int, output_file, allow_anchor_dock)

beacons.comment: node.resolve: the node family's identity verb ([ap:CZ95R6], Dan's REVISED 074 ruling — per-family verbs, ONE shared implementation). Accepts any handle form (exact UUID | its 8-hex first segment | a unique longer prefix | [ap:CORE], UUID-first with the AP-ID leg on unresolved fall-through) through the ONE shared resolve_node_identity_record (which wraps the ONE prefix kernel — no second resolver), against the operation's pinned cache map, and returns the unified non-raising 0/1/N record: on a unique match the node's full identifier vocabulary {short, uuid, ap_id} at the top level ('no anchor point available' in words when the node carries none), every candidate row carrying its vocabulary on ambiguity. A resolve is for citations/records — never needed before an ordinary handle call: every handle parameter already accepts all the forms directly.

node.ancestors: the extension's F3 ancestor chain as a real MCP verb — 'where does this node live in the full document, and is it inside a mapped file/folder?'. Pure cache read through the existing operation boundary (NO new transport): resolve handle against the pinned snapshot, walk + compose via ancestor_path.build_ancestor_path_document (the ONE core the F3/F2 WS handler delegates to, so the two homes can never drift; the WS frame-sending _resolve_uuid_path_and_respond is NEVER called from here), Dock-marker vocabulary via the ONE established Direction-A config read (skipped entirely when markers=false). detail='compact' returns the raw Markdown document (key line + chain + → uuid tail); detail='full' adds structured rows (title/tags/dock flags/completed/map_state/metrics + ap_id via the ONE shared leading-AP splitter) beside the same markdown.

beacons.role: ⚡ lightning_rod(mode, root_uuid, tags, query, query_mode, tag_match, postfix_policy, as_markdown, sort_by, sort_direction, headings_only, since, output_file)
beacons.comment: LIGHTNING ROD public MCP tool. Thin wrapper over the internal _lightning_rod_from_cache orchestrator: rate-limit acquire, then dispatch. Modes: gather (discover tags under a root -> feeds render_tags), render_tags (Option-B prefix-family tag filter; NO deprecation/suppress/expand semantics by DEFAULT -- the opt-in postfix_policy='slice' (ap:IMPPTX) instead routes it through the FULL Stage-1 funnel build_stage1_base_tree with the live postfix words + the real f8_global_never_expand_tags list), render_search (shlex 'smart' boolean/glob OR 'regex' free-text filter), render_symbols (dynamic tag-free beacon slice from a UUID/symbol/AP-ID list). Mutation modes: ensure_beacons/remove_beacon_tags (Q3 DISK beacons) and mutate_node_tags (Q4 batch Workflowy #tag add/remove/rename on NODES by UUID/[ap:CORE] handle -- operations-only; a thin ledger wrapper over the per-node tag primitives). Render modes are cache-only; no WebSocket (except one postfix config read for render_tags 'slice'), no slice-group persistence, no Workflowy-UI. Shared render knobs mirror glimpse and flow through render_stage2_filter_sort. since='curated' rejected (no slice tag set); live-GUI-sync never supported. The traversal pair rides the shared selection fragment ([ap:EPR86W] 4b): the walking verbs (gather/render_tags/render_search) carry recursive+descend_policy, and recursive=False is refused LOUDLY at the top of this body -- before the push branch, so a pushed selection cannot silently drop the request (one refusal text with the orchestrator's backstop, _lightning_recursive_refusal). The grammar docstring here is the AGENT-FACING interface (the caller is an LLM building the query from natural language, so it is small+explicit+deterministic with normative examples). PUSH-TO-MODAL: push_to_modal=True + target_tab route through the SAME _glimpse_push_slice_to_modal channel the GLIMPSE tool uses (the 4th push scope cell -> apply_slice_in_dock carrying a `lightning` scope -> the ONE shared applySliceGroupIntoDock apply path), so a pushed Lightning Rod render is identical to a ribbon-triggered one; as_markdown/output_file are inapplicable to a push (returns a small ack, not content). Only the injected predicate (or, under postfix_policy='slice', the shared funnel) differs from the other cache-projection + push scopes -- the same universal pipeline.

Canonical Node-family ETCH front. Selects the existing synchronous or asynchronous ETCH primitive, standardizes sync mutation acknowledgements, and converts async legacy job handles into the shared family job envelope without changing ETCH payload semantics.

Canonical Tag-family batch front. Reuses the one Q4 operations normalizer and the existing preflight-all-then-commit Lightning Rod tag orchestrator, preserving its complete ledger and batch-gating semantics.

Node-as-a-file paged grep front: single-node search delegates to the existing ONE live read and decoder; subtree search consumes the operation-pinned canonical map and established ordered scope walker, never live publisher state or per-descendant GETs, and hides completed nodes (plus their descendants) by default -- the dock.peek/render default; include_completed opts back in; suppressed nodes and child Docks stay included (search is a grep). The query is the ONE span matcher compile_note_query; the report is the ONE compact grep formatter search_note_documents (ripgrep-style rows, match_width/context_width crops, occurrences in the footer), which also owns the all-caps pagination banner that opens every multi-page report (the Source line rides the formatter's header_line slot, below the banner); each call uses the standard family boundary/finalizer for adoption and advisories. _note_grep_plan delegates grep values/defaults/bounds AND the [ap:O3MDOY] match controls (sort_by orders the node groups; recent='last N'/'newest N' keeps the N newest matching NODES by resolve_item_count_basis -- trimmed ones counted in the footer; max_nodes caps matching nodes distinct from the matched-line cap; ranking is dock_peek_metrics.apply_dock_peek_recency, the ONE idiom) to the ONE _normalize_note_grep_params; node.search/anchor.search/sift schemas share _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties. lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' ([ap:2EG7TD], landed) calls both owners too -- through the SAME _render_sift_grep_result tail (CF-30, no third producer). The plan keeps literal/regex query compilation and the report tail (_note_grep_report) stays shared with anchor.search. No retained snapshot, cache writes, transport fork, or renderer.

Assembly point for the consolidated public Node family. Thin handlers re-front lifecycle primitives, node-as-a-file read/search, and AP-aware leading-emoji mutations while the registry remains the sole authority for canonical verbs, role-named handles, transition aliases, schemas, effects, async metadata, and describe output.
Config-only Slice Group deletion. Resolves through the shared id/prefix/name resolver, clears active_group_id atomically when needed, persists once, and never touches Workflowy tags.

Recursive LensSpec merge persistence orchestrator. Evaluates once against the immutable S06 T1 snapshot, materializes the authoritative tree, preflights reproducibility/identity/collisions, reuses the shipped plan-simulate-Q4-verify compiler, then performs a fresh T2 config identity check and atomic create/reuse update.

Shared low-level/group-aware purge apply orchestrator. Recomputes and fingerprint-gates the preview, refuses shared families by default, delegates exact removals to Q4, rebuilds the eager-patched cache, and verifies no mutable family occurrence remains.

Assembly point for the consolidated public Tag family. Six operations preserve surgical single-node primitives, the complete batch ledger, and the fingerprint-gated purge workflow while the registry owns canonical verbs, aliases, schemas, effects, and describe output.

Shared Anchor-Dock root guard behind the two IN-BAND full-dump returns (node.scry and the bare-root_handle glimpse raw dump). Resolves the handle (UUID / unique prefix / [ap:CORE]) and classifies the root node's NAME tags against ONE welded snapshot (the resolver's echoed cache map + ONE live Dock-vocabulary read, optionally injected so the stop_at_child_anchors boundary shares it). Verdicts: root IS an Anchor Dock (global or local) -> raise _AnchorDockRootDetected with a peek/render teaching message; root ABSENT from the cache -> raise _FullDumpRootCacheMiss (FAIL CLOSED -- an unclassifiable in-band full-dump root is refused, never allowed to fall through to the API subtree fetch; the message points at system.cache.refresh); otherwise return {resolved, anchor_vocabulary} so the caller's downstream resolution and boundary predicate reuse the same operands. The live extension-settings WS read is FIRST-CLASS (the historical 'scry never touches the WebSocket' doctrine is retracted: node CONTENTS come from the cache/API, the Dock-tag VOCABULARY from the tab; a failed config read is loud, never a silent skip). Out-of-band deliveries (output_file, push_to_modal) are exempt by caller placement, never by this helper; allow_anchor_dock=true skips the guard wholesale at each caller.

Pure six-character uppercase-base36 AP-ID generator. Retries against an injected collision predicate and fails loudly after the bounded attempt budget; allocation locking and reservation live in the caller.

beacons.role: ƒ _render_dock_peek_raw_text(dock_name, root_note, rows, show_ids, show_counts, show_description, max_chars, max_description_chars, root_metrics, recursive, descend_policy, selection, sort, root_uuid, uuid_prefix_collisions, parent_handles)
beacons.comment: Pure compact Dock-peek serializer. One globally padded AP-only column over visible rows; blank for missing APs, no column if none. Names are shown in full (trailing #tags included) -- max_chars is an opt-in middle-ellipsis budget, 0/None = unlimited. The Dock's own '> …' description excerpt is budgeted SEPARATELY (max_description_chars, default 256, CF-MST-015; the name budget never touches it and show_description=false still suppresses it entirely). Only the trimmed body indents (four spaces per real node depth) and only while the rows are the plain document-order walk: a recent-N selection or a timestamp sort renders FLAT (a timestamp order is not a tree order), and UTAERZ shows the nesting per row there instead -- one ' ← in ‹parent handle›' hint (the parent's [ap:CORE], else its short UUID) on every row whose parent is not the peeked Dock (parent_handles is the impl's precomputed map; depth stays in the JSON). The header names the selection/order, including 'N completed hidden' whenever the default completed-exclusion removed rows (recency views AND the plain inventory alike, U6/J11); under a recent-N selection [ap:TVIIBN] 4e adds ONE explicit rule line directly below the header (describe_dock_peek_recency_rule, the peek-side twin of the render verbs' _recency_header_sentence): sort_direction only orders the selected rows, it never changes which rows were chosen. Row handles ([ap:0M6VP8] peek half): rows without an AP-ID show a bracketed short UUID handle in the body by default; show_ids=true adds it to every row; both route through the ONE shortener unique_short_uuid_prefix over the caller's uuid_prefix_collisions index (CF-22/O3), never a second shortener. Four source metrics and Dock/favorite/local/completed flags (marker order ⚓ ⭐ Ⓛ ✓; ⭐ only on a Dock row) with a policy-aware legend. No acquisition, source mutation, document rendering or traversal decisions.

Pure compact serializer for slice_group.list: one raw-text nested outline of the persisted slice groups. Rows come from build_slice_group_display_items -- the exact Python twin of the client's buildNestedDisplayItems (auto-vivified synthetic categories, the lowest-indexed canonical expander owning descendants, duplicate expander rows marked ' ⚠ duplicate category', null-index-last case-insensitive ordering, every category expanded). Category rows are bare '▾ name' (organizational; no ID, and hidden category-group tags are never exposed); leaf rows are '[<bare 8-hex group prefix>] short-name — up to 4 #tags (+N more) ✅' (✅ on the active group only). The header counts every stored record and ends detail='full' for JSON. Pure; no I/O.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_list_impl(include_local, target_tab, detail, max_chars, favorites_only, max_description_chars, show_description)
beacons.comment: Anchor Dock inventory front. detail='compact' (THE default everywhere -- consolidated registry, impl, and the legacy list_anchors delegate) returns ONE raw-text inventory string from one _list_anchors_internal(tree_view=True) acquisition, serialized by the ONE shared _render_anchor_tree_raw_text compact mode; detail='full' is the explicit escape hatch returning the established structured payload (rows gain is_favorite; the favorites echo keys ride along). favorites_only defaults TRUE HERE (the public shortlist default; _list_anchors_internal and the legacy tool stay False): the ⭐ favorites shortlist with the zero-favorites fallback, compact header counts taken from the echoed shown_global_count/shown_local_count so the arithmetic is correct under favorites. Row descriptions ([ap:YLHDIN] part 2): every compact row carries the Dock's FIRST description line as a ' — excerpt' tail (show_description=true default; max_description_chars budgets it, default 120, 0 hides; the same metadata-stripped text the structured rows carry). An inventory serializer, never a document render: no RenderProjectionSpec, no Stage 1/2, no composer.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_create_impl(topic, description, parent_handle, local, extra_tags, target_tab, favorite)
beacons.comment: Dock-create front: description is OPTIONAL (VBIKIZ) and defaults to empty -- the registry (not this impl) owns the name=topic / note=description aliases via param_aliases. Creates via client.create_note_session, so no tag-write path exists.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_update_impl(dock_handle, topic, description, local, target_tab, favorite, families)
beacons.comment: Atomic Dock update front. All name work goes through _node_edit_core + the ONE protected-name composer from ONE live GET snapshot (title, AP-ID, and the tag list the attribute transform rewrites never mix cache/live). Topic follows the public protected-name rules (supplied tags/AP changes rejected) and preserves the Dock's existing leading emoji run (Z8Q0PF+LITF2F: the caller need not pass an emoji; a supplied topic run wins explicitly; replace_emoji=True hands the run to the supplied topic wholesale -- its run replaces the existing one, its absence clears it; the SAME composed name is computed for the no-op/name_changed verdict and the write, so the two composer calls can never disagree); explicit local/favorite attribute writes are the ONLY tag rewrite, delivered via the narrow _tag_transform channel as a per-FAMILY set/unset-ONE-attribute transform (I6/I7): for each targeted family it removes ONLY that family's proper tags and re-inserts one canonical tag per remaining attribute (fixed order local, favorite; existing words preserved; bare base when the last attribute is unset -- Dock identity is never deleted), leaving every other family's tags, every --deprecated tag, every unknown-postfix tag and every unrelated tag byte-for-byte in place. NEVER canonicalises to base_tags[0] (the old family-switch bug). families= names the family to write when the node carries more than one (dock_families_ambiguous otherwise; a family without a proper tag on the node is dock_family_not_on_node; --deprecated-only does not count as present). Zero writes on any validation error. One live GET, at most one write.

anchor.dock.get_description: the Dock-description getter (TODO [ap:YLHDIN] part 1, Dan's "get description") as a thin Dock-checked PRESET over the ONE metadata header -- it resolves against the pinned cache, checks Dock-hood with the same classify_anchor_tags matcher the dock mutation verbs use (a non-Dock is a loud not_an_anchor_dock teaching error pointing at anchor.point.read), counts DIRECT child Docks through build_dock_peek_index's priority-ordered child lists classified by the ONE boundary predicate (build_anchor_boundary_predicate), then delegates to _anchor_point_read_impl with extra_header_lines=("child docks: N",) -- the ONE header composer serves both verbs; no second metadata header exists. The description (the note) rides the getter UNGUARDED and untruncated: fetching the description is the point (dock.peek's compact excerpt budgets it at 256 and detail='full' carries it whole -- the same norm). The vocabulary read fails loudly with no Workflowy tab (dock.peek's rule): the Dock check itself needs it. Pure read.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_peek_impl(dock_handle, target_tab, detail, show_ids, show_counts, show_description, max_chars, recursive, descend_policy, recent, recent_by, sort_by, sort_direction, include_completed)
beacons.comment: Dock-peek read-only inventory front: existing one config read/resolver/pinned map and owned source-metrics index. Direct children remain default; recursive=true uses real node depth and stops at nested Docks unless descend_policy='all' explicitly opens them (global and local alike). Rows carry the FULL node name verbatim (trailing #tags included; title/tags split alongside), the item's own created_at/modified_at, and parent_id (UTAERZ: the walked parent, so the flat recent/timestamp compact view shows a per-row ' ← in ‹parent handle›' hint for rows whose parent is not the peeked Dock; document order keeps indentation and no hints). Row handles ([ap:0M6VP8] peek half): rows without an AP-ID show a bracketed short UUID handle in the body by default; show_ids=true adds it to every row -- both through the ONE shortener unique_short_uuid_prefix over a build_uuid_prefix_collisions index built once per call from the same pinned cache map (CF-22/O3; parent hints use the same authority, the parent's [ap:CORE] when it carries one). recent=N selects the N newest walked rows on recent_by (default modified) and sort_by/sort_direction order the whole inventory -- one pure policy (apply_dock_peek_recency) applied between the walk and BOTH renderers so compact and detail='full' select identical items; neither knob given = document order, unchanged. Completed rows are marked but HIDDEN by default on EVERY view -- recency, timestamp sort, and the plain document-order inventory alike (U6/J11; include_completed=true opts back in) -- the filter lives solely inside the policy. detail='full' additionally carries the Dock's untruncated one-line 'description'; the compact '> …' excerpt budgets it at 256 chars. Totals always cover the full subtree. No new live reads, mutation claims, cache publication, renderer or broker path.

anchor.search: a node.search-shaped grep scoped to ONE Anchor Dock's subtree. Acquisition is dock.peek's own pattern -- the ONE note-session config read (the live Dock vocabulary; loud with no tab, like dock.peek), the generic handle resolver, the pinned operation cache -- then the ONE generic Stage-1 walk build_selected_subtree_from_cache with member_all=True, the shared build_anchor_boundary_predicate (descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' default stops at child Docks; each child Dock's own name/note is still searched as a signpost; 'all' enters them) and exclude_completed (completed nodes hidden by default, root exempt -- node.search's own default; include_completed opts back in). Documents from _anchor_scope_documents feed the ONE shared grep tail (_note_grep_plan + _note_grep_report + note_lines.search_note_documents): query machinery identical to node.search (literal or is_regex line-local, context_lines/context_width/match_width, matched-LINE offset/max_matches paging with the all-caps banner). _note_grep_plan delegates grep values/defaults/bounds AND the [ap:O3MDOY] match controls (sort_by/sort_direction/recent/recent_by/max_nodes -- node-level: recent keeps the N newest matching nodes, hidden ones counted in the footer; max_nodes caps matching nodes) to _normalize_note_grep_params; the registry takes the ONE schema fragment _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties, shared with node.search/sift/render_search. lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' ([ap:2EG7TD], landed) calls both owners too. match_scope ('name_and_note' default, sift's vocabulary) picks WHAT the query reads: name_and_note = note lines plus the TITLE (a title-only match renders its header row with the D6 '(title match)' marker -- the formatter drops the marker when note lines also hit); 'name' = title rows only (the document carries no note, so the shared formatter cannot leak note rows). No second formatter, second matcher, second walk, second vocabulary reader or second ranking idiom exists.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_render_impl(dock_handle, sort_by, sort_direction, recent, headings_only, as_markdown, output_file, push_to_modal, target_tab)
beacons.comment: Named raw-root GLIMPSE preset for an Anchor Dock. Reuses the existing root projection/modal-push paths while mapping the public most-recent token `recent` (legacy `tail`/`since` accepted as silent aliases at the registry) to the existing SinceSpec edge. [ap:EPR86W] part a: carries the traversal pair with EXACTLY dock.peek's names and values (defaults differ by design: recursive=True, descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' -- today's behavior unchanged); recursive=False renders the Dock + its DIRECT children (child Docks and plain nodes alike) and nothing deeper, with descend_policy moot, on both the content path (max_depth=1 through the ONE shared walker) and the push path (the flag rides the pushed spec blob).

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_point_capture_impl(parent_handle, nodes, tags, target_tab, note_file, content, name, ap_id)
beacons.comment: Canonical Anchor Point capture front. Preserves all guarded add_to_anchor payload/tag behavior and optionally reserves plus injects a collision-checked AP-ID before the one ETCH, preventing post-create partial state.

MOVE-only single/batch note-range extraction. ONE live source snapshot and the shared note_lines planner; captures run in document order through _anchor_point_capture_impl, EVERY success/root-id acknowledgement is checked before ONE whole-note _node_edit_core call with the original snapshot injected. No direct cache edits or parallel mutation transport. Failure ledger distinguishes source-not-written from an uncertain update outcome and preserves typed coherence refusals.

Assign a collision-checked AP-ID to an existing point via the narrow _assign_ap_core channel of _node_edit_core -- the composer's assign leg preserves the existing title and trailing tags automatically (no more raw prefix-string splice). Existing IDs are never replaced; a process-local lock plus reservation ledger closes same-server allocation races.

Dedicated idempotent AP-ID removal path. Resolves the node handle before mutation (so the AP-ID itself may be used to target the node), performs one live structured read, then delegates through _node_edit_core's narrow _remove_ap_id channel using that SAME snapshot. The pure composer removes only the leading AP token while preserving leading decoration, ordinary title, trailing tags, and one-layer entity semantics. Returns the removed handle + a loud citation-invalidation warning; an AP-less node is a true no-op with zero write. The removed core is deliberately NOT released from the process-local allocation ledger -- immediate same-process reuse would make old citations resolve to the wrong node.

anchor.point.resolve: the AP-ID-first identity resolve ([ap:CZ95R6]) through the ONE shared resolve_node_identity_record (prefer='anchor_point': the AP leg runs first, the UUID leg only on unresolved fall-through, so a UUID / 8-hex handle resolves here too and a bare base36 core that is also hex stays AP-domain first). Established 0/1/N shape preserved for the live consumers (success/match_count/candidates/resolved_ap_id), now with the unified identifier vocabulary {short, uuid, ap_id} at the top level on a unique match and per candidate row ('no anchor point available' when a node carries none). Never needed before an ordinary call: every handle parameter accepts an AP-ID directly.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_point_read_impl(node_handle, offset, limit, with_line_numbers, view, target_tab, extra_header_lines)
beacons.comment: anchor.point.read: node.read with Anchor usability defaults — metadata header over the LIVE note through _read_live_node_note (ONE rate-limited fetch/decode) and snippet_view.render_note_body (ONE guard/window/number/exact body), with validate_note_read_lines before I/O and normalize_note_view_params at the public front. Numbered by default; guard 400, size_only = header plus size line; no output_file/as_raw_node. Header metadata still uses the resolver's echoed pinned map, walk_ancestor_chain/build_ancestor_path_document/node_timestamp, peek markers and source metrics, dates, 8-hex handle and path. Dock vocabulary still degrades VISIBLY with no tab; ✓/🗺️/📄 need no tab. Only the framing and defaults differ from node.read. extra_header_lines (internal channel, anchor.dock.get_description only) splices Dock-only lines directly under the name/metrics line -- the ONE header composer serves both verbs.

anchor.point.touch: ordered batch, content-preserving modifiedAt advance so a chosen working set surfaces FIRST in dock.peek recent_by='modified'. handles[0] = highest priority = newest afterwards, achieved by touching in REVERSE input order, one governed write per item (~1 s each) through _node_edit_core's narrow _touch channel (layoutMode echo, name-identity fallback; never composes text). Preflight: duplicate handles (literal or same resolved UUID) = batch REFUSE, zero writes; unresolvable / not-in-cache / mapped (non-'unmapped' _classify_node_map_state -- disk is truth) / Anchor Dock (unless allow_docks) = per-item SKIP, batch continues. Execution: live GET before, write, verify content fingerprint unchanged and modifiedAt strictly increasing (one re-touch after a short sleep on a tie); an unknown write outcome, a content change or a non-advancing timestamp STOPS the batch (remaining rows not_run, never re-sent). Complete ledger in INPUT order + summary with order_established; success only when every row touched; partial_success on mixed outcomes.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_point_promote_impl(items, handles, destination, tags, mode, children, include_completed, target_tab)
beacons.comment: anchor.point.promote: the curation pass made atomic -- batch move-with-provenance (mode: move, default) and promote-as-COPY (mode: derivative). Two grammars (items=[{handle, destination, tags?, mode?, children?}] | handles=[...] + destination + tags? + mode? + children?) normalized by the pure normalize_promote_items before any I/O. Per item: resolve handle + destination through the generic resolver against ONE pinned cache map; origin = nearest ancestor Anchor Dock (global or local; else the immediate parent) via nearest_anchor_dock_ancestor; STRUCTURAL mapped-node refusal on source AND destination (_classify_node_map_state != 'unmapped' -- stricter than capture's guard, Markdown included) plus the first-line Cartographer-metadata content check (delegated to the ONE managed-metadata registry, managed_metadata.py). Batch grammar modelled on beacon.tags.ensure: per-item SKIP (unresolvable, not in cache, mapped) continues; batch REFUSE with zero writes (malformed, duplicate handles literal or same resolved UUID, destination inside the source's own subtree); STOP on any ambiguous post-send outcome (remaining rows not_run, nothing re-sent). MOVE = _node_move_impl(src, dest, 'bottom') + ONE _node_edit_core(note=trail+old, _tag_transform=add, _current_node=live) = 2 governed writes; the trail line '↩ moved from <origin> (<uuid8>) · <date>' is plain text, newest on top. MANAGED METADATA ([ap:BNNUZ4]): a note carrying a recognised managed block (program_interface YAML, estate payloads, manifests, snapshot/ledger names, … -- detect_trail_skip_metadata over the registry) STILL moves/copies but writes NO trail line: the move path skips the trail write (tags-only edit when tags are wanted, zero second writes otherwise; trail_written stays false) and the derivative path bakes no '↩ derived from' line; the row's info field names the kind and row["trail_line"] keeps the would-be line for provenance. DERIVATIVE = ONE subtree ETCH (_node_etch_sync_impl) built from the pinned cache with a fresh AP core reserved for the root and every AP-bearing descendant BEFORE the create (zero transient duplicate AP-IDs), decoded wire text, the '↩ derived from … · source [ap:X] <uuid8>' line baked into the root note and the tags into the root name; completed descendants skipped unless include_completed (then re-completed after the create via list_nodes + complete_node); children:false copies the root alone; the source is never written. ARCHIVED SOURCE (U2, Axiom 6/G8): a derivative's source may be an archived node -- the one sanctioned copy that reads archived content: move skips it with the §5.2.1 + how-to-copy story (reason archived_node, archive provenance on the row), derivative copies the archive file's VERBATIM records via ArchiveStore.verbatim_subtree_records (original names/parents/priorities, no 📦, no marker; text served verbatim, never re-decoded, E7), mints fresh AP-IDs, names the ARCHIVE as the trail-line origin ('↩ derived from archive "name" (basename, exported date) · date · source <uuid8>'), never installs an overlay, never touches the file; an archived DESTINATION refuses with §5.2.3 as a skipped row. Ledger in input order + summary; success only when every row landed; partial_success on mixed outcomes.

Assembly point for the public Anchor family. Re-fronts Dock/Point primitives, verified-before-delete range extraction, bounded peek/render presets, the Dock-scoped grep (anchor.search -- the ONE shared note-grep tail over a Dock boundary walk), and collision-checked AP-ID allocation while the registry remains the sole dispatch/describe/schema/effects authority.

The one pure Stage-0 normalizer for the opaque Lightning render_lens selection. Parses the recursive LensSpec, makes query/query_mode/match_scope defaults explicit (an omitted match_scope defaults name-only for a recipe render, name_and_note for a sift query), and preserves path-bearing LensSpecError failures for every ingress surface.

Immutable Lens Stage-0 bundle welding the pure LensEvalContext to the exact cache mapping, copied group/config operands, active-group id, and raw config reply used for one projection. MCP and modal origins retain distinct transport rails but converge on this one snapshot shape.

The one transport-free Lens Stage-0 interpreter. It parses an already-read config reply, captures or accepts exactly one cache mapping, builds snapshot-backed group/root resolvers plus the Anchor Dock boundary, and returns the immutable _LensStage0Snapshot consumed by both MCP and modal origins.

Compatibility context-only seam over the MCP-origin Lens Stage-0 snapshot builder. Performs the existing one config read through _build_lens_stage0_snapshot and returns only its pure LensEvalContext for callers/tests that need the engine operand directly.

Transport-free shared LensSpec projection core. Both the MCP family path and the docked-modal handler inject one already-read Lens Stage-0 snapshot, then reuse this single normalize/evaluate/materialize/sift implementation so canonical adoption, leaf algebra, and cache identity cannot drift. Threads the surface match_scope as the default for lens atoms that omit their own (recipe render = the surface value, default name-only; sift = 'name' for tag atoms while the query keeps its own name_and_note scope). A sift query returns sift_predicate -- the ONE build_search_predicate instance that decided the sifted tree -- so the MCP grep tier classifies its documents with the SAME predicate. The result ALWAYS carries lens_scaffold_ids ([ap:I506WY]): lens_engine.lens_scaffold_ancestor_ids receives the final tree, per-atom resolved roots AND the SAME pinned cache, so only strict input-root ancestors outside every member region become scaffold even when an input root is absent from the final tree. Every lens tail forwards this set to the existing materializer cause; ancestor_notes is folded producer-side. No second suppression path.

Thin MCP-origin consumer of the shared render_lens projector. It performs the ordinary tab-agnostic config read, builds one Lens Stage-0 snapshot, delegates normalize/evaluate/materialize/sift to _project_render_lens_from_cache, then uses the shared Stage-2 render/file tail -- EXCEPT under the sift grep tier ([ap:47B7WO], grep_params set by slice_group.sift tier='context'): the branch after projection bypasses the Stage-2 composer and returns the ONE compact grep formatter's report over exactly the lens's admitted nodes, so selection is never re-decided and the report is node.search's shape by construction. No write, lease, refresh, job, Workflowy call or tab (it never reads the suppress list); computes no row, count or summary of its own.

Persist latched relevance and positive terminal evidence; reconcile restart reservations via existing identity authority, never omission or age.
Serialize before off-loop scan through conservative durable observation and exact final-batch extraction; only positive stop proofs reserve work, execution receipts discharge it.

Exact token/incarnation final obligation transition under admission.mutex; unmatched callbacks release neither durable responsibility nor the live attempt; publication requires new-fetch receipt and adoption.

Watcher and startup trigger adapter for the single A1 governance sweep; supplies configured grace/cooldown values, loud diagnostics, and claim-aware terminal/orphan auxiliary cleanup without introducing a parallel lifecycle loop.

F3/F2 ancestor-chain WS handler: virtual-UUID (mirror) parsing, /nodes-export cache fetch + dirty-ID advisory, shaped error frames — but the walk and the WHOLE Markdown grammar are delegated to ancestor_path.build_ancestor_path_document, the ONE shared core the node.ancestors MCP verb also calls, so the hotkey and the verb can never drift. The document carries dock.peek-vocabulary right-side markers (⚓ ⭐ Ⓛ ✓ + ▸N/desc/self/tree metrics) plus the 🗺️ mapped-folder / 📄 mapped-file markers with the key at the top, so this handler reads the configured Dock vocabulary via a nested get_extension_settings Direction-A read — which is why websocket_handler TASK-dispatches it (an inline await would deadlock the pump, the list_anchors_for_widget reason).

Derive a safe .md filename from a Workflowy node name for F12+4 materialize. Strips leading decoration/emoji, trailing #tags, illegal filename chars; collapses whitespace to underscores; guarantees a non-empty stem and a .md extension.

F12+4 leading-text fix: if the note's body (after optional YAML frontmatter) starts with prose BEFORE the first Markdown heading, synthesize a leading '# Leading text' H1 above that prose so the pre-heading text is not lost when the note is split into a heading subtree. No-op when the body already opens with a heading or is empty.

F12+4 hygiene: strip a LEADING Cartographer metadata block (MD_PATH: … --- or BEACON (…) … ---) from a node's note before materializing it to a .md. Needed because a Dump-Bay child that was already written back to the primary file via F12+3 carries such a block at the top of its note; without stripping it, that metadata would be written into the new .md as body content (and then split into bogus child nodes). Mirrors markdown_roundtrip._strip_md_path_block / _strip_md_ast_beacon_block but kept local to avoid importing module privates.

Bulk F12+4 helper: classify a node's note as a Cartographer FILE/FOLDER header. Returns ('Root'|'Path', value) or None using the strict first-line-only _extract_path_header_from_note. A folder/path node has a header whose value has no recognized file extension; a file node's value has one (e.g. .md/.py).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a Markdown file (.md/.markdown)? Used by the bulk walk + eligibility classifier to decide whether to recurse INTO a file node (markdown -> yes; any other extension -> skip+prune).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a FILE (has a filename extension) rather than a FOLDER segment? A folder node's Path: is a bare segment (no dot-extension); a file node's Path: ends in an extension. Used to distinguish path/folder nodes (recurse through) from file nodes (skip unless .md). Thin wrapper: the canonical implementation now lives in api_client_nexus (single source of truth, co-located with _extract_path_header_from_note + _classify_node_map_state); imported here via a function-scoped local import to avoid the api_client_nexus->server cycle, mirroring the other unguarded server->client local imports. NO inline fallback copy on purpose: a bool predicate has no safe 'unknown' value (returning False would mislabel a real file node as a folder and misroute the F12 menus), and if api_client_nexus is unimportable the whole server is non-functional anyway -- so we let the import raise loudly rather than keep a divergent second copy of the logic.

FIRST server-queried F12 menu-visibility check. Walks UP the nodes-export cache ancestor chain (zoom-proof, unlike the DOM) to classify the hovered node, then combines that with the client-reported visible/hidden child booleans to decide whether the F12+4 entry appears and which bulk sub-options enable. Returns {show, mode, visible_option_enabled, all_option_enabled, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+4 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_materialize). Reads node_id + has_visible_children/has_hidden_children from the payload, runs _classify_bulk_materialize_eligibility, and echoes the verdict back (with node_id for client-side correlation).

Zoom-proof resolver for F12+3: given ANY node_id, walk UP the /nodes-export cache ancestor chain (which never hides anything, unlike the zoomed-in DOM) to find the enclosing Markdown FILE node. If the node itself IS a markdown FILE node, returns it. Crucially IGNORES the md-in-md temp node's SECOND-line Path: (that node is never a reverse-Markdown target); the true primary file is the enclosing markdown FILE ancestor. Returns the FILE node's UUID, or None when no enclosing markdown file exists (e.g. inside a non-markdown file, or no file at all).

Cache-backed (zoom-proof) eligibility classifier for the BULK F12+3 menu entry. Decision tree is SIMPLER than F12+4 (no submenu for availability, no child-visibility input needed to decide SHOW): a markdown FILE node -> single F12+3 (mode='single', no bulk entry); a node INSIDE a mapped file -> no bulk entry (degenerates to standard single F12+3 on the enclosing file, which the server resolves zoom-safely); any node that is NOT a file node and NOT inside a file (a folder/Root: node OR a plain unmapped Workflowy node) -> bulk. Returns {show, mode, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+3 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_f12p3). Reads node_id, runs _classify_bulk_f12p3_eligibility, echoes the verdict {show,mode,reason,classification} back (with node_id for client-side correlation). No child-visibility input is needed (F12+3 bulk has no availability submenu).

Bulk F12+3 collection walk (source-agnostic, mirrors _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves plumbing). DFS over a tree (client visible-DOM payload OR nodes-export cache subtree) gathering MARKDOWN FILE nodes only. Per-node rules: a markdown FILE node QUALIFIES and we do NOT descend into it (F12+3 regenerates the whole file from its Workflowy subtree); a non-markdown FILE node is skipped+pruned; folder/Root: nodes and plain nodes are recursed THROUGH. Uses the universal first-line-only header classifier, so a md-in-md temp node (Path on line 2) is never mistaken for a file node. Returns ordered list of {id,name} file-node descriptors.

Bulk F12+3 execution handler (action=bulk_generate_markdown). Performs ONE gesture-level /nodes-export freshness read (L9 GESTURE) before any cache walk or child launch, builds the tree (walk_mode='visible' -> client visible_tree payload; 'all' -> cache subtree via _build_cache_subtree_for_bulk_materialize), runs _collect_bulk_f12p3_markdown_file_nodes to gather every Markdown FILE node, then fires ONE INDEPENDENT detached _start_carto_markdown_generate_job per file (N widget status lines, no parent coordinator -- per Dan). Every child consumes the one shared gesture snapshot and admits/claims its own region independently; this handler does not block.

WebSocket handler for the docked-modal SERVER render (action=render_markdown_modal). Direction-A request_id rail: composes Markdown STRING(s) on the server from a DOM/captured-tree payload: snapshot -> all row option-Y views, rows_only -> server-authored row list only, single -> one focus_leaf row, rows -> frozen-DOM multi-select minimal covering subtree via _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture. Echoes request_id. Never forces a /nodes-export refresh (detect+warn staleness). TASK-DISPATCHED from the reader loop (U4), and the three SYNCHRONOUS compose_markdown_modal_* calls run via asyncio.to_thread so a large compose cannot monopolize the event loop -- the task's S03 operation-boundary snapshot propagates into the thread (contextvars).

WebSocket handler for the slice-group copy button (action=compile_slice_search). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id). TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) so it can do a NESTED Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the ORIGINATING tab without deadlocking the single websocket_handler pump. Reads the live slice-group config from that tab, resolves the requested group_id (or active group), and compiles the Workflowy membership search string via the single Python compiler compile_slice_search_expression (#P -#P--deprecated OR ...). Replies compile_slice_search_result with request_id + expression.

WebSocket handler for the live F8 keypress (action=f8_expansion_plan). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id) carrying the visible DOM subtree. TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab to read the active slice group's prefixes + the live postfix config (one settings reader, no client-side policy). Then runs Phase 0 (validate_subtree_against_cache, fail-closed) and Phase 2 (build_expansion_plan) over the validated visible tree and replies f8_expansion_plan_result (echoing request_id) with {collapse_suppressed, collapse_deprecated, expand, warnings} for the client to execute mechanically. No fallback: on validation failure or no live tab it replies with an error the client surfaces loudly.

Apply-slice Tier-1 handler (action=render_slice_modal): the docked Markdown modal sourced from the CACHE-PROJECTED slice group instead of the live virtualized DOM. Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id); TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_f8_expansion_plan / _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab, which would deadlock the single websocket_handler pump if awaited inline. Resolves the requested slice group (by group_id, else active), then runs the SHARED cache-projection funnel build_stage1_base_tree (Phase 1 build_slice_subtree_from_cache -> Phase 2 build_expansion_plan -> Phase 3 apply_expansion_plan_to_subtree -> Phase 4 prune_collapsed_leaf_zombies) -- the EXACT SAME funnel _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache calls, so the Apply-slice modal and the slice-group GLIMPSE can never diverge on the projection (incl. the Phase-4 render-only zombie prune, the deliberate divergence from the live Workflowy expansion state) -- then _build_markdown_preview_from_tree (the SAME shared composer the live-DOM modal uses) with the _root_in_non_md_file_from_cache seed. Returns ONE Markdown STRING that is complete BY CONSTRUCTION (cache-sourced, not virtualized), so the dock can display it with no scroll/F8/refresh-dance and the client suppresses the scroll-to-bottom warning (cache_sourced=true). Replies render_slice_modal_result echoing request_id so the broker routes it to ONLY the originating tab. | Build the stable STRING key for a tree-view row's (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) identity triple, used both to key the Apply-slice SNAPSHOT map server-side and (echoed by the client on a row click) to select the exact occurrence in the SINGLE per-row path. NUL-joined ancestor_path so it cannot collide with a uuid; occurrence suffixed. Deterministic + pure -- the same row produces the same key on the original render and on any re-projection (MATCH = EMIT).

beacons.role: _compose_render_scope(kind, group_id, group_name, root_uuid, sort_by, sort_direction, since, headings_only)
beacons.comment: Build the SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE render_scope echo object for a cache-projected render. This is the ONE object every consumer (client adoptRenderScope -> per-tab render state + ribbon widgets + footer; and the MCP push tool output) treats as the normalized ground truth of what was ACTUALLY rendered, regardless of which SURFACE (ribbon click or MCP glimpse() call) triggered the render. Carries ONLY the normalized structured render-defining fields: scope identity (kind/group_id/group_name/root_uuid) + view params (sort_by/sort_direction/since object-or-null/headings_only). There is no pre-composed display string -- the status footer is the ONE consumer that renders a human string, composing it from THESE fields, so string-composition lives in exactly one place. kind is 'slice' (group at its own root), 'slice_override' (group tags scoped to an override root), 'raw_root' (bare root_uuid raw dump, no group -> the footer labels it 'raw dump of <root8>'), or 'lightning_rod' (a temporary Lightning Rod selection via the `lightning` param, which takes PRECEDENCE). LIGHTNING SELECTION: a lightning render carries ONE opaque `selection` object {mode:'gather'|'render_tags'|'render_search'|'render_symbols', + per-mode fields (tags+postfix_policy | query/query_mode | symbols/root_uuids/favor) + match_scope} that the client round-trips VERBATIM for BEHAVIOR (routing is by selection.mode, never selection_kind). selection_kind ('gather'|'tags'|'search'|'symbols') + workflowy_search_equivalent are DERIVED from selection.mode and are DISPLAY-ONLY (footer/status-bar label). UNMOORED SIGNAL: live_gui_sync_supported is a TOP-LEVEL bool emitted for EVERY kind (+ live_gui_sync_skipped_reason naming why when False) -- False for a raw dump (no membership search), a descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' render (inexpressible as a Workflowy search), a search_too_many_variants refusal, or any lightning selection; the client surfaces the unmoored state on the yellow bar. It is DISPLAY/observability only, never a behavior driver. EVERY kind also carries the explicit CONTENT/TREE CONTRACT fields content_format ('markdown'|'raw_text') + tree_mode ('render_tree'|'root_only') so the client never guesses how to paint the one rendered string or populate the top-half list (only a lightning GATHER is raw_text/root_only today). Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

Phase-E1 SPEC-AWARE BRIDGE to the ONE render_scope composer. Given a RESOLVED RenderProjectionSpec (kind/root/group already canonicalized by the caller's resolution step -- NOT the raw incoming spec), DELEGATE to _compose_render_scope by unpacking exactly the scalar params it already takes (Option A, Dan-decided: delegate, do NOT reimplement from spec.to_render_scope_fields(), so there stays ONE render_scope-assembly implementation and this never becomes a second scope factory / caller-side fabrication site). The is_raw_dump / root_overridden booleans the scalar composer wants are read straight off the spec's kind-derived properties (spec.is_raw_dump / spec.root_overridden), and sort_by is passed via spec.sort_by_internal() (the ONE wire-'none'<->internal-None translation). search_too_many_variants is a POST-RENDER fact (not a spec input field, per invariant 5) so it is threaded as an explicit kwarg here, exactly as the scalar composer already accepts it. This is the E1 seam that lets every downstream server call site (modal handler E3, content-return GLIMPSE paths E4, push frame E5) compose render_scope FROM the same spec it projected from, instead of from a parallel bag of locals -- the two-parallel-assembly-points seam Phase E removes. Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

The ONE inherited slice-group root policy seam shared by MCP/lens renders and every stored-root consumer (APPLY, copy-search, named merge, scoped reprojection, push and group purge). Delegates resolution to resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle with the caller's pinned map; exact UUIDs, clean prefixes including 8 hex, and AP-IDs are adopted with existing archive semantics. Corrective UUID shaves are rejected and only their speculative correction echo is discarded. Transport, scope notes and miss envelopes stay per-origin; explicit input roots keep the standard forgiving boundary.

PURE formatter for the ambiguous/missing error ENVELOPE returned by the cache-projection root_uuid resolution sites (the bare-root RAW-DUMP GLIMPSE, the slice-group override root, the push scope root, and Lightning Rod). Given a resolve_uuid_like_node_handle result that did NOT resolve (candidates present => ambiguous; else => missing), returns the standard {success:False, error, [candidates/matched_prefix_len/truncated], **extra} dict -- so the several sites can't DRIFT on the field set. Deliberately NOT a resolver wrapper: each caller keeps its own resolution and control flow (plain return vs await _reply) and its own error WORDING (via display/label); this only unifies the payload SHAPE. Chain-1 W4 (F5): in the MISSING branch, a refusal-reason operation (a sink, a write, an export, a purge preview) whose root names a visible archived node RAISES ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError with the exact §5.2/§5.3 text and provenance — before any file/modal/preview work; reads (reason None/flag) and no-context callers keep today's hint-only text. Returns None when the handle actually resolved (caller should not call it then). Pure; no I/O.

ONE handler for every cache-projected docked-modal render + per-row re-render (the 'Apply slice' feature). Resolves the four-cell scope truth table: slice (group_id), slice_override (group_id+root_uuid), raw_root (root_uuid only), lightning_rod (lightning{mode,...}; group-less, Phase-1-only via an injected member_predicate BY DEFAULT -- render_tags + postfix_policy='slice' (ap:IMPPTX) upgrades the cell to the shared build_stage1_base_tree funnel with one nested postfix config read). Lightning modes: gather (short-circuits to the raw-text tag outline), render_tags{tags} (DEFAULT: no config read; 'slice': one nested postfix config read), render_search{query,query_mode} (both scope via one frame root_uuid), and render_symbols{symbols,root_uuids,favor} (the tag-free beacon slice: roots via its own root_uuids -> their LCA, does one nested config read for the global-suppression filter, resolves via the shared _project_render_symbols_from_cache, and appends its unresolved/ambiguous report to the full-document reply), plus render_lens{lens,query?} (the recursive LensSpec cell: one nested config read, the shared immutable Stage-0 snapshot + transport-free _project_render_lens_from_cache, derived-LCA rooting, and explicit empty artifact). All five modes emit one opaque `selection` object into the render_scope. Then runs the shared projection -> prepare_stage2_render_forest -> rows -> snapshot-vs-single machinery and echoes the server-authoritative render_scope.

Bulk F12+4 qualification walk (source-agnostic). DFS over a tree (fed EITHER by the client visible-DOM payload OR the nodes-export cache subtree) applying the rules: recurse THROUGH folder/path nodes; into .md file nodes; SKIP+prune non-md file nodes; never qualify a node with children; qualify a childless non-path/non-file node iff its note (leading metadata block stripped) parses to >=1 markdown heading via _note_body_has_heading. Returns the ordered list of qualifying leaf descriptors.

Bulk F12+4 (mode B, recurse-all-incl-hidden) tree source: build a nested {id,name,note,children[]} subtree rooted at root_uuid directly from the /nodes-export cache, ignoring Workflowy expansion state entirely (like F12+3's synthetic-tree path). Returns the root node dict, or None if root not in cache.

Bulk F12+4 filename assignment. ONE accumulating pass over the full qualifying-leaf set: derive each leaf's stem (FILEBASE-ancestor prefix + sanitized node name, same logic as single-node F12+4) and resolve collisions against BOTH on-disk files AND already-assigned in-set names (siblings can share identical markdown headings). The in-set reservation makes prior leaves act as though already on disk so the integer-suffix increment is race-free and deterministic.

Bulk F12+4 execution handler (action=bulk_materialize_markdown). Builds the tree (mode='visible' -> client visible_tree payload; mode='all' -> cache subtree), runs _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves, assigns collision-safe filenames across the whole in-memory set FIRST (single accumulating process, race-free), then for EACH qualifying leaf writes the metadata-stripped note to its .md, sets the node note (Path: header for persist, dummy MD_PATH: block for in-md-file persist, or clears for temp), patches the snapshot, and fires an INDEPENDENT detached F12+1 job per leaf (N status lines, no parent coordinator -- per Dan).

Browser-initiated UUID Explorer anchor-list convenience endpoint. TASK-DISPATCHED because it delegates to the SAME list_anchors MCP tool wrapper, which performs a nested Direction-A get_extension_settings read; awaiting inline would deadlock the websocket pump. Replies list_anchors_for_widget_result with the exact list_anchors payload (global anchors only; local anchors suppressed by the shared server path) plus request_id for broker/tab correlation. Client formats it as UUID/name text and copies/displays it; no client-side anchor enumeration logic.

The ONE module-level coroutine the WS reader loop spawns (via create_isolated_context_task) for the long handlers whose inline failure frame was the generic {action, success:false, node_id, error} shape, instead of awaiting the handler inline: the two F12 refresh actions and (since U4) open_node_in_windsurf / materialize_markdown_file / bulk_materialize_markdown / bulk_generate_markdown. Awaits handler(data, websocket) inside the same try/except the inline clauses carried (log_event error line, then the best-effort failure frame), so the pump keeps servicing frames while a handler runs and a failed spawned handler still reports exactly as before. Handlers whose failure frames are shaped/correlated differently own their envelopes and spawn bare (the compile_slice_search precedent)

WebSocket handler for the widget's once-a-second CARTO jobs poll (action=carto_list_jobs), spawned by the pump through _carto_list_jobs_poll (single-flight + 0.5 s spacing: the reply is untargeted, so the broker broadcasts it to every tab and a coalesced poll loses nothing). Scans the job JSONs in a worker thread (asyncio.to_thread(_scan_carto_job_files)) so the pump never stalls, and sends only the rows the widget shows (drops exactly completed/cancelled, the widget's own filter). APPLY-Timeout fix: the old inline clause (0.25 s scan + multi-MB send per poll per tab) backlogged the pump until APPLY's nested config read timed out. Cache-free (tests/coherence_s03b_registry.json); same carto_list_jobs_result wire shapes and error log line as before

WebSocket handler for the widget's 'Clear job history' sweep (action=carto_clear_job_history). U4 (WS reader loop): the inline clause body LIFTED VERBATIM into a module-level coroutine so the pump can spawn it via create_isolated_context_task -- the sweep deletes terminal job JSONs/logs/folders (disk I/O that can take a moment with a long history) and must not hold the reader loop. Cache-free by classification (tests/coherence_s03b_registry.json ws_actions.cache_free -- job-file GC only), so it carries NO @_ws_cache_boundary, exactly like the inline clause it replaced. Owns its shaped carto_clear_job_history_result success/failure frames (no node_id/request_id correlation on this action -- unchanged wire shape)

WebSocket handler for the widget's per-job CANCEL button (action=carto_cancel_job). U4 (WS reader loop): the inline clause body LIFTED VERBATIM into a module-level coroutine so the pump can spawn it via create_isolated_context_task -- cancellation runs the sentinel-first controller (durable sentinel write, cooperative claim/PID poll, terminate-to-kill escalation) whose awaits must not hold the reader loop. Cache-free by classification (tests/coherence_s03b_registry.json ws_actions.cache_free -- cancellation sentinel only), so it carries NO @_ws_cache_boundary, exactly like the inline clause it replaced. Delegates to the SAME _system_job_cancel_impl the system.job.cancel MCP verb uses; owns its shaped carto_cancel_job_result frames (unchanged wire shape)
Shared FastMCP registration seam for every published tool in both profiles: merge the Claude Code 500000-character result declaration without changing unrelated metadata or execution

Import-time FastMCP registration gate: active profiles register through _workflowy_tool (including the shared large-result catalog metadata) while inactive profiles receive a type-compatible identity decorator

S03-CR-03 legacy-profile boundary migration: the selectable 'legacy' MCP profile is a first-class migrated surface — every cache-backed legacy tool is wrapped in ONE journal-adoption cache_operation_boundary at FastMCP registration (never a boundaryless loud failure, never a fail-soft cache-less render); cache-free legacy tools (system.* and slice-group CRUD equivalents per LEGACY_TOOL_MAPPING) keep zero-coherence-work contracts. Profile-inactive behavior is the unchanged identity decorator.

S03-CR-03 legacy-profile boundary migration: the selectable 'legacy' MCP profile is a first-class migrated surface — every cache-backed legacy tool is wrapped in ONE journal-adoption cache_operation_boundary at FastMCP registration (never a boundaryless loud failure, never a fail-soft cache-less render); cache-free legacy tools (system.* and slice-group CRUD equivalents per LEGACY_TOOL_MAPPING) keep zero-coherence-work contracts. Profile-inactive behavior is the unchanged identity decorator. S04: the same shared hard-stop admission gate and read advisory apply here too (resolved mode-aware through LEGACY_TOOL_MAPPING), with the legacy typed failure shape for refusals. S04 Remediation Chain 5 (expanded item 3): the canonical lookup is repaired (derived from LegacyToolMapping.routes — the gate is now LIVE for every legacy mutation tool) and the read advisory is shaped INSIDE the boundary while the captured status is live, with the glimpse/lightning_rod family skip (internal render seams own provenance). 9a ([ap:G2UALX]): the ONE empty-output stub (stub_empty_text_result) runs on the raw handler result BEFORE the advisory, so the legacy surface delivers the literal '(empty)' exactly as the consolidated funnel does.

Admission footprint derivation for CARTO launches. S03-CR-04: one operation, one generation — when an operation boundary is active the footprint derives from the operation's PINNED view (the same generation that resolved and classified the target), never from the freshness selection's newer cache_by_id; the selection map remains the no-boundary fallback. Job-basis freshness (the selection lineage the worker adopts at current head) is deliberately a separate concern from admission-time topology.

S04 §7.2 hard-stop admission for CARTO launches: every CARTO job family may mutate Workflowy, so all three server-side launch seams (detached refresh, markdown generate, in-process bulk apply) plus the phase-8 continuation refuse under the hard barrier BEFORE any job artifact, admission, or freshness work — the refusal uses the established error_kind idiom so every F12/WS/MCP ingress echoes it unchanged.

Thin server compatibility wrapper over the dependency-light shared CARTO_REFRESH launch authority; supplies credentials, explicit snapshot freshness, and path/graph footprint resolution while preserving structured governance_cleanup_required launch failures unchanged; S03B Chain-3 (W1): wraps every prepared callback in ONE execution-site cache_operation_boundary (the isolated prepared task's only operation boundary, entered via prepared_runner after obtain_freshness); S04 Remediation Chain 2: the wrapped callback rechecks the shared require_coherence_mutation_admission authority AFTER boundary adoption + freshness, immediately before preparation side effects — refusal persists typed coherence_barrier_active diagnostics, finalizes the exact claim, and never spawns the worker.
Whitens visible-DOM vs cache text for spurious-UPDATE detection in F12 bulk-apply pre-pass; tied to F12+3 timeout investigation

Helper that compares visible Workflowy DOM against /nodes-export cache; deliberately NOT used as bulk-apply pre-filter (see comment in _collect_bulk_visible_apply_groups). Always returned True after refresh and caused F12+2 nothing-happens bug.

Bulk-apply candidate filter for F12+3 step [3] pre-pass. Tightened May 2026 to require either an existing BEACON block OR trailing #tags - excludes plain MD_PATH-only heading nodes that cannot possibly need a disk write.
Universal trailing-#tag detector shared by Class 1 (AST_QUALNAME) and Class 3 (MD_PATH) of the bulk-visible-apply candidate filter. Same shape recognized by split_name_and_tags.

Bulk-visible-apply candidate filter. Class 1 (AST) and Class 3 (Markdown) both require a trailing #tag when no BEACON metadata block is present in the note. Class 2 admits any node whose note already carries a real BEACON block. See May 18 2026 archaeological-dig commentary for the full reasoning (new-paradigm name-tag-as-source-of-truth).

Bulk-apply pre-filter for F12+3 step [3]. Detects nodes whose name #tags + decoration-stripped base text already match the BEACON (MD AST) block in their own note and skips them - avoiding the ~480ms-per-call cost of update_beacon_from_node_markdown's full MarkdownIt parse on a fully-synced file.

ASCII-folding normalizer for the in-sync filter's role: comparison. Must be applied to BOTH the Workflowy NAME-derived role text AND the on-disk BEACON block's role: line so semantically-equal strings (smart-quote vs ASCII, & vs &) compare equal.

beacons.role: ⚡ _bulk_apply_per_file_inner_loop(client: Any, candidate_nodes, file_name: str, summary, cancel_check, log, progress_tick)
beacons.comment: Single-source-of-truth implementation of the F12+2/F12+3 bulk-apply per-candidate inner loop. Called from BOTH _run_carto_bulk_visible_apply_job (server.py) and run_bulk_apply_inline (markdown_generate_pipeline.py) to eliminate the duplicate-codepath gotcha that hid the original Bug #2 fix from F12+3 until a follow-up patch was needed.
Build bulk-visible-apply root tree from F12+3 payload (visible_tree+root+children) before _collect_bulk_visible_apply_groups walk

Walk visible tree and group bulk-apply candidates by enclosing FILE node. NOTE: deliberately NO pre-filter via _visible_node_differs_from_cache (see inline comment); every candidate flows through update_beacon_from_node_<lang>. KEY DIAGNOSTIC FOR F12+3 TIMEOUT: this is where ~533 candidates get fanned out per refresh.

Async runner for F12+3 step [3] bulk-apply pre-pass.
