Accepts any handle form (exact UUID | its 8-hex first segment | a unique longer prefix | [ap:CORE], UUID-first with the AP-ID leg on unresolved fall-through) through the ONE shared resolve_node_identity_record (which wraps the ONE prefix kernel — no second resolver), against the operation's pinned cache map, and returns the unified non-raising 0/1/N record: on a unique match the node's full identifier vocabulary {short, uuid, ap_id} at the top level ('no anchor point available' in words when the node carries none), every candidate row carrying its vocabulary on ambiguity. A resolve is for citations/records — never needed before an ordinary handle call: every handle parameter already accepts all the forms directly.

node.ancestors: the extension's F3 ancestor chain as a real MCP verb — 'where does this node live in the full document, and is it inside a mapped file/folder?'. Pure cache read through the existing operation boundary (NO new transport): resolve handle against the pinned snapshot, walk + compose via ancestor_path.build_ancestor_path_document (the ONE core the F3/F2 WS handler delegates to, so the two homes can never drift; the WS frame-sending _resolve_uuid_path_and_respond is NEVER called from here), Dock-marker vocabulary via the ONE established Direction-A config read (skipped entirely when markers=false). detail='compact' returns the raw Markdown document (key line + chain + → uuid tail); detail='full' adds structured rows (title/tags/dock flags/completed/map_state/metrics + ap_id via the ONE shared leading-AP splitter) beside the same markdown.

beacons.role: ⚡ lightning_rod(mode, root_uuid, tags, query, query_mode, tag_match, postfix_policy, as_markdown, sort_by, sort_direction, headings_only, since, output_file)
beacons.comment: LIGHTNING ROD public MCP tool. Thin wrapper over the internal _lightning_rod_from_cache orchestrator: rate-limit acquire, then dispatch. Modes: gather (discover tags under a root -> feeds render_tags), render_tags (Option-B prefix-family tag filter; NO deprecation/suppress/expand semantics by DEFAULT -- the opt-in postfix_policy='slice' (ap:IMPPTX) instead routes it through the FULL Stage-1 funnel build_stage1_base_tree with the live postfix words + the real f8_global_never_expand_tags list), render_search (shlex 'smart' boolean/glob OR 'regex' free-text filter), render_symbols (dynamic tag-free beacon slice from a UUID/symbol/AP-ID list). Mutation modes: ensure_beacons/remove_beacon_tags (Q3 DISK beacons) and mutate_node_tags (Q4 batch Workflowy #tag add/remove/rename on NODES by UUID/[ap:CORE] handle -- operations-only; a thin ledger wrapper over the per-node tag primitives). Render modes are cache-only; no WebSocket (except one postfix config read for render_tags 'slice'), no slice-group persistence, no Workflowy-UI. Shared render knobs mirror glimpse and flow through render_stage2_filter_sort. since='curated' rejected (no slice tag set); live-GUI-sync never supported. The traversal pair rides the shared selection fragment ([ap:EPR86W] 4b): the walking verbs (gather/render_tags/render_search) carry recursive+descend_policy, and recursive=False is refused LOUDLY at the top of this body -- before the push branch, so a pushed selection cannot silently drop the request (one refusal text with the orchestrator's backstop, _lightning_recursive_refusal). The grammar docstring here is the AGENT-FACING interface (the caller is an LLM building the query from natural language, so it is small+explicit+deterministic with normative examples). PUSH-TO-MODAL: push_to_modal=True + target_tab route through the SAME _glimpse_push_slice_to_modal channel the GLIMPSE tool uses (the 4th push scope cell -> apply_slice_in_dock carrying a `lightning` scope -> the ONE shared applySliceGroupIntoDock apply path), so a pushed Lightning Rod render is identical to a ribbon-triggered one; as_markdown/output_file are inapplicable to a push (returns a small ack, not content). Only the injected predicate (or, under postfix_policy='slice', the shared funnel) differs from the other cache-projection + push scopes -- the same universal pipeline.

Canonical Node-family ETCH front. Selects the existing synchronous or asynchronous ETCH primitive, standardizes sync mutation acknowledgements, and converts async legacy job handles into the shared family job envelope without changing ETCH payload semantics.

Canonical Tag-family batch front. Reuses the one Q4 operations normalizer and the existing preflight-all-then-commit Lightning Rod tag orchestrator, preserving its complete ledger and batch-gating semantics.

Node-as-a-file paged grep front: single-node search delegates to the existing ONE live read and decoder; subtree search consumes the operation-pinned canonical map and established ordered scope walker, never live publisher state or per-descendant GETs, and hides completed nodes (plus their descendants) by default -- the dock.peek/render default; include_completed opts back in; suppressed nodes and child Docks stay included (search is a grep). The query is the ONE span matcher compile_note_query; the report is the ONE compact grep formatter search_note_documents (ripgrep-style rows, match_width/context_width crops, occurrences in the footer), which also owns the all-caps pagination banner that opens every multi-page report (the Source line rides the formatter's header_line slot, below the banner); each call uses the standard family boundary/finalizer for adoption and advisories. _note_grep_plan delegates grep values/defaults/bounds AND the [ap:O3MDOY] match controls (sort_by orders the node groups; recent='last N'/'newest N' keeps the N newest matching NODES by resolve_item_count_basis -- trimmed ones counted in the footer; max_nodes caps matching nodes distinct from the matched-line cap; ranking is dock_peek_metrics.apply_dock_peek_recency, the ONE idiom) to the ONE _normalize_note_grep_params; node.search/anchor.search/sift schemas share _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties. lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' ([ap:2EG7TD], landed) calls both owners too -- through the SAME _render_sift_grep_result tail (CF-30, no third producer). The plan keeps literal/regex query compilation and the report tail (_note_grep_report) stays shared with anchor.search. No retained snapshot, cache writes, transport fork, or renderer.

Assembly point for the consolidated public Node family. Thin handlers re-front lifecycle primitives, node-as-a-file read/search, and AP-aware leading-emoji mutations while the registry remains the sole authority for canonical verbs, role-named handles, transition aliases, schemas, effects, async metadata, and describe output.
Config-only Slice Group deletion. Resolves through the shared id/prefix/name resolver, clears active_group_id atomically when needed, persists once, and never touches Workflowy tags.

Recursive LensSpec merge persistence orchestrator. Evaluates once against the immutable S06 T1 snapshot, materializes the authoritative tree, preflights reproducibility/identity/collisions, reuses the shipped plan-simulate-Q4-verify compiler, then performs a fresh T2 config identity check and atomic create/reuse update.

Shared low-level/group-aware purge apply orchestrator. Recomputes and fingerprint-gates the preview, refuses shared families by default, delegates exact removals to Q4, rebuilds the eager-patched cache, and verifies no mutable family occurrence remains.

Assembly point for the consolidated public Tag family. Six operations preserve surgical single-node primitives, the complete batch ledger, and the fingerprint-gated purge workflow while the registry owns canonical verbs, aliases, schemas, effects, and describe output.

Shared Anchor-Dock root guard behind the two IN-BAND full-dump returns (node.scry and the bare-root_handle glimpse raw dump). Resolves the handle (UUID / unique prefix / [ap:CORE]) and classifies the root node's NAME tags against ONE welded snapshot (the resolver's echoed cache map + ONE live Dock-vocabulary read, optionally injected so the stop_at_child_anchors boundary shares it). Verdicts: root IS an Anchor Dock (global or local) -> raise _AnchorDockRootDetected with a peek/render teaching message; root ABSENT from the cache -> raise _FullDumpRootCacheMiss (FAIL CLOSED -- an unclassifiable in-band full-dump root is refused, never allowed to fall through to the API subtree fetch; the message points at system.cache.refresh); otherwise return {resolved, anchor_vocabulary} so the caller's downstream resolution and boundary predicate reuse the same operands. The live extension-settings WS read is FIRST-CLASS (the historical 'scry never touches the WebSocket' doctrine is retracted: node CONTENTS come from the cache/API, the Dock-tag VOCABULARY from the tab; a failed config read is loud, never a silent skip). Out-of-band deliveries (output_file, push_to_modal) are exempt by caller placement, never by this helper; allow_anchor_dock=true skips the guard wholesale at each caller.

Pure six-character uppercase-base36 AP-ID generator. Retries against an injected collision predicate and fails loudly after the bounded attempt budget; allocation locking and reservation live in the caller.

beacons.role: ƒ _render_dock_peek_raw_text(dock_name, root_note, rows, show_ids, show_counts, show_description, max_chars, max_description_chars, root_metrics, recursive, descend_policy, selection, sort, root_uuid, uuid_prefix_collisions, parent_handles)
beacons.comment: Pure compact Dock-peek serializer. One globally padded AP-only column over visible rows; blank for missing APs, no column if none. Names are shown in full (trailing #tags included) -- max_chars is an opt-in middle-ellipsis budget, 0/None = unlimited. The Dock's own '> …' description excerpt is budgeted SEPARATELY (max_description_chars, default 256, CF-MST-015; the name budget never touches it and show_description=false still suppresses it entirely). Only the trimmed body indents (four spaces per real node depth) and only while the rows are the plain document-order walk: a recent-N selection or a timestamp sort renders FLAT (a timestamp order is not a tree order), and UTAERZ shows the nesting per row there instead -- one ' ← in ‹parent handle›' hint (the parent's [ap:CORE], else its short UUID) on every row whose parent is not the peeked Dock (parent_handles is the impl's precomputed map; depth stays in the JSON). The header names the selection/order, including 'N completed hidden' whenever the default completed-exclusion removed rows (recency views AND the plain inventory alike, U6/J11); under a recent-N selection [ap:TVIIBN] 4e adds ONE explicit rule line directly below the header (describe_dock_peek_recency_rule, the peek-side twin of the render verbs' _recency_header_sentence): sort_direction only orders the selected rows, it never changes which rows were chosen. Row handles ([ap:0M6VP8] peek half): rows without an AP-ID show a bracketed short UUID handle in the body by default; show_ids=true adds it to every row; both route through the ONE shortener unique_short_uuid_prefix over the caller's uuid_prefix_collisions index (CF-22/O3), never a second shortener. Four source metrics and Dock/favorite/local/completed flags (marker order ⚓ ⭐ Ⓛ ✓; ⭐ only on a Dock row) with a policy-aware legend. No acquisition, source mutation, document rendering or traversal decisions.

Pure compact serializer for slice_group.list: one raw-text nested outline of the persisted slice groups. Rows come from build_slice_group_display_items -- the exact Python twin of the client's buildNestedDisplayItems (auto-vivified synthetic categories, the lowest-indexed canonical expander owning descendants, duplicate expander rows marked ' ⚠ duplicate category', null-index-last case-insensitive ordering, every category expanded). Category rows are bare '▾ name' (organizational; no ID, and hidden category-group tags are never exposed); leaf rows are '[<bare 8-hex group prefix>] short-name — up to 4 #tags (+N more) ✅' (✅ on the active group only). The header counts every stored record and ends detail='full' for JSON. Pure; no I/O.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_list_impl(include_local, target_tab, detail, max_chars, favorites_only, max_description_chars, show_description)
beacons.comment: Anchor Dock inventory front. detail='compact' (THE default everywhere -- consolidated registry, impl, and the legacy list_anchors delegate) returns ONE raw-text inventory string from one _list_anchors_internal(tree_view=True) acquisition, serialized by the ONE shared _render_anchor_tree_raw_text compact mode; detail='full' is the explicit escape hatch returning the established structured payload (rows gain is_favorite; the favorites echo keys ride along). favorites_only defaults TRUE HERE (the public shortlist default; _list_anchors_internal and the legacy tool stay False): the ⭐ favorites shortlist with the zero-favorites fallback, compact header counts taken from the echoed shown_global_count/shown_local_count so the arithmetic is correct under favorites. Row descriptions ([ap:YLHDIN] part 2): every compact row carries the Dock's FIRST description line as a ' — excerpt' tail (show_description=true default; max_description_chars budgets it, default 120, 0 hides; the same metadata-stripped text the structured rows carry). An inventory serializer, never a document render: no RenderProjectionSpec, no Stage 1/2, no composer.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_create_impl(topic, description, parent_handle, local, extra_tags, target_tab, favorite)
beacons.comment: Dock-create front: description is OPTIONAL (VBIKIZ) and defaults to empty -- the registry (not this impl) owns the name=topic / note=description aliases via param_aliases. Creates via client.create_note_session, so no tag-write path exists.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_update_impl(dock_handle, topic, description, local, target_tab, favorite, families)
beacons.comment: Atomic Dock update front. All name work goes through _node_edit_core + the ONE protected-name composer from ONE live GET snapshot (title, AP-ID, and the tag list the attribute transform rewrites never mix cache/live). Topic follows the public protected-name rules (supplied tags/AP changes rejected) and preserves the Dock's existing leading emoji run (Z8Q0PF+LITF2F: the caller need not pass an emoji; a supplied topic run wins explicitly; replace_emoji=True hands the run to the supplied topic wholesale -- its run replaces the existing one, its absence clears it; the SAME composed name is computed for the no-op/name_changed verdict and the write, so the two composer calls can never disagree); explicit local/favorite attribute writes are the ONLY tag rewrite, delivered via the narrow _tag_transform channel as a per-FAMILY set/unset-ONE-attribute transform (I6/I7): for each targeted family it removes ONLY that family's proper tags and re-inserts one canonical tag per remaining attribute (fixed order local, favorite; existing words preserved; bare base when the last attribute is unset -- Dock identity is never deleted), leaving every other family's tags, every --deprecated tag, every unknown-postfix tag and every unrelated tag byte-for-byte in place. NEVER canonicalises to base_tags[0] (the old family-switch bug). families= names the family to write when the node carries more than one (dock_families_ambiguous otherwise; a family without a proper tag on the node is dock_family_not_on_node; --deprecated-only does not count as present). Zero writes on any validation error. One live GET, at most one write.

anchor.dock.get_description: the Dock-description getter (TODO [ap:YLHDIN] part 1, Dan's "get description") as a thin Dock-checked PRESET over the ONE metadata header -- it resolves against the pinned cache, checks Dock-hood with the same classify_anchor_tags matcher the dock mutation verbs use (a non-Dock is a loud not_an_anchor_dock teaching error pointing at anchor.point.read), counts DIRECT child Docks through build_dock_peek_index's priority-ordered child lists classified by the ONE boundary predicate (build_anchor_boundary_predicate), then delegates to _anchor_point_read_impl with extra_header_lines=("child docks: N",) -- the ONE header composer serves both verbs; no second metadata header exists. The description (the note) rides the getter UNGUARDED and untruncated: fetching the description is the point (dock.peek's compact excerpt budgets it at 256 and detail='full' carries it whole -- the same norm). The vocabulary read fails loudly with no Workflowy tab (dock.peek's rule): the Dock check itself needs it. Pure read.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_peek_impl(dock_handle, target_tab, detail, show_ids, show_counts, show_description, max_chars, recursive, descend_policy, recent, recent_by, sort_by, sort_direction, include_completed)
beacons.comment: Dock-peek read-only inventory front: existing one config read/resolver/pinned map and owned source-metrics index. Direct children remain default; recursive=true uses real node depth and stops at nested Docks unless descend_policy='all' explicitly opens them (global and local alike). Rows carry the FULL node name verbatim (trailing #tags included; title/tags split alongside), the item's own created_at/modified_at, and parent_id (UTAERZ: the walked parent, so the flat recent/timestamp compact view shows a per-row ' ← in ‹parent handle›' hint for rows whose parent is not the peeked Dock; document order keeps indentation and no hints). Row handles ([ap:0M6VP8] peek half): rows without an AP-ID show a bracketed short UUID handle in the body by default; show_ids=true adds it to every row -- both through the ONE shortener unique_short_uuid_prefix over a build_uuid_prefix_collisions index built once per call from the same pinned cache map (CF-22/O3; parent hints use the same authority, the parent's [ap:CORE] when it carries one). recent=N selects the N newest walked rows on recent_by (default modified) and sort_by/sort_direction order the whole inventory -- one pure policy (apply_dock_peek_recency) applied between the walk and BOTH renderers so compact and detail='full' select identical items; neither knob given = document order, unchanged. Completed rows are marked but HIDDEN by default on EVERY view -- recency, timestamp sort, and the plain document-order inventory alike (U6/J11; include_completed=true opts back in) -- the filter lives solely inside the policy. detail='full' additionally carries the Dock's untruncated one-line 'description'; the compact '> …' excerpt budgets it at 256 chars. Totals always cover the full subtree. No new live reads, mutation claims, cache publication, renderer or broker path.

anchor.search: a node.search-shaped grep scoped to ONE Anchor Dock's subtree. Acquisition is dock.peek's own pattern -- the ONE note-session config read (the live Dock vocabulary; loud with no tab, like dock.peek), the generic handle resolver, the pinned operation cache -- then the ONE generic Stage-1 walk build_selected_subtree_from_cache with member_all=True, the shared build_anchor_boundary_predicate (descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' default stops at child Docks; each child Dock's own name/note is still searched as a signpost; 'all' enters them) and exclude_completed (completed nodes hidden by default, root exempt -- node.search's own default; include_completed opts back in). Documents from _anchor_scope_documents feed the ONE shared grep tail (_note_grep_plan + _note_grep_report + note_lines.search_note_documents): query machinery identical to node.search (literal or is_regex line-local, context_lines/context_width/match_width, matched-LINE offset/max_matches paging with the all-caps banner). _note_grep_plan delegates grep values/defaults/bounds AND the [ap:O3MDOY] match controls (sort_by/sort_direction/recent/recent_by/max_nodes -- node-level: recent keeps the N newest matching nodes, hidden ones counted in the footer; max_nodes caps matching nodes) to _normalize_note_grep_params; the registry takes the ONE schema fragment _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties, shared with node.search/sift/render_search. lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' ([ap:2EG7TD], landed) calls both owners too. match_scope ('name_and_note' default, sift's vocabulary) picks WHAT the query reads: name_and_note = note lines plus the TITLE (a title-only match renders its header row with the D6 '(title match)' marker -- the formatter drops the marker when note lines also hit); 'name' = title rows only (the document carries no note, so the shared formatter cannot leak note rows). No second formatter, second matcher, second walk, second vocabulary reader or second ranking idiom exists.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_render_impl(dock_handle, sort_by, sort_direction, recent, headings_only, as_markdown, output_file, push_to_modal, target_tab)
beacons.comment: Named raw-root GLIMPSE preset for an Anchor Dock. Reuses the existing root projection/modal-push paths while mapping the public most-recent token `recent` (legacy `tail`/`since` accepted as silent aliases at the registry) to the existing SinceSpec edge. [ap:EPR86W] part a: carries the traversal pair with EXACTLY dock.peek's names and values (defaults differ by design: recursive=True, descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' -- today's behavior unchanged); recursive=False renders the Dock + its DIRECT children (child Docks and plain nodes alike) and nothing deeper, with descend_policy moot, on both the content path (max_depth=1 through the ONE shared walker) and the push path (the flag rides the pushed spec blob).

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_point_capture_impl(parent_handle, nodes, tags, target_tab, note_file, content, name, ap_id)
beacons.comment: Canonical Anchor Point capture front. Preserves all guarded add_to_anchor payload/tag behavior and optionally reserves plus injects a collision-checked AP-ID before the one ETCH, preventing post-create partial state.

MOVE-only single/batch note-range extraction. ONE live source snapshot and the shared note_lines planner; captures run in document order through _anchor_point_capture_impl, EVERY success/root-id acknowledgement is checked before ONE whole-note _node_edit_core call with the original snapshot injected. No direct cache edits or parallel mutation transport. Failure ledger distinguishes source-not-written from an uncertain update outcome and preserves typed coherence refusals.

Assign a collision-checked AP-ID to an existing point via the narrow _assign_ap_core channel of _node_edit_core -- the composer's assign leg preserves the existing title and trailing tags automatically (no more raw prefix-string splice). Existing IDs are never replaced; a process-local lock plus reservation ledger closes same-server allocation races.

Dedicated idempotent AP-ID removal path. Resolves the node handle before mutation (so the AP-ID itself may be used to target the node), performs one live structured read, then delegates through _node_edit_core's narrow _remove_ap_id channel using that SAME snapshot. The pure composer removes only the leading AP token while preserving leading decoration, ordinary title, trailing tags, and one-layer entity semantics. Returns the removed handle + a loud citation-invalidation warning; an AP-less node is a true no-op with zero write. The removed core is deliberately NOT released from the process-local allocation ledger -- immediate same-process reuse would make old citations resolve to the wrong node.

anchor.point.resolve: the AP-ID-first identity resolve ([ap:CZ95R6]) through the ONE shared resolve_node_identity_record (prefer='anchor_point': the AP leg runs first, the UUID leg only on unresolved fall-through, so a UUID / 8-hex handle resolves here too and a bare base36 core that is also hex stays AP-domain first). Established 0/1/N shape preserved for the live consumers (success/match_count/candidates/resolved_ap_id), now with the unified identifier vocabulary {short, uuid, ap_id} at the top level on a unique match and per candidate row ('no anchor point available' when a node carries none). Never needed before an ordinary call: every handle parameter accepts an AP-ID directly.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_point_read_impl(node_handle, offset, limit, with_line_numbers, view, target_tab, extra_header_lines)
beacons.comment: anchor.point.read: node.read with Anchor usability defaults — metadata header over the LIVE note through _read_live_node_note (ONE rate-limited fetch/decode) and snippet_view.render_note_body (ONE guard/window/number/exact body), with validate_note_read_lines before I/O and normalize_note_view_params at the public front. Numbered by default; guard 400, size_only = header plus size line; no output_file/as_raw_node. Header metadata still uses the resolver's echoed pinned map, walk_ancestor_chain/build_ancestor_path_document/node_timestamp, peek markers and source metrics, dates, 8-hex handle and path. Dock vocabulary still degrades VISIBLY with no tab; ✓/🗺️/📄 need no tab. Only the framing and defaults differ from node.read. extra_header_lines (internal channel, anchor.dock.get_description only) splices Dock-only lines directly under the name/metrics line -- the ONE header composer serves both verbs.

anchor.point.touch: ordered batch, content-preserving modifiedAt advance so a chosen working set surfaces FIRST in dock.peek recent_by='modified'. handles[0] = highest priority = newest afterwards, achieved by touching in REVERSE input order, one governed write per item (~1 s each) through _node_edit_core's narrow _touch channel (layoutMode echo, name-identity fallback; never composes text). Preflight: duplicate handles (literal or same resolved UUID) = batch REFUSE, zero writes; unresolvable / not-in-cache / mapped (non-'unmapped' _classify_node_map_state -- disk is truth) / Anchor Dock (unless allow_docks) = per-item SKIP, batch continues. Execution: live GET before, write, verify content fingerprint unchanged and modifiedAt strictly increasing (one re-touch after a short sleep on a tie); an unknown write outcome, a content change or a non-advancing timestamp STOPS the batch (remaining rows not_run, never re-sent). Complete ledger in INPUT order + summary with order_established; success only when every row touched; partial_success on mixed outcomes.

beacons.role: ⚡ _anchor_point_promote_impl(items, handles, destination, tags, mode, children, include_completed, target_tab)
beacons.comment: anchor.point.promote: the curation pass made atomic -- batch move-with-provenance (mode: move, default) and promote-as-COPY (mode: derivative). Two grammars (items=[{handle, destination, tags?, mode?, children?}] | handles=[...] + destination + tags? + mode? + children?) normalized by the pure normalize_promote_items before any I/O. Per item: resolve handle + destination through the generic resolver against ONE pinned cache map; origin = nearest ancestor Anchor Dock (global or local; else the immediate parent) via nearest_anchor_dock_ancestor; STRUCTURAL mapped-node refusal on source AND destination (_classify_node_map_state != 'unmapped' -- stricter than capture's guard, Markdown included) plus the first-line Cartographer-metadata content check (delegated to the ONE managed-metadata registry, managed_metadata.py). Batch grammar modelled on beacon.tags.ensure: per-item SKIP (unresolvable, not in cache, mapped) continues; batch REFUSE with zero writes (malformed, duplicate handles literal or same resolved UUID, destination inside the source's own subtree); STOP on any ambiguous post-send outcome (remaining rows not_run, nothing re-sent). MOVE = _node_move_impl(src, dest, 'bottom') + ONE _node_edit_core(note=trail+old, _tag_transform=add, _current_node=live) = 2 governed writes; the trail line '↩ moved from <origin> (<uuid8>) · <date>' is plain text, newest on top. MANAGED METADATA ([ap:BNNUZ4]): a note carrying a recognised managed block (program_interface YAML, estate payloads, manifests, snapshot/ledger names, … -- detect_trail_skip_metadata over the registry) STILL moves/copies but writes NO trail line: the move path skips the trail write (tags-only edit when tags are wanted, zero second writes otherwise; trail_written stays false) and the derivative path bakes no '↩ derived from' line; the row's info field names the kind and row["trail_line"] keeps the would-be line for provenance. DERIVATIVE = ONE subtree ETCH (_node_etch_sync_impl) built from the pinned cache with a fresh AP core reserved for the root and every AP-bearing descendant BEFORE the create (zero transient duplicate AP-IDs), decoded wire text, the '↩ derived from … · source [ap:X] <uuid8>' line baked into the root note and the tags into the root name; completed descendants skipped unless include_completed (then re-completed after the create via list_nodes + complete_node); children:false copies the root alone; the source is never written. ARCHIVED SOURCE (U2, Axiom 6/G8): a derivative's source may be an archived node -- the one sanctioned copy that reads archived content: move skips it with the §5.2.1 + how-to-copy story (reason archived_node, archive provenance on the row), derivative copies the archive file's VERBATIM records via ArchiveStore.verbatim_subtree_records (original names/parents/priorities, no 📦, no marker; text served verbatim, never re-decoded, E7), mints fresh AP-IDs, names the ARCHIVE as the trail-line origin ('↩ derived from archive "name" (basename, exported date) · date · source <uuid8>'), never installs an overlay, never touches the file; an archived DESTINATION refuses with §5.2.3 as a skipped row. Ledger in input order + summary; success only when every row landed; partial_success on mixed outcomes.

Assembly point for the public Anchor family. Re-fronts Dock/Point primitives, verified-before-delete range extraction, bounded peek/render presets, the Dock-scoped grep (anchor.search -- the ONE shared note-grep tail over a Dock boundary walk), and collision-checked AP-ID allocation while the registry remains the sole dispatch/describe/schema/effects authority.

The one pure Stage-0 normalizer for the opaque Lightning render_lens selection. Parses the recursive LensSpec, makes query/query_mode/match_scope defaults explicit (an omitted match_scope defaults name-only for a recipe render, name_and_note for a sift query), and preserves path-bearing LensSpecError failures for every ingress surface.

Immutable Lens Stage-0 bundle welding the pure LensEvalContext to the exact cache mapping, copied group/config operands, active-group id, and raw config reply used for one projection. MCP and modal origins retain distinct transport rails but converge on this one snapshot shape.

The one transport-free Lens Stage-0 interpreter. It parses an already-read config reply, captures or accepts exactly one cache mapping, builds snapshot-backed group/root resolvers plus the Anchor Dock boundary, and returns the immutable _LensStage0Snapshot consumed by both MCP and modal origins.

Compatibility context-only seam over the MCP-origin Lens Stage-0 snapshot builder. Performs the existing one config read through _build_lens_stage0_snapshot and returns only its pure LensEvalContext for callers/tests that need the engine operand directly.

Transport-free shared LensSpec projection core. Both the MCP family path and the docked-modal handler inject one already-read Lens Stage-0 snapshot, then reuse this single normalize/evaluate/materialize/sift implementation so canonical adoption, leaf algebra, and cache identity cannot drift. Threads the surface match_scope as the default for lens atoms that omit their own (recipe render = the surface value, default name-only; sift = 'name' for tag atoms while the query keeps its own name_and_note scope). A sift query returns sift_predicate -- the ONE build_search_predicate instance that decided the sifted tree -- so the MCP grep tier classifies its documents with the SAME predicate. The result ALWAYS carries lens_scaffold_ids ([ap:I506WY]): lens_engine.lens_scaffold_ancestor_ids receives the final tree, per-atom resolved roots AND the SAME pinned cache, so only strict input-root ancestors outside every member region become scaffold even when an input root is absent from the final tree. Every lens tail forwards this set to the existing materializer cause; ancestor_notes is folded producer-side. No second suppression path.

Thin MCP-origin consumer of the shared render_lens projector. It performs the ordinary tab-agnostic config read, builds one Lens Stage-0 snapshot, delegates normalize/evaluate/materialize/sift to _project_render_lens_from_cache, then uses the shared Stage-2 render/file tail -- EXCEPT under the sift grep tier ([ap:47B7WO], grep_params set by slice_group.sift tier='context'): the branch after projection bypasses the Stage-2 composer and returns the ONE compact grep formatter's report over exactly the lens's admitted nodes, so selection is never re-decided and the report is node.search's shape by construction. Grep values/defaults/bounds AND the [ap:O3MDOY] match controls are owned by _normalize_note_grep_params and the schemas by _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties; lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' (5c, [ap:2EG7TD]) calls both too, through the SAME _render_sift_grep_result tail (CF-30). max_nodes ([ap:O3MDOY] half 2) caps the headings tier: it rides the Stage-2 call with the lens's sift_predicate so the cap counts only MATCHING nodes AFTER the sort and the since prune (selection -> order -> cap). lens_scaffold_ids ([ap:I506WY], unit 5g) rides the Stage-2 call too -- the projection's lens_scaffold_ids (the connective scaffolding above the input roots, lens_engine.lens_scaffold_ancestor_ids) forwarded so that ancestor path renders headings-only even in document order; the spec's ancestor_notes opt-out folds HERE (producer-side, like the chronological boolean's fold): an overridden render passes nothing and stays byte-identical.

Slice Group registry and existing render-recipe origin. Render/sift/merge.render lower simple forms through ONE pure grammar and snapshot interpretation before the unchanged render_lens pipeline; formal lens requests and merge.persist retain their grammar. Schemas/describe/errors remain registry-owned; recipe match_scope defaults name, sift query defaults name_and_note. Render/sift/merge.render return through _shape_glimpse_family_return: raw Markdown by default, the structured result without rows when as_markdown=false. Sift's tier 'context' (the default, [ap:47B7WO]) branches AFTER projection: the ONE grep formatter reports line hits over the lens's admitted nodes; tier 'headings' keeps the tree render; push_to_modal is headings-tier only. _normalize_note_grep_params is the ONE grep value/default/bound owner AND the ONE owner of the [ap:O3MDOY] node-level match controls (sort_by/sort_direction/recent/recent_by/max_nodes -- active on BOTH sift tiers; on 'context' at node level through _render_sift_grep_result, on 'headings' the render semantics plus the max_nodes cap through the Stage-2 tail), and _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties are the ONE schema fragments shared with node.search/anchor.search/render_search; lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' ([ap:2EG7TD], landed) calls both too, through the SAME _render_sift_grep_result tail (CF-30). [ap:I506WY] (unit 5g): render/sift/merge.render all expose ancestor_notes -- on a lens render the flag restores the LENS-SCAFFOLD notes (the connective scaffolding above the input roots renders heading-only by default, even in document order; the projection computes lens_scaffold_ids, the lens tail forwards it, the materializer owns the cause), besides its U6 chronological meaning.

The ONE global-suppression list read for every beacon SYMBOL resolution (beacon.resolve, beacon.snippet symbol leg and the symbol fallback of a UUID-shaped handle, legacy snippet tools, beacon.tags.ensure/remove, and -- via resolve_node_handle's suppress_tags_provider -- the tag.add/remove/rename and node-mutator symbol legs). Reuses the tab-agnostic _resolve_slice_group_config(None) read that render_symbols uses and returns its f8_global_never_expand_tags list (e.g. ['wfy-suppress']); fail-loud (raises) when no Workflowy tab is connected, because suppression is resolution semantics. Dan's ruling [ap:7ORCPL].

THE UUID-shaped-handle gate for the beacon source_handle (snippet/resolve + the shared snippet body): True when the handle — after ONE pass through the shared bracket unwrapper unwrap_bracketed_uuid_handle — is a hyphen-normalized pure-hex string of >= 8 chars (the shared prefix kernel's min_prefix_len floor, i.e. a full UUID or any of its prefixes down to the 8-hex first segment, bracketed forms included). Resolution itself is NOT done here: the gate only routes to the UUID leg, which resolves through the ONE shared kernel _resolve_uuid_with_prefix_fallback (via resolve_uuid_like_node_handle / beacon_get_code_snippet); a symbol that happens to be 8+ hex chars still resolves on the symbol fallback. [ap:G5C9BX]: widened from the old >= 32-char rule that made beacon.snippet refuse the 8-hex segment its own describe recommends.

Unified S08 live source reader behind beacon.snippet. UUID-shaped handles (full UUID or 8-hex segment, via the shared gate _looks_like_uuid_source_handle) keep the forgiving UUID-first/symbol-fallback posture ([ap:G5C9BX]; a colliding prefix surfaces as a loud did-you-mean, never a guess); source symbols use the existing client resolver with retry-without-file_path. root_handles ([ap:WB323O]) resolves through _resolve_beacon_scope_roots (fail loud on an unresolvable root) and scopes the SYMBOL leg only -- candidates outside every root are dropped before the 0/1/N decision, so a duplicate symbol in another repository or a file copy resolves instead of colliding; an explicit UUID source_handle is read as given. Resolves live with context=0 (no engine padding — context is a render-layer knob), then returns the numbered, length-guarded snippet view from snippet_view.render_snippet_view.

The beacon identity resolve ([ap:CZ95R6]) behind beacon.resolve, through the ONE shared resolve_node_identity_record (prefer='symbol', with server.py's _looks_like_uuid_source_handle passed as the family's uuid_shaped_gate): the symbol leg stays first for symbol-shaped handles (suppress list + root_handles scope honoured, read lazily ONLY when the symbol leg actually runs so a UUID- or AP-shaped resolve never needs a connected tab), with U1's landed gates — a UUID-shaped handle (full UUID or 8-hex segment) routes to the uuid leg first (a colliding prefix is a loud N-candidate record, never a guess, never a symbol fallback; only fully-unresolved falls through to symbols) and an explicitly AP-shaped handle ([ap:CORE] / ap:CORE / [CORE]) routes to the AP leg first, with AP also the last fall-through for everything else. Returns the unified non-raising 0/1/N record: on a unique match the resolved node's full identifier vocabulary {short, uuid, ap_id} at the top level plus the symbol descriptor fields (resolved_symbol / resolved_symbol_kind / scope_filtered_count passthroughs); every candidate row carries its vocabulary. root_handles ([ap:WB323O]) resolves through _resolve_beacon_scope_roots (fail loud on an unresolvable root) and scopes the SYMBOL leg only; the UUID and AP legs ignore the scope, exactly as they ignore #wfy-suppress.

beacons.role: async _beacon_tags_mutate_impl(mode, operations, symbols, tags, comment, comment_mode, atomic, root_handles, favor)
beacons.comment: Shared S08 Q3 re-front for beacon.tags.ensure/remove. Every request flows through LightningRodMutationSpec.normalize_from_tool_args and the unchanged disk-only preflight/JIT/CAS orchestrator. 2R4E1P: carries comment_mode (fill | replace | append) beside comment -- fill keeps a conflicting existing comment as a row warning (labels still ensured), replace/append apply the requested text explicitly. [ap:LPC157] residue: carries atomic (batch-level all-or-nothing opt-in, default false) through to the orchestrator's post-preflight veto.

THE ONE root_handles resolver for beacon.snippet / beacon.resolve ([ap:WB323O]): normalizes the parameter (one handle string or a list) and resolves every entry through _resolve_beacon_graph_handle -- the SAME resolver and pinned operation cache every Beacon front uses, so root scoping cannot drift from the family. Every entry must resolve EXACTLY: an ambiguous prefix raises with the did-you-mean candidates, a missing handle raises with the cache-miss framing (render_symbols' fail-loud root rule, code invalid_parameter_value). Returns the deduped root UUID list in input order, or None when nothing was requested (no cache touch on the no-scope path, so today's calls are unchanged). The returned UUIDs scope SYMBOL resolution only -- an explicit UUID source_handle is read as given, exactly as #wfy-suppress behaves.
Single-target Q3 lease boundary shared by beacon.sync_node and the retained legacy direct wrapper; resolves path/graph footprint before the disk-only writer.

S08 node-handle-only disk beacon writer. Resolves the graph handle, performs one live structured node read, decodes the note exactly once into semantic bytes, then calls the literally disk-only low-level writer; no Workflowy/cache mutation follows. NBBW follow-up: the writer runs in a worker thread that is never abandoned (_await_thread_to_completion), inside the Q3 lease.

S08 async F12+1 front. Resolves to an exact UUID, rejects predictably-invalid FILE/FOLDER targets before any job artifact is created, then returns the normalized cross-family job record. U5: carries the explicit per-run force override (never the default) into the job JSON via extra_job_fields so the detached worker's fail-closed delete-threshold guards are overridden only for that run.

The read-only integrity check behind beacon.check. Takes exactly one target: a node_handle, resolved through _resolve_beacon_graph_handle against the pinned cache and classified FILE / FOLDER / Root: as map.refresh classifies it, or one file_path, resolved through resolve_tool_path(direction=read). Runs the beacon_integrity engine (collect_mapped_beacon_files + run_beacon_check) in a worker thread via _await_thread_to_completion and returns its summary_line, counts and rows with a target record. Fails only with the family's existing codes (node_handle_unresolved, map_target_invalid, beacon_target_unsupported, invalid_parameter_value). No write, lease, refresh, job, Workflowy call or tab (it never reads the suppress list); computes no row, count or summary of its own.

Assembly point for the seven-operation public Beacon family. Re-fronts live mapped-source reads, the read-only beacon.check integrity report, disk-only Q3/sync mutation, and validated async map refresh while the registry owns schemas, aliases, effects, errors, and describe output.

Shared render-family error boundary. Successes pass through byte-identically; success:false retains the whole payload under error.extra.legacy_result and honors a string code only when that operation declares it, otherwise the historical family failure code. No changed execution/admission path.

GLIMPSE registry: run keeps the explicit-scope truth table and modal readback, with simple forms on render_spec; estate accepts parcels and named estates on handle (simple / qualified short+long / {lens} sugar / formal JSON) and owns the per-kind default reads (named groups render as the group defines; {tags}/{dock}/{subtree} bake headings-only on the estate surfaces; the plain-node fallback). ONE pure grammar, unchanged render funnel. Registry owns schema/describe/errors and the output-only reserved-tabs contract; default tag scope remains name-only.

Assembly point for the render-only progressive-disclosure Lightning Rod family. Five tight schemas dissolve the legacy mode mega-schema while every handler fixes one mode and delegates to the one hoisted legacy authority. render_nodes ([ap:OSQHRG]) is render_symbols NAMED FOR NODES: without root_handles it resolves every item as a NODE via the ONE shared resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle and defaults the scope to the resolved nodes themselves (a {symbol} item or an unresolvable string refuses loud -- symbols need root_handles), then delegates to the ONE render_symbols path, so the wire still carries mode=render_symbols (no new lightning mode, no extension change). Permanent mutation vocabulary is intentionally absent. match_scope default is name-only for the tag-search modes (gather/render_tags) and name_and_note for the free-text mode (render_search). render_search ([ap:2EG7TD], 5c) is sift's same search over a root: tier 'headings' (the default, headings_only defaulting True at THIS boundary only) renders the matching nodes; tier 'context' validates grep values through _normalize_note_grep_params and returns the ONE shared grep tail (_sift_grep_documents + _render_sift_grep_result, CF-30), with sift-mirroring push/inert-knob refusals at this boundary.

S03 §7.1 MCP-side boundary factory (twin of _ws_cache_boundary): injected into dispatch_operation by every family front; wraps only the handler invocation of cache_backed specs. Cache-free operations never touch it.

S04 MCP dispatch hooks injected into every family front: result finalizer applies the ONE standardized hard-barrier read advisory to cache-backed read-safe non-render-family results (render families are covered at their internal cache-render seams, which also covers modal delivery); mutation admission classifies each spec and runs the fresh LOCKED hard-stop gate only for refuse-class operations, returning the universal coherence_barrier_active envelope; the exception mapper keeps typed coherence refusals from collapsing into operation_failed. 23db916f: the finalizer ALSO drains the per-operation handle-correction echo state first (handle_corrections) and applies it to EVERY family -- one 'resolved: <short> <name> (corrected from <supplied>)' line prefixed to string results, a top-level resolved_corrections list on dict results -- BEFORE the advisory, so a prefixed result reads advisory -> correction line -> body; the render-family and cache-back guards govern only the advisory, never the echo.

S04 §7.5 MCP result finalizer + Archive Reads U2 banner order + U3 footer: the coherence layers run first (handle-correction echo, then the ONE hard-barrier read advisory on cache-backed read-safe non-render results), then the archive steps — the §5.5 FOOTER first (fallback-mode success of one of the 16 flag verbs: \n + the line as the LAST string line, archives_left_out on dicts, counted from the overlay's precomputed planted chains), and the ARCHIVE BANNER drains LAST (§5.1), applied as the finalizer's final step so the ⚠️⚠️⚠️ ARCHIVED NODE line is the FIRST line of the result, above the advisory and above every resolved: correction line, on EVERY family (the two render families included: their internal seams advise, the banner still drains here). Strings gain the banner line(s) (one per archive file that answered, first-answered order) prefixed above the body; dicts gain archive_warning + archived; a PYDANTIC MODEL result (Chain-1 W1/F1: the archived structured node.read) is delivered as its own by-alias field mapping plus the same two keys, so an archive-answered structured read can never escape the warning; operations where no archive answered and nothing was left out are byte-identical.

Its 'tags' key and # subtree 'descend' are NOT shorthand keys. Keep that grammar separate. if surface == "slice_group" and "kind" in data and not {"dock", "symbols", "group"}.intersection(data): return SimpleFormResult(True, "formal_spec", lens=data, raw=data) def invalid(message, code="simple_form_unresolved"): from dataclasses import replace return replace(_error(message, code), is_simple=bool(_FORMS.intersection(data))) if "descend" in data and "dock" not in data: return invalid("descend is legal only on the Dock form, not a group/dock/node/subtree/tags/symbols or formal spec", "simple_form_descend_refused") form_keys = _FORMS.intersection(data) if form_keys and _BLOB_KEYS.intersection(data): return invalid("both simple-form and render_spec keys supplied; choose one form or a full spec") # Preserve the established spec-first Saved-Tabs wrapper contract. if isinstance(data.get("spec"), dict): return SimpleFormResult(True, "formal_spec", spec=data["spec"], raw=data) if kind in {"glimpse-slice-groups-export", "glimpse_anchor_views_export"} or isinstance(data.get("expand_groups"), list) or isinstance(data.get("anchor_views"), list): return SimpleFormResult(True, "formal_spec", raw=data) if len(form_keys) > 1: return invalid("multiple simple-form keys supplied; choose one of group, dock, node, subtree, tags or symbols") if not form_keys: if _looks_like_spec_blob(data):  # CF-10: the ONE blob recogniser. return SimpleFormResult(True, "formal_spec", spec=data, raw=data) return _error('no "spec" object or simple form; expected a JSON array, group name or render_spec blob') form = next(iter(form_keys)) _settings = _SETTINGS_KEYS.intersection(data) if _settings: # QBCTWU addendum item 3 (strict-JSON ruling): settings are split # from the parcel by key name; " "pass the bare parcel", "simple_form_settings_in_parcel", ) if form == "group": allowed = {"group", "alias", "title", "url"} elif form in {"node", "subtree"}: allowed = {form, "alias"} else: allowed = {form, "alias", "descend" if form == "dock" else "root"} # [ap:EPR86W] part a: the depth leg of the traversal pair rides the # dock parcel on the spec-consuming surfaces only. No lens atom. spec = {"lightning": {"mode": "render_symbols", "symbols": [root], "root_uuids": [root]}} lens = None else: # Every descendant, headings-only by default on the estate # surfaces (the per-kind default read below — this unit, 3d). spec = {"root_uuid": root, "descend_policy": "all"} lens = {"kind": "subtree", "root_handle": root, "descend": "all"} elif form == "dock": if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip(): return invalid("dock must be a non-empty node handle") if "descend" in data and not isinstance(data["descend"], bool): return invalid("Dock descend must be a JSON boolean (true or false)") if "recursive" in data and not isinstance(data["recursive"], bool): return invalid("Dock recursive must be a JSON boolean (true or false)") root = text = value.strip() policy = "all" if data.get("descend", False) else "stop_at_child_anchors" spec = {"root_uuid": root, "descend_policy": policy} # [ap:EPR86W] part a: the depth leg of the traversal pair, named and # valued exactly like dock.peek's. Deliberately NOT baked: a NAMED # slice group renders as the group defines (Dan's ruling — its stored # defaults are the read), and {node}/{symbols} whose bodies ARE the read # (the node alone; a beacon slice of signatures + comments). if surface in {"estate_call", "estate_note"} and form in {"dock", "tags", "subtree"}: spec["headings_only"] = True alias = data["alias"] if isinstance(data.get("alias"), str) else text return SimpleFormResult(True, form, text=text, alias=alias, spec=spec, lens=lens, root=root, requires_dock=form == "dock", raw=data) # @beacon[ #   id=simple-form@bare-decision, #   slice_labels=nexus--mcp-api, #   kind=ast, #   comment=Pure node/group hit decision over caller-acquired candidates; refuses any ambiguous hit or cross-domain collision instead of guessing., # ] def resolve_bare_string_decision(text, *, node_hits, group_hits) -> BareStringDecision: """Choose a unique identity only after BOTH resolver results are known.""" if len(node_hits) > 1 or len(group_hits) > 1 or (node_hits and group_hits): return BareStringDecision("error", error_code="simple_form_double_match", error_message=f"{text!r} matches nodes {node_hits!r} and groups {group_hits!r}; choose an explicit group or Dock form; see describe") if node_hits: return BareStringDecision("node", node_hits[0]) if group_hits: return BareStringDecision("group", group_hits[0]) return BareStringDecision("error", error_code="simple_form_unresolved", error_message=f"{text!r} did not resolve to a node or slice group; check the handle or system.cache.refresh; see describe") # @beacon[ #   id=simple-form@node-role, #   slice_labels=nexus--mcp-api, #   kind=ast, #   comment=Pure Dock-first node-role decision: dock > estate > plain node at the top level (QBCTWU U3-2 — a bare handle that is neither a Dock nor an estate reads the node on its own); a non-Dock inside an estate note is never another estate. Acquisition and note parsing remain with the originator., # ] def decide_node_role(*, is_anchor, note_parses_as_estate, inside_note) -> NodeRoleDecision: """Dock identity wins even when its description happens to parse.""" if is_anchor: return NodeRoleDecision("dock") if inside_note: return NodeRoleDecision("error", "simple_form_nesting_refused", "estates do not nest: a bare handle inside a note must be an Anchor Dock, not an estate/plain node; see describe") if note_parses_as_estate is None: return NodeRoleDecision("read_note") if note_parses_as_estate: return NodeRoleDecision("estate") # QBCTWU U3-2: at the TOP level a node that is neither an Anchor Dock nor # an estate is read on its own (the skill's plain-node row); the caller # lowers one {"node": uuid} entry through the render_nodes machinery. # Inside a note the nesting refusal above already spoke.

THE one snippet-side normalizer: validates and defaults the beacon.snippet view knobs (numbering, coordinates, explicit window, context, max_lines guard, size_only) into one frozen SnippetViewOptions; the note-read twin for node.read/anchor.point.read is normalize_note_view_params. Pure, no I/O.

THE one snippet size header — one format, never two: "[<prefix>lines S-E of N | L lines, B bytes, ~T tokens]" (bytes counted over the span, one newline per line; ~3 bytes/token; the " | relative 1 = line S" suffix when relative_start is given). Extracted verbatim out of render_guarded_lines so beacon.snippet and render_symbols' metadata tier (54e8356f(ii)) print the SAME line; the guard core delegates here and render_symbol_tier_note calls it directly. Pure, no I/O.

THE one head+tail guard core behind beacon.snippet AND node.read (and anchor.point.read): clamps a span to max_lines rows (head + tail, ONE elision row naming the hidden range and the start_line/end_line window that reads it back) through the ONE clamp_span_to_head_tail arithmetic (shared with the note-edit diff renderer, [ap:4JSBO5]), honors explicit start_line/end_line/limit windows in file or span-relative coordinates, and delegates the one-line size header to format_snippet_header (the one format render_symbols' metadata tier reuses verbatim). Pure, no I/O; render_snippet_view and the note fronts are thin wrappers over this.

THE one head+tail clamp arithmetic behind every guarded view ([ap:4JSBO5]): the exact split render_guarded_lines has always applied (tail = max_lines // 4, head = the rest), extracted so the note-edit diff renderer can share it and no second clamp can exist. Returns the 1-based span split (head_end, tail_start, elided_start, elided_end, elided_count); each caller renders its OWN elision row (the read names the start_line/end_line readback, the diff names the omitted hunks and the +/- totals). Pure; total_lines = span_end - span_start + 1 <= max_lines is the caller's guard.

THE snippet-side wrapper over the one shared guard core (render_guarded_lines): labels the size header "snippet: <file>" and hides it in numbering='none' mode exactly as before; the same core serves node.read's note view under a "note:" label, so the two verbs can never drift. Pure, no I/O, never re-reads the file.

THE one tier-body presentation authority for lightning_rod render_symbols (54e8356f(ii)): consumes the SAME carrier dict render_snippet_view does (file_path/file_lines/core_start_line/core_end_line) and returns the complete fenced note for tier 'metadata' (exactly the format_snippet_header line — the same numbers beacon.snippet prints) or 'context' (beacon comment + def line + first context_lines body lines, one trailer row naming the rest, optional tail_lines footer). The def line comes from the cached node's mapped line when it lies inside the span, else the first non-comment non-blank span line. Everything rides in a composer-parseable fence so source '#' lines are never promoted to headings. Pure, no I/O.

THE one note-guard policy behind BOTH public note fronts (node.read and anchor.point.read): decides when the shared guard core applies to a whole note (size_only always renders the "[note: ...]" size header, "[note: empty]" for an empty note; an explicit window is never guarded; otherwise guard iff max_lines > 0 and the note is longer) and renders it via render_guarded_lines under the "note: " label. Returns the guarded body, or None when the caller's own banner/header is followed by unguarded rows. Pure, no I/O.

THE one pure note-body renderer behind node.read and anchor.point.read: shared guard/size header first, otherwise windowed or numbered rows through split_note_lines and format_note_lines, otherwise the semantic note EXACTLY (including CRLF and a final terminator). The two fronts only add their own banner or metadata header; validation happens before I/O through validate_note_read_lines. Internal callers with view=None stay unguarded.

THE one note-read flag set shared by node.read and anchor.point.read: validates and merges the two window spellings (offset XOR start_line, limit XOR end_line), the numbering/with_line_numbers alias pair, and the shared guard knobs (max_lines default 400 = 300 head + 100 tail, 0 = off; size_only) into one NoteReadPlan for the public read fronts. default_numbered selects the verb's numbered-rows default (node.read False, anchor.point.read True) when neither spelling is given. Internal callers never pass through here, so they read unguarded. Pure, no I/O.

The loud teaching refusal (I3 — never silent): a ValueError subclass carrying the COMPLETE teaching message (offending path · daemon host · why the form cannot work · what to pass instead). Raised BEFORE any side effect — a refused path writes zero bytes anywhere. Consumers surface it through their ESTABLISHED error shapes (NetworkError at the note_file reader, the kernel operation_failed envelope at node.read, the {success:false,error(s)} dicts at the render tails/etch/estate) — never a new envelope.

The structured echo every path-consuming acknowledgement carries (I5): as_dict() IS the path_record payload — requested (the path exactly as supplied, stripped) · resolved (the path actually used on the daemon host) · translated (False ⇔ resolved is byte-identical to requested) · host (windows|wsl|linux) — in this key order. P3 echo rule: argument-echo ack fields carry `requested` byte-identically; `resolved` lives in path_record and in derived-path fields. Frozen dataclass — the record is immutable once minted.

The ONE host-detection probe reader (the monkeypatch seam — tests patch THIS). In order: os.name/sys.platform → 'windows'; else WSL iff /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease (read failures → empty string) contains 'microsoft' case-insensitively (catches WSL1 '…-Microsoft' and WSL2 '…-microsoft-standard-WSL2') OR WSL_DISTRO_NAME/WSL_INTEROP is present in the environment; else 'linux'. Darwin falls through to 'linux' (POSIX semantics). Stateless — no cache. The ONLY osrelease/WSL_* reader in the package (spec postcondition P2d).

The daemon's runtime host family — exactly one of 'windows' | 'wsl' | 'linux'. Stateless (reads the probes via _detect_host_raw() on every call; no cache, no TTL); nothing is hard-coded to today's topology. WSL and plain Linux ARE distinguishable (the osrelease 'microsoft' marker / WSL_* environment).

THE ONE host-aware path authority: every agent-supplied tool file-path parameter (output_file, note_file, nodes_file) resolves here BEFORE any open(), existence check, temp-file creation, or path-derived side effect. PURE — path in, PathResolution or ToolPathError out; no I/O, no display text beyond the refusal builder. Classification is REGEX-driven (§6.2 C1–C7, first match wins; never os.path.isabs). Action table (§6.3, host × class): windows passes UNC/drive forms verbatim and translates /mnt/<drive>/rest → <UPPER>:\rest, refusing every other POSIX-absolute path (WSL-only locations like /tmp would silently resolve under the daemon's current drive), drive-relative, ~ and relative forms; wsl translates X:\rest|X:/rest → /mnt/<lower>/rest, passes /mnt/<drive> and POSIX absolute verbatim, refuses UNC (no /mnt equivalent), drive-relative, ~ and relative; linux passes /mnt/<drive> and POSIX absolute verbatim and refuses every Windows form, drive-relative, ~ and relative. Translation is prefix-mechanical and byte-faithful (no normpath/probing/symlinks/case-folding beyond the drive letter); an already-correct path passes through byte-identically with translated=False. direction ('write'|'read') selects ONLY the refusal-message verb, never the action. Refusals are loud, teaching (offending path · daemon host · why · what to pass instead), side-effect-free, and prefixed '{context} {param}' exactly as the established note_file messages are.

The ONE shared read shape for tool file-path parameters (note_file, nodes_file): resolve_tool_path FIRST (loud teaching ToolPathError before any side effect), then os.path.isfile on the RESOLVED path (missing/directory → ToolPathError with the established 'not an existing file' wording class), then strict UTF-8 with universal newlines (CRLF/CR → LF; never errors='replace'). Returns (PathResolution, text) so the caller can attach the path_record. UnicodeDecodeError/OSError from the read itself propagate for the consumer's established error mapping (NetworkError at the note_file reader; the etch error dicts).

The ONE exact-byte text writer (rehomed from server.py's _glimpse_estate_write_bytes — move, not copy; exactly one definition site per spec postcondition P2c). newline='' suppresses Windows CRLF translation, so the file holds the EXACT composed bytes and the returned count equals len(Path(resolved).read_bytes()) on every platform. Takes an ALREADY-RESOLVED path string (callers reach it through resolve_tool_path / write_tool_text_file, or hold a resolution-derived companion path); it performs no resolution of its own.

The ONE shared write shape for tool output_file parameters whose byte contract is the plain exact-byte text write: resolve_tool_path FIRST (a refusal writes ZERO bytes anywhere — never a silent write to a location the caller cannot see), then the single exact-byte writer (_write_resolved_text_file, newline=''). Returns (PathResolution, bytes_written) so the caller can attach the path_record and keep bytes_written == len(Path(resolved).read_bytes()). Sites with a unique write shape (node.read's atomic temp+os.replace, the json.dump fan-outs) resolve through resolve_tool_path and open the RESOLVED string themselves.

In order: os.name/sys.platform → 'windows'; else WSL iff /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease (read failures → empty string) contains 'microsoft' case-insensitively (catches WSL1 '…-Microsoft' and WSL2 '…-microsoft-standard-WSL2') OR WSL_DISTRO_NAME/WSL_INTEROP is present in the environment; else 'linux'. Darwin falls through to 'linux' (POSIX semantics). Stateless — no cache. The ONLY osrelease/WSL_* reader in the package (spec postcondition P2d).

The daemon's runtime host family — exactly one of 'windows' | 'wsl' | 'linux'. Stateless (reads the probes via _detect_host_raw() on every call; no cache, no TTL); nothing is hard-coded to today's topology. WSL and plain Linux ARE distinguishable (the osrelease 'microsoft' marker / WSL_* environment).

THE ONE host-aware path authority: every agent-supplied tool file-path parameter (output_file, note_file, nodes_file) resolves here BEFORE any open(), existence check, temp-file creation, or path-derived side effect. PURE — path in, PathResolution or ToolPathError out; no I/O, no display text beyond the refusal builder. Classification is REGEX-driven (§6.2 C1–C7, first match wins; never os.path.isabs). Action table (§6.3, host × class): windows passes UNC/drive forms verbatim and translates /mnt/<drive>/rest → <UPPER>:\rest, refusing every other POSIX-absolute path (WSL-only locations like /tmp would silently resolve under the daemon's current drive), drive-relative, ~ and relative forms; wsl translates X:\rest|X:/rest → /mnt/<lower>/rest, passes /mnt/<drive> and POSIX absolute verbatim, refuses UNC (no /mnt equivalent), drive-relative, ~ and relative; linux passes /mnt/<drive> and POSIX absolute verbatim and refuses every Windows form, drive-relative, ~ and relative. Translation is prefix-mechanical and byte-faithful (no normpath/probing/symlinks/case-folding beyond the drive letter); an already-correct path passes through byte-identically with translated=False. direction ('write'|'read') selects ONLY the refusal-message verb, never the action. Refusals are loud, teaching (offending path · daemon host · why · what to pass instead), side-effect-free, and prefixed '{context} {param}' exactly as the established note_file messages are.

The ONE shared read shape for tool file-path parameters (note_file, nodes_file): resolve_tool_path FIRST (loud teaching ToolPathError before any side effect), then os.path.isfile on the RESOLVED path (missing/directory → ToolPathError with the established 'not an existing file' wording class), then strict UTF-8 with universal newlines (CRLF/CR → LF; never errors='replace'). Returns (PathResolution, text) so the caller can attach the path_record. UnicodeDecodeError/OSError from the read itself propagate for the consumer's established error mapping (NetworkError at the note_file reader; the etch error dicts).

The ONE exact-byte text writer (rehomed from server.py's _glimpse_estate_write_bytes — move, not copy; exactly one definition site per spec postcondition P2c). newline='' suppresses Windows CRLF translation, so the file holds the EXACT composed bytes and the returned count equals len(Path(resolved).read_bytes()) on every platform. Takes an ALREADY-RESOLVED path string (callers reach it through resolve_tool_path / write_tool_text_file, or hold a resolution-derived companion path); it performs no resolution of its own.

The ONE shared write shape for tool output_file parameters whose byte contract is the plain exact-byte text write: resolve_tool_path FIRST (a refusal writes ZERO bytes anywhere — never a silent write to a location the caller cannot see), then the single exact-byte writer (_write_resolved_text_file, newline=''). Returns (PathResolution, bytes_written) so the caller can attach the path_record and keep bytes_written == len(Path(resolved).read_bytes()). Sites with a unique write shape (node.read's atomic temp+os.replace, the json.dump fan-outs) resolve through resolve_tool_path and open the RESOLVED string themselves.

beacons.comment: Diagnostic-only detached CARTO heartbeat controller: writes immutable pid/job/claim identity once, advances only mtime on a daemon thread, and stops with a bounded non-wedging join. Never participates in liveness, admission, cancellation, reaping, killing, or claim release.

Server-side (worker) computation of the REPO-ROOT-RELATIVE path for a CARTO progress file_uuid, written into progress.current_file_relpath so the UUID widget status line can show a human path instead of a raw UUID (the browser DOM walk only works when that file node happens to be rendered; the worker always knows the path). Delegates the composition (resolve_cartographer_path_from_node + _portable_relpath + basename fallback) to the ONE shared helper resolve_cartographer_file_relpath in api_client_nexus (U1, MasterSpec §5.4); keeps its memo. Fully best-effort (never raises, never affects reconcile).

beacons.role: boundary split: shared detached worker bootstrap and environment setup

beacons.comment: S02/S03-B launcher-selected lineage VALIDATION + the SINGLE current manifest-head adoption (pin_worker_operation_cache, audit amendment A3) in weave_worker main (Gate c); S03B Chain-3 (W2): explicit four-way account binding (adopted claim = admitted job = snapshot lineage = client/coherence paths) BEFORE the pin — a mismatch fails the bootstrap loudly with zero mutation work. S04 Remediation Chain 1 (item 1): execution-side coherence barrier recheck via the shared require_coherence_mutation_admission authority after adoption/validation/pin and BEFORE any mutation dispatch — refusal persists a typed coherence_barrier_active job failure and finalizes the adopted claim through the exact-token path with zero mutation dispatch.

beacons.role: core keeper: detached cartographer refresh job runner

beacons.comment: Detached worker dispatch for CARTO_REFRESH jobs (FILE mode → refresh_file_node_beacons; FOLDER mode → refresh_folder_cartographer_sync). Reads job JSON, runs Cartographer reconcile, writes status back. RELEVANT TO F12+3 TIMEOUT: this entire branch runs OUT-OF-PROCESS via subprocess detach, so foreground MCP server is not directly waiting on it — BUT the foreground bulk-apply runner DOES await per-file refresh_file_node_beacons in-process (see _run_carto_bulk_visible_apply_job). HYPOTHESIS (unverified): if the foreground in-process refresh hangs while a separate detached CARTO_REFRESH worker is also active, deadlock-like symptoms could result. Closures _carto_should_cancel{,_file} and _carto_progress{,_for_file} live inside this branch and are individually beaconed.

beacons.role: • 🔱 weave worker MARKDOWN_GENERATE job runner (F12+3 detached pipeline)
beacons.comment: Detached worker dispatch for MARKDOWN_GENERATE jobs (F12+3). Reads CARTO job JSON for root_uuid, runs the 8-phase markdown generate pipeline (bulk-apply tags + write Markdown to disk + reapply beacons + post-flight refresh) via markdown_generate_pipeline.run_markdown_generate_pipeline(). Writes status/progress back to job JSON. Survives MCP server restart.

beacons.comment: Saved-Tabs Tier-2 DRIVE orchestrator (SW half, spec [ap:7S217K] §6/§8; U01 per contract [ap:08ZEAO]): strictly sequential (A5/G6) — per entry: STEP 0 the configurable inter-tab delay (saved_tabs_drive_delay_seconds re-read per gap via loadExtensionSettings — a mid-drive change takes effect at the next tab; interruptible; never before this drive's first create), the cancel check (a stopped drive reports this and every remaining entry skipped-cancelled, then the summary), STEP 3 create at PLAIN https://workflowy.com/ (SAVED_TABS_DRIVE_TAB_URL — the entry's saved page url is IGNORED since U02 [ap:DLGU66]; no url admission, no entry ever fails over its url) — REUSING the previous drive's window when it still exists (savedTabsDriveLastWindowId via chrome.windows.get; otherwise ONE new window: first entry chrome.windows.create unfocused, later entries chrome.tabs.create in that window, active:false — G1/D5 rev-2 as amended; a failed create unbinds and the next entry re-resolves), STEP 4 await THAT tab's endpoint_register observation via pendingTabReadiness RACED against the drive's cancel signal (the ONE hook in the frame-inspection branch — never a timer/poll, G2/D2; the caps are liveness hygiene; a stop tears the waiter down and reports the entry failed with a cancelled reason — its tab stays open), deliver alias+spec in ONE saved_tabs_drive_apply frame via sendToTab (spec by object identity — A1/G4), STEP 6 await the correlated saved_tabs_drive_apply_response raced against the cancel signal the same way; a failing entry never aborts the rest (D7 — every failure named with phase+reason); progress frames per transition to the ORIGIN tab (D4; origin death now STOPS the drive at once via stopSavedTabsDrive — cancellation semantics, D8 amended); a delaying progress frame announces each inter-tab gap; terminal summary (G7/G8), then singleton + eviction marker cleared; entered via the saved_tabs_drive_request branch (handleSavedTabsDriveRequest — acceptance ack; a concurrent request SUPERSEDES the running drive instead of being refused); extension-INTERNAL kinds only — never the broker wire (A2)
Outbound frame queue + TTL for the cold-SW race: frames sent while the broker socket is not yet OPEN are buffered here and flushed on hello_ack-accepted instead of being dropped
Flush the outbound queue once the broker handshake is live: sends every non-expired buffered frame in order; called from the hello_ack-accepted branch

SINGLE source of truth for the interactive client<->server WS reply-timeout (how long a client-initiated round trip waits for its correlated reply before resolve(null)). Shared by ALL SIX interactive round-trip helpers -- requestSliceModalRender (Apply/per-row/multi-select), requestMarkdownModalRender (live-DOM modal), requestCompileSliceSearch, requestAnchorListForWidget, the scoped Lightning Rod, and the F8 expansion plan -- so the ceiling can never drift between them. Raised from 12s to 30s (Dan) because a genuinely large server render can legitimately exceed 12s. DISTINCT from: the push path's generous 180000ms leak-cap (a ~minute-long render is decoupled from the MCP ack), and MODAL_KEEPALIVE_MS=12000 (the SW keepalive, which MUST stay < ~30s MV3 idle-eviction and is NOT a reply timeout).

THE modal render-parameter store: a single IN-MEMORY object (dockedModalRenderState) holding the dock's render-defining VIEW parameters sort_by / sort_dir / since / headings_only. getTabModalState() returns it ({} when unset); setTabModalState(patch) merge-patches it (null/undefined value DELETES a key -> 'inherit the hardcoded default'). Aug-2026 DE-STORAGE: formerly sessionStorage-backed (key glimpse_modal_state) so the knobs survived a full page reload; Dan's explicit decision made that reload-persistence unwanted (a refresh SHOULD reset the dock -- you re-Apply the slice and retype any since/item-count override; slice groups now carry their own stored default SORT (SGSORT, 2026), so Apply seeds the sort knob for free via the server render_scope echo -- the `since` feature is fully implemented but has no per-group stored default, so an item-count/window override is retyped per render), so the backing is now a plain module var that dies with the page. Function names/signatures UNCHANGED so every getMdPreview*/setTabModalState call site is unaffected; still per-page-context (per-tab), still the SOLE authority the accessors read; ribbon widgets write on user edit, adoptRenderScope writes on a successful server render echo. NOT chrome.storage.sync and NO LONGER sessionStorage.

beacons.comment: THE PAGE-WORLD (main-world content script) connectWebSocket -- distinct from the SW-side background.js connectWebSocket (nexus--broker). It constructs the BridgeSocket polyfill (page proxy to the SW's real socket), wires ws.onopen (endpoint register + ping + CARTO poll), the giant ws.onmessage Direction-A dispatch (extract_dom / get_extension_settings / get_slice_group_config / render_slice_modal_result / render_slice_row_result / the apply_slice_in_dock push receiver IIFE / etc.), ws.onerror, and ws.onclose (reconnect loop). ⭐ G3 EDIT SITE for the async dock-render-task refactor: ws.onclose here is where pending pendingSliceModalRenders promises must be REJECTED (liveness cleanup) so a socket drop mid-render routes through the ONE G2 error sink instead of hanging until a wall-clock timeout. Beaconed to DISAMBIGUATE from the SW-side twin (an agent told 'edit connectWebSocket's onclose for G3' must land HERE, in the page world, NOT background.js).

MCP-initiated Direction-A LEAF query backing glimpse(render_spec='modal') -- the 'GLIMPSE exactly what I'm looking at in the docked modal' capability. The server asks THIS tab for the scope+focus it is CURRENTLY showing; we answer from the ONE shared helper currentDockRenderSpecWithSelectedFocus(), which reads in-memory dock state ONLY (no compute, no nested round-trip, so NO deadlock note applies): dockedSliceContext.render_spec (the server-adopted RenderProjectionSpec the dock last rendered) with the currently-selected tree-view row (dockedListRows[dockedSelectedIndex]) merged in as the occurrence-exact focus field. Only well-defined for a cache-sourced SLICE render (dockedRenderSource==='slice'); a live-DOM dock has no server-side scope to reproduce, so we reply success:false with actionable guidance. The agent types ZERO UUIDs -- the blob is the tab's OWN server-canonical scope -- so this eliminates focus-UUID hallucination at the source. Echoes request_id so the broker routes the reply to ONLY the originating MCP server (generic request_id rail).

This is the latent hook for automating GLIMPSE-this-topic without a human pressing F8; there is currently no server/MCP sender of this action.

Classify a hovered Workflowy node as folder/file/node from Path:/Root: and Cartographer note headers

Detect the F12+4 "saved generated file" dummy metadata block: first line exactly 'MD_PATH:' with a 'Path:' line inside the block (before its closing '---'). Mirrors the Python _extract_dummy_path_from_metadata_block contract so classifyF12Target can route a saved-regime node to the 'file' action set rather than the generic 'node' set.

Route extension-side F12 actions to file vs folder refresh requests based on classified Path:/Root: semantics.
