Walk DOM ancestors from an AST/beacon node to find the enclosing FILE node by Path:/Root: header
Run F12+2 bulk visible apply targeting the AST node's enclosing FILE - safe to invoke when the file node is scrolled out of view
Select available F12 actions from extension-side file/folder/node classification derived from Cartographer headers

Top-level F12 popup entrypoint that classifies the current node using Path:/Root: semantics before presenting actions | F12+4 eligibility check: does a Workflowy node have ANY children (visible OR hidden/collapsed)? Mirrors the canonical hidden-children detection in extractChildren() (visible child row, OR .collapsed class, OR an expand-toggle icon). F12+4 (materialize note -> .md) requires a CHILDLESS node so the auto-F12+1 reconcile is a pure create; the server re-checks authoritatively against the cache as belt-and-suspenders.

Correlation map for the F12+4 bulk eligibility round-trip. Keyed by node_id -> {resolve, timer}. requestBulkMaterializeVerdict registers an entry and sends classify_bulk_materialize; handleClassifyBulkMaterializeResult resolves it. This is the FIRST server-queried F12 menu-visibility check; all other menu items remain client-side.
Resolve the pending F12+4 bulk eligibility promise for message.node_id with the server verdict {show,mode,visible_option_enabled,all_option_enabled,...}.

Correlation map for the BULK F12+3 eligibility round-trip. Keyed by node_id -> {resolve, timer}. requestBulkF12p3Verdict registers an entry and sends classify_bulk_f12p3; handleClassifyBulkF12p3Result resolves it. Twin of the F12+4 pendingBulkMaterializeVerdicts map.
Resolve the pending BULK F12+3 eligibility promise for message.node_id with the server verdict {show,mode,reason,classification}. Twin of handleClassifyBulkMaterializeResult.

Fire the BULK F12+3 eligibility query (classify_bulk_f12p3) and return a Promise that resolves with the server verdict (or null on timeout). Unlike the F12+4 twin it needs NO child-visibility booleans (F12+3 bulk has no availability submenu). The server walks the cache ancestor chain (zoom-proof). Used on F12-popup open.

Fire the F12+4 bulk eligibility query (classify_bulk_materialize) and return a Promise that resolves with the server verdict (or null on timeout). The server walks the cache ancestor chain (zoom-proof) using the client-reported visible/hidden child booleans. Used on F12-popup open.

Return {hasVisible, hasHidden} for a node's children from the DOM. hasVisible = >=1 rendered child row. hasHidden = node is collapsed OR shows an expand toggle (children exist but are not rendered). The server cannot know visible-vs-hidden (it's pure DOM/expansion state), so the client must report it for the F12+4 bulk sub-option enable/disable decision.

Send the F12+4 bulk execution frame (bulk_materialize_markdown). walkMode 'visible' attaches the client visible-DOM subtree payload (extractVisibleActionTree); 'all' sends only the root UUID so the server walks the cache (incl. hidden). Carries persist_files + the live DOM ancestor chain + default_markdown_folder, mirroring the single-node F12+4 payload.

Second-stage BULK F12+3 sub-popup. Two choices: (1) recurse VISIBLE only and (2) recurse ALL incl. hidden. SIMPLER than the F12+4 bulk sub-popup -- NO persist checkbox (F12+3 just regenerates existing on-disk Markdown files in place; there is no temp/persist regime). Reuses f12PopupState.actions + executeF12PopupAction so the existing 1/2/ESC keydown handler drives it.

Send the BULK F12+3 execution frame (bulk_generate_markdown). walkMode 'visible' attaches the client visible-DOM subtree payload (extractVisibleActionTree); 'all' sends only the root UUID so the server walks the cache (incl. hidden). No persist/ancestor/default-folder fields needed -- F12+3 regenerates files already mapped on disk. Twin shape of dispatchF12BulkMaterialize minus the F12+4-only fields.

Shared refusal/ack feedback for the four single-shot CARTO launch results (F12+1 file/folder, F12+3 single, F12+4/+5). Surfaces governance outcomes that otherwise appear to do nothing: cooldown_active (with retry_after), overlap_conflict (with conflicting job id), dedupe reuse, governance_state_unclassifiable, launch_preflight_failed, and success acks. Writes a DEDICATED child line at the top of cartoJobsEl (not textContent, which the ~1Hz poll repaint would stomp); the poll re-inserts the line each repaint so the message survives. Transient: fades after ~8s; never fabricates a persistent job row.

Feedback handler for the BULK F12+3 execution result: reports file_count / launched job count (and any errors) via the CARTO jobs widget status line; the N per-file F12+3 jobs each show their own status line as usual. Twin of handleBulkMaterializeMarkdownResult.

Feedback handler for the F12+4 bulk execution result: reports leaf_count / launched job count (and any errors) via the CARTO jobs widget status line; the N per-leaf F12+1 jobs each show their own status line as usual.

Second-stage F12+4 BULK sub-popup. Two primary choices: (1) recurse VISIBLE only (enabled iff verdict.visible_option_enabled) and (2) recurse ALL incl. hidden (always enabled in bulk). Plus a two-line 'Persist backing .md files' checkbox (default OFF) whose sub-line states it ONLY applies to Markdown-in-Markdown leaves (a leaf already inside a mapped .md); plain Workflowy nodes are unmapped and always produce a kept .md so the toggle is a no-op for them. Reuses f12PopupState.actions + executeF12PopupAction so the existing 1/2/ESC keydown handler drives it. The checkbox state is read live at dispatch time.

Second-stage F12+4 sub-popup for the markdown-inside-markdown case. Forces the user to choose Save (keep the generated subset .md permanently, node gets a dummy MD_PATH: Path: block) vs Delete (throwaway split-vehicle, historical default). Reuses the same popup element + f12PopupState.actions so the existing 1/2/ESC keydown handler and executeF12PopupAction route the choice. THE single monotonic RENDER-GENERATION counter for the docked modal -- the keystone of the dock's async-render supersession model. A new render INTENT (a genuine selection change in setDockedSelection, a root-set/Refresh in prepareDockedServerRender, and -- as of the async dock-render-task refactor -- a slice APPLY/PUSH via displaySliceInDock) claims a fresh generation by ++dockedRenderGeneration; each async request captures the value it was fired under and acts ONLY if it still equals the current one at reply/paint time, so EVERY stale reply (success, failure, null, timeout) is dropped by ONE rule and a superseded render can never clobber a newer view. ONE shared clock governs BOTH the DOM-render path and the slice/push paint path (most-recent intent wins the paint chokepoint, independent of which async render finishes first). Historically unbeaconed, which hid it from the f8-expand/md-preview slice and led an architecture session to propose a NEW counter instead of extending this one; beaconed now so the next agent to touch async-render correctness sees it. NOTE: a bare top-level `let` is not symbol-addressable via read_text_snippet_by_symbol, so this block is also the read handle for the counter.

Find-in-source query compiler for the dock Source view -- the HIGHLIGHT-only JS mini-twin of the server's build_search_predicate smart grammar (lightning_rod_search.py; twins-by-one-grammar, the SinceCodec-pair precedent). Tokenizes whitespace with "quoted phrase" support (unbalanced quote = loud {ok:false}), skips the OR/AND keywords and negated (- / !) terms (negation is meaningful for node FILTERING but not for highlight-in-place; ignored in v1), escapes every regex metacharacter then restores the * / ? GLOB wildcards, drops patterns that could match the empty string (a bare '*' would yield an infinite zero-length-match stream), and returns ONE combined case-insensitive alternation RegExp. Returns {ok:true, regex:null} for a blank/all-negated query (= clear highlights). Keep in lockstep with the server grammar's positive-term subset.

Instant LOCAL re-paint of the dock bottom pane from the held dockedRenderedSource through composedContentToHtml (current content_format honored) -- the Source/Rendered toggle's apply step and the find-in-source re-highlight step. NO server round trip, NO render-generation claim (synchronous; an in-flight reply that lands afterward paints through the current mode, correct by construction); preserves scrollTop. Cluster siblings: compileDockSourceSearch / dockedSourceHtml / applyDockSourceSearch / navigateDockSourceSearch / refreshDockSourceSearchUi.

The ONE dock toast lifecycle authority. Replaces/starts the transient top-center toast; manual click dismissal clears the timer and leaves controls immediately usable, while automatic timeout dismissal alone arms a 1000ms capture-phase click shield over interactive dock controls. This prevents the toast-vanished-before-mouseup race from accidentally clicking Freeze/Sync behind it without using pointer-events:none (which would pass clicks through to Workflowy). New toast display clears any prior shield. Pure client UI state; no persistence.

beacons.role: ƒ surfaceRenderFailure(res, opts): the single UI helper that turns a render/action reply into the right user-facing failure message
beacons.comment: The ONE place that converts a dock render/action reply into a user-facing failure, so every caller surfaces the server's actionable text identically instead of a bare 'ERR' flash or a silent blank. Distinguishes the three failure modes the endpoint-liveness work defined: res==null -> TRANSPORT failure (no reply / cold socket / timeout); res.code=='unknown_endpoint' -> endpoint-liveness GHOST (tab dropped on an MV3 SW reconnect, already asked to re-register in the background -> retry), preferring the server's own res.error; res.success!==true -> any other structured failure surfaced verbatim (fallback to the caller's fallbackMessage). Returns true iff a failure was surfaced (caller early-returns), false on a success to render. UI propagation ONLY: shows a toast, optionally paints the message into the supplied dock render element and clears the source/leaf-count -- it NEVER renders content and touches no protocol/routing/retry/broker behavior.

Docked Markdown modal 'Copy ID' feature: copy a tree-view row's Workflowy SEARCH STRING `id:<uuid>` to the clipboard (via the shared navigator.clipboard->fallbackCopy path) and flash a showDockToast telling the user to paste it into Workflowy's search box to reveal the node. Invoked (toggle-gated on dockedCopyIdMode) from setDockedSelection so both click and arrow-key selection copy; the full search string is copied (not the bare UUID) so a single paste locates the node.

ONE shared client helper that builds the full render_spec blob for the dock's current cache-sourced view, merging dockedSliceContext.render_spec (the server-adopted scope) with the currently-selected row as spec.focus. Used by BOTH the get_current_modal_render_spec WS leaf query (render_spec='modal') and the '⌖ focus' copy button (fallback paste blob), so the two surfaces cannot drift. Pure in-memory state read; no rendering, no WS round-trip; the server re-projects through the Python composer.

Page-world responder for the SW's cross-tab Saved-Tabs export survey: answer with currentDockRenderSpecWithSelectedFocus()'s stored render_spec blob VERBATIM (cache_render_spec only; frozen-DOM/refusals reported as-is for the not-exportable list) plus this tab's endpoint_id/alias, over the page-to-sw bridge — never the server wire

beacons.role: handleSavedTabsDriveApply(payload): apply ONE drive-delivered entry (alias + spec) in this freshly created tab
beacons.comment: Saved-Tabs Tier-2 drive receiver (page world, spec [ap:7S217K] §6): non-empty alias -> setEndpointAlias FIRST (re-registers + retitles immediately, P4/G3); admission via savedTabsValidateEntrySpec (the SAME kernel as single-entry import — exact group_id pre-validation); apply through the ONE shared funnel applySliceGroupIntoDock with applySavedTabsEntry's receiver-identical opts (spec untouched by object identity — A1/G4, [ap:HVAWAF]; generation unclaimed — displaySliceInDock claims at paint and force-freezes, G5); a NAME-ONLY frame (spec null + non-empty alias, follow-up 2) stops after the alias-set and answers ok:true with nothing applied; the terminal saved_tabs_drive_apply_response rides the page-to-sw bridge and is ALWAYS sent (bounded by the long render timeout + the socket-death settle, P7); failures loud via the funnel's ONE sink + the Saved-Tabs status line

Feature 2 dock affordance ('GLIMPSE what the modal is showing right now'): copy the FULL render_spec blob (scope + selected-row focus) as compact JSON to the clipboard, so the human hands it to an agent verbatim as workflowy_glimpse(render_spec=<blob>) to render EXACTLY this row's option-Y view server-side. Uses the SAME currentDockRenderSpecWithSelectedFocus() helper as the render_spec='modal' WS leaf query, preventing copy-vs-query drift. This closes the old scope gap from the bare focus triple: the blob carries group_id/root_uuid/match_scope/etc. AND the focus field. Reuses the shared navigator.clipboard->fallbackCopy idiom + showDockToast. Only meaningful for a cache-sourced SLICE render (dockedRenderSource==='slice'); in DOM mode it toasts guidance instead. One-shot (not a toggle).

Serialize the docked modal's VISIBLE DOM subtree into the nested {root,children} payload the server composer consumes, accumulating total visible name+note char size for the pre-render-threshold decision.

Fire a render_slice_modal WS request (client-minted request_id + this tab's endpoint_id + the group_id, plus the dock's current sort_by/sort_direction) and resolve with the server's cache-projected slice render {success, markdown, cache_sourced, node_count, warnings}, or null on cold-socket/timeout. Mirrors requestCompileSliceSearch / requestMarkdownModalRender exactly. The server composes the Markdown (single source of truth); the client only paints the returned string into the dock.

Browser twin of the server's _slice_row_key. Builds the stable string key for a tree-view row's (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) identity triple, MUST stay byte-for-byte identical to the Python side (same \x1f separators + layout) so a snapshot lookup (dockedSliceSnapshot keyed by this) and a re-projected server render agree. Cross-language contract point -- change both together.

Shared generated timeout policy for cache-backed row renders. Grows from the interactive floor using the already-known final row count, caps at the established 180s long-render ceiling, and never inspects opaque LensSpec atoms; socket-close cleanup remains the immediate failure detector.

Fire an occurrence-exact render_slice_row re-projection from the stored RenderProjectionSpec. The opaque scope (including a canonical render_lens recipe) and row focus ride in one render_spec blob; the request uses the shared row-count-generated cache timeout with an optional bounded override, while socket death still settles immediately through failAllPendingSliceRenders.

SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the on-the-wire lightning selection block carried on render_slice_modal / render_slice_row / apply_slice_in_dock frames. Emits the opaque per-mode selection, including render_lens{lens,query,query_mode,match_scope}; LensSpec is copied verbatim and never interpreted client-side. Used by requestSliceModalRender + requestSliceRowRender so Refresh, row focus, readback, and push cannot drop mode-specific fields.

Client-side SGSORT sort normalizer, the JS twin of the Python RenderProjectionSpec kind-aware sort rule. Requires kind to be known before sort coercion: null/omitted survives only for slice/slice_override request specs (inherit the group's saved default at the server resolve-point), raw_root/lightning collapse null to the explicit 'none' document-order sentinel, and the string 'none' remains distinct from null. Used by the spec builders and normalizeRenderScopeToSpec so Apply/push/request frames preserve the no-cracks null-vs-'none' boundary across the client wire.

CLIENT-side reconstruction of a RenderProjectionSpec from the SERVER's authoritative render_scope echo -- the single fan-in that makes the client half of the shared-object architecture work. adoptRenderScope calls this and stores the result as the SOLE field of dockedSliceContext (dockedSliceContext.render_spec), so the client Refresh (refreshDockedMarkdownPanel) and per-row re-render (requestSliceRowRender) reuse the EXACT scope the server just rendered -- kind / group_id / group_name / root_uuid / opaque lightning selection / match_scope / descend_policy / recursive ([ap:EPR86W] part a: the depth leg of the traversal pair; false = the scope root + its DIRECT children only, raw-root-only today) / sort / since / recent_by ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a): the recency basis of a 'newest' item_count selection; null = the server resolves it) / headings_only / content_format / tree_mode. This IS the client's scope handle: there are no separate scalar mirrors beside it. Derives kind from scope.kind, falling back to the (lightning|group_id+root_uuid|group_id|else) presence truth table for a partial/older scope; preserves the opaque lightning selection verbatim (never interprets it -- the server routes by selection.mode). Tolerant of missing fields (each falls back to RENDER_SPEC_DEFAULTS). This is the JS twin of the Python RenderProjectionSpec normalizers; the small make{Slice,RawRoot,Lightning}RenderSpec factories (used by the human Apply / Lightning ribbon spec-build sites) sit just above and ride under this block. descend_policy and recursive round-trip through here, so Refresh/per-row preserve them for free.

G3 liveness cleanup: settle EVERY in-flight render_slice_modal / render_slice_row promise on transport death (page-world BridgeSocket ws.onclose). Resolves each pending waiter with null -- the SAME 'render failed' signal the 180s leak-cap timeout and a cold-socket send use -- so the failure flows through the ONE existing G2 sink (the caller's `!res` branch: the push receiver's dock toast, the APPLY button's flash('ERR')) instead of hanging until a wall-clock timeout. GENERATION-AGNOSTIC by design: the transport is gone, so ALL pending renders are moot regardless of dockedRenderGeneration -- settle them all to avoid a promise/timer leak. NEVER-REJECT: resolve(null) (not reject) keeps the contract every caller already handles (a rejection would need new try/catch at each await site); the timers are cleared here so no stale resolve(null) fires later.

Fire a render_slice_modal WS request (the Apply-slice FULL-DOCUMENT render). SPEC-ONLY signature: the SOLE arg is a RenderProjectionSpec (+ an optional { renderTimeoutMs } opts bag); a non-spec 1st arg is a loud fail-fast (no positional fallback). The spec is unpacked at the top into the SAME locals the body uses -- group_id + this tab's endpoint_id are sent on the frame, and the spec's view fields drive the sort. SORT PRECEDENCE (now entirely spec-expressed): the spec's sort_by/sort_direction map onto the internal explicit-sortOverride branch, which ALWAYS wins over the internal forceDefaultSort (fixed false for a spec) and never reads/mutates the global md_preview_sort_* store -- so the agent/server push honors the GLIMPSE call's sort, and the human APPLY button expresses its 'default view' intent by BUILDING a spec with sort_by:'none'. The spec's `since` is forwarded verbatim ('' => no since on this render); the global dock since is never inherited here. The server RE-PROJECTS the slice from cache (build_stage1_base_tree) and returns the composed Markdown + tree-view rows + Tier-2 live-GUI-sync fields; resolves with the reply dict or null on cold-socket/timeout. Rides the generic request_id rail (handleRenderSliceModalResult resolves render_slice_modal_result AND render_slice_row_result).

SHARED cache-scope apply orchestration: render any cache-projected scope into the docked modal through ONE RenderProjectionSpec path (requestSliceModalRender -> captureSinceFieldsFromResult -> displaySliceInDock, forwarding Tier-2 live-GUI-sync fields when applicable). Handles slice groups (group_id), slice overrides (group_id + root_uuid), raw-root dumps (root_uuid only), anchor views (raw_root + descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors'), and Lightning Rod selections. The human slice APPLY button, anchor-view APPLY rows, and agent/server push all funnel through this one function. Sort/since/headings are EXPLICIT per-render args (never read from global dock state when supplied), and UI feedback is injected via optional hooks. Returns the server result (or null) so callers can branch on success.

Resolve the root UUID a Lightning Rod ribbon action should scope to = whatever the docked modal is CURRENTLY rooted at, regardless of provenance. SLICE mode (Apply/push/prior Lightning Rod) has dockedRootUuid=null, so read the adopted render_scope's root_uuid (dockedRenderScope || dockedSliceContext); DOM mode uses dockedRootUuid. Returns '' when neither is set (nothing displayed yet) so the caller shows the 'select a node first' toast. The Lightning Rod ribbon has NO paste-a-UUID field BY DESIGN -- it always acts on the current modal root.

SHARED render-into-dock tail for a Lightning Rod spec: requestSliceModalRender -> captureSinceFieldsFromResult -> surfaceRenderFailure -> displaySliceInDock with the standard group-less meta block (group_id:null, the lightning root, empty sync bundle). Extracted from triggerLightningRod's Global fork so the dynamic-slice-group dialog submit can reuse it byte-for-byte (STAGE-0 DOCTRINE: a duplicated pure block is the only Stage-0 crack).

beacons.role: async function triggerLightningRod(mode, query, matchScope, scoped)
beacons.comment: Fire a Lightning Rod from the dock ribbon. mode is 'gather' | 'render_tags' | 'render_search'; the single text box feeds BOTH render modes (render_search verbatim as `query`, render_tags split on whitespace/commas into `tags`); matchScope ('name'|'name_and_note') rides inside the opaque lightning selection. Roots at resolveLightningRodRootUuid() (the current modal root; NO paste-a-UUID field). scoped (the 4th arg, ap:LRSCOPE/ap:LRHAND2) selects between TWO forks: (GLOBAL, scoped falsy) the original path -- build a kind='lightning_rod' RenderProjectionSpec and requestSliceModalRender -> displaySliceInDock, walking the WHOLE cache root; (SCOPED, scoped truthy) confine the search to the dock's CURRENT frozen artifact via requestScopedLightningDomCapture, producing an EPHEMERAL kind='dom_capture' result routed through displaySliceInDock -> the crack-closer -> displayScopedDomCaptureInDock (one-way door; the durable slice/raw origin is discarded, re-Apply to return). Scoped requires dockedFrozen; it sends the pinned captured tree (DOM-frozen) OR the durable base_render_spec + wasSlice (slice-frozen, server projects+filters), plus the optional occurrence-exact selected-row focus as the DOMAIN re-root pre-step (distinct from plain row-click navigation). Global is byte-for-byte the prior behavior.

Trigger for the Dynamic Slice Group dialog. If exactly one row is selected, opens the dialog normally with that row as the root. If multiple rows are selected (or zero), opens the dialog with the main fields DISABLED — only the recent entries list is interactive, so the user can pick a recent definition to pre-populate and re-enable the fields.

Floating dialog for the Dynamic Slice Group feature. When row is non-null, the root UUID + name are shown as static text and all fields are enabled. When row is null (multi-select or no selection), the fields are DISABLED and only the recent entries list at the bottom is interactive — clicking a recent entry pre-populates the fields, updates the static root text, and re-enables everything. On Submit: builds a lightning {mode:'render_tags', tags, postfix_policy:'slice', match_scope} spec, saves the definition to localStorage (_saveDynSliceRecent), builds a RenderProjectionSpec via makeLightningRenderSpec, and delegates to _renderLightningSpecIntoDock. Esc = Cancel, Enter = Submit.

TIER-2 deferred-on-scroll live-GUI-sync watcher installed after an Apply-slice. Reissues the slice membership search, then fires each server pending expand/collapse op by UUID as its row materializes during natural reading-scroll (MutationObserver + scroll listener, rAF-coalesced). EXPAND fires freely (additive; recursive expandSubtreeSafeById -> cascade re-scan catches newly-materialized targets). COLLAPSE fires only when its gated_by expansion ancestors have ALL fired (asymmetric-merge gating; gated_by=[] fires freely). Full safety set after Sync starts: query-bound/tab-bound/keypress-disarm/new-slice-disarm/fire-once/getItemById-recheck/isExpanded-guard + configurable timeout (slice_watcher_timeout_seconds, default 30s, started by the Sync button -- NOT at Apply). While dormant before Sync, modal reading/navigation keypresses do NOT tear down the stored sync plan. Single global watcher; a new install tears down the prior one. Updates the dock status with a flashing GUI-sync countdown and a pending-ops remaining count.

THE single client-side fan-out for a server-echoed render_scope (Option Y, Dan's 'server is the one choke point' model). Called by displaySliceInDock on EVERY successful cache-projected render, regardless of which SURFACE triggered it (a ribbon-widget click -> usually a no-op adopt of the client's own values; an MCP glimpse(push_to_modal=true) call -> a real update that lights up the ribbon). It (1) stores the whole scope in dockedRenderScope (footer display source), (2) mirrors scope IDENTITY into dockedSliceContext (the re-render/per-row scope handle: group_id + root_uuid), and (3) mirrors the VIEW params (sort_by/sort_direction/since/headings_only) into the per-tab render state via setTabModalState so the ribbon widgets + since field repaint to match. Adoption is fail-closed for invalid server-echo `since`: the scope is decoded before any state mutation, and a malformed/string wire value surfaces through the yellow bar and aborts adoption, preserving last-known-good state. Otherwise the since field's existing draft guard (refreshSinceHeadingsUi skips overwriting sinceInput while it is focused) is preserved so a reply landing mid-type never stomps the user's keystrokes. Pure UI/state fan-out; no I/O, no server round-trip.

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD (ap:LRSCOPE) EPHEMERAL display path — the destination of the crack-closer branch in displaySliceInDock for a kind='dom_capture' render_scope. It does NOT adoptRenderScope / normalizeRenderScopeToSpec / set dockedSliceContext.render_spec (that is exactly the launder the crack-closer prevents). Instead it RE-PINS the server-filtered forest as the dock's FROZEN-DOM-SINGLE captured tree (dockedRenderSource='dom', dockedFrozen=true, dockedFrozenSingleActive=true, dockedFrozenSingleTree/Rows set from meta.filtered_forest/rows), so EVERY downstream operation (per-row single render, sort/since via refreshFrozenDomAfterViewChange, frozenDomCapturedTree, resolveLightningRodRootUuid's DOM branch) is handled by the EXISTING frozen-DOM machinery with NO new per-consumer branching. This is the Lightning-within-Lightning wholesale forest replacement: the next Scoped run filters THIS pinned forest. Paints row 0's markdown immediately (raw_text for a gather outline, else marked); suppresses the scroll warning (complete by construction). Ephemeral by construction — nothing durable is stored, so it can never be Refreshed/re-projected as a cache scope.

Display an Apply-slice server render in the dock as a standalone, cache-sourced, inherently-FROZEN document. Sets render PROVENANCE to 'slice' (+ dockedSliceContext={group_id,group_name} so a SLICE-mode Refresh re-applies the same slice), force-FREEZES (dockedRootUuid stays null -- a slice is NOT a DOM view, so live Workflowy clicks must not re-walk it), and POPULATES the top-half tree-view from the server's ordered rows (each carrying the (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) identity triple) instead of blanking it. Records the slice render mode -- 'snapshot' (server pre-rendered every row's option-Y view, kept in dockedSliceSnapshot keyed by sliceRowKey -> instant row clicks) or 'single' (large slice -> requestSliceRowRender on demand). Paints the full-document markdown (row 0's view) immediately, selects row 0 without re-rendering, and SUPPRESSES the scroll warning (cache_sourced; wired through selectionProvablyComplete). Sets dockedPaneHasGoodContent + the rendered source for char-count/Copy-MD.

Resolve the pending merge_slice_groups promise keyed on request_id (the handleMutateNodeTagsResult analog). The reply carries the full merge report (root, tag counts, Q4 mutation ledger, verification block, persistence record) from the server handler.

Q4 Lightning Rod batch tag-mutation wire helper (the section-9 wire contract). CALLED BY _submitTagMutation (the dock 🏷️ Tags… popup submit) -- the older "NO UI affordance calls this yet" note is stale. Fire a mutate_node_tags WS request {action, request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, operations:[{handle, operation:'add'|'remove', tags:[...]} | {handle, operation:'rename', old_tag, new_tag}]} (client-minted request_id) and resolve with the server's mutate_node_tags_result ledger, or null on cold-socket/timeout. OWN 180s timeout class (a batch runs tens of seconds) -- deliberately NOT the shared 30s INTERACTIVE_WS_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS. Socket-drop settling rides failAllPendingSliceRenders (G3). The server handler runs the SAME WorkflowyTagMutationSpec.from_wire grammar core + _lightning_rod_mutate_tags orchestrator as the MCP boundary. The dock already has everything a future UI needs to harvest handles: occurrence-exact row UUID triples + multi-select (dockedSelectedIndices / handleDockRowClick / updateDockRowMarkers).

Resolve the pending anchor_dock_update promise keyed on request_id (the handleMutateNodeTagsResult analog). The reply carries the canonical _anchor_dock_update_impl result (success, no_op, favorite, local, attributes, families_updated, tags, warnings) or a structured error (error_code + extra for dock_families_ambiguous).

Fire an anchor_dock_update WS request (the section-9 wire contract) and resolve with the server's anchor_dock_update_result, or null on cold-socket/timeout. Carries INTENT ONLY: {action, request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, dock_handle, favorite?|local?, families?}. The client composes NO tag, resolves NO handle, picks NO postfix word. OWN pending map (pendingAnchorDockUpdate) + the shared 30s interactive timeout class; socket-drop settling rides failAllPendingSliceRenders. The server handler runs AnchorDockUpdateSpec.from_wire (transport shell only) + the ONE canonical _anchor_dock_update_impl seam the MCP anchor.dock.update tool uses.

THE ONE client-side group-refs normalizer (the JS twin of Python _normalize_group_refs in merge_slice_groups_spec.py). Mirrors the Python checks: groups is a list of 2+ items; STRING items are named groups (id-or-name); OBJECT items are dynamic definitions with root_uuid + tags ('#'-stripped, de-duped, '--' postfix tails rejected). Returns {groups, error} — never throws. The server's from_wire remains the authoritative boundary; this is the client pre-flight twin (dual-normalizer doctrine).
Mint the normalized client-side merge spec object (the JS twin of MergeSliceGroupsSpec). { groups, mode, tag } — frozen-by-convention. Consumed by requestMergeSliceGroups.

THE wire helper for merge_slice_groups (the requestMutateNodeTags analog). Sends {action:'merge_slice_groups', request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, groups, mode, tag} with CANONICAL group refs (named = bare string; dynamic = {root_uuid, tags}) -- the Python _normalize_group_refs grammar, NOT the internal normalized refs. Timeout: args.timeout_seconds (an optional caller-declared wait deadline, e.g. set near a UI button) rides the frame as INTERIM transport metadata (NOT a spec field; REMOVED on the async-CARTO-job migration); fallback = conservative estimate (2.0 s x groups.length*20, 30 s floor; the true A8 value is server-side). Socket-drop settling rides failAllPendingSliceRenders. NO client-side persistence (A9): the server handler persists via create_slice_group; the reply carries the persistence record. NO UI affordance calls this in v1 (exactly how requestMutateNodeTags shipped).

THE ONE client-side operations-grammar normalizer (the JS twin of Python _normalize_operations in lightning_rod_tag_mutation_spec.py). Mirrors the Python checks 1:1: non-empty list, per-verb allowed fields, handle required, duplicate handles rejected, add/remove need tags, rename needs old_tag+new_tag. Returns {operations, error} — never throws. Consumed by makeTagMutationSpec + buildTagMutationSpecFromDockSelection (the dock funnel). The server's from_wire remains the authoritative boundary; this is the client pre-flight twin (dual-normalizer doctrine, same as the render-spec precedent).

The async submit handler for the dock-UI batch tag mutation popup. Fires the shipped requestMutateNodeTags wire helper (the section-9 frame, 180s timeout class), surfaces the result as a toast (committed/noop/failed or batch-abort error) + console ledger, and runs a provenance-aware post-mutation refresh: SLICE provenance auto-Refresh via refreshDockedMarkdownPanel (the server eagerly patches the /nodes-export cache, so the re-projection reflects tag changes including membership/policy effects); frozen-DOM provenance toasts a pinned-view note (does NOT fake freshness). This is the ONE place the mutate_node_tags wire round-trip meets the dock UI.

Client half of the UUID Explorer List anchors round-trip: mints request_id + endpoint_id, sends action=list_anchors_for_widget (with tree_view / show_local_anchors / include_raw_text / favorites_only flags), and resolves the correlated list_anchors_for_widget_result. Mirrors requestCompileSliceSearch; the server owns anchor enumeration. favorites_only rides beside show_local_anchors; the server treats an absent/false flag as the full inventory, so the Saved-Tabs Dock picker (which omits it) keeps seeing every Dock while the Anchors popup sends true for the favorites shortlist.

Fire a render_lightning_dom_capture WS request (the client half of the Scoped Lightning Rod). Mirrors requestCompileSliceSearch's small self-contained round-trip (client-minted request_id, this tab's endpoint_id, ensureSocketReady, 12s timeout, single pending map pendingScopedLightning). Sends ONE of two payload shapes: DOM-frozen carries capturedTree (the pinned frozen forest from frozenDomCapturedTree().tree); slice-frozen carries baseRenderSpec (the durable dockedSliceContext.render_spec) + wasSlice=true and NO capturedTree, so the server projects the base slice to a tree then filters it. Forwards the opaque lightning selection, the optional occurrence-exact row focus (for the domain re-root pre-step), and the dock's current view knobs (as_markdown/headings_only/sort_by/sort_direction/since). Resolves with the reply dict (kind='dom_capture' ephemeral artifact) or null on cold-socket/timeout; the caller routes it through displaySliceInDock -> the crack-closer -> displayScopedDomCaptureInDock.

Defensive collapse helper for the F8 plan: resolves a UUID to a WF item and calls WF.collapseItem(item) if that API exists, else logs a loud console error and returns false (no silent no-op). Counterpart to expandSubtreeSafeById; collapsing a topmost target hides its whole subtree in one call.

Mechanically apply a server F8 plan to the live DOM: expand (via expandSubtreeSafeById) FIRST, then collapse_suppressed then collapse_deprecated (via collapseSubtreeRootById), in that order. Expand-first so a contraction nested inside an expansion region survives (expanding first then collapsing the pocket sticks; the reverse would re-open it). Pure realizer of the returned UUID sets; no client-side policy. Logs any plan warnings.

Build an F8 node's NAME string with its tags guaranteed space-separated and '#'-prefixed, by harvesting .contentTag data-val (the authoritative tag source rowHasNexusExpandTag uses) and appending them to the plain base text. Fixes the textContent tag-gluing bug where server-side extract_name_tags lost glued/'#'-less tags and F8 returned expand=0.

In-place post-pass over an extractSearchResults/extractChildren tree: for each node, look up its live DOM element by projectid and replace its name with extractNodeNameWithTagsForF8(el) so glued/'#'-less tags survive into the server's extract_name_tags. Structure (ids, parent nesting) is left exactly as the proven extractor produced it.

F8 visible-DOM serializer. Delegates to the proven GLIMPSE extraction (extractSearchResults under active search, else extractChildren) rooted like extractDOMTree, so parent nesting is CANONICAL and matches the /nodes-export cache even in search mode (fixes the rootId=None 'Home' + edge-mismatch bug). Then runs retagF8TreeNames so the server's extract_name_tags sees tag-faithful names. Returns {success, root:{id,name,note}, children}.

Resolve the DOM root for server-driven F8: prefer div.project.root[projectid] (the currently zoomed Workflowy root), falling back to the first visible project row. Deliberately does NOT use resolveCurrentPreviewNode, because rooting at the hovered/focused #...--expand node makes Phase 2 discard that node as root and yields expand=0.

Top-level F8 keypress entry point (server-driven): resolve the currently-zoomed Workflowy root (resolveF8VisibleRootNode), serialize its visible DOM subtree tag-faithfully (serializeVisibleTreeForF8), await ensureSocketReady, request the server expansion plan (requestF8ExpansionPlan), and execute it (executeF8ExpansionPlan). Fail-loud, no client-side policy, no fallback.

Fire a render_markdown_modal WS request (client-minted request_id) and resolve with the server-composed Markdown result, or null on cold-socket/timeout so the caller can show the server-unavailable error in the dock. Supports DOM modal modes snapshot (all rows), rows_only (server-authored row list for captured tree), single (one focus_leaf row), and rows (frozen-DOM multi-select covering render with focus={mode:'rows'}).

THE success-paint primitive for the docked modal: renders a server-composed Markdown STRING into the bottom pane (truncation footer + Copy-MD source sync), sets dockedRenderedGoodUuid + dockedPaneHasGoodContent so a later transport failure preserves last-known-good, and returns true iff it painted non-empty. The single place 'good content is now on screen' is recorded; shared by the slice-snapshot, DOM-snapshot, DOM-single, and frozen code paths. Beaconed for the async-render-correctness slice (it is the paint half of the render-generation model + the intended success sink alongside renderDockedSelectionLocal).

Centralized capture of the `since` validation/empty-window signal from ANY docked-modal render reply (DOM or slice; snapshot, single, apply, refresh). On a since_error refusal (success:false + since_error) it stashes the human error string into dockedServerSinceError so applyDockedServerWarning paints the yellow bar at TOP priority (the render was refused -- supersedes the staleness/root bars); otherwise it clears the error and records empty_window (a VALID empty result -> an informational note, not an error). Also repaints the fine-print footer. Returns true iff a since_error was captured so callers can early-out (avoid the local-render fallback that would show stale content instead of teaching the invalid combination).

THE single monotonic RENDER-GENERATION counter for the docked modal -- the keystone of the dock's async-render supersession model. A new render INTENT (a genuine selection change in setDockedSelection, a root-set/Refresh in prepareDockedServerRender, and -- as of the async dock-render-task refactor -- a slice APPLY/PUSH via displaySliceInDock) claims a fresh generation by ++dockedRenderGeneration; each async request captures the value it was fired under and acts ONLY if it still equals the current one at reply/paint time, so EVERY stale reply (success, failure, null, timeout) is dropped by ONE rule and a superseded render can never clobber a newer view. ONE shared clock governs BOTH the DOM-render path and the slice/push paint path (most-recent intent wins the paint chokepoint, independent of which async render finishes first). Historically unbeaconed, which hid it from the f8-expand/md-preview slice and led an architecture session to propose a NEW counter instead of extending this one; beaconed now so the next agent to touch async-render correctness sees it. Find-in-source query compiler for the dock Source view -- the HIGHLIGHT-only JS mini-twin of the server's build_search_predicate smart grammar (lightning_rod_search.py; twins-by-one-grammar, the SinceCodec-pair precedent). Tokenizes whitespace with "quoted phrase" support (unbalanced quote = loud {ok:false}), skips the OR/AND keywords and negated (- / !) terms (negation is meaningful for node FILTERING but not for highlight-in-place; ignored in v1), escapes every regex metacharacter then restores the * / ? GLOB wildcards, drops patterns that could match the empty string (a bare '*' would yield an infinite zero-length-match stream), and returns ONE combined case-insensitive alternation RegExp. Returns {ok:true, regex:null} for a blank/all-negated query (= clear highlights). Keep in lockstep with the server grammar's positive-term subset.

THE single <pre> paint choke for the dock's TEXT views: the Source-view branch of composedMarkdownToHtml AND the native raw_text content format (composedContentToHtml) both route through here. Re-runs on EVERY paint, so highlights re-apply automatically after row clicks / Refresh / Apply / push. SAME escapeHtmlForPreview + glimpse-md-preview-plain idiom the marked-failure fallback always used -- no new rendering path.

Instant LOCAL re-paint of the dock bottom pane from the held dockedRenderedSource through composedContentToHtml (current content_format honored) -- the Source/Rendered toggle's apply step and the find-in-source re-highlight step. The ONE dock toast lifecycle authority. Replaces/starts the transient top-center toast; manual click dismissal clears the timer and leaves controls immediately usable, while automatic timeout dismissal alone arms a 1000ms capture-phase click shield over interactive dock controls. This prevents the toast-vanished-before-mouseup race from accidentally clicking Freeze/Sync behind it without using pointer-events:none (which would pass clicks through to Workflowy). New toast display clears any prior shield. Pure client UI state; no persistence.

beacons.role: ƒ surfaceRenderFailure(res, opts): the single UI helper that turns a render/action reply into the right user-facing failure message
beacons.comment: The ONE place that converts a dock render/action reply into a user-facing failure, so every caller surfaces the server's actionable text identically instead of a bare 'ERR' flash or a silent blank. Distinguishes the three failure modes the endpoint-liveness work defined: res==null -> TRANSPORT failure (no reply / cold socket / timeout); res.code=='unknown_endpoint' -> endpoint-liveness GHOST (tab dropped on an MV3 SW reconnect, already asked to re-register in the background -> retry), preferring the server's own res.error; res.success!==true -> any other structured failure surfaced verbatim (fallback to the caller's fallbackMessage). Returns true iff a failure was surfaced (caller early-returns), false on a success to render. UI propagation ONLY: shows a toast, optionally paints the message into the supplied dock render element and clears the source/leaf-count -- it NEVER renders content and touches no protocol/routing/retry/broker behavior.

Docked Markdown modal 'Copy ID' feature: copy a tree-view row's Workflowy SEARCH STRING `id:<uuid>` to the clipboard (via the shared navigator.clipboard->fallbackCopy path) and flash a showDockToast telling the user to paste it into Workflowy's search box to reveal the node. Invoked (toggle-gated on dockedCopyIdMode) from setDockedSelection so both click and arrow-key selection copy; the full search string is copied (not the bare UUID) so a single paste locates the node.

ONE shared client helper that builds the full render_spec blob for the dock's current cache-sourced view, merging dockedSliceContext.render_spec (the server-adopted scope) with the currently-selected row as spec.focus. Used by BOTH the get_current_modal_render_spec WS leaf query (render_spec='modal') and the '⌖ focus' copy button (fallback paste blob), so the two surfaces cannot drift. Pure in-memory state read; no rendering, no WS round-trip; the server re-projects through the Python composer.

beacons.role: handleSavedTabsDriveApply(payload): apply ONE drive-delivered entry (alias + spec) in this freshly created tab
beacons.comment: Saved-Tabs Tier-2 drive receiver (page world, spec [ap:7S217K] §6): non-empty alias -> setEndpointAlias FIRST (re-registers + retitles immediately, P4/G3); admission via savedTabsValidateEntrySpec (the SAME kernel as single-entry import — exact group_id pre-validation); apply through the ONE shared funnel applySliceGroupIntoDock with applySavedTabsEntry's receiver-identical opts (spec untouched by object identity — A1/G4, [ap:HVAWAF]; generation unclaimed — displaySliceInDock claims at paint and force-freezes, G5); a NAME-ONLY frame (spec null + non-empty alias, follow-up 2) stops after the alias-set and answers ok:true with nothing applied; the terminal saved_tabs_drive_apply_response rides the page-to-sw bridge and is ALWAYS sent (bounded by the long render timeout + the socket-death settle, P7); failures loud via the funnel's ONE sink + the Saved-Tabs status line

Feature 2 dock affordance ('GLIMPSE what the modal is showing right now'): copy the FULL render_spec blob (scope + selected-row focus) as compact JSON to the clipboard, so the human hands it to an agent verbatim as workflowy_glimpse(render_spec=<blob>) to render EXACTLY this row's option-Y view server-side. Uses the SAME currentDockRenderSpecWithSelectedFocus() helper as the render_spec='modal' WS leaf query, preventing copy-vs-query drift. This closes the old scope gap from the bare focus triple: the blob carries group_id/root_uuid/match_scope/etc. AND the focus field. Reuses the shared navigator.clipboard->fallbackCopy idiom + showDockToast. Only meaningful for a cache-sourced SLICE render (dockedRenderSource==='slice'); in DOM mode it toasts guidance instead. One-shot (not a toggle).

Serialize the docked modal's VISIBLE DOM subtree into the nested {root,children} payload the server composer consumes, accumulating total visible name+note char size for the pre-render-threshold decision.

Fire a render_slice_modal WS request (client-minted request_id + this tab's endpoint_id + the group_id, plus the dock's current sort_by/sort_direction) and resolve with the server's cache-projected slice render {success, markdown, cache_sourced, node_count, warnings}, or null on cold-socket/timeout. Mirrors requestCompileSliceSearch / requestMarkdownModalRender exactly. The server composes the Markdown (single source of truth); the client only paints the returned string into the dock.

Browser twin of the server's _slice_row_key. Builds the stable string key for a tree-view row's (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) identity triple, MUST stay byte-for-byte identical to the Python side (same \x1f separators + layout) so a snapshot lookup (dockedSliceSnapshot keyed by this) and a re-projected server render agree. Cross-language contract point -- change both together.

Shared generated timeout policy for cache-backed row renders. Grows from the interactive floor using the already-known final row count, caps at the established 180s long-render ceiling, and never inspects opaque LensSpec atoms; socket-close cleanup remains the immediate failure detector.

Fire an occurrence-exact render_slice_row re-projection from the stored RenderProjectionSpec. The opaque scope (including a canonical render_lens recipe) and row focus ride in one render_spec blob; the request uses the shared row-count-generated cache timeout with an optional bounded override, while socket death still settles immediately through failAllPendingSliceRenders.

SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the on-the-wire lightning selection block carried on render_slice_modal / render_slice_row / apply_slice_in_dock frames. Emits the opaque per-mode selection, including render_lens{lens,query,query_mode,match_scope}; LensSpec is copied verbatim and never interpreted client-side. Used by requestSliceModalRender + requestSliceRowRender so Refresh, row focus, readback, and push cannot drop mode-specific fields.

Client-side SGSORT sort normalizer, the JS twin of the Python RenderProjectionSpec kind-aware sort rule. Requires kind to be known before sort coercion: null/omitted survives only for slice/slice_override request specs (inherit the group's saved default at the server resolve-point), raw_root/lightning collapse null to the explicit 'none' document-order sentinel, and the string 'none' remains distinct from null. Used by the spec builders and normalizeRenderScopeToSpec so Apply/push/request frames preserve the no-cracks null-vs-'none' boundary across the client wire.

CLIENT-side reconstruction of a RenderProjectionSpec from the SERVER's authoritative render_scope echo -- the single fan-in that makes the client half of the shared-object architecture work. adoptRenderScope calls this and stores the result as the SOLE field of dockedSliceContext (dockedSliceContext.render_spec), so the client Refresh (refreshDockedMarkdownPanel) and per-row re-render (requestSliceRowRender) reuse the EXACT scope the server just rendered -- kind / group_id / group_name / root_uuid / opaque lightning selection / match_scope / descend_policy / recursive ([ap:EPR86W] part a: the depth leg of the traversal pair; false = the scope root + its DIRECT children only, raw-root-only today) / sort / since / recent_by ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a): the recency basis of a 'newest' item_count selection; null = the server resolves it) / headings_only / content_format / tree_mode. This IS the client's scope handle: there are no separate scalar mirrors beside it. Derives kind from scope.kind, falling back to the (lightning|group_id+root_uuid|group_id|else) presence truth table for a partial/older scope; preserves the opaque lightning selection verbatim (never interprets it -- the server routes by selection.mode). Tolerant of missing fields (each falls back to RENDER_SPEC_DEFAULTS). This is the JS twin of the Python RenderProjectionSpec normalizers; the small make{Slice,RawRoot,Lightning}RenderSpec factories (used by the human Apply / Lightning ribbon spec-build sites) sit just above and ride under this block. descend_policy and recursive round-trip through here, so Refresh/per-row preserve them for free.

G3 liveness cleanup: settle EVERY in-flight render_slice_modal / render_slice_row promise on transport death (page-world BridgeSocket ws.onclose). Resolves each pending waiter with null -- the SAME 'render failed' signal the 180s leak-cap timeout and a cold-socket send use -- so the failure flows through the ONE existing G2 sink (the caller's `!res` branch: the push receiver's dock toast, the APPLY button's flash('ERR')) instead of hanging until a wall-clock timeout. GENERATION-AGNOSTIC by design: the transport is gone, so ALL pending renders are moot regardless of dockedRenderGeneration -- settle them all to avoid a promise/timer leak. NEVER-REJECT: resolve(null) (not reject) keeps the contract every caller already handles (a rejection would need new try/catch at each await site); the timers are cleared here so no stale resolve(null) fires later.

Fire a render_slice_modal WS request (the Apply-slice FULL-DOCUMENT render). SPEC-ONLY signature: the SOLE arg is a RenderProjectionSpec (+ an optional { renderTimeoutMs } opts bag); a non-spec 1st arg is a loud fail-fast (no positional fallback). The spec is unpacked at the top into the SAME locals the body uses -- group_id + this tab's endpoint_id are sent on the frame, and the spec's view fields drive the sort. SORT PRECEDENCE (now entirely spec-expressed): the spec's sort_by/sort_direction map onto the internal explicit-sortOverride branch, which ALWAYS wins over the internal forceDefaultSort (fixed false for a spec) and never reads/mutates the global md_preview_sort_* store -- so the agent/server push honors the GLIMPSE call's sort, and the human APPLY button expresses its 'default view' intent by BUILDING a spec with sort_by:'none'. The spec's `since` is forwarded verbatim ('' => no since on this render); the global dock since is never inherited here. The server RE-PROJECTS the slice from cache (build_stage1_base_tree) and returns the composed Markdown + tree-view rows + Tier-2 live-GUI-sync fields; resolves with the reply dict or null on cold-socket/timeout. Rides the generic request_id rail (handleRenderSliceModalResult resolves render_slice_modal_result AND render_slice_row_result).

SHARED cache-scope apply orchestration: render any cache-projected scope into the docked modal through ONE RenderProjectionSpec path (requestSliceModalRender -> captureSinceFieldsFromResult -> displaySliceInDock, forwarding Tier-2 live-GUI-sync fields when applicable). Handles slice groups (group_id), slice overrides (group_id + root_uuid), raw-root dumps (root_uuid only), anchor views (raw_root + descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors'), and Lightning Rod selections. The human slice APPLY button, anchor-view APPLY rows, and agent/server push all funnel through this one function. Sort/since/headings are EXPLICIT per-render args (never read from global dock state when supplied), and UI feedback is injected via optional hooks. Returns the server result (or null) so callers can branch on success.

Resolve the root UUID a Lightning Rod ribbon action should scope to = whatever the docked modal is CURRENTLY rooted at, regardless of provenance. SLICE mode (Apply/push/prior Lightning Rod) has dockedRootUuid=null, so read the adopted render_scope's root_uuid (dockedRenderScope || dockedSliceContext); DOM mode uses dockedRootUuid. Returns '' when neither is set (nothing displayed yet) so the caller shows the 'select a node first' toast. The Lightning Rod ribbon has NO paste-a-UUID field BY DESIGN -- it always acts on the current modal root.

SHARED render-into-dock tail for a Lightning Rod spec: requestSliceModalRender -> captureSinceFieldsFromResult -> surfaceRenderFailure -> displaySliceInDock with the standard group-less meta block (group_id:null, the lightning root, empty sync bundle). Extracted from triggerLightningRod's Global fork so the dynamic-slice-group dialog submit can reuse it byte-for-byte (STAGE-0 DOCTRINE: a duplicated pure block is the only Stage-0 crack).

beacons.role: async function triggerLightningRod(mode, query, matchScope, scoped)
beacons.comment: Fire a Lightning Rod from the dock ribbon. mode is 'gather' | 'render_tags' | 'render_search'; the single text box feeds BOTH render modes (render_search verbatim as `query`, render_tags split on whitespace/commas into `tags`); matchScope ('name'|'name_and_note') rides inside the opaque lightning selection. Roots at resolveLightningRodRootUuid() (the current modal root; NO paste-a-UUID field). scoped (the 4th arg, ap:LRSCOPE/ap:LRHAND2) selects between TWO forks: (GLOBAL, scoped falsy) the original path -- build a kind='lightning_rod' RenderProjectionSpec and requestSliceModalRender -> displaySliceInDock, walking the WHOLE cache root; (SCOPED, scoped truthy) confine the search to the dock's CURRENT frozen artifact via requestScopedLightningDomCapture, producing an EPHEMERAL kind='dom_capture' result routed through displaySliceInDock -> the crack-closer -> displayScopedDomCaptureInDock (one-way door; the durable slice/raw origin is discarded, re-Apply to return). Scoped requires dockedFrozen; it sends the pinned captured tree (DOM-frozen) OR the durable base_render_spec + wasSlice (slice-frozen, server projects+filters), plus the optional occurrence-exact selected-row focus as the DOMAIN re-root pre-step (distinct from plain row-click navigation). Global is byte-for-byte the prior behavior.

Trigger for the Dynamic Slice Group dialog. If exactly one row is selected, opens the dialog normally with that row as the root. If multiple rows are selected (or zero), opens the dialog with the main fields DISABLED — only the recent entries list is interactive, so the user can pick a recent definition to pre-populate and re-enable the fields.

Floating dialog for the Dynamic Slice Group feature. When row is non-null, the root UUID + name are shown as static text and all fields are enabled. When row is null (multi-select or no selection), the fields are DISABLED and only the recent entries list at the bottom is interactive — clicking a recent entry pre-populates the fields, updates the static root text, and re-enables everything. On Submit: builds a lightning {mode:'render_tags', tags, postfix_policy:'slice', match_scope} spec, saves the definition to localStorage (_saveDynSliceRecent), builds a RenderProjectionSpec via makeLightningRenderSpec, and delegates to _renderLightningSpecIntoDock. Esc = Cancel, Enter = Submit.

TIER-2 deferred-on-scroll live-GUI-sync watcher installed after an Apply-slice. Reissues the slice membership search, then fires each server pending expand/collapse op by UUID as its row materializes during natural reading-scroll (MutationObserver + scroll listener, rAF-coalesced). EXPAND fires freely (additive; recursive expandSubtreeSafeById -> cascade re-scan catches newly-materialized targets). COLLAPSE fires only when its gated_by expansion ancestors have ALL fired (asymmetric-merge gating; gated_by=[] fires freely). Full safety set after Sync starts: query-bound/tab-bound/keypress-disarm/new-slice-disarm/fire-once/getItemById-recheck/isExpanded-guard + configurable timeout (slice_watcher_timeout_seconds, default 30s, started by the Sync button -- NOT at Apply). While dormant before Sync, modal reading/navigation keypresses do NOT tear down the stored sync plan. Single global watcher; a new install tears down the prior one. Updates the dock status with a flashing GUI-sync countdown and a pending-ops remaining count.

THE single client-side fan-out for a server-echoed render_scope (Option Y, Dan's 'server is the one choke point' model). Called by displaySliceInDock on EVERY successful cache-projected render, regardless of which SURFACE triggered it (a ribbon-widget click -> usually a no-op adopt of the client's own values; an MCP glimpse(push_to_modal=true) call -> a real update that lights up the ribbon). It (1) stores the whole scope in dockedRenderScope (footer display source), (2) mirrors scope IDENTITY into dockedSliceContext (the re-render/per-row scope handle: group_id + root_uuid), and (3) mirrors the VIEW params (sort_by/sort_direction/since/headings_only) into the per-tab render state via setTabModalState so the ribbon widgets + since field repaint to match. Adoption is fail-closed for invalid server-echo `since`: the scope is decoded before any state mutation, and a malformed/string wire value surfaces through the yellow bar and aborts adoption, preserving last-known-good state. Otherwise the since field's existing draft guard (refreshSinceHeadingsUi skips overwriting sinceInput while it is focused) is preserved so a reply landing mid-type never stomps the user's keystrokes. Pure UI/state fan-out; no I/O, no server round-trip.

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD (ap:LRSCOPE) EPHEMERAL display path — the destination of the crack-closer branch in displaySliceInDock for a kind='dom_capture' render_scope. It does NOT adoptRenderScope / normalizeRenderScopeToSpec / set dockedSliceContext.render_spec (that is exactly the launder the crack-closer prevents). Instead it RE-PINS the server-filtered forest as the dock's FROZEN-DOM-SINGLE captured tree (dockedRenderSource='dom', dockedFrozen=true, dockedFrozenSingleActive=true, dockedFrozenSingleTree/Rows set from meta.filtered_forest/rows), so EVERY downstream operation (per-row single render, sort/since via refreshFrozenDomAfterViewChange, frozenDomCapturedTree, resolveLightningRodRootUuid's DOM branch) is handled by the EXISTING frozen-DOM machinery with NO new per-consumer branching. This is the Lightning-within-Lightning wholesale forest replacement: the next Scoped run filters THIS pinned forest. Paints row 0's markdown immediately (raw_text for a gather outline, else marked); suppresses the scroll warning (complete by construction). Ephemeral by construction — nothing durable is stored, so it can never be Refreshed/re-projected as a cache scope.

Display an Apply-slice server render in the dock as a standalone, cache-sourced, inherently-FROZEN document. Sets render PROVENANCE to 'slice' (+ dockedSliceContext={group_id,group_name} so a SLICE-mode Refresh re-applies the same slice), force-FREEZES (dockedRootUuid stays null -- a slice is NOT a DOM view, so live Workflowy clicks must not re-walk it), and POPULATES the top-half tree-view from the server's ordered rows (each carrying the (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) identity triple) instead of blanking it. Records the slice render mode -- 'snapshot' (server pre-rendered every row's option-Y view, kept in dockedSliceSnapshot keyed by sliceRowKey -> instant row clicks) or 'single' (large slice -> requestSliceRowRender on demand). Paints the full-document markdown (row 0's view) immediately, selects row 0 without re-rendering, and SUPPRESSES the scroll warning (cache_sourced; wired through selectionProvablyComplete). Sets dockedPaneHasGoodContent + the rendered source for char-count/Copy-MD.

Resolve the pending merge_slice_groups promise keyed on request_id (the handleMutateNodeTagsResult analog). The reply carries the full merge report (root, tag counts, Q4 mutation ledger, verification block, persistence record) from the server handler.

Q4 Lightning Rod batch tag-mutation wire helper (the section-9 wire contract). CALLED BY _submitTagMutation (the dock 🏷️ Tags… popup submit) -- the older "NO UI affordance calls this yet" note is stale. Fire a mutate_node_tags WS request {action, request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, operations:[{handle, operation:'add'|'remove', tags:[...]} | {handle, operation:'rename', old_tag, new_tag}]} (client-minted request_id) and resolve with the server's mutate_node_tags_result ledger, or null on cold-socket/timeout. OWN 180s timeout class (a batch runs tens of seconds) -- deliberately NOT the shared 30s INTERACTIVE_WS_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS. Socket-drop settling rides failAllPendingSliceRenders (G3). The server handler runs the SAME WorkflowyTagMutationSpec.from_wire grammar core + _lightning_rod_mutate_tags orchestrator as the MCP boundary. The dock already has everything a future UI needs to harvest handles: occurrence-exact row UUID triples + multi-select (dockedSelectedIndices / handleDockRowClick / updateDockRowMarkers).

Resolve the pending anchor_dock_update promise keyed on request_id (the handleMutateNodeTagsResult analog). The reply carries the canonical _anchor_dock_update_impl result (success, no_op, favorite, local, attributes, families_updated, tags, warnings) or a structured error (error_code + extra for dock_families_ambiguous).

Fire an anchor_dock_update WS request (the section-9 wire contract) and resolve with the server's anchor_dock_update_result, or null on cold-socket/timeout. Carries INTENT ONLY: {action, request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, dock_handle, favorite?|local?, families?}. The client composes NO tag, resolves NO handle, picks NO postfix word. OWN pending map (pendingAnchorDockUpdate) + the shared 30s interactive timeout class; socket-drop settling rides failAllPendingSliceRenders. The server handler runs AnchorDockUpdateSpec.from_wire (transport shell only) + the ONE canonical _anchor_dock_update_impl seam the MCP anchor.dock.update tool uses.

THE ONE client-side group-refs normalizer (the JS twin of Python _normalize_group_refs in merge_slice_groups_spec.py). Mirrors the Python checks: groups is a list of 2+ items; STRING items are named groups (id-or-name); OBJECT items are dynamic definitions with root_uuid + tags ('#'-stripped, de-duped, '--' postfix tails rejected). Returns {groups, error} — never throws. The server's from_wire remains the authoritative boundary; this is the client pre-flight twin (dual-normalizer doctrine).
Mint the normalized client-side merge spec object (the JS twin of MergeSliceGroupsSpec). { groups, mode, tag } — frozen-by-convention. Consumed by requestMergeSliceGroups.

THE wire helper for merge_slice_groups (the requestMutateNodeTags analog). Sends {action:'merge_slice_groups', request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, groups, mode, tag} with CANONICAL group refs (named = bare string; dynamic = {root_uuid, tags}) -- the Python _normalize_group_refs grammar, NOT the internal normalized refs. Timeout: args.timeout_seconds (an optional caller-declared wait deadline, e.g. set near a UI button) rides the frame as INTERIM transport metadata (NOT a spec field; REMOVED on the async-CARTO-job migration); fallback = conservative estimate (2.0 s x groups.length*20, 30 s floor; the true A8 value is server-side). Socket-drop settling rides failAllPendingSliceRenders. NO client-side persistence (A9): the server handler persists via create_slice_group; the reply carries the persistence record. NO UI affordance calls this in v1 (exactly how requestMutateNodeTags shipped).

THE ONE client-side operations-grammar normalizer (the JS twin of Python _normalize_operations in lightning_rod_tag_mutation_spec.py). Mirrors the Python checks 1:1: non-empty list, per-verb allowed fields, handle required, duplicate handles rejected, add/remove need tags, rename needs old_tag+new_tag. Returns {operations, error} — never throws. Consumed by makeTagMutationSpec + buildTagMutationSpecFromDockSelection (the dock funnel). The server's from_wire remains the authoritative boundary; this is the client pre-flight twin (dual-normalizer doctrine, same as the render-spec precedent).

The async submit handler for the dock-UI batch tag mutation popup. Fires the shipped requestMutateNodeTags wire helper (the section-9 frame, 180s timeout class), surfaces the result as a toast (committed/noop/failed or batch-abort error) + console ledger, and runs a provenance-aware post-mutation refresh: SLICE provenance auto-Refresh via refreshDockedMarkdownPanel (the server eagerly patches the /nodes-export cache, so the re-projection reflects tag changes including membership/policy effects); frozen-DOM provenance toasts a pinned-view note (does NOT fake freshness). This is the ONE place the mutate_node_tags wire round-trip meets the dock UI.

Client half of the UUID Explorer List anchors round-trip: mints request_id + endpoint_id, sends action=list_anchors_for_widget (with tree_view / show_local_anchors / include_raw_text / favorites_only flags), and resolves the correlated list_anchors_for_widget_result. Mirrors requestCompileSliceSearch; the server owns anchor enumeration. favorites_only rides beside show_local_anchors; the server treats an absent/false flag as the full inventory, so the Saved-Tabs Dock picker (which omits it) keeps seeing every Dock while the Anchors popup sends true for the favorites shortlist.

Fire a render_lightning_dom_capture WS request (the client half of the Scoped Lightning Rod). Mirrors requestCompileSliceSearch's small self-contained round-trip (client-minted request_id, this tab's endpoint_id, ensureSocketReady, 12s timeout, single pending map pendingScopedLightning). Sends ONE of two payload shapes: DOM-frozen carries capturedTree (the pinned frozen forest from frozenDomCapturedTree().tree); slice-frozen carries baseRenderSpec (the durable dockedSliceContext.render_spec) + wasSlice=true and NO capturedTree, so the server projects the base slice to a tree then filters it. Forwards the opaque lightning selection, the optional occurrence-exact row focus (for the domain re-root pre-step), and the dock's current view knobs (as_markdown/headings_only/sort_by/sort_direction/since). Resolves with the reply dict (kind='dom_capture' ephemeral artifact) or null on cold-socket/timeout; the caller routes it through displaySliceInDock -> the crack-closer -> displayScopedDomCaptureInDock.

Defensive collapse helper for the F8 plan: resolves a UUID to a WF item and calls WF.collapseItem(item) if that API exists, else logs a loud console error and returns false (no silent no-op). Counterpart to expandSubtreeSafeById; collapsing a topmost target hides its whole subtree in one call.

Mechanically apply a server F8 plan to the live DOM: expand (via expandSubtreeSafeById) FIRST, then collapse_suppressed then collapse_deprecated (via collapseSubtreeRootById), in that order. Expand-first so a contraction nested inside an expansion region survives (expanding first then collapsing the pocket sticks; the reverse would re-open it). Pure realizer of the returned UUID sets; no client-side policy. Logs any plan warnings.

Build an F8 node's NAME string with its tags guaranteed space-separated and '#'-prefixed, by harvesting .contentTag data-val (the authoritative tag source rowHasNexusExpandTag uses) and appending them to the plain base text. Fixes the textContent tag-gluing bug where server-side extract_name_tags lost glued/'#'-less tags and F8 returned expand=0.

In-place post-pass over an extractSearchResults/extractChildren tree: for each node, look up its live DOM element by projectid and replace its name with extractNodeNameWithTagsForF8(el) so glued/'#'-less tags survive into the server's extract_name_tags. Structure (ids, parent nesting) is left exactly as the proven extractor produced it.

F8 visible-DOM serializer. Delegates to the proven GLIMPSE extraction (extractSearchResults under active search, else extractChildren) rooted like extractDOMTree, so parent nesting is CANONICAL and matches the /nodes-export cache even in search mode (fixes the rootId=None 'Home' + edge-mismatch bug). Then runs retagF8TreeNames so the server's extract_name_tags sees tag-faithful names. Returns {success, root:{id,name,note}, children}.

Resolve the DOM root for server-driven F8: prefer div.project.root[projectid] (the currently zoomed Workflowy root), falling back to the first visible project row. Deliberately does NOT use resolveCurrentPreviewNode, because rooting at the hovered/focused #...--expand node makes Phase 2 discard that node as root and yields expand=0.

Top-level F8 keypress entry point (server-driven): resolve the currently-zoomed Workflowy root (resolveF8VisibleRootNode), serialize its visible DOM subtree tag-faithfully (serializeVisibleTreeForF8), await ensureSocketReady, request the server expansion plan (requestF8ExpansionPlan), and execute it (executeF8ExpansionPlan). Fail-loud, no client-side policy, no fallback.

Fire a render_markdown_modal WS request (client-minted request_id) and resolve with the server-composed Markdown result, or null on cold-socket/timeout so the caller can show the server-unavailable error in the dock. Supports DOM modal modes snapshot (all rows), rows_only (server-authored row list for captured tree), single (one focus_leaf row), and rows (frozen-DOM multi-select covering render with focus={mode:'rows'}).

THE success-paint primitive for the docked modal: renders a server-composed Markdown STRING into the bottom pane (truncation footer + Copy-MD source sync), sets dockedRenderedGoodUuid + dockedPaneHasGoodContent so a later transport failure preserves last-known-good, and returns true iff it painted non-empty. The single place 'good content is now on screen' is recorded; shared by the slice-snapshot, DOM-snapshot, DOM-single, and frozen code paths. Beaconed for the async-render-correctness slice (it is the paint half of the render-generation model + the intended success sink alongside renderDockedSelectionLocal).

Centralized capture of the `since` validation/empty-window signal from ANY docked-modal render reply (DOM or slice; snapshot, single, apply, refresh). On a since_error refusal (success:false + since_error) it stashes the human error string into dockedServerSinceError so applyDockedServerWarning paints the yellow bar at TOP priority (the render was refused -- supersedes the staleness/root bars); otherwise it clears the error and records empty_window (a VALID empty result -> an informational note, not an error). Also repaints the fine-print footer. Returns true iff a since_error was captured so callers can early-out (avoid the local-render fallback that would show stale content instead of teaching the invalid combination).

Phase 0 universal row adoption: whenever the server returned ordered rows (now EVERY snapshot, sorted or not), rebuild the docked top-half flat list from them -- the ONE server-authored occurrence-exact (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) row contract -- instead of the browser DOM walk; re-derives the browser-local per-row icon kind + hidden-children halo + el anchor from the live DOM keyed by uuid. Returns false only when there are NO server rows (cold socket), where the caller falls back to buildFlatVisibleNodeList. Supersedes the old sort-gated applySortedServerRows (kept as a thin alias).

FROZEN-DOM-SINGLE twin of applySortedServerRows (FIX 2 corollary). Rebuilds the docked top-half list from the server rows-only ordering of the captured frozen tree so a frozen sort's top list mirrors the bottom pane; carries the (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) triple for occurrence-exact per-row single renders. No-op (false) when unsorted / no rows.

Per-root-set/refresh: measure the visible tree and choose snapshot (pre-render all rows, cached) vs single (render-on-demand) vs local (cold-socket fallback); records cache_stale/root_matched for the warning bars. RENDER-GENERATION PARTICIPANT: bumps the shared monotonic dockedRenderGeneration on each prepare intent and gates its own snapshot install on it, so a superseded prepare cannot clobber a newer root's strategy. This is the DOM-render half of the ONE shared supersession clock the slice/push paint path also rides (see dockedRenderGeneration + displaySliceInDock). Tagged f8-expand so it surfaces in the async-render-correctness slice.

Renders the selected row's option-Y view across all sources (slice snapshot, slice single, frozen snapshot, DOM snapshot, DOM single). Captures the shared dockedRenderGeneration per async request (reqGeneration) and drops any reply whose generation is no longer current -- the DOM-render half of the ONE shared supersession clock the slice/push paint path also rides. Tagged f8-expand for the async-render-correctness slice.

THE transport-failure sink for the docked modal (misnamed 'local' -- there is NO local composition since the server became the sole renderer). Rule: if dockedPaneHasGoodContent it is a pure no-op (last-known-good is sacred -- suppresses spontaneous MV3/WebSocket-blip wipes); only on a genuine COLD START (pane never rendered) does it paint the actionable 'GLIMPSE server unavailable' message. This is the DOM-path error sink the G2 unified-error-sink work must fold together with the slice/push failure modes. Beaconed for the async-render-correctness slice.

Dock Refresh (ribbon ↻), the user's explicit re-sync gesture. Dispatches on render provenance: SLICE mode RE-APPLIES the same slice (requestSliceModalRender(dockedSliceContext.group_id) -> displaySliceInDock), re-projecting from the current nodes cache + group config + dock sort so edits made while curating a frozen slice are pulled in (deprecated nodes vanish, etc.); DOM mode re-walks the visible tree under dockedRootUuid and RESETS the bottom view to the root (index 0), deliberately NOT chasing the previously-selected row (occurrence can shift under sorting). Frozen-DOM rebuilds the in-memory snapshot and serves from it (no round trip).
